DISCUSSION: PwMS have more chronic comorbidities and are at a considerable heightened risk of infections. Prevention, early detection and treatment of comorbidities may ameliorate prognosis of MS and the presence of comorbidities should be part of individualized DMT MS patient care.

etudes.titre: Surgical outcomes of the SIBS microshunt in pediatric glaucoma: a retrospective study.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Surgical »
etudes.resume:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the surgical outcomes of the ab externo SIBS microshunt (PreserFlo MicroShunt; Glaukos Corporation, Aliso Viejo, CA) in the treatment of pediatric glaucoma.
METHODS: This single-centre retrospective case series was conducted at a tertiary pediatric care centre in Montreal, Ontario. All pediatric patients (<18 years of age) with primary or secondary glaucoma, who underwent SIBS microshunt implantation between January 2022 and April 2025, were included. The primary endpoint was surgical success (intraocular pressure 6-21 mm Hg), defined as complete without glaucoma medications and qualified with medications but without further surgery. Secondary outcomes included postoperative IOP, number of glaucoma medications, and postoperative complications.
RESULTS: Eighteen eyes from 14 patients were included. Mean age was 13.7 ± 4.2 years. Mean follow-up was 15.3 ± 9.2 months. Across all eyes, mean intraocular pressure decreased from 28.3±4.5 mm Hg preoperatively to 19.1 ± 7.7 mm Hg at 12 months (p = .02). The mean number of glaucoma medications decreased from 5.1 ± 0.6 preoperatively to 1.6 ± 2.2 at 12 months (p = .002). Complete surgical success rates were 61% at 6 months and 49% at 12 months, while qualified success rates were 67% and 55%, respectively. Postoperative complications occurred in 2 eyes: malignant glaucoma (n = 1) and choroidal and serous retinal detachment (n = 1).
CONCLUSIONS: In pediatric glaucoma, the ab externo SIBS microshunt demonstrated reasonable 1-year surgical success rates with few complications, supporting its potential as a therapeutic alternative in selected cases within this population. Long-term, prospective studies are warranted to further assess its durability and safety in this population.
etudes.revue: Canadian journal of ophthalmology. Journal canadien d'ophtalmologie

etudes.titre: Resveratrol attenuates diabetic RGC degeneration through TRIM23-dependent VDAC1 ubiquitination and mitophagy.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « RGC »; mot du titre : « mitophagy »
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: Retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) degeneration is an early event in diabetic retinopathy (DR), tightly coupled to mitochondrial dysfunction. While the mitochondrial gatekeeper voltage-dependent anion channel 1(VDAC1) is a known mediator of apoptosis, its regulation and therapeutic targeting in diabetic RGCs remain unclear.
METHODS: We examined VDAC1 expression in human donor retinas, streptozotocin-induced diabetic mice, and high glucose-treated SH-SY5Y cells. VDAC1-knockdown SH-SY5Y cells were established to explore its functional role in the context. Using virtual screening and molecular docking, we identified resveratrol (RSV) as a potential VDAC1 inhibitor, which was further validated by surface plasmon resonance binding assays and RSV-based pull-down experiments. The effects of RSV were assessed by RGCs survival, retinal electrophysiological function, and mitochondrial quality control. Tripartite motif-containing 23 (TRIM23)-VDAC1 interaction along with ubiquitination modifications were confirmed by co-immunoprecipitation. Finally, combination therapy involving RSV and adeno-associated virus serotype 2 (AAV2) carrying the γ-synuclein (SNCG) promoter mediated Trim23 overexpression was applied in both DR and acute ocular hypertension (AOH) animal models.
RESULTS: VDAC1 was upregulated in diabetic RGCs, and its knockdown was protective. We further discovered that RSV recruits the E3 ligase TRIM23 to VDAC1, inducing a K27-linked ubiquitination switch that promotes mitophagy instead of apoptosis. We propose that RSV binding acts as an allosteric switch, reconfiguring VDAC1 to favor this protective ubiquitination pathway. Consequently, RSV restored mitochondrial health and RGCs viability. Therapeutically, enhancing this axis via RSV and RGCs-targeted Trim23 overexpression synergistically protected against RGCs loss in both DR and AOH models.
CONCLUSION: Our study unveils a pharmacologically inducible switch wherein RSV, via direct VDAC1 binding, redirects its function toward TRIM23-mediated K27-linked ubiquitination and mitophagy. The TRIM23-VDAC1 allosteric axis represents a novel therapeutic paradigm for neuroprotective intervention in DR and beyond.

etudes.titre: Metformin as an Emerging Candidate for Diabetic Retinopathy, Agerelated Macular Degeneration and Glaucoma Pharmacotherapy: Evidence and Perspectives.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Pharmacotherapy »
etudes.resume: Varying degrees of visual impairment up to complete blindness are widespread and represent a public health problem with a highly demarсated escalation. Currently, the leading causes of blindness are Diabetic Retinopathy (DR), Age-Related Macular Degeneration (AMD), and glaucoma, with an obvious exponential enlargement of vulnerable population groups as a result of urbanization followed by lifestyle changes and growth of the aging population. Management of these diseases is still challenging. The development of intraocular therapy with antiangiogenics or Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor inhibitors (anti-VEGF) opens a new avenue in eye disease treatment; however, despite these advances, new concerns are raised. DR, AMD, and glaucoma represent diseases with bilateral involvement, which underscores a need for oral systemic preventive therapy targeting both eyes simultaneously, as a cost-effectively optimized approach. At the same time, there is a need for a multi-target drug with preventive and therapeutic potential not only for eye diseases, but also for systemic diseases in patients with multimorbidity. Continued research has the potential to enhance druggability of the leading causes of blindness. A growing body of evidence suggests that metformin, as a drug with multimodal activity, has good preventive and therapeutic potential, opening a new avenue in ocular pharmacotherapy.
etudes.revue: Current reviews in clinical and experimental pharmacology

etudes.titre: Goniotomy as a safe and effective option for glaucoma secondary to typical ocular coloboma: A 12-month follow-up case.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Goniotomy »
etudes.resume: A woman in her mid-50s presented with lifelong poor vision and progressive, painless bilateral visual deterioration. Clinical evaluation revealed markedly reduced visual acuity, elevated intraocular pressure, bilateral inferior iris coloboma, zonular laxity, nuclear cataracts, partially closed angles and hypoplastic trabecular meshwork. Sequential phacoemulsification with intraocular lens implantation combined with a 120° goniotomy was performed in both eyes. Intraoperatively, residual embryonic tissue overlying the trabecular meshwork and a diminished red reflex were observed. Postoperatively, the patient experienced rapid improvement in visual acuity and intraocular pressure, with restoration of corneal clarity and wide opening of the anterior chamber angles within 1 week. Fundus examination subsequently revealed an inferonasal choroidal coloboma with retinal vessels traversing the defect. At 1-year, visual acuity remained significantly improved and intraocular pressure was stable without medication, with no complications such as hypotony or retinal detachment. This case demonstrates the safety and efficacy of combined cataract extraction and goniotomy in patients with complex anterior segment anomalies associated with iris and choroidal coloboma.
etudes.revue: The Journal of international medical research

etudes.titre: Clinical Profile and Visual Outcomes of Pre- and Postembolization of Carotid-cavernous Fistula-induced Glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Carotid-cavernous fistula (CCF) requires comprehensive postembolization management to address secondary complications, including glaucoma. A 70-year-old male presented with the inability to open his left eye, progressive eyelid swelling, and orbital congestion. Examination revealed severe conjunctival chemosis with dilated episcleral vessels, elevated intraocular pressure (IOP; 20 mmHg), and corneal Descemet's folds. Imaging confirmed an arteriovenous fistula at the left sphenoid bone draining into the superior ophthalmic vein. The patient underwent successful endovascular embolization of the left sphenoid arteriovenous fistula. Medical management included topical dorzolamide, beta-blockers, and oral acetazolamide for IOP control. Postembolization, there was a significant reduction in orbital congestion, improved eyelid function, and stabilization of IOP. Visual acuity improved from counting fingers to 6/12 with successful preservation of optic nerve function. This case highlights the importance of timely multispecialty collaboration between ophthalmology and interventional radiology in managing CCF-related secondary glaucoma.

etudes.titre: Quantitative detection of the diabetic retinopathy-associated microRNA-1281 via a CRISPR/Cas12a-RCA ratiometric sensing platform.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « detection »

labos.nom: National Natural Science Foundation of China
Department of Science and Technology of Jilin Province

etudes.resume: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a major microvascular complication of diabetes, yet accessible molecular tools for early-stage screening remain limited. Circulating microRNAs are promising non-invasive biomarkers for DR, but their reliable quantification in serum is hindered by low abundance, matrix interference, and limited robustness of single-signal assays. Here, we report a Cas12a-RCA ratiometric sensing platform (CRRSP) for the quantitative detection of the DR-associated biomarker miR-1281. The assay is constructed using a target-triggered cascaded strand-displacement circuit that enforces sequential molecular recognition prior to amplification, thereby improving specificity. Upon target recognition, rolling circle amplification (RCA) generates DNA products that simultaneously produce a thioflavin T (ThT) fluorescence signal via G-quadruplex (G4) formation and sequester the Cas12a/gRNA Activator strand to suppress ROX fluorescence. This dual-channel ThT/ROX readout enables intrinsic ratiometric normalization, effectively compensating for matrix effects and experimental variability. The workflow operates under sequential constant-temperature steps without PCR-type thermal cycling. The assay achieves a detection limit of 0.83 pM with high selectivity and shows excellent agreement with RT-qPCR in clinical serum samples from healthy controls, glaucoma patients, and patients with non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy (NPDR) or proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR).

etudes.titre: Current Trends in AI and Eye Disease Diagnostics.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « AI »; mot du titre : « Diagnostics »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly advanced as an approach for ophthalmic disease detection, driven by the widespread use of high-dimensional imaging modalities (e.g., optical coherence tomography). This review summarises the machine learning and AI approaches for disease detection in ophthalmology and discusses emerging paradigms and highlights key challenges impacting clinical translation.
RECENT FINDINGS: AI-based systems have demonstrated suitably high diagnostic performance across major ophthalmic diseases, including diabetic retinopathy (DR), diabetic macular oedema, glaucoma, age-related macular degeneration and retinopathy of prematurity. Several tools have even received regulatory approval for commercial DR screening. More recently, foundation models trained using self-supervised learning have enabled more generalisable and data-efficient disease detection across datasets and imaging modalities. In parallel, multimodal large language model systems are emerging that integrate imaging and clinical data to support more comprehensive diagnostic workflows. Early agentic AI systems extend this paradigm further by coordinating multiple models to perform disease detection, provide clinical decision support and generate reports. AI-based disease detection in ophthalmology has achieved substantial technical progress but only limited translation into routine clinical practice. Key barriers include technical, clinical, ethical, economic and regulatory concerns. Future efforts should prioritise prospective evaluation in real-world settings, addressing model transparency and bias and alignment with clinical and regulatory requirements. With continued advances, AI has the potential to expand access to care, improve diagnostic accuracy and reduce the global burden of vision loss.
etudes.revue: Ophthalmic & physiological optics : the journal of the British College of Ophthalmic Opticians (Optometrists)

etudes.titre: Integrated bioinformatics identification and independent validation of FLNA, CCL2, and VMO1 as candidate biomarkers for dexamethasone-induced glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « biomarkers »
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: Dexamethasone-induced glaucoma (DIG) lacks early diagnostic biomarkers, and exosome-associated signatures remain underexplored, hindering timely clinical intervention.
METHODS: We integrated three GEO trabecular meshwork transcriptomic datasets. GSE16643 and GSE37474 (11 control, 11 treated) formed the training set; GSE124114 (9 control, 9 treated) served as independent validation. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were intersected with an exosome-associated gene set from GeneCards (relevance score >2). Candidate biomarkers were prioritized via LASSO, SVM-RFE, and Random Forest, followed by cross-validation. A nomogram was constructed and internally validated using 200 bootstrap resamples. Functional enrichment and molecular docking (CB-Dock2) were also performed.
RESULTS: We identified 399 DEGs, of which 16 overlapped with exosome-related genes. Six candidates emerged from multi-algorithm screening, but only three (FLNA, CCL2, and VMO1) passed independent validation; ITGB4 was excluded due to inconsistent expression trends between cohorts. These three genes demonstrated robust discriminative ability in both training and validation sets. Enrichment analyses implicated MAPK signaling, extracellular matrix remodeling, oxidative stress, and lipid metabolic reprogramming, including adipogenesis and cholesterol homeostasis. The nomogram integrating these genes exhibited favorable calibration. Molecular docking revealed strong binding affinity of ellagic acid to FLNA and moderate affinity to CCL2.
CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that FLNA, CCL2, and VMO1 may serve as promising exosome-associated biomarkers for DIG, potentially involved in immune-metabolic regulation and extracellular matrix homeostasis. However, given the limited cohort size and the computational nature of the docking predictions, these results should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating and require further validation in independent cohorts and experimental systems.

etudes.titre: Integrating epidemiology and mechanistic studies links PFAS exposure to ocular diseases and implicates PFOS-associated glaucoma risk through the PI3K/Akt-MMP3 axis.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « axis »

labos.nom: Natural Science Foundation of Nantong City
National Natural Science Foundation of China
Special Funds for the Basic Research and Development Program in the Central Non-profit Research Institutesof China
Graduate Research and Innovation Projects of Jiangsu Province
National College Students Innovation and Entrepreneurship Training Program
High Level Innovation and Entrepreneurial Research Team Program in Jiangsu
Natural Science Foundation of Nantong Municipality
Special Funds for the Basic Research and Development Program in the Central Non-profit Research Institutes of China

etudes.resume: Perfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) pose health risks, but their association with glaucoma, cataracts, and age-related macular degeneration remains uncertain. First, a cross-sectional analysis of NHANES (2005-2008) was performed using multiple logistic regression and mixture models, including weighted quantile sum (WQS), quantile g-computation (QGC), and Bayesian kernel machine regression (BKMR), to examine single and mixed PFAS exposures in relation to ocular diseases. Second, Mendelian randomization was applied to further explore the PFOS-glaucoma association. Third, network toxicology and in vitro experiments were employed to generate mechanistic hypotheses. Cross-sectional results suggested positive associations between PFOS and glaucoma, and between PFNA and cataracts. Sex-stratified analyses revealed positive associations of PFOS with glaucoma in females, and in males, of PFDA with glaucoma and PFNA with cataracts. Mixture models suggested that PFOS may be a driving factor for glaucoma risk. Sensitivity analyses yielded results generally consistent with the primary findings. Mendelian randomization supported a positive PFOS-glaucoma association. Network toxicology and in vitro experiments indicated that PFOS activates PI3K/Akt signaling and reduces MMP3 expression. LY294002 treatment partly restored MMP3 expression, supporting a role for PI3K/Akt signaling in this response. These results suggest that the PI3K/Akt-MMP3 axis may be involved in PFOS-induced extracellular matrix changes in trabecular meshwork cells.
etudes.revue: Food and chemical toxicology : an international journal published for the British Industrial Biological Research Association

etudes.titre: Knocking down FSTL1 reduces TGF-β2-induced trabecular meshwork fibrosis and ocular hypertension via inhibition of the Smad3 signaling pathway.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « pathway »; étiquette : stade préclinique (indexation PubMed)

labos.nom: National Natural Science Foundation of China
Ministry of Science and Technology of the People's Republic of China
National Key Research and Development Program of China
Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine

etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: Excessive accumulation of extracellular matrix (ECM) in the trabecular meshwork (TM) increases aqueous humor outflow resistance, leading to elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) and the development of primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG). Transforming growth factor-β2 (TGF-β2) is a well-established profibrotic mediator implicated in TM fibrosis. Despite its recognized role in promoting ECM deposition, the downstream regulatory mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Follistatin-like 1 (FSTL1), a secreted glycoprotein involved in various fibrotic diseases, has recently drawn attention, yet its role in TM fibrosis and IOP regulation in POAG remains unclear.
METHODS: TGF-β2-induced human trabecular meshwork (HTM) cells and a murine model of TGF-β2-induced ocular hypertension were employed. Proteomic analysis, Western blotting, quantitative real-time PCR, and immunofluorescence were used to assess ECM expression and TGF-β2/Smad3 signaling. Loss-of-function approaches were applied to examine the role of FSTL1 in trabecular meshwork fibrosis and intraocular pressure regulation.
RESULTS: FSTL1 was induced by TGF-β2 and associated with enhanced ECM accumulation and Smad3 activation in HTM cells. Silencing FSTL1 reduced TGF-β2 induced ECM deposition and p-Smad3 accumulation in vitro, and intraocular FSTL1 knockdown mitigated TM fibrosis and lowered TGF-β2-induced ocular hypertension in mice.
CONCLUSION: These findings identify FSTL1 as an important regulator of TGF-β2-induced TM fibrosis. FSTL1 contributes to ECM accumulation and IOP elevation with Smad3 signaling under profibrotic conditions. Targeting FSTL1 may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for limiting TM fibrosis and IOP elevation in POAG.

etudes.titre: The Heterogeneity of the Neurovascular Unit in the Optic Nerve Head During Glaucomatous Neurodegeneration Based on Single-Cell RNA Sequencing.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Sequencing »; mot du titre : « Neurodegeneration »

MOST National Natural Science Foundation of China
Beijing Municipal Public Welfare Development and Reform Pilot Project for Medical Research Institutes

Xi'an Jiaotong University Basic Scientific Research Funding
The First Affiliated Hospital of Xi'an Jiaotong University
Key Research & Development Program of Shaanxi Province
National Natural Science Foundation of China

etudes.resume: Glaucoma is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disease, and the dysfunction of the neurovascular unit (NVU) in optic nerve head (ONH) has been gradually recognized to contribute to the neurodegeneration progression, yet its heterogeneity features remain poorly understood. Here, we established rat models of high intraocular pressure (HIOP) and lipopolysaccharide-induced ocular inflammation (LPS), and performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of ONH-centered tissues to characterize the cellular and molecular characteristics of NVU and its main cell components. Distinct alterations in the cellular composition and intercellular communication of the ONH-NVU were observed among Ctrl, HIOP and LPS conditions. Astrocytes showed a prominent increase of relative proportion in the HIOP group, whereas microglia were preferentially expanded under LPS stimulation. Astrocytes, microglia and endothelial cells showed a firm interaction via cell-cell communication analysis, in which the interactions within astrocytes and endothelial cells were the highest. Reclustering of main NVU cell types were further identified distinct subpopulations, including Dcn+Myoc+ astrocytes, S100a8+S100a9+ microglia and Nebl+Cytl1+ endothelial cells with prominent heterogeneity features, and their cellular interactions exhibited a prominent integrin-collagen network in orchestrating ECM restructuring under HIOP conditions. Additional histomorphological analysis further verified the early collapse of ONH astrocytic network and RGC degeneration. Therefore, these findings reveal the distinct ONH-NVU heterogeneity under HIOP condition, the astrocyte-mediated ECM remodeling may serve as a key early mechanobiological event for subsequent ONH cupping and glaucomatous neurodegeneration.
etudes.revue: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology

etudes.titre: Bilateral Keratouveitis and Secondary Glaucoma in a Young Dog With Immune-Mediated Polyarthritis and Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome.
etudes.phase: Stade : Vétérinaire (animaux soignés) — hors veille principale
etudes.raison_rubrique: étiquette vétérinaire (revue vétérinaire (Veterinary ophthalmology))
etudes.resume: A 7-month-old intact female mixed-breed dog presented emergently for inability to walk, lethargy, and vomiting. The patient was diagnosed with immune-mediated polyarthritis (IMPA) and secondary systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS). Bilateral keratouveitis and secondary glaucoma developed within 24 h of presentation. Thorough diagnostic testing failed to identify an underlying etiology. Despite aggressive medical management, the patient developed rapid vision loss. Due to poor visual prognosis and anticipated need for long-term medical management, both eyes were enucleated. Histopathological evaluation of both globes revealed severe corneal endothelial injury most consistent with endotheliitis with associated uveitis and endophthalmitis. Testing of ocular tissue with PCR and immunohistochemistry for canine adenovirus was negative, and comprehensive infectious disease screening, joint cultures, and ocular histopathology identified no other causative agents. Following enucleation, the dog systemically improved with anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial medical management. This report highlights a unique and severe case of bilateral keratouveitis with glaucoma following a systemic inflammatory event.

etudes.titre: Paul glaucoma implant extrusion following post-surgical scleritis in patients with uveitic glaucoma: A case series.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « surgical »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: This report describes two cases of plate exposure and severe extrusion of the Paul Glaucoma Implant (PGI) following post-surgical exacerbation of scleritis. Additionally, it outlines the management approach used to control ocular inflammation and perform explantation, including exchange to a Preserflo MicroShunt in one of the cases.
OBSERVATIONS: Two females receiving systemic immunosuppression developed exacerbation of scleritis 7 and 5 months post PGI implantation. One patient demonstrated scleral melt and conjunctival thinning beneath the large PGI plate. Both patients received maximum doses of systemic corticosteroids and mycophenolate mofetil to control ocular inflammation. Owing to the high risk of infection and re-exposure, each patient underwent PGI explantation. In one case, a Preserflo MicroShunt was implanted during the same surgical session to minimize conjunctival manipulation and maintain long-term intraocular pressure control, which remained stable for more than a year.
CONCLUSIONS: Surgically induced scleral necrosis occurs in patients following glaucoma drainage device surgery, even in patients already receiving systemic corticosteroids and steroid-sparing immunomodulators. In these cases, inflammation may progress silently beneath the glaucoma drainage device plate until scleral melt and conjunctiva damage become evident intraoperatively. Early recognition of scleritis exacerbation and prompt escalation of systemic immunosuppression are essential, and explantation may be required when structural integrity is compromised.
etudes.revue: American journal of ophthalmology case reports

etudes.titre: Clinical and refractive outcomes of secondary intraocular lens fixation using small-incision scleral suture fixation vs intrascleral haptic fixation.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To compare clinical and refractive outcomes of small-incision scleral suture fixation (SSF) vs intrascleral haptic fixation (ISHF) for secondary intraocular lens (IOL) implantation in adults.
SETTING: Single outpatient ophthalmology clinic.
DESIGN: Retrospective, single-center cohort study.
METHODS: Eyes undergoing small-incision SSF or ISHF between 2019 and 2024 were identified. Demographics, surgical indications, IOL types, refractive accuracy, and postoperative complications were analyzed. Refractive outcomes were evaluated using spherical equivalent refractive accuracy (SERA) and absolute SERA (ASERA).
RESULTS: 132 eyes from 125 adult patients were included. 56 eyes underwent SSF, and 76 underwent ISHF. Indications included subluxated IOL (58%), dislocated IOL (17%), aphakia (20%), and uveitis-glaucoma-hyphema syndrome (5%). In the SSF group, MX60E or ET IOLs predominated, while CT Lucia 602 was most common in ISHF. Mean SERA was -0.45 diopters (D) for SSF and -0.36 D for ISHF ( P = .48); mean ASERA was 0.52 D and 0.54 D, respectively ( P = .96). At postoperative month 3, 70% of SSF vs 62% of ISHF eyes were within ±0.50 D of target and 85% vs 86% were within ±1.00 D. Complication rates were low and comparable, with trends toward higher early hypotony in SSF and more reoperations in ISHF.
CONCLUSIONS: Both small-incision SSF and ISHF are safe and effective for secondary IOL implantation in adults. Refractive outcomes were comparable, with SSF demonstrating slightly greater predictability and fewer reoperations, while ISHF was associated with less early hypotony. Technique selection should be guided by surgeon experience, IOL choice, and patient-specific factors.
etudes.revue: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

etudes.titre: Early Intraocular Pressure Changes After Laparoscopic Sleeve Gastrectomy: A Prospective Comparative Study.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: Obesity is a serious health problem worldwide and is associated with several ocular conditions, including glaucoma, cataract, and age-related macular degeneration. Elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) is a well-established and modifiable risk factor for glaucomatous optic neuropathy. This study aimed to evaluate early changes in IOP following laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy and to examine their relationship with weight loss. A secondary exploratory aim was to describe whether postoperative improvement in hypertension or diabetes mellitus was accompanied by additional changes in IOP.
METHODS: This prospective comparative study included 82 patients who underwent laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy between 2024 and 2025 and completed the predefined 6-month follow-up, together with 82 prospectively enrolled age- and sex-comparable non-obese control participants serving as a reference cohort. The control cohort was used to contextualize IOP values in non-obese individuals and was not designed to isolate the independent effects of surgical stress, weight loss, or metabolic improvement. Ophthalmologic evaluations, including IOP measurement, were performed at baseline and at 6 months according to the study protocol, whereas systemic comorbidity outcomes were ascertained from routine clinical follow-up records at 6 months. For correlation analyses, right- and left-eye IOP values were evaluated separately, whereas mean IOP values were used for patient-level analyses. Changes in IOP were assessed before and after surgery, and correlations between changes in body mass index (BMI) and IOP were examined. Subgroup observations according to postoperative improvement in hypertension and diabetes mellitus were considered exploratory.
RESULTS: The mean age was 37.4 ± 9.2 years in the sleeve gastrectomy group and 39.6 ± 9.6 years in the control group. The surgical group included 36 men and 46 women, and the control group included 43 men and 39 women. No significant differences were observed between the groups in age or sex distribution. Six months after surgery, BMI and body weight decreased significantly (both p < 0.001). Mean IOP decreased significantly after sleeve gastrectomy, with a mean change of approximately - 3.0 mmHg (p < 0.001). Baseline mean IOP was significantly higher in the sleeve gastrectomy group than in controls (p = 0.012). At 6 months, mean IOP in the sleeve gastrectomy group had decreased to 12.8 ± 2.2 mmHg compared with 13.3 ± 3.5 mmHg in controls (p = 0.038). Significant positive correlations were observed between reductions in BMI and decreases in IOP in both the right eye (r = 0.545, p < 0.001) and left eye (r = 0.489, p < 0.001). Exploratory subgroup observations suggested a greater IOP reduction in patients with postoperative improvement in hypertension, whereas improvement in diabetes mellitus did not appear to confer an additional short-term effect.
CONCLUSIONS: Laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy was associated with a significant short-term reduction in intraocular pressure in obese patients, and greater BMI reduction was associated with greater IOP reduction. Postoperative improvement in hypertension may also be associated with a greater decrease in IOP; however, this finding should be interpreted cautiously because the subgroup observations were exploratory. Larger prospective controlled studies are needed to clarify the independent contributions of weight loss, metabolic improvement, and surgery-related factors.

etudes.titre: Adipose-derived stem cell exosomes alleviate oxidative damage and reduce intraocular pressure in primary open-angle glaucoma via the ROS-mediated PI3K/AKT pathway.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « pathway »
etudes.resume:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic effect and underlying mechanism of adipose-derived stem cell exosomes (ADSC-Exos) on oxidative injury in trabecular meshwork (TM) cells of primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG).
MATERIAL AND METHODS: In vitro, human TM cells (HTMCs) were exposed to hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) to establish an oxidative damage model. In vivo, an Ad5.myocilinY437H mouse model of POAG was constructed. Western blotting, immunofluorescence, reactive oxygen species (ROS) detection, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) and intraocular pressure (IOP) monitoring were performed to evaluate the intervention effects of ADSC-Exos and the activation of the PI3K/AKT pathway.
RESULTS: Compared with the PBS group, ADSC-Exos significantly increased the phosphorylation levels of PI3K and AKT, reduced intracellular ROS accumulation, and decreased laminin expression in HTMCs (P < 0.05). In the Ad5-MYOCY437H-EGFP mice group, day 30 IOP reached 15.2 ± 4.1 mmHg, representing a significant increase over day 0 values (8.7 ± 1.9 mmHg, n = 16, P < 0.001). Furthermore, these eyes exhibited significantly higher IOP compared to the Ad5-EGFP controls (11.0 ± 1.9 mmHg, n = 16, P < 0.05). From day 15 onwards, the IOP in the Ad5-MYOCY437H-EGFP + ADSC-Exos group progressively declined, showing a significant difference from the PBS-injected group (11.63 ± 2.6 vs. 15.84 ± 1.6 mmHg, n = 10, P < 0.001). This downward trajectory continued, resulting in a significant IOP difference by day 30 (11.19 ± 2.3 vs. 16.93 ± 3.04 mmHg, P < 0.0001).
CONCLUSION: ADSC-Exos can alleviate TM oxidative damage, reduce extracellular matrix deposition, and effectively decrease IOP in POAG via the ROS-mediated PI3K/AKT pathway, providing a potential therapeutic strategy for POAG.

etudes.titre: Conclusions and Therapeutic Implications of AA.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: AA is essential for several tissues in the body, as they are involved in many physiological and pathological processes. Its regulatory role in inflammation, immune response regulation, cell cycle, and membrane structural organization and its ability to control the expression and function(s) of several receptors and convey messages to and from the nucleus are of particular significance. Fine-tuning the metabolism of AA may lead to the development of prevention and management strategies for several diseases, including but not limited to sepsis, inflammatory bowel disease, diabetes mellitus, cancer, coronary heart disease, atherosclerosis, MASLD (NAFLD), hypertension, metabolic syndrome, uveitis, glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy, glomerulonephritis, ischemia-reperfusion injury, lupus, rheumatoid arthritis, and drug-resistant infections and cancer. AA is needed for normal brain growth and development, pregnancy, regeneration of the liver and heart, and hematopoiesis. AA can be administered orally, parenterally as needed, and as lipid nanoparticles to target specific tissues.
etudes.revue: Reviews of physiology, biochemistry and pharmacology

etudes.titre: Win Ratios in Ophthalmology-a Hierarchical Metric to Evaluate Adverse Outcomes in Comparative Studies.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: Clinical trials in ophthalmology frequently report multiple efficacy and safety outcomes of varying clinical importance analyzed either in isolation or as simple composites. The Win Ratio (WR) is a hierarchical composite metric originally developed to address such limitations in cardiovascular research by integrating outcomes according to their clinical priority. In this study, we assess its potential utility in ophthalmology outcomes with glaucoma surgery as the exemplar.
DESIGN: Retrospective registry-based study.
SUBJECTS: There are 1257 eyes that underwent a Xen gel stent (Xen) implantation or trabeculectomy (Trab) with a minimum 12 months of follow-up.
METHODS: Propensity score matching yielded two comparable cohorts (212 eyes each) without significant differences in age, baseline intraocular pressure, number of medications, visual acuity, or visual field mean deviation. A predefined hierarchy of eight adverse outcomes was constructed, headed by loss of light perception vision, secondary glaucoma surgery, followed by early postoperative complications (e.g., hypotony and hyphaema) or bleb needling. Each Xen-Trab pair was evaluated sequentially and classified as a win, loss, or tie.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The overall WR with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) and P value was estimated, and sensitivity analyses examined the robustness of results under alternative outcome hierarchies and random permutations.
RESULTS: The Xen group accumulated fewer wins than Trab (WR 0.83, 95% CI 0.63-1.10, P = 0.19), although the difference was not significant. Differences were driven by higher rates of secondary glaucoma surgery (18.4% vs. 12.7%) and bleb needling within the first 6 months (28.8% vs. 13.2%) in the Xen group, with remaining outcomes occurring infrequently and evenly distributed in each group. Sensitivity analyses with alternative hierarchies yielded consistent results (WR range 0.80-0.98), and random permutations of lower-ranked outcomes clustered around WR 0.77, supporting the consistency of the final outcome.
CONCLUSIONS: The WR offers a clinically meaningful, hierarchical approach to comparing multidimensional treatments that respects clinical priorities. Our findings illustrate the potential utility of this metric in the prospective evaluation of trial outcomes in ophthalmology.
FINANCIAL DISCLOSURES: The authors have no proprietary or commercial interest in any materials discussed in this article.

etudes.titre: 1,3,4-Oxadiazole-sulfonamide hybrids: recent advances in biological activities, structure-activity relationships, and therapeutic applications.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Molecular hybridization has emerged as an effective strategy in medicinal chemistry for the development of multifunctional therapeutic agents with improved biological performance. Among the various hybrid scaffolds investigated, 1,3,4-oxadiazole-sulfonamide hybrids have gained considerable attention owing to the complementary pharmacological properties of both pharmacophores. The integration of the 1,3,4-oxadiazole nucleus and sulfonamide moiety within a single molecular framework has generated structurally diverse compounds exhibiting promising activities against a broad range of biological targets. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the biological activities and structure-activity relationships (SARs) of 1,3,4-oxadiazole-sulfonamide hybrids reported over the past two decades. Particular emphasis is placed on their antimicrobial, anticancer, anti-Alzheimer, anti-HIV, antidiabetic, anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, antimalarial, anti-glaucoma, and carbonic anhydrase inhibitory activities. Furthermore, the influence of key structural modifications on biological performance is critically discussed, highlighting the pharmacophoric features and substitution patterns associated with enhanced potency and selectivity. Collectively, the available evidence demonstrates the remarkable therapeutic versatility of 1,3,4-oxadiazole-sulfonamide hybrids and supports their continued exploration as promising scaffolds for future drug discovery and development.

etudes.titre: Association of Topical Therapy and Surgical Management with Corneal Parameters in Congenital PAX6-Related Classical Aniridia: a Cross-Sectional Study.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Surgical »
etudes.resume:
INTRODUCTION: This study aimed to investigate associations of topical therapy and surgical management with the severity of aniridia-associated keratopathy (AAK), limbal stem cell deficiency (LSCD) and corneal microstructural alterations in patients with PAX6-related congenital aniridia (CA).
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included eyes with genetically confirmed CA. Medical history, including preservative-free artificial tears, antiglaucoma medications (beta-blockers, brimonidine, carbonic anhydrase inhibitors, prostaglandin analogues), and ocular surgery was recorded. AAK and LSCD were graded. Anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) assessed epithelial and total corneal thickness, while in vivo confocal microscopy (IVCM) assessed subbasal nerve plexus parameters, Langerhans cell density (LCD), and stromal keratocyte density. Associations were analyzed using generalized estimating equations.
RESULTS: Sixty-one eyes of 31 patients were analyzed. More advanced AAK and LSCD were associated with more frequent preservative-free artificial tear use. Antiglaucoma medications were associated with differences in corneal thickness, keratocyte and Langerhans cell densities, and subbasal nerve plexus parameters. Prostaglandin analogue use was associated with a heterogeneous pattern, including higher corneal nerve fiber density and length, higher middle stromal keratocyte density, and lower LCD. Previous ocular surgery showed limited associations with corneal microstructural parameters but was associated with lower corneal nerve network complexity. All findings were exploratory and hypothesis-generating.
CONCLUSIONS: Topical therapy use is associated with differences in corneal structural and cellular parameters in congenital aniridia. Preservative-free artificial tear use is associated with more advanced AAK and LSCD, while antiglaucoma medications are associated with differences in corneal thickness, keratocyte and Langerhans cell densities, and corneal nerve parameters. Prostaglandin-treated eyes show a heterogeneous pattern of associations with corneal microstructural parameters. Given the cross-sectional design, whether these treatment-associated differences reflect medication effects, underlying disease severity, treatment selection, concomitant therapies, or residual confounding cannot be determined. These findings require longitudinal confirmation.

etudes.titre: Rodent models of glaucoma: Pathogenic mechanisms, phenotyping strategies, and translational relevance.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « mechanisms »; étiquette : stade préclinique (indexation PubMed)
etudes.resume: Glaucoma comprises a heterogeneous group of optic neuropathies characterized by progressive degeneration of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and their axons. Rodent models have been widely used to investigate disease mechanisms, identify neuroprotective targets and evaluate emerging therapeutic strategies because they are cost-effective, genetically tractable and experimentally controllable. However, mice and rats differ substantially from humans in anterior-segment anatomy, trabecular meshwork architecture, Schlemm's canal development, lamina cribrosa structure, RGC composition and optic nerve head vascular supply. These interspecies differences influence model construction, phenotypic interpretation and the translational value of preclinical findings. This narrative review summarizes key anatomical differences between rodent and human eyes and discusses major categories of rodent glaucoma models, including intraocular pressure (IOP)-dependent models, IOP-independent models, immune-mediated and multifactorial models, and spontaneous or genetically engineered models. We emphasize that no single rodent model can fully reproduce the chronic, multifactorial, and regionally selective nature of human glaucoma. Instead, model selection should be driven by the specific scientific question, disease subtype, observation window, and translational goal. IOP-dependent models are particularly useful for investigating pressure-induced RGC degeneration and optic nerve injury, while selected models also reproduce aspects of aqueous outflow dysfunction, linking anterior-segment abnormalities with posterior-segment neurodegeneration. IOP-independent and genetic models, by contrast, are ideal for studying normal-tension glaucoma, neurodegeneration, neuroinflammation, metabolic stress, and gene-specific mechanisms. Future efforts should prioritize standardized phenotypic evaluation, multimodal imaging and multi-omics integration to improve the reliability and translational relevance of findings from rigorously validated rodent models.

etudes.titre: Shear Stress and Pressure Homeostasis in the Eye's Aqueous Outflow Pathway.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Pathway »
etudes.resume: Glaucoma is the most common cause of irreversible blindness. Many patients with glaucoma suffer from elevated intraocular pressure (IOP), due to impaired drainage of aqueous humor fluid from the eye, and all current treatments are designed to lower IOP, implicating dysregulation of IOP as an important clinical problem. Because IOP is maintained within a narrow range over a lifetime in a healthy eye, it is thought that mechanically driven feedback loops within the eye maintain IOP homeostasis, and in fact, good evidence for such loops now exists. Here we revisit the fluid mechanics of aqueous humor flow in the eye to estimate fluid shear stresses in relevant aqueous drainage tissues, in order to identify mechanical signals that may be involved in IOP homeostatic feedback loops. We find that shear stresses within the juxtacanalicular tissue are likely too small to play a significant role, except perhaps in the very immediate vicinity of the inner wall of Schlemm's canal. We estimate that the basement membrane underlying the inner wall of Schlemm's canal is exposed to high shear stresses. Furthermore, we find remarkably large shear stresses acting on the cell membrane-delimited pores passing through the inner wall of Schlemm's canal. Finally, the inner wall of Schlemm's canal is exposed to moderate shear stresses that, unlike other locations in the outflow pathway, increase as IOP increases. Thus, the inner wall endothelial cells of Schlemm's canal are well-suited to participate in a shear stress-driven IOP homeostatic feedback loop.

etudes.titre: Corrigendum to "TrkB Receptor Agonist 7,8 Dihydroxyflavone is Protective Against the Inner Retinal Deficits Induced by Experimental Glaucoma" [Neuroscience 490 (2022) 36-48].
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Agonist »

etudes.titre: Associations between Retinal Nerve Fiber Layer Thickness, Axial Length, and Generation in the 2-Continent Eye Study.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To assess the associations between peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer thickness (RNFLT) and ocular and systemic parameters, in particular axial length (A).
DESIGN: Population based studies.
METHODS: Ocular and systemic examinations including OCT RNFLT measurement.
PARTICIPANTS: Participants of 4 population-based studies (Beijing Eye Study [n = 3246; age: 40+ years], Ural Eye and Medical Study [n = 5023; age: 40+ years], Ural Very Old Study [n = 407; age: 85+ years], Ural Children Eye Study [UCES, n = 3109; age: 6+ years]).
OUTCOME MEASURES: RNFLT.
RESULTS: The study cohort consisted of 23 384 eyes (11 785 individuals). In multivariable analysis with exclusion of eyes with an IOP of >21 mmHg, thicker RNFLT was associated (all P < 0.001) with the systemic parameters of younger age, female sex, urban region of habitation, taller body height, higher educational level, lower systolic blood pressure, and higher estimated cerebrospinal fluid pressure; and with lower intraocular pressure. In all studies on adults (Beijing Eye Study, Ural Eye and Medical Study, and Ural Very Old Study), total RNFLT increased with AL up to an AL of 24.0 mm, plateaued, and decreased for an AL >26.5 mm. In the UCES, RNFLT linearly increased with longer AL, also in the highly myopic range. Differentiated sectorially, temporal RNFLT in the UCES linearly increased with AL (including the highly myopic range), while in the adult studies it plateaued beyond an AL of 26.0 mm. In all other sectors in all cohorts, the sectorial RNFLT decreased with longer AL in the highly myopic range.
CONCLUSIONS: The AL-related increase in RNFLT up to an AL of 24 mm, found in all ages, may correspond to an AL-related larger retinal surface area with a higher number of retinal ganglion cells per eye. The RNFLT decrease beyond an AL of 26.5 mm in adults corresponds to an increased prevalence of optic neuropathies in highly myopic eyes. The sectorial differences in the RNFLT/AL relationship corresponds to the axial elongation-related RNFL shift to the macula, with a secondary RNFL crowding temporally and a geometrically explained RNFLT decrease nasally. Sectorial normative RNFLT data depend on AL.
FINANCIAL DISCLOSURES: Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found in the Footnotes and Disclosures at the end of this article.

etudes.titre: The Emerging Role of Cellular Mechanical Memory in Aqueous Humor Outflow Dysfunction in Glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Emerging evidence suggests that cells can retain information about previous mechanical environments and subsequently exhibit altered phenotypes even after the original mechanical stimulus is removed. This phenomenon is known as cellular mechanical memory that occurs in three phases: memory acquisition, storage, and recall. The literature supports a model in which mechanical experiences become encoded through interconnected cytoskeletal, nuclear, metabolic, and epigenetic mechanisms. Mechanical memory is increasingly recognized as a central regulator of cell fate and tissue remodeling, as well as a fundamental principle in development, aging, fibrosis, cancer, and regenerative medicine. We here give a concise overview of the historical origins and defining features of mechanical memory, discuss the emergence of mechanical memory in aqueous humor outflow dysfunction in glaucoma, summarize key unanswered questions, and close with a discussion of the clinical relevance of targeting mechanical memory for therapeutic purposes.

etudes.titre: Glaucoma Severity and Progression in Individuals with Asymmetric β-zone Parapapillary Atrophy: An Intra-patient Comparative Study.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To investigate inter-eye differences in glaucoma severity and progression in patients with asymmetric baseline β-zone parapapillary atrophy (PPA) morphology.
DESIGN: Retrospective, intra-patient comparative study.
PARTICIPANTS: Sixty-four eyes of 32 patients with bilateral primary open-angle glaucoma and asymmetric β-zone PPA morphology.
METHODS: Baseline β-zone PPA was quantitatively assessed using optic disc photographs. Each eye was classified according to angular extent as either Crescent type (<180°) or Solar-eclipse type (≥180°), and according to radial extent as either Short-extent type or Long-extent type. Glaucoma progression was evaluated using linear mixed-effects models with random intercepts and random slopes at both the patient and eye-within-patient levels.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Rates of change in visual field mean deviation (MD), visual field index (VFI), and retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness.
RESULTS: The mean age was 53.2 ± 15.6 years, and the mean follow-up duration was 11.4 ± 3.2 years. Eyes with the Solar-eclipse type demonstrated significantly faster functional progression, with greater model-estimated rates of VFI loss (-1.37 vs. -0.71 %/year; P = 0.004) and MD decline (-0.49 vs. -0.27 dB/year; P = 0.006), whereas no significant differences were observed in the rates of change in average, superior, inferior, or temporal RNFL thickness (all P ≥ 0.30). Similarly, eyes with the Long-extent type showed faster decline than those with the Short-extent type for both VFI (-1.33 vs. -0.76 %/year; P = 0.014) and MD (-0.47 vs. -0.29 dB/year; P = 0.026). In multivariable mixed-effects models, β-zone PPA angular extent was the only factor independently associated with the rate of functional progression for both MD (standardized β = -0.123; P = 0.008) and VFI (standardized β = -0.312; P = 0.022). A complementary paired inter-eye difference analysis did not reach statistical significance (all P > 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: In this intra-individual analysis, eyes with greater angular extent of β-zone PPA showed faster functional progression, whereas structural progression did not differ. Although this association was not confirmed in a paired inter-eye difference analysis, these findings suggest that β-zone PPA angular extent may be a useful marker of future functional worsening in glaucoma.

etudes.titre: Comparative Outcomes of Stent vs. Non-Stent Trabecular Minimally Invasive Glaucoma Surgeries: A 4-Year Retrospective Propensity-Matched Study.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Stent »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To compare 48-month outcomes of stent-based versus non-stent trabecular minimally invasive glaucoma surgery (MIGS) performed with phacoemulsification in open-angle glaucoma.
DESIGN: Retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study.
PARTICIPANTS: 250 eyes of 250 patients with open-angle glaucoma, matched 1:1 into Stent and Non-Stent groups.
METHODS: All eyes underwent combined phacoemulsification and trabecular MIGS and were followed through 48 months.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was surgical success through 48 months at IOP thresholds of ≤15 mmHg and ≤18 mmHg, defined as achieving target IOP, on reduced (qualified) or without (complete) glaucoma medications and ≥20% IOP reduction from baseline without secondary incisional glaucoma surgery. Our secondary endpoints included complete success and qualified success, mean IOP and number of glaucoma medication classes, visual field mean deviation, secondary interventions, and adverse events at each postoperative visit through 48 months.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were well balanced. By 48 months, there were no statistically significant differences between the Non-Stent and Stent groups in surgical success, visual field mean deviation, or medication burden. At the ≤15 mmHg threshold, surgical success was higher in the Stent group at month 12 (64.5% vs 45.3%; p=0.005) and month 24 (61.7% vs 40.7%; p=0.012), driven primarily by higher qualified success. At the ≤18 mmHg threshold, surgical success was similar between groups throughout follow-up, despite different success patterns: Non-Stent eyes achieved higher complete medication-free success at months 12 and 24, whereas Stent eyes achieved higher qualified success at the same visits. Non-Stent eyes had greater IOP reduction at month 24 and fewer medications at months 24 and 36, but these differences were no longer significant by month 48. Rescue SLT was required more often in Non-Stent eyes (6.2% vs 1.9%; p=0.025), while secondary incisional surgeries and adverse events were uncommon with no significant difference between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Stent and non-stent trabecular MIGS combined with phacoemulsification achieved comparable 48-month outcomes through different success patterns.

etudes.titre: Evaluation and Comparison of Large Language Models in Answering Frequently Asked Patient Questions on Glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PRCIS: ChatGPT-o1 and DeepSeek-R1 demonstrated similar performance in answering frequently asked patient questions. However, limitations in reliability and high reading levels underscore the need for greater oversight and refinement to improve their role in patient education.
PURPOSE: This study evaluated and compared the reliability and readability of responses generated by ChatGPT-o1 and DeepSeek-R1 to frequently asked patient questions (FAQs) on glaucoma. The findings aim to elucidate the utility of each model in supporting effective patient education.
METHODS: Glaucoma FAQs were obtained from the first 10 questions on Google's "People Also Ask" section. Topics included foundational knowledge, treatment description, lifestyle, and prognosis. Each question was input into ChatGPT-o1 and DeepSeek-R1, and responses were independently graded for reliability by two glaucoma specialists using a 4-point scale (1=excellent, no clarification needed; 4=unsatisfactory, substantial clarification needed). For further comparison, the top two Google search result webpages for the same queries were similarly graded. Readability grade levels were assessed using validated metrics.
RESULTS: ChatGPT-o1 and DeepSeek-R1 received comparable median reliability scores (2.3 [1.6-3] vs. 2.8 [2.1-3], P=0.08), which were similar to scores of top Google webpages (2.3 [1.8-2.7], P=0.18). Both chatbots struggled with questions on foundational knowledge (i.e. falsely suggesting that glaucoma may cause tunnel vision) and lifestyle (i.e. offering unsubstantiated advice on chugging water, dietary recommendations, and screen time). Responses generated by both models were presented at the 8th-12th grade reading level.
CONCLUSION: ChatGPT-o1 and DeepSeek-R1 responses were comparable, demonstrating notable limitations in accuracy. Reading levels similarly exceeded average U.S. adult literacy, posing challenges for patient comprehension. Rigorous oversight and targeted refinement of LLMs is necessary to enhance the reliability and accessibility of content for patient education in glaucoma.

etudes.titre: Trabeculectomy versus Transscleral Cyclophotocoagulation as a Primary Surgical Procedure in Glaucoma: A Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Trabeculectomy »; mot du titre : « Cyclophotocoagulation »
etudes.resume:
PRCIS: In this randomized multicenter trial, both TRAB and CPC lowered IOP at 12 months as primary glaucoma surgeries, with TRAB yielding lower final IOP with fewer medications, while both procedures demonstrated meaningful clinical effectiveness.
PURPOSE: To compare the efficacy and safety of trabeculectomy (TRAB) and slow-burn transscleral cyclophotocoagulation (CPC) as primary surgical treatments for glaucoma.
METHODS: Prospective, randomized, multicenter trial including one eye per patient from July 2020 to July 2023, with 12-month follow-up. Participants were allocated to TRAB (GI) or CPC (GII). The primary endpoint was surgical success at 12 months, defined by intraocular pressure (IOP) between 6 and 18 mm Hg without non-protocol glaucoma surgery or serious complications.
RESULTS: Eighty-six eyes were included; nine were excluded (four in GI; five in GII). Baseline demographics were similar between groups. Both significantly reduced IOP at 12 months (GI: 22.97±8.23 mm Hg to 10.14±2.89 mm Hg; GII: 23.47±6.34 mm Hg to 14.58±3.66 mm Hg; P<0.001 for both). Medication use decreased significantly in both groups, with a lower mean number of medications per year in GI (P<0.001). An IOP of 6-14 mm Hg was achieved in 91.4% of GI and 39.4% of GII (P=0.007). Final IOP between 6 and 18 mm Hg was reached by 97.1% of GI and 90.9% of GII (P=0.708). Qualified success rates were high and comparable (GI: 97.4%; GII: 86.8%; P=0.08), while complications were infrequent (four in GI; one in GII; P=0.3). Quality of life improved after TRAB (EQ-5D: 0.71±0.19 to 0.78±0.14; P=0.031) but remained unchanged after CPC (P=0.424).
CONCLUSIONS: Both procedures reduced IOP at 12 months as primary glaucoma surgeries. TRAB achieved lower final IOP, required fewer medications, and was associated with improved quality of life, whereas CPC required more adjunctive medication and retreatment in some eyes.

etudes.titre: Learning How to Implement Glaucoma Coaching in Academic Medical Centers from a Successful Clinical Trial Using Implementation Science.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To evaluate implementation of the Support, Educate, Empower (SEE) personalized glaucoma coaching program.
DESIGN: Prospective, two-site randomized clinical trial with an implementation evaluation using the Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, and Maintenance framework and the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR).
PARTICIPANTS: Adults aged ≥40 years with glaucoma, glaucoma suspect, or ocular hypertension and poor self-reported medication adherence who were prescribed ≥1 glaucoma medication (n = 236 enrolled; additional screened individuals declined [n = 1750] or were ineligible [n = 1701]). Stakeholders (n = 8) and participants (n = 32) contributed qualitative data.
METHODS: Participants were randomized to a motivational interviewing (MI)-based glaucoma coaching intervention (SEE program) or standard education. Reach was assessed by comparing demographics across recruitment stages. Effectiveness was evaluated by changes in medication adherence, coach autonomy support, and attrition. Implementation fidelity was measured using counselor MI competency scores (passing ≥5). Adoption and maintenance were evaluated through CFIR-guided interviews, postintervention adherence monitoring, and cost estimates.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Glaucoma medication adherence, program reach, implementation fidelity (MI competency scores), and qualitative stakeholder-informed measures of adoption and maintenance, including postintervention adherence and program cost.
RESULTS: Of the 2057 individuals screened, 356 (17.3%) were eligible, of which 236 (66.3%) enrolled; no demographic differences were observed between enrollees and nonenrollees; however, those who declined screening (n = 1750) were older and more likely to be White (both P < 0.0001). Adherence was better with personalized coaching than standard education (77.6% ± 19.7% versus 58.0% ± 25.2%; P < 0.001). Motivational interviewing fidelity was high (mean score 5.7). Facilitators of implementation included participant engagement and workflow compatibility, while barriers included limited awareness, resource constraints, and concerns about financial sustainability. Participants reported improved engagement and motivation. 84% of participants continued monitoring after counseling ended; adherence declined by 10.0% ± 21.1% at 1 month and an additional 3.6% ± 11.7% by 2 months and remained below intervention levels thereafter. A coach could manage approximately 431 patients per year, with an estimated net revenue of $19,272 annually after costs.
CONCLUSIONS: The SEE MI-based program demonstrated high fidelity and improved adherence during the intervention. Postintervention adherence decline demonstrates the need for continued coaching. Strong uptake, stakeholder support, and projected reimbursement suggest feasibility and organizational sustainability in clinical practice.
FINANCIAL DISCLOSURE(S): Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found in the Footnotes and Disclosures at the end of this article.

etudes.titre: Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Systemic Immunomodulatory Therapies for Non-Infectious Uveitis: A Systematic Review With Pairwise and Network Meta-Analyses.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique

labos.nom: National Science and Technology Council Taiwan
National Science and Technology Council Taiwan

etudes.resume:
INTRODUCTION: Non-infectious uveitis (NIU) is a chronic immune-mediated ocular inflammatory disease that may cause irreversible visual impairment. The comparative efficacy and safety of systemic immunomodulatory therapies, including conventional agents and biologics, remain incompletely defined. This systematic review and network meta-analysis evaluated systemic immunosuppressive therapies for NIU.
METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from inception to May 2, 2026. Randomized controlled trials and prospective comparative cohort studies evaluating systemic immunomodulatory or biologic therapies for NIU were included. The primary efficacy outcome was treatment failure. Safety outcomes included mortality, urinary tract infection, upper respiratory tract infection, injection-site reactions, ocular hypertension, macular edema, and headache. Random-effects pairwise meta-analysis and frequentist network meta-analysis were performed using risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Seven studies including 992 participants were included; six were randomized controlled trials and one was a prospective cohort. In the pairwise meta-analysis, adalimumab significantly reduced treatment failure compared with placebo (RR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.58-0.78; p < 0.0001; I² = 28.1%). The mortality estimate was inconclusive (RR, 3.80; 95% CI, 0.42-34.15), with three deaths in the adalimumab groups and none in the placebo groups. Adalimumab was associated with a higher risk of injection-site reactions than placebo (RR, 2.67; 95% CI, 1.73-4.12). Network meta-analysis showed no significant differences for most safety outcomes, including upper respiratory tract infection, ocular hypertension, macular edema, and headache. Infliximab showed an imprecise urinary tract infection signal versus placebo (RR, 40.98; 95% CI, 1.82-922.17), based on sparse events and one nonrandomized comparison.
CONCLUSION: Adalimumab provides the most consistent evidence for reducing treatment failure in NIU. Comparative safety estimates, particularly for infliximab, remain uncertain and hypothesis-generating. Larger, long-term, head-to-head trials are required.

etudes.titre: Topical Tacrolimus in Ocular Disease: A Narrative Review of Mechanism of Action and Therapeutic Applications.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Mechanism »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: Immune-mediated inflammatory disorders of the ocular surface and anterior segment frequently require sustained immunosuppression, yet prolonged topical corticosteroid use carries the risk of glaucoma, cataract, and infection. Tacrolimus, a macrolide calcineurin inhibitor, has emerged as a steroid-sparing alternative for T-cell-mediated ocular disease. This review summarizes the mechanism of action, ocular pharmacology, clinical applications, and safety profile of topical tacrolimus.
METHODS: Narrative synthesis of the peer-reviewed literature.
RESULTS: Tacrolimus binds the immunophilin FK506-binding protein 12; the resulting complex inhibits the phosphatase calcineurin, preventing dephosphorylation and nuclear translocation of the nuclear factor of activated T-cells (NFAT) and thereby suppressing transcription of interleukin-2 and a broad program of pro-inflammatory cytokines. The downstream result is reduced activation across the Th1, Th2, and Th17 lineages, diminished T-follicular helper and B-cell responses, stabilization of mast cells and eosinophils, and anti-angiogenic effects. Compounded topical formulations (typically 0.01%-0.1%) penetrate the cornea and reach therapeutic aqueous concentrations. Topical tacrolimus has shown efficacy in vernal and atopic keratoconjunctivitis, anterior uveitis, scleritis, ocular graft-versus-host disease, cicatrizing conjunctivitis, Thygeson superficial punctate keratitis, autoimmune polyglandular syndrome-1-associated keratitis, and corneal graft rejection.
CONCLUSIONS: Topical tacrolimus is an effective steroid-sparing immunomodulator for a broad spectrum of T-cell-mediated ocular disease, with a favorable safety profile notable for the absence of steroid-related rises in intraocular pressure or cataractogenesis. Standardized formulations and prospective comparative trials remain priorities.
etudes.revue: Journal of ocular pharmacology and therapeutics : the official journal of the Association for Ocular Pharmacology and Therapeutics

etudes.titre: Breaking the Rules: Museum Data Reveal Divergent Support for Classic Ecogeographical Rules in North American Flying Squirrels.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique

labos.nom: University of North Carolina at Greensboro

etudes.resume: Ecogeographic generalizations or "rules", such as Bergmann's rule and Allen's rule, propose that endotherms in colder climates evolve larger bodies and shorter appendages to minimize heat loss. These patterns are hypothesized to reflect physiological adaptations to thermal stress through reduced surface area-to-volume ratios. Although these rules have been extensively evaluated across birds and mammals, their applicability to arboreal gliders remains untested, with little consideration of how alternative ecological and evolutionary drivers may structure morphological variation in flying squirrels across environmental gradients. Using digitized museum specimens of North American flying squirrels (Glaucomys sabrinus, Glaucomys oregonensis, and Glaucomys volans), we tested these classic ecogeographic principles by examining how weight, total length, tail length, and ear length vary across a latitudinal gradient. We found significant support for Bergmann's rule, with body mass and total length increasing with latitude. In contrast, patterns in appendage morphology provided limited support for Allen's rule. Ear length exhibited a weak positive relationship with latitude, while tail length strongly increased with latitude, contradicting the prediction that appendages become shorter in colder climates. These findings suggest that thermoregulatory selection alone cannot explain morphological variation in North American flying squirrels and that functional demands, particularly those associated with gliding performance, may play a stronger role in shaping tail morphology. Overall, our results demonstrate that although classic ecogeographic rules provide a useful framework for understanding morphological variation, they do not fully capture the multiple selective pressures acting on Glaucomys species.

etudes.titre: Feasibility and immediate effects of a multimodal, dance-integrated educational video package on eye health knowledge and intentions in Nigeria: A pre-post pilot study.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Dance, as a culturally embedded and universally accessible form of art, offers a promising medium for health education in settings with diverse literacy levels. This pilot study evaluated the feasibility and immediate effects of a multimodal, dance-integrated educational video package designed to improve eye health knowledge, attitudes, and preventive intentions among Nigerian adults. Between April 11 and June 22, 2025, adults recruited through optometry clinics and community outreach programmes viewed culturally tailored educational videos addressing at least one eye condition (myopia, cataract, or glaucoma) and general eye health, including common myths and preventive practices. Pre-post changes were assessed using paired comparisons, with subgroup analyses by educational attainment. Among 438 participants, 77.7% were aged 18-44 years, 52.5% were female, 75.1% had higher education, 80.0% reported existing health-promoting behaviours, and 79.7% considered regular eye examinations important. Following the intervention, perceived eye health knowledge increased from 42.0% to 68.0% (absolute increase, 26.0 percentage points; relative increase, 61.9%; p = 0.013; Cramér's V = 0.279), while objective eye health knowledge scores increased by 52.4 percentage points (p = 0.013; Cramér's V = 0.069). Self-reported intentions to adopt protective practices, including wearing sunglasses, reducing screen time, and attending regular eye examinations, also increased. Overall intention to visit an eye clinic increased by 10%, although this change was not statistically significant (p = 0.443), likely reflecting high baseline health-seeking intentions. The largest improvements in willingness to attend regular check-ups occurred among participants with secondary education (27.5% to 96.3%, p < 0.001) and those with primary or no formal education (41.4% to 96.6%, p < 0.001). Dance-integrated educational videos were associated with immediate improvements in eye health knowledge and preventive intentions, particularly among participants with lower educational attainment, supporting their potential as a culturally relevant and scalable approach to eye health communication in diverse, resource-limited settings and community-based health promotion programmes.

etudes.titre: The Second and Third Decade After 103Pd Plaque Brachytherapy for Choroidal Melanoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To determine long-term visual and ocular outcomes in a large cohort of patients with choroidal melanoma treated using palladium-103 (103Pd) plaque brachytherapy.
DESIGN: This is a retrospective cohort study.
PARTICIPANTS: 170 patients with a minimum of 10 years of continuous follow-up at The New York Eye Cancer Center following 103Pd plaque brachytherapy treatment for choroidal melanoma.
METHODS: The study includes collected data consisting of patient demographic characteristics, tumor features, such as size, location, and AJCC clinical T-category (cT), visual outcomes, variables related to post-treatment retinopathy management, and long-term ocular comorbidities.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary endpoints were tumor control, ocular conservation, and visual acuity. Secondary endpoints included long-term radiation-related complications, additional ocular interventions, and associated comorbidities. Statistical analyses were performed using the Kaplan-Meier survival method, t-tests, Wilcoxon rank-sum tests, chi-square tests, and linear regression plots.
RESULTS: Among 170 patients with a minimum 10-year follow-up there was 100% local tumor control. One eye (0.6%) was enucleated due to neovascular glaucoma and patient choice. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated visual acuity retention rates of 92.7% at 12 years, 87.0% at 15 years, and 63.7% at 20 years defined as vision of 20/200 or better. Radiation retinopathy was managed with anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy, intravitreal corticosteroids, and laser treatment. Tumors located closer to the fovea were associated with increased foveal radiation doses and poorer visual acuity outcomes. Treatment of juxtapapillary and circumpapillary tumors was associated with the highest rates of vision loss.
CONCLUSIONS: This study is the largest and longest follow-up analysis of 103Pd plaque brachytherapy for choroidal melanoma. It provides new long-term information on tumor control, ocular morbidity, and visual outcomes that are valuable for patient counseling and therapeutic decision-making.
