etudes.titre: Nudix hydrolase 15 deficiency and azathioprine toxicity in a liver transplant recipient: A case report.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Thiopurines, such as azathioprine (AZA), are among the immunosuppressants used to prevent allograft rejection. Thiopurines are metabolized by thiopurine S-methyltransferase (TPMT) and nudix hydrolase 15 (NUDT15) enzymes, and their functions are highly influenced by genetic variation. We present a 6-year-old female with recurrent acute cellular rejection and steroid-induced glaucoma due to high-dose corticosteroid therapy. Consequently, AZA was incorporated into her calcineurin-inhibitor-based regimen to reduce steroid dose. Within 33 days of initiating AZA, alopecia and pancytopenia developed despite confirmed TPMT enzyme activity with normal phenotype and low 6-Thioguanine and 6-Methylmercaptopurine levels in the blood. Pharmacogenomic analysis revealed an NUDT15 *3/*3 genotype, indicating two "no function" alleles, classified as NUDT15 poor metabolizer at high risk of myelosuppression with standard thiopurine doses. Liver donor pharmacogenomic testing was not performed. This case highlights the consideration of pharmacogenomic testing for recipient and donor prior to thiopurine use in liver-transplant recipients.

etudes.titre: Trends in glaucoma diagnosis and medical management in Germany: A nationwide claims data analysis over 10 years.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « diagnosis »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: Analysing longitudinal trends in recorded diagnosis and medical management of glaucoma in Germany over a 10-year period.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study using nationwide outpatient claims and prescription data from the German statutory health insurance system. Patients with documented glaucoma or glaucoma suspect (ICD-10 H40.*) between 2014 and 2023 were included. Analyses assessed annual diagnosed glaucoma patients, demographic characteristics, proportions of medically treated patients and prescribing patterns of glaucoma medications. Trends in medication classes and number of active ingredients per patient were evaluated.
RESULTS: In 2014, 2 065 065 glaucoma patients were registered. Documented patient numbers increased until 2019, reaching 2 129 673 and subsequently declined after the pandemic year to 2 025 226 in 2023. Mean patient age increased from 71.0 to 72.4 years. The proportion of medically treated patients increased from 68% to 71.5% across all glaucoma subtypes, except for primary open-angle glaucoma, where it remained stable (86.2%-86.1%) and primary angle-closure glaucoma, where it decreased (68.7%-65.6%). Among treated patients, monotherapy declined from 54.8% to 46.8%, while the proportion on two medications increased from 30.7% to 33.7%, three medications from 10.3% to 12.3%, four medications from 3.2% to 4.9% and 5 or more from 1.0% to 1.9%. Among patients receiving multiple agents, fixed-combinations increased from 75.7% to 80.5%. Prescribing patterns shifted towards greater use of prostaglandin analogues and reduced use of beta-blockers.
CONCLUSION: After increasing until 2019, the number of documented glaucoma patients in Germany declined despite an ageing population. Concurrently, treatment strategies shifted towards intensified medical therapy with greater use of multiple medications and fixed combinations, particularly prostaglandin-based regimens.

etudes.titre: Evaluation of anterior segment and lamina cribrosa parameters in primary open-angle glaucoma, pseudoexfoliation glaucoma, and healthy controls.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To compare anterior segment and lamina cribrosa parameters between primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) and pseudoexfoliation glaucoma (PEXG) using swept-source optical coherence tomography (SS-OCT).
METHODS: This cross-sectional, observational study included 34 POAG, 30 PEXG, and 30 healthy control eyes. The groups were comparable for age, sex, axial length, and anterior chamber depth. Temporal corneoscleral sections and optic disc radial scans were obtained via SS-OCT. Schlemm's canal area (SCA), trabecular meshwork thickness (TMT), scleral spur length (SSL), and anterior scleral thickness (AST) were measured using ImageJ. Lamina cribrosa thickness (LCT) and curvature index (LCCI) were assessed.
RESULTS: SCA was significantly reduced in both glaucoma groups compared to controls (adjusted p = 0.001 for PEXG, adjusted p = 0.003 for POAG; overall p < 0.001). In POAG, perilimbal AST (AST0, AST1), TMT and SSL were significantly lower than in controls (p < 0.05); these perilimbal measurements did not differ significantly from those of healthy controls in PEXG (all p > 0.18). LCCI was highest in POAG, while LCT was thinnest in PEXG (p < 0.001). A nominal positive correlation was observed between SSL and AST0 in healthy eyes, alongside nominal negative correlations between SSL and LCCI in both glaucoma groups (all uncorrected p < 0.05); however, none remained statistically significant after false discovery rate (FDR) correction (all q > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Differences in anterior scleral, iridocorneal angle, and lamina cribrosa parameters indicate shared structural features but distinct anatomical profiles in POAG and PEXG. Because correlational findings did not survive FDR correction, the proposed structural links between the anterior and posterior segments must be interpreted as exploratory, warranting further longitudinal studies.

etudes.titre: Reporting quality assessment of sham acupuncture randomized controlled trials for acupuncture intervention in glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique

labos.nom: Key Technologies Research and Development Program

etudes.resume:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the reporting quality of sham-acupuncture-randomized controlled trials (RCTs) investigating acupuncture intervention for glaucoma.
METHODS: A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, the Cochrane Library, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, EBSCO, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Wanfang Database, SinoMed, and China Science and Technology Journal Database (VIP) for Chinese and English RCTs on acupuncture intervention for glaucoma published from database inception until August 2025. The Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials 2025 (CONSORT), Standards for Reporting Interventions in Clinical Trials of Acupuncture (STRICTA), and the Sham Acupuncture Reporting Guidelines and a Checklist in Clinical Trials (SHARE) were used by the investigators to assess the Overall Quality Score (OQS) of the RCTs that met the pre-defined inclusion criteria. Inter-rater agreement was evaluated using Cohen's κ coefficient.
RESULTS: The systematic search initially identified 1289 relevant records. After a stepwise screening process, it was found that RCTs utilizing sham acupuncture controls were very limited; consequently, only 6 RCTs meeting the pre-defined criteria were ultimately included. According to the CONSORT statement, the median OQS for the 6 RCTs was 16 items (range: 10-23). Among all CONSORT items, the positive rate for 9 items (21%) was greater than 80%, while for 20 items (48%) it was below 20%. Based on the STRICTA guidelines, the median OQS for the 6 RCTs was 10.5 items (range: 8-14). For the STRICTA guidelines, the positive rate for 6 items (35%) was greater than 80%, and for 1 item (6%) it was below 20%. According to the SHARE guidelines, the median OQS for the 6 RCTs was 6.5 items (range: 3-10). For the SHARE checklist, 3 items (18%) had a reporting rate > 80%, while 10 items (53%) had a rate < 20%. The overall average reporting rates based on CONSORT, STRICTA, and SHARE were 39.7%, 62.7%, and 35.1%, respectively.
CONCLUSION: The current reporting quality of sham acupuncture RCTs on acupuncture intervention for glaucoma is generally suboptimal. There is a particular and urgent need to improve the reporting of detailed information regarding the sham acupuncture control. It is recommended that future relevant RCTs strictly adhere to the CONSORT statement, STRICTA standards, and SHARE checklist for standardized reporting.

etudes.titre: Impact of Limited English Proficiency on Glaucoma Outcomes, Access to Eye Care, and Health Literacy in the NIH All of Us Database.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: To explore the associations between limited English proficiency and glaucoma outcomes, access to eye care, and health literacy in a national database.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included participants in the NIH All of Us Research Program with available health records and responses to surveys about language. Main Outcome Measures included glaucoma prevalence, severity, and surgical history as well as access to eye care and health literacy measures. Logistic regression analyses of associations between self-reported English proficiency and outcomes, adjusting for other demographic and socioeconomic characteristics, were conducted.
RESULTS: Of 79,635 individuals in the study population, 1268 (1.6%) had low English proficiency (LEP) and 3296 (4.1%) had a glaucoma diagnosis. Compared to those with high English proficiency (HEP), individuals with glaucoma with LEP had a higher likelihood of incisional glaucoma surgery (aOR = 4.79, 95% CI = 1.03-22.22). Those with LEP were more likely to understand health information only "some or none of the time" as opposed to "always" (aOR = 6.36, 95% CI = 1.17-34.57) and experience problems learning about medical conditions "sometimes or occasionally" as opposed to "never" (aOR = 3.18, 95% CI = 1.22-8.34). No statistically significant associations between LEP and glaucoma prevalence, severity, or eye care access were observed in adjusted analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Among individuals with glaucoma, those with LEP had a higher likelihood of undergoing incisional glaucoma surgery. Although LEP does not cause increased surgery, this correlation suggests that the decision to operate and its acceptance by the patient are more likely in individuals with LEP. Future studies on improving health literacy may reduce this association.

etudes.titre: Gonioscopy-assisted transluminal trabeculotomy versus trabeculectomy with phacoemulsification in primary open angle glaucoma - One-year outcomes.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « trabeculectomy »; mot du titre : « trabeculotomy »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To assess the safety and efficacy of gonioscopy-assisted transluminal trabeculotomy (GATT) with phacoemulsification in primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG).
METHODS: In this prospective, nonrandomized, comparative study, patients with POAG underwent either phaco-GATT (Group A, n = 75) or phacotrabeculectomy (Group B, n = 77) and were followed up for one year. Changes in intraocular pressure (IOP), antiglaucoma medications (AGMs), complications, and success rates over one year were compared. Success rate was described under two criteria: 1: IOP between 6 and 21 mmHg and a decrease of >20% from the baseline; 2: IOP between 6 and 18 mmHg and a decrease of >25% from the baseline.
RESULTS: Mean IOP decreased by 25.1%, from 17.93 ± 4.29 mmHg to 13.00 ± 3.18 mmHg (P < 0.001) in Group A (n = 70) and by 28% from 17.81 ± 4.52 mmHg to 12.16 ± 3.28 mmHg (P < 0.001) in Group B (n = 74) at one year. AGM reduced from 1.03 ± 0.43 to 0.09 ± 0.29 in Group A (P < 0.001) and from 1.04 ± 0.41 to 0.16 ± 0.37 in Group B (P < 0.001), with no significant difference between the groups (P = 0.24). 91.4% of patients in Group A and 85.1% in Group B were free of medications. The cumulative one-year success was 68% and 63.6% by Criteria 1 (P = 0.52) and 60% and 50.7% by Criteria 2 (P = 0.23) in Groups A and B, respectively, with no significant difference between the groups. Sixteen patients in Group A had microhyphema, seven had macrohyphema, and two patients underwent anterior chamber (AC) wash. Four patients in Group B had hypotony, one required conjunctival resuturing, and one required AC reformation.
CONCLUSION: Phaco-GATT demonstrated comparable intraocular pressure reduction, medication independence, and surgical success rates to phacotrabeculectomy at one year, with minimal complications.

etudes.titre: Clinical Spectrum and Insights from One Year of Ocular Genetics at a Single Tertiary Eye Care Centre.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Genetics »
etudes.resume:
INTRODUCTION: Genetic testing benefits individuals and families with inherited eye diseases by facilitating accurate diagnosis, informing prognosis, enabling assessment for at-risk family members, and supporting targeted therapies. This study aimed to characterize the spectrum of inherited eye disorders and evaluate the diagnostic yield of genetic testing at a single tertiary eye care centre over a one-year period.
METHODS: A retrospective review of patients attending the ocular genetics service at a tertiary eye care centre in India from January 1 to December 31, 2024, was conducted.
RESULTS: Of 1325 patients evaluated, 862 (65%) underwent genetic testing. Inherited retinal disorders were the most common (n = 440, 51%), followed by cornea and anterior segment disorders (n = 107, 12.4%). Other conditions included hereditary optic nerve disorders (n = 75, 8.7%), glaucoma (n = 70, 8.1%), lenticular disorders (n = 54, 6.3%), phacomatoses (n = 25, 2.9%), ocular tumours (n = 20, 2.3%), strabismus and albinism (n = 19 and 18; ~2% each), MAC spectrum disorders (n = 10, 1.4%), and systemic syndromes (n = 22, 2.5%). Diagnostic yield was achieved in 605 (70%), while 257 (30%) remained inconclusive. Of the 463 untested families, the motivations were unascertained reasons (n = 156, 33%), financial constraints (n = 138, 30%), intent to test later (n = 90, 19%), and belief that no treatment was available (n = 79, 17%).
DISCUSSION: Inherited retinal and anterior segment disorders constitute the most frequent genetic eye diseases. Genetic testing has enabled genotype-phenotype correlation in over two-thirds of cases. Financial constraints and limited availability of disease-modifying treatments remain key barriers for uptake of genetic testing.

etudes.titre: Outcomes of phaco-endocyclophotocoagulation in acute on chronic primary angle closure glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To report the outcomes of endocyclophotocoagulation (ECP) combined with phacoemulsification in primary angle closure glaucoma (PACG) eyes presenting with acute symptoms (A-o-C-PACG) and to compare the biometric characteristics of these eyes with PACG controls.
METHODS: Retrospective data collection of consecutive PACG subjects presenting with symptoms of acute angle closure between May 2021 and September 2023. Such subjects were compared to severity-of-glaucoma-matched PACG controls. Only those eyes that underwent phaco-ECP were included. The main outcome measure was intraocular pressure (IOP) and a comparison of biometric parameters between cases and controls. The secondary outcome measures were the number of anti-glaucoma medications (AGMs), best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), and complications.
RESULTS: Fifteen study eyes and 26 PACG controls were included; the mean age was 54.2 ± 7.4 years. The mean IOP (34.6 ± 13.4 mmHg, 95%CI [27.2,42.0]), AGM (4.3 ± 1.2,95%CI [3.6,5.0]), synechial angle closure (3.3 ± 1.0 quadrants, 95%CI [2.7,3.8]), and lens thickness (5.1 ± 0.3, 95%CI [4.9,5.3]) were significantly more, and the anterior chamber depth (2.3 ± 0.3 mm, 95%CI [2.1,2.5]) and relative lens position (0.20 ± 0.01, 95%CI [0.19,0.20]) were significantly less when compared to PACG controls. IOP at the last follow-up postprocedure (mean 18 months) was 12.7 ± 2.3 mmHg, 95%CI [11.4,13.9] on 0.7 ± 0.8, 95%CI [0.2, 1.1], number of AGM ( P < .001). BCVA improved significantly from 0.9 ± 0.7, 95%CI [0.5,1.3], to 0.2 ± 0.3, 95%CI [0.03,0.4]; none had serious sight-threatening complications.
CONCLUSION: Phaco-endocyclophotocoagulation is not only effective but also very safe in controlling IOP and reducing topical medications in PACG eyes that present with acute symptoms. Biometric parameters are significantly different in such eyes when compared to PACG controls.

etudes.titre: Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease misdiagnosed as angle closure: Demographic characteristics, clinical presentation, and visual outcomes.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To describe the clinical presentation, diagnostic delay, management, and visual outcomes of Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada (VKH) disease presenting initially as angle closure.
METHODS: This retrospective study reviewed the medical records of patients diagnosed with VKH who initially presented with angle closure between January 2013 and December 2020. Clinical features, intraocular pressure (IOP), imaging, treatment modalities, and final visual outcomes were analyzed. Univariate and multivariate analyses were performed to identify factors influencing final BCVA (best corrected visual acuity).
RESULTS: Among 768 VKH patients, 18 patients (36 eyes; 3.94%) presented with angle closure with a mean age of 44.4 years and a female preponderance (89%). Eighteen eyes had primary angle closure (PAC), and 18 eyes had secondary angle closure glaucoma (SACG) at presentation. The mean IOP at final follow-up decreased from 26.3 to 14 mmHg. Fundus evaluation was deferred in many due to media opacities, leading to delayed VKH diagnosis (median delay: 1 month to 7 years). Ancillary imaging revealed choroidal thickening and ciliochoroidal effusion in four eyes. Poorer presenting BCVA and delayed diagnosis (>1 month) were associated with worse final BCVA ( P = 0.011 and P = 0.0066, respectively) in univariate analysis, while presenting BCVA remained a statistically significant independent predictor of final visual outcome (p 0.039) in multivariate analysis.
CONCLUSION: VKH can uncommonly present as angle closure, often mimicking PAC or SACG. Early clinical suspicion, use of posterior segment imaging (optical coherence tomography, B-scan, ultrasound biomicroscopy), and prompt immunosuppressive therapy are essential for optimal management.

etudes.titre: Characterizing the Modern Interventional Glaucoma Treatment Paradigm: The Newton Registry.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
INTRODUCTION: We aim to describe the development of the Newton Registry which characterizes the frequency and nature of interventional glaucoma (IG) procedures used for treatment in the USA between 2022 and 2025.
METHODS: The Newton Registry contains International Classification of Disease Tenth Edition (ICD-10) codes and Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codes from encounters with patients with glaucoma and providers in ophthalmology practices in the USA. Each practice provided a window of data 18-36 months in duration that captured all glaucoma patient and procedure encounters of the practice's providers. Robust data cleaning techniques were applied. Analyses were descriptive in nature and included a qualitative description of the dataset and its structure, the types and severity of glaucoma included, the duration of follow-up and lapse rate, and the frequency and nature of therapeutic IG.
RESULTS: The Registry contains data from 724,728 encounters between 157,246 patients with glaucoma and 605 providers at 35 practices. Most patients had open-angle glaucoma (82.1%) or were glaucoma suspects (10.5%). The glaucoma was coded as mild in 51.8% of patients, moderate in 13.5%, and severe in 17.8%. The mean follow-up duration was 15.4 (10.7) months with 56.3% having a > 12-month lapse in glaucoma care during the 18-36 month observation window. The glaucoma procedures rate (≥ 1 procedure during the observation window) was 12.2%; common procedures included selective laser trabeculoplasty (44.4%), stent implantation (25.7%), canaloplasty (12.3%), and goniotomy (12.1%), as well as traditional filtering surgeries (4.5%).
CONCLUSIONS: The Newton Registry provides important information on current glaucoma treatment practice patterns. In subsequent analyses, this dataset may reveal the current status of the use of IG, provide insight into how IG is currently being deployed, supply a standard against which practices can compare when examining their own treatment patterns, and establish a baseline against which future changes in practice patterns can be measured.

etudes.titre: Preoperative Topical Steroid Use and Trabeculectomy Outcomes.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Trabeculectomy »
etudes.resume:
PRCIS: Preoperative topical steroid use was associated with greater surgical success and thicker, less reflective bleb walls on anterior segment optical coherence tomography 1 year after trabeculectomy.
PURPOSE: To assess the associations of preoperative topical steroid administration with surgical outcomes and filtering bleb morphology 1 year after trabeculectomy.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This study included 304 eyes from 272 patients who underwent primary trabeculectomy with mitomycin C. Eyes were classified into steroid and nonsteroid groups based on preoperative topical steroid administration for 7 days. The primary outcome was surgical success at 1 year, defined by either criterion A [intraocular pressure (IOP) ≤15 mm Hg and a ≥20% reduction from preoperative IOP] or criterion B (IOP ≤12 mm Hg and a ≥30% reduction from preoperative IOP), achieved without glaucoma medication or additional glaucoma surgery. Bleb morphology was evaluated using anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT). Multivariable Cox regression was used to adjust for potential confounders.
RESULTS: At 1 year, surgical success rates were significantly higher in the steroid group than in the nonsteroid group for both criterion A (85.5% vs. 71.1%, P =0.005) and criterion B (76.4% vs. 65.4%, P =0.040). Preoperative steroid use was significantly associated with a lower hazard of surgical failure (criterion A: adjusted hazard ratio, 0.47; 95% CI: 0.27-0.82; P =0.008). Compared with the nonsteroid group, the steroid group exhibited greater bleb wall thickness (0.812 vs. 0.723 mm, P =0.038) and lower bleb wall reflectivity (130.3 vs. 141.9 arbitrary units, P =0.011).
CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative administration of topical steroids, compared with no steroids, was associated with higher surgical success rates, thicker bleb walls, and lower bleb wall reflectivity on AS-OCT at 1 year.

etudes.titre: Anterior Segment Ischemia and Neurotrophic Keratopathy Following Ultrasound Cycloplasty in Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Ultrasound cycloplasty (UCP) is a minimally invasive, non-incisional glaucoma procedure that has emerged in recent years and is generally associated with few complications. We report a case of a patient with acute angle-closure glaucoma underwent UCP for IOP control. She developed iris neovascularization and neurotrophic keratopathy（NK）at postoperative week 6, followed by hypopyon, flattening of the anterior chamber, and thinning of the peripheral cornea at postoperative week 11, 12, and 14, respectively. We concluded that UCP can lead to anterior segment ischemia (ASI) and NK, which manifest as iris neovascularization, painless corneal epithelial defects, peripheral corneal thinning, hypopyon, and flattening of the anterior chamber. Preoperative screening for high-risk factors is essential before performing UCP.

etudes.titre: Evaluating Long-Term Effectiveness and Safety of Glaucoma Surgical Innovations: A Systematic Review.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Surgical »
etudes.resume:
PRCIS: A systematic review examining the reporting of long-term safety of glaucoma surgical innovations. Twenty-seven studies met the inclusion criteria and demonstrated effectiveness over the short to medium term. Use of registries to optimise future long-term evaluation is recommended.
PURPOSE: To synthesise evidence on the long-term effectiveness and safety of glaucoma surgical innovations introduced since 2004 and appraise reporting quality against IDEAL Stage 4 recommendations, designed to promote transparent study of the long-term impact of surgical innovations.
METHODS: MEDLINE, EMBASE, and CENTRAL were searched for studies published from January 1, 2014, to October 21, 2024. Eligible studies evaluated novel glaucoma surgery with ≥2 years' follow-up and ≥100 participants. Randomised controlled trials, observational studies, registry analyses, and case series were included. Reporting was assessed using a 16-item adaptation of the IDEAL Stage 4 checklist. Risk of bias was assessed using Cochrane RoB 2, the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and the Joanna Briggs Institute case-series checklist.
RESULTS: The search strategy retrieved 1758 matches, with 27 studies meeting the inclusion criteria. Procedures included iStent, Xen-45 Gel stent, Hydrus microstent, Endoscopic photocoagulation, Trabectome and Kahook dual blade. Follow-up ranged from 2 to 6 years. All studies described design and 22 reported prespecified outcomes sufficiently; however, only 4 explained how missing data were handled. Intraocular-pressure and medication outcomes generally favoured the intervention, but heterogeneity in design, comparators, outcomes, and surgical context precluded pooled estimates. Adverse-event reporting was inconsistent. One cohort study was of poor quality; 14 case series had unclear or unreported methodological items; and 4 RCTs had at least one high-risk domain.
CONCLUSIONS: Glaucoma surgical innovations appear effective over the medium term, but limited long-term follow-up and inconsistent safety reporting preclude firm conclusions about comparative effectiveness and long-term safety. Standardised reporting and prospective registries are needed.

etudes.titre: Advancing nanomaterials for treatment of eye diseases: a review.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Ocular diseases involving both the anterior and posterior segments-such as dry eye disease, keratitis, glaucoma, cataracts, diabetic retinopathy, retinal vein occlusion, and ocular tumors-remain major contributors to global visual impairment. Conventional topical and systemic therapies are limited by rapid clearance, restricted penetration across ocular barriers, and poor bioavailability, particularly for posterior-segment targets. Nanotechnology has introduced a transformative therapeutic paradigm by enabling controlled pharmacokinetics, enhanced tissue penetration, and site-specific delivery. A wide range of engineered nanomaterials-including polymeric nanoparticles, lipid-based carriers, dendrimers, metallic and metal-oxide nanoparticles, mesoporous silica systems, cerium oxide nanozymes, carbon quantum dots, nanogels, and electrospun nanofibers-has demonstrated improved drug loading, sustained release, ocular surface retention, and compatibility with biologics and gene-based agents. Emerging minimally invasive platforms, such as 4D printed smart scaffolds, dissolving microneedles and magnetically driven microrobots, further enable precise transscleral or intravitreal delivery, active navigation through the vitreous, and targeted interaction with retinal lesions. Parallel clinical advances, including FDA-approved nanoformulations and ongoing trials, confirm the translational potential of these technologies. Plus, artificial intelligence now accelerates both ophthalmic diagnosis and nanocarrier design, enabling predictive modeling of nano-bio interactions, personalized delivery strategies, and real-time disease assessment. This review integrates current advances in nanomaterial engineering and AI-guided innovation, outlining their convergent roles in shaping next-generation precision therapeutics for vision preservation and restoration.

etudes.titre: Presence of lower limb joint arthritis moderates the interrelationship between vision impairment and fear of falling avoidance behavior in older adults: A cross-sectional study.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Falling is a common concern for older adults. Previous studies showed that mobility performance is significantly lower in those with age-related eye diseases or lower limb arthritis, contributing to their increased fall risk. However, it is currently unknown how the co-presence of these 2 age-related sensorimotor impairments interacts to affect fear of falling (FOF) and associated activity-avoidance behaviors. A total of 200 participants recruited from an outpatient regional medical center (127 women, 73 men, age = 65.5 ± 8.4 years) participated in this study. The presence of age-related, uncorrected eye diseases (i.e., cataracts, glaucoma, retinopathy, and macular degeneration) and arthritis in the lower limb joints were recorded. Geriatric Fear of Falling Measure, Fear of Falling Avoidance Behavior Questionnaire, and Timed Up-and-Go test were used to assess FOF, avoidance behavior, and physical mobility, respectively. Moderated mediation analyses, corrected for age and body mass index, were performed. With the Geriatric Fear of Falling Measure as mediator, lower limb arthritis significantly moderated the indirect effects of eye disease on Timed Up-and-Go test performance (B = 1.00; 95% confidence interval = 0.06-2.11) and the Fear of Falling Avoidance Behavior Questionnaire score (B = 5.68; 95% confidence interval = 0.36-11.11). Namely, participants with uncorrected age-related eye disease and lower limb arthritis exhibited significantly poorer mobility and greater avoidance behavior than those without arthritis. The presence of age-related eye diseases exacerbates FOF avoidance behavior and leads to diminished mobility in older adults. The severity of FOF is moderated by the presence of lower limb arthritis. These findings suggest that effective fall prevention strategies for older adults should incorporate comprehensive vision, musculoskeletal, and behavioral evaluations.

etudes.titre: Epidemiology of visual impairment and rehabilitation measures in adults-Data from the Swedish Quality Registry for Rehabilitation in Visual Impairment.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique

labos.nom: Stiftelsen för Synskadade i f d Malmöhus län
Stiftelsen Kronprinsessan Margaretas Arbetsnämnd för Synskadade
Skåne County Council Research and Development Foundation

etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To describe the Swedish Quality Registry for Rehabilitation in Visual Impairment (SKRS) and present rehabilitation measures and underlying diagnoses of visual impairment and blindness in adults in Sweden.
METHODS: The study includes data from the SKRS collected between January 2016 and December 2025 for patients aged ≥20 years who received rehabilitation services from low vision centres in Sweden. The degree and underlying causes of visual impairment, as well as rehabilitation interventions, were analysed.
RESULTS: In 2025, SKRS recorded 12 622 registrations for 11 810 unique patients, with women accounting for 62%. The median waiting time from referral to first visit was 37 days. Most patients had a moderate visual impairment. In 2025, age-related macular degeneration (AMD) represented the most common diagnosis (50.2%), followed by glaucoma (18.3%), blindness of unspecified cause/visual impairment (5.9%), retinal diseases (5%), diabetic retinopathy (2.8%) and optic nerve diseases (2.2%). The most frequently registered procedure codes were in the group of assistive technology with 30.3%, followed by investigative procedures with 26.1% and follow-up with 19.9%. The proportion of International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health based instruments had increased significantly; from 0.04% in 2016 to 72.5% in 2025. The proportion of individual rehabilitation plans had risen by 18.6% since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic-from 53.2% in 2020 to 71.8% in 2025.
CONCLUSION: SKRS provides representative data on rehabilitation measures and associated diagnoses among adults with visual impairments in Sweden. The data confirm that AMD and glaucoma are the most common causes and highlight inequalities in access to visual rehabilitation.

etudes.titre: Long-Term Efficacy of Phacoemulsification Combined With Trabeculectomy for Advanced Chronic Primary Angle-Closure Glaucoma With Cataract: A 3-Year Retrospective Study.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Trabeculectomy »

labos.nom: National Natural Science Foundation of China
Natural Science Foundation of Guangdong Province

etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the long-term efficacy of phacoemulsification combined with trabeculectomy (Phaco-Trab) for advanced chronic primary angle-closure glaucoma (PACG) with cataract.
METHODS: Patients with advanced chronic PACG coexisting with cataracts who underwent Phaco-Trab were enrolled. The morphologic structures of filtering blebs, including characteristics under slit-lamp examination, anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT), and in vivo confocal microscopy (IVCM), were used to evaluate the filtering function.
RESULTS: A total of 30 eyes from 27 patients were enrolled. The mean preoperative intraocular pressure (IOP) of 19.98 ± 6.48 mmHg significantly decreased to 13.73 ± 2.35 mmHg at year 3 (p < 0.0001). A statistically significant decrease in postoperative IOP-lowering medications was observed, but the number of drugs used increased annually (0.50 ± 0.82 at year 1, 1.00 ± 0.98 at year 2, and 1.47 ± 0.97 at year 3, p < 0.0001). Following Phaco-Trab, a high surgical qualified success rate was maintained over 3 years (93.3% at year 1, 90.0% at year 2, and 80.0% at year 3, p = 0.117). However, the complete success rate significantly decreased each year (70.0% at year 1, 36.7% at year 2, and 20.0% at year 3, p < 0.0001), along with an increase in the rate of failure filtering blebs, reaching 46.7%, 83.3%, and 90.0% at each time point (p < 0.0001). Overall, 46.7% (14/30) of participants developed complications and required postoperative procedures after Phaco-Trab, which were mainly induced by the trabeculectomy procedure.
CONCLUSIONS: Phaco-Trab can significantly lower IOP and reduce the use of IOP-lowering medications for advanced chronic PACG with cataracts, but it is associated with a higher rate of complications and a higher failure rate of the filtering bleb.

etudes.titre: Next-Generation Sequencing to Identify Genetic Causes of Chinese Patients Affected With Non-retinal Developmental Eye Disorders.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Genetic »; mot du titre : « Sequencing »

labos.nom: National Natural Science Foundation of China
Fundamental Research Funds for the Central Universities

etudes.resume: To investigate the genetic causes of non-retinal developmental eye disorders in 14 Chinese different families, we subjected participants to a specific hereditary eye disease enrichment panel (HEDEP) or whole exome sequencing. We further validated disease-causing variants and performed co-segregation analyses on the available family members by Sanger sequencing. We classified sequence changes according to the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics and the Association for Molecular Pathology variant interpretation guidelines. Fourteen probands with diverse clinical diagnoses were analyzed, including microphthalmia (with or without microcornea and congenital cataract or congenital corneal opacification (CCO), four cases), anterior segment dysgenesis (ASD, six cases)-including Peter's anomaly (PA, one case), PA and microphthalmia (one case), iridocoloboma or aniridia (with microcornea and/or congenital cataract, two cases), and primary congenital glaucoma (PCG, two cases)-congenital cataract (with CCO or microcornea, three cases), and Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome (RSTS, one case). Initial inheritance patterns for 1, 5, and 8 cases were autosomal recessive, autosomal dominant, and sporadic, respectively. We identified 17 (likely) pathogenic variants and one variant of uncertain significance (VUS) in 16 genes, including BMP4, BCOR, PITX3, and PAX6. Among them, eight were novel variants, and two were de novo. We confirmed the pathogenicity of PAX6 intronic mutation using in vitro splice assays and redefined the pathogenicity of the variants of uncertain significance as likely pathogenic. Patients with developmental eye diseases typically have complex ocular and systemic phenotypes, possibly leading to significant visual impairment and high blindness rates. Identifying the genetic causes facilitates early diagnosis and effective treatment and rehabilitation strategies, thereby providing valuable insights for genetic and clinical counseling of these patients.

etudes.titre: Association between distance from the angle recess to the tube entry site and corneal endothelial cell loss after PreserFlo MicroShunt implantation.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « tube »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To investigate the association between anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT)-derived tube parameters and corneal endothelial cell density (ECD) changes after PreserFlo MicroShunt (PMS) surgery in primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) and exfoliation glaucoma (XFG).
STUDY DESIGN: Prospective cohort study.
METHODS: This study included pseudophakic patients with POAG or XFG who underwent PMS implantation. ECD was measured preoperatively and at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months post operatively, and every 6 months thereafter. Intracameral tube parameters, including tube position and length, were assessed using AS-OCT images obtained 1 month postoperatively. Associations between OCT parameters and the monthly rate of ECD change (ECD slope) were evaluated using linear mixed-effects models.
RESULTS: Mean preoperative ECD was 2384 ± 391 cells/mm2. Mean follow-up period was 15 ± 7 months, with 5.1 ± 1.3 ECD measurements per eye. Tube parameters did not differ significantly between POAG (67 eyes of 61 patients) and XFG (18 eyes of 16 patients). The mean ECD slope was -11.8 ± 2.2 cells/mm2/month in XFG and -9.8 ± 1.1 cells/mm2/month in POAG (p = 0.38). A greater distance from the angle recess to the intracameral tube entry site was significantly associated with a more negative ECD slope in both XFG and POAG groups (p = 0.02 and 0.03). Its contribution to ECD slope variance was greater in XFG than in POAG (R2 = 0.243 vs. 0.069).
CONCLUSION: A longer distance from the angle recess to the intracameral tube entry site may predict accelerated ECD loss after PMS implantation, particularly in XFG.

etudes.titre: Spatial corneal endothelial cell loss after preserflo microshunt implantation: association with tube insertion position.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « tube »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To investigate spatial corneal endothelial cell density (ECD) changes after PreserFlo MicroShunt™ (PFM) implantation and identify tube-related factors associated with localized endothelial cell loss.
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective clinical study.
METHODS: This study included 118 eyes of 118 patients with medically refractory glaucoma who underwent PFM implantation and were followed for ≥6 months. Anterior-segment optical coherence tomography was used to evaluate tube-cornea distance, tube-cornea angle, and intracameral tube length. Gonioscopic images obtained 1 month postoperatively were used to classify tube insertion as iris-side, trabecular, or corneal-side. ECD was measured at nine corneal regions using specular microscopy. The primary outcome was the ECD reduction rate at the tube insertion site (Position 3) at 3 and 6 months. Linear mixed-effects models were used to identify factors associated with localized endothelial cell loss.
RESULTS: Tube insertion locations were iris-side in 36 eyes, trabecular in 73 eyes, and corneal-side in 9 eyes. In the primary linear mixed-effects analysis, compared with iris-side insertion, both trabecular-contact insertion (β = 12.8%, P = 0.026) and corneal-side insertion (β = 28.6%, P = 0.007) were associated with greater localized endothelial cell loss after multivariable adjustment. Central ECD reduction was mild (2.1% at 6 months).
CONCLUSIONS: Early localized endothelial cell loss after PFM implantation was associated with tube insertion position, particularly corneal-side insertion. Central ECD measurements may underestimate localized endothelial cell loss.

etudes.titre: Stage-dependent differences in recalculated mean deviation between 24plus(1-2) and 24plus(1) test locations in glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To evaluate stage-dependent differences in mean deviation (MD) recalculated from the 24plus(1-2) and 24plus(1) test locations and to identify the MD range at which divergence between the reduced and full location sets exceeds a prespecified operational threshold in glaucoma.
METHODS: This retrospective, cross-sectional study included 394 eyes from 197 patients with glaucoma including preperimetric glaucoma (PPG). The 24plus(1) MD was recalculated from a subset of 36 test locations derived from the 24plus(1-2) grid. Glaucoma severity was classified as PPG, early, moderate, or advanced based on MD. Differences between the full and reduced location sets were assessed using cluster-adjusted Bland-Altman analysis and linear mixed-effects models. Mixed-effects logistic regression was applied to estimate the probability of exceeding a prespecified operational MD-difference threshold (|ΔMD|> 1 dB), with patient-level bootstrap confidence intervals.
RESULTS: The overall mean difference in recalculated MD was - 0.52 dB (95% limits of agreement: - 2.82 to 1.78 dB). The proportion of eyes with |ΔMD|> 1 dB was 1.9% in PPG, 17.8% in early glaucoma, 50.0% in moderate glaucoma, and 67.5% in advanced glaucoma. Worse MD was significantly associated with a higher probability of exceeding the prespecified operational MD-difference threshold (β = - 0.169; P < 0.001). MD values of - 5.4 dB (95% CI: - 7.0 to - 4.0) and - 11.9 dB (95% CI: - 14.1 to - 9.9) corresponded to 25% and 50% predicted probabilities of deviation, respectively.
CONCLUSION: In this recalculation/subsampling analysis, 24plus(1)-derived MD was similar to 24plus(1-2)-derived MD in early glaucoma but diverged with advancing disease, particularly beyond approximately - 5 to - 6 dB, suggesting caution when interpreting 24plus(1)-derived MD in more advanced glaucoma.
etudes.revue: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie

etudes.titre: 36-month multi-centre outcomes of XEN45 gel stent implantation in Asian versus non-Asian eyes with primary open angle glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « stent »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: Ethnicity has been shown to influence outcomes of bleb-forming glaucoma filtering surgery. This study evaluated 3-year outcomes of XEN45 Gel Stent (XGS) in Asian versus non-Asian eyes with primary open angle glaucoma (POAG).
METHODS: This multicentre, retrospective cohort included 117 eyes with POAG undergoing XGS implantation, with or without concomitant phacoemulsification, between January 2017 and March 2023. Eyes were categorized as Asian or non-Asian based on recorded ethnicity. The primary outcome was cumulative surgical success at three years using survival analyses across intraocular pressure (IOP) thresholds (≤ 18, ≤ 15, and ≤ 12 mmHg with ≥ 20% reduction from baseline). Secondary analysis incorporating a medication reduction goal was performed. Secondary outcomes included longitudinal changes in IOP and medications, predictors of time-to-failure, and postoperative interventions and complications. Longitudinal outcomes were analysed using linear mixed-effects models. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models evaluated predictors of failure.
RESULTS: 92 Asian and 25 non-Asian eyes were included. Both groups demonstrated sustained reductions in IOP and medication burden over 36 months. Three-year cumulative success rates were comparable between Asian and non-Asian eyes across all success definitions (AR-18: 72.2% vs. 76.5%; AR-15: 72.7% vs. 76.5%; AR-12: 68.6% vs. 63.9%; all p > 0.30). No significant differences in cumulative success were observed between Phaco-XEN and standalone XEN procedures. Ethnicity and concomitant phacoemulsification were not independently associated with time-to-failure. Post-operative interventions and complications were infrequent.
CONCLUSION: XGS demonstrated no significant differences in 3-year surgical success, safety, and durability between broadly categorized Asian and non-Asian eyes with POAG. Neither ethnicity nor concomitant phacoemulsification independently influenced failure risk.
