etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Inhibitor »

etudes.titre: The Paul Glaucoma Implant versus the Ahmed and Baerveldt Glaucoma Implants: A Systematic Review and Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To compare the efficacy and safety of the Paul Glaucoma Implant (PGI) with those of the two established glaucoma drainage devices, the Ahmed Glaucoma Valve (AGV) and the Baerveldt Glaucoma Implant (BGI).
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane CENTRAL, ClinicalTrials.gov, ScienceDirect and Google Scholar were searched. Eligible studies were randomised or comparative observational studies reporting outcomes in patients who received the PGI alongside a concurrent AGV or BGI comparator. The primary outcomes were intraocular pressure (IOP) reduction, surgical success rate, and reduction in glaucoma medications. A Bayesian network meta-analysis was performed, with treatment ranking summarized by surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA). Quality assessment and evidence certainty was performed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool and GRADE framework respectively.
RESULTS: Five comparative studies (238 patients) were included. Relative to the AGV, the PGI was associated with a mean difference in IOP at 12 months of -3.344 (95% CrI -7.743 to 1.058) mmHg, and relative to the BGI of 4.387 (95% CrI -0.288 to 9.074) mmHg. Corresponding differences in medication number at 12 months were]-0.186 (95% CrI -0.858 to 0.545) and 0.444 (95% CrI -0.358 to 1.272). Credible intervals crossed the null for 29 of the 30 primary contrasts. Ranking probabilities favoured the AGV for IOP reduction from 3 to 12 months (SUCRA 0.885 to 0.976) and the PGI for early medication reduction (SUCRA 0.769 at 1 month), but these rankings were derived from imprecise estimates. Safety estimates were based on small numbers of events and several were unstable. Certainty of evidence was low to very low for most comparisons.
CONCLUSION: Within the limits of a small and predominantly non-randomised evidence base, the PGI achieved intraocular pressure and medication reduction broadly comparable to those of the AGV and BGI over the first postoperative year, with a distinct complication profile. The rankings reported here are hypothesis-generating and should not by themselves determine device selection. Adequately large randomised comparisons with follow-up beyond one year are required.

etudes.titre: One-Year Outcomes of PreserFlo MicroShunt implantation Using Intraoperative Sub-Tenon Triamcinolone Acetonide.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the 1-year efficacy, postoperative intervention burden, and safety of PreserFlo MicroShunt (PMS) implantation using intraoperative sub-Tenon triamcinolone acetonide (STTA).
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This two-center retrospective study included 107 eyes of 107 consecutive patients who underwent standalone PMS implantation between December 2023 and May 2025. Mitomycin C (0.4 mg/mL) was applied for 5 min, followed by 20 mg STTA. Complete success was defined as an intraocular pressure (IOP) of 6-12 mmHg, with at least a 20% reduction from baseline, without medication or additional surgery. Qualified success allowed the use of glaucoma medications. Needling-free complete success was considered when the first needling procedure failed. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to estimate success rates, and Cox proportional hazards regression analysis was used to evaluate factors associated with surgical failure.
RESULTS: Median preoperative IOP was 22.0 mmHg (interquartile range [IQR], 17.0-28.0), and median medication score was 5.0 (IQR, 4.0-5.0). At 12 months, median IOP decreased to 9.0 mmHg (IQR, 6.0-12.0), and median medication score decreased to 0.0 (IQR, 0.0-0.0; both P<0.001). The estimated 12-month complete, qualified, and needling-free complete success rates were 83.1%, 85.0%, and 67.7%, respectively. Needling was performed in 18 eyes (16.8%), and 16 of those eyes (88.9%) met the complete success criteria at the final assessment within 12 months. Hypotony was present at 1 month in 37 eyes (34.6%), including persistent hypotony in 25 eyes (23.4%). Most hypotony-related events resolved without surgery. One eye developed suprachoroidal hemorrhage with severe visual loss. No significant baseline predictors of failure were identified.
CONCLUSION: This protocol achieved substantial IOP and medication reduction with favorable 12-month success rates. Needling is an important component of postoperative management, and persistent numerical hypotony is common, but usually resolves without surgery. Comparative studies are needed to determine the specific contributions of STTA.

etudes.titre: AKAP1 Protects Retinal Ganglion Cells and Preserves Vision by Improving Mitochondrial and Synaptic Health in Glaucomatous Neurodegeneration.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Retinal Ganglion Cells »; mot du titre : « Neurodegeneration »

labos.nom: University of California Gene Therapy Initiative
National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke

etudes.resume: Glaucoma, a leading cause of irreversible blindness, is characterized by progressive loss of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and lacks effective neuroprotective therapies. Despite evidence implicating mitochondrial dysfunction in glaucoma, the mechanisms linking elevated intraocular pressure, synaptic dysfunction, mitochondrial failure, and RGC death remain incompletely understood. Here we identify the mitochondrial scaffold protein A-kinase anchoring protein 1 (AKAP1) as a critical regulator of RGC resilience in glaucoma. AKAP1 expression is reduced in glaucomatous retinas and correlates with disrupted mitochondrial dynamics, oxidative stress, synaptic impairment, and visual decline. AAV2-mediated restoration of AKAP1 preserves RGC survival and visual function in two independent experimental glaucoma models. These data suggest that retinal AKAP1 promotes mitochondrial fusion, cristae integrity, and bioenergetic capacity in the inner retina and in stressed cultured RGCs, and is accompanied by increased mitochondrial content in presynaptic terminals of the inner plexiform layer. Retinal AKAP1 is further associated with higher PKA abundance, normalized CaMKII and synapsin phosphorylation, preserved synaptophysin, and lower complement C1q and glial activation markers; these associations do not, by themselves, establish causality. These findings identify AKAP1 as a candidate regulator of mitochondrial and synaptic homeostasis and highlight AAV2-AKAP1 gene therapy as a promising neuroprotective strategy for vision preservation in glaucoma.

etudes.titre: The German National Cohort: Ophthalmic Assessment, Baseline Profile, and Potential for Artificial Intelligence-Based Eye Research.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Artificial Intelligence »
etudes.resume:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the ophthalmic examination protocol within the German National Cohort (NAKO)/NAKO Gesundheitsstudie, to report the baseline profile of participants undergoing ophthalmic assessment, and to illustrate the potential as a population-based resource for artificial intelligence (AI) research in eye health.
DESIGN: Baseline analysis of ophthalmic data within the nationwide, population-based multicenter prospective NAKO study.
PARTICIPANTS: Forty-eight thousand four hundred and sixty adults in the ophthalmic level 2 module of 205 053 adults enrolled in NAKO, aged 19-74 years, with a mean age 48.9 ± 12.5 years, and 52.7% were male.
METHODS: All participants underwent standardized biomedical examinations and detailed questionnaire-based data collection, including nondilated color fundus imaging, visual acuity testing, and a brief ocular history. Ocular health was summarized using descriptive statistics. Fundus image quality and morphological features (e.g., cup-to-disc ratio and arteriolar-to-venular ratio) were assessed using open-source deep learning models. Standard deep learning architectures were trained on the fundus images to predict age, sex, and blood pressure.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Percentage of fundus images graded as good quality; mean absolute error (MAE) for age and blood pressure prediction; accuracy for sex prediction.
RESULTS: The analysis includes 48 460 participants who completed the ophthalmic baseline examination of NAKO. Mean visual acuity (logarithm of the minimum angle of resolution) was 0.01 ± 0.20 (left eye, mean ± standard deviation) and 0.03 ± 0.21 (right eye). Self-reported ocular disease prevalence was 4.2% for cataract, 2.0% for glaucoma, and 0.9% for macular degeneration; 68.2% of fundus images were classified as gradable using 4 deep learning-based quality grading models. Morphological features showed systematic differences across age groups. Standard deep learning architectures showed comparative performance to the state-of-the-art for age, sex, and blood pressure prediction (2.96 MAE for age prediction, 0.84 accuracy for sex prediction, and 10.78 and 6.97 MAE for systolic and diastolic blood pressure prediction).
CONCLUSIONS: The German National Cohort provides a large-scale, nationwide population-based resource with visual acuity measurements and systemic health indicators, as well as color fundus images in about 50 000 NAKO participants. These data lay the groundwork for studying eye health in the general adult population in Germany and can serve as a strong foundation for developing and validating AI tools in eye health research.
FINANCIAL DISCLOSURES: Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found in the Footnotes and Disclosures at the end of this article.

etudes.titre: Factors Associated With Hyperopic Shift After Phacoemulsification Combined With Intraocular Lens Implantation in Patients With Primary Angle-Closure Glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
AIM: To investigate the factors associated with hyperopic shift (HS) after phacoemulsification (PE) combined with intraocular lens (IOL) implantation in patients with primary angle-closure glaucoma (PACG).
METHODS: A total of 167 eyes with PACG that underwent PE+IOL were retrospectively included. Postoperative refractive prediction error (RPE) was calculated as the actual postoperative spherical equivalent minus the Barrett-predicted postoperative spherical equivalent. HS (RPE >+0.50 D) was the primary outcome. Group comparisons and univariable logistic regression were performed, followed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses of selected variables and multivariable logistic regression to identify independent factors.
RESULTS: Postoperative HS occurred in 54 eyes (32.3%). ROC curve analysis showed that axial length/corneal radius (AL/CR) ratio, anterior chamber depth (ACD), and white-to-white distance (WTW) showed moderate discriminative ability for postoperative HS, with areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.779, 0.764, and 0.730, respectively. Multivariable logistic regression analysis showed that higher relative lens position (RLP), AL/CR, and WTW were associated with a lower likelihood of postoperative HS, whereas capsular tension ring (CTR) implantation was associated with a higher likelihood of postoperative HS.
CONCLUSIONS: Lower RLP, AL/CR, and WTW values and CTR implantation were independently associated with postoperative HS. ROC analyses showed that AL/CR, ACD, and WTW had discriminative ability for HS.

etudes.titre: Effects of Aging and Early-Onset Menopause on Intraocular Pressure and Aqueous Humor Conventional Outflow Facility.
etudes.raison_rubrique: étiquette : stade préclinique (indexation PubMed)
etudes.resume: Biomechanical parameters play a crucial role in glaucoma development, the world-leading cause of irreversible blindness. Although age is known to affect the tissues' biomechanical properties, early-onset menopause has recently been associated with the risk of developing glaucoma, and the effects of aging relative to early-onset menopause on eyes' biomechanical parameters remain underexplored. This work's goals were to study the effects of aging and early-onset menopause on intraocular pressure (IOP), aqueous humor outflow facility, and ocular compliance. Female Brown Norway rats underwent Sham or surgical menopause (ovariectomy; OVX) at 3-4 months of age and were split into young (5-6 months) or middle-aged groups (9-10 months). We monitored IOP until the established aging time points and performed ex vivo biomechanical measurements via the iPerfusion system. IOP was higher for the middle-aged Sham and OVX animals by 25% and 35%, respectively (p < 0.001), when compared to their respective initial IOPs. Furthermore, middle-aged OVX animals had an 11% higher IOP compared to Sham animals (p = 0.005), and a 20% lower outflow facility (p = 0.031). Ocular compliance decreased with age in the Sham (24.9%, p = 0.011) and OVX (24.5%, p = 0.005) cohorts and by 24.1% independent of cohort (p = 0.0001). Elucidating the effects of age and early-onset menopause on biomechanical parameters that contribute to glaucoma pathology is necessary to move the field forward and help preserve the eyesight of millions of patients.

etudes.titre: Emerging microfluidic diagnostic systems for anterior segment diseases: a systematic review.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « diagnostic »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To evaluate emerging microfluidic diagnostic systems for anterior segment ocular diseases, emphasizing translational diagnostic relevance, clinical innovation, and current limitations.
METHODS: This systematic review followed the PRISMA guidelines. A comprehensive PubMed search was conducted for studies assessing microfluidic diagnostic systems applied to anterior segment diseases, including ectatic corneal disorders, dry eye and tear-film abnormalities, infectious keratitis, and glaucoma, up to September 09, 2025. Methodological quality was assessed using the Standards for Reporting of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies (STARD) framework.
RESULTS: The literature search identified 228 publications, of which 11 studies met inclusion criteria after screening and quality assessment. In ectatic corneal diseases, cornea-on-a-chip models reproduced multilayer corneal architecture under dynamic conditions, enabling quantitative assessment of wound healing, barrier function, and biomechanical responses. For dry eye and tear-film disorders, paper-based and wearable microfluidic platforms enabled objective microliter-scale tear analysis, with electrochemical sensing demonstrating strong correlation with conventional measurement methods (R² ≥0.99) and reduced analytical costs. In infectious keratitis, integrated microfluidic real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) systems achieved rapid multiplex pathogen detection with markedly shortened diagnostic times compared with culture methods. In glaucoma, implantable and wearable microfluidic sensors enabled continuous intraocular pressure monitoring with detection limits near 1 mm Hg and strong agreement with reference methods (R²>0.99), although some systems required individual calibration (R²≈0.78).
CONCLUSIONS: Microfluidic technologies provide a rapid, low-cost, and minimally invasive approach for real-time physiological assessment in anterior segment diagnostics and represent a promising strategy for earlier detection and more personalized, evidence-based ophthalmic care.
etudes.revue: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie

etudes.titre: Progress in the Synthesis of Evidence in Glaucoma: What We Know and the Gaps that Remain.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: Glaucoma is one of the leading causes of blindness worldwide, necessitating evidence-informed interventions and strategies to improve the quality of life of affected individuals. In this review, we examined progress in evidence over the past decade and discussed its implications and the ways forward for delivery of glaucoma care globally, embedded within a rapid evidence and gap-mapping exercise of systematic reviews and/or meta-analyses published between 2015 and 2025.
METHODS: Using a predefined conceptual framework, ten domains were identified as relevant to evidence synthesis in glaucoma care. Within each domain, we assessed areas of strength and identified remaining evidence gaps. Findings were synthesised narratively and recommendations provided to inform future research priorities and advancement in glaucoma care.
RECENT FINDINGS: Across the systematic reviews published over the past decade, the majority focused on risk factors (15.6%), genetic factors (12.4%) and the effectiveness of various treatment modalities (44.4%). In the absence of a coordinated global approach, substantial duplication of effort across review groups was observed. In addition, several critical gaps remain in the evidence base, particularly regarding the cost-effectiveness of the interventions, improving equitable access to care and the availability of context-specific evidence for low- and middle-income countries. Improved rigour in the evidence from primary studies should be a key priority for future research. A substantial gap exists in the glaucoma care evidence base that limits its utility for informing clinical guidelines and policy development. Systematic reviewers should have a comprehensive understanding of the existing evidence landscape in glaucoma care prior to conceptualising and designing review projects. Strengthening the methodological quality of both systematic reviews and the underlying primary studies is essential to support the development of robust clinical guidelines and effective global policies in glaucoma care.
etudes.revue: Ophthalmic & physiological optics : the journal of the British College of Ophthalmic Opticians (Optometrists)

etudes.titre: Microneedle-based drug delivery for inflammatory and immune-mediated ocular diseases: current applications and future perspectives.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « drug »

labos.nom: National Natural Science Foundation of China
Natural Science Foundation of Tianjin City
Tianjin Municipal Science and Technology Program

etudes.resume: Inflammatory and immune-mediated ocular diseases encompass a spectrum of conditions that arise from dysregulated immune-inflammatory responses marked by a chronic clinical course, a propensity for relapse, and a tendency to cause significant ocular tissue damage, which can lead to profound impairment of visual function. Dysregulation of the balance between immune cell subpopulations is central to the pathogenesis of many of these diseases. At present, non-specific treatments such as glucocorticoids and immunosuppressants form the cornerstone of therapy for inflammatory and immune-mediated ocular diseases. However, these treatments often suffer from poor bioavailability and targeting, cumbersome or invasive administration methods, and are associated with side effects such as increased intraocular pressure (IOP), cataracts, or glaucoma with frequent administration. These limitations underscore the urgent need for alternative drug delivery methods. Microneedles have emerged as an innovative approach to ocular drug delivery, offering distinct advantages over traditional eye drops and intravitreal injections. They enhance drug penetration and targeting, provide sustained release, and may reduce unnecessary drug exposure, thus holding great promise for the treatment of inflammatory and immune-mediated ocular diseases. This review aims to shed light on the unique benefits and efficacy of microneedles as drug-delivery systems for inflammatory and immune-mediated ocular diseases, with particular attention to noninfectious uveitis, corneal inflammatory disorders, inflammation-associated corneal neovascularization, and allergic conjunctivitis. It also discusses ocular safety and toxicity, manufacturing and standardization, regulatory challenges, and future prospects of microneedle applications, providing a comprehensive overview of their potential for ocular drug delivery.

etudes.titre: Directional OCT Assessment of Henle's Fiber Layer in Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « OCT »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of Henle's fiber layer (HFL) in eyes with mild to moderate primary open-angle glaucoma and to compare its performance with established optical coherence tomography (OCT) parameters, including the retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) and ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GC-IPL).
DESIGN: Retrospective cross-sectional study.
PARTICIPANTS: Twenty-five eyes of 25 patients with mild to moderate primary open-angle glaucoma and 50 age- and sex-matched healthy control eyes.
METHODS: Spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) was used to obtain macular and peripapillary measurements. HFL was visualized with directional OCT and quantified using ImageJ within a standardized 6,000-μm horizontal region centered on the fovea. One eye from each participant was included in the analysis to avoid inter-eye correlation. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to evaluate diagnostic accuracy.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: HFL area and its ability to distinguish glaucomatous eyes from healthy controls in comparison with RNFL and GC-IPL measurements.
RESULTS: HFL area was significantly smaller in glaucomatous eyes than in healthy controls (p < 0.001). ROC analysis showed excellent diagnostic accuracy for HFL (AUC, 0.990; 95% confidence interval, 0.974-1.000). HFL showed higher diagnostic performance than average RNFL and GC-IPL in DeLong analysis. All GC-IPL parameters and selected RNFL quadrants were significantly thinner in the glaucoma group (all p < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: HFL was significantly reduced in eyes with primary open-angle glaucoma and showed high diagnostic accuracy. HFL assessment may provide complementary information about retinal structural changes in glaucoma. Because of the relatively small sample size, these findings should be interpreted with caution.

etudes.titre: Prescriptive Trends of Hyaluronic Acid Eye Drops: Analysis of Korean Health Insurance Claims Database.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Eye Drops »; mot du titre : « Eye Drops »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: Hyaluronic acid (HA) eye drops are widely prescribed in South Korea, where they are available only by prescription and reimbursed by the National Health Insurance Service, yet recent evidence on prescribing patterns is limited. This study described HA eye drop prescription trends using National Health Insurance claims data from 2017 to 2021.
METHODS: This retrospective descriptive study used serial annual cross-sectional claims data from a proportionally stratified 8.5% sample of HA eye drop users, extrapolated to national estimates. Prescriptions were analyzed by demographics, formulation, and annual prescription duration. Annual percentage changes (APCs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using log-linear regression, confirmed by the exact Mann-Kendall trend test.
RESULTS: The number of patients increased from 7,434,447 in 2017 to 7,929,058 in 2021 (+6.7%; APC 1.10%, 95% CI -2.26 to 4.59), and prescriptions by 6.3% (APC 1.06%, 95% CI -2.01 to 4.22); neither trend was significant. Total prescription quantity increased 75.4%, to 44,885,574 standardized units (APC 15.24%, 95% CI 9.09 to 21.73). Multi-dose quantity declined (APC -3.35%, 95% CI -4.78 to -1.90) while unit-dose quantity increased by 162% (APC 27.54%, 95% CI 16.76 to 39.30). Patients with cumulative annual supply exceeding 180 day-equivalents increased from 12.9% to 24.2%, accounting for 62.8% of total quantity in 2021. Mean annual quantity per patient increased by 64.4% (3.44 to 5.66 units). These long-term users had higher recorded prevalences of retinal and choroidal disease (18.8% versus 8.5%) and glaucoma (12.5% versus 5.1%) as the principal diagnosis than short-term users.
CONCLUSIONS: The number of patients receiving HA eye drops increased without significant trend, whereas total prescription quantity rose by three-quarters, with increased supply per patient, marked shift toward unit-dose formulations, and growth concentrated among long-term users. These findings illustrate recent prescribing patterns of HA eye drops in South Korea and indicate that patient counts alone understate HA eye drop utilization growth.

etudes.titre: Application of nanozyme-based drug delivery systems in the treatment of ROS-related ophthalmic diseases.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « drug »

labos.nom: Natural Science Foundation of Shandong Province
Weifang University of Science and Technology

etudes.resume: ROS-related ophthalmic diseases span the ocular surface as well as the anterior and posterior segments of the eye. Dry eye disease (DED), glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy (DR) and age-related macular degeneration (AMD) have distinct anatomical targets but share common pathophysiological features, including oxidative stress, inflammation, vascular dysfunction, epithelial injury or neurodegeneration. Conventional ocular drug delivery and therapeutic modalities are hindered by severe limitations, including low bioavailability in the posterior segment of the eye and the requirement for frequent invasive administration. Nanozymes, an emerging class of therapeutic agents that integrate the properties of nanomaterials with natural enzyme-like catalytic activity, can efficiently scavenge excess reactive oxygen species (ROS) in focal lesions, modulate inflammatory factors, and remodel the pathological microenvironment, thereby providing a novel approach to the treatment of ROS-related ophthalmic diseases. This review systematically elucidates the core characteristics and therapeutic mechanisms of four major categories of nanozymes, namely metal-based, metal oxide-based, carbon-based, and composite nanozymes. To overcome physiological barriers in ocular drug delivery, such as the cornea and the blood-retinal barrier (BRB), we discuss active targeted delivery strategies based on mucin-binding retention, biomimetic cell membrane coating, and molecular ligand-mediated targeting. Furthermore, we summarize the development of intelligent and controlled-release systems in response to specific pathological microenvironments, such as ROS, pH values, and others. Additionally, this review details the latest cutting-edge applications and therapeutic efficacies of nanozymes in specific ophthalmic diseases, including AMD, DR, dry eye disease, and glaucoma. Finally, we highlight the challenges of long-term biosafety evaluation in the bench-to-bedside clinical translation of nanozymes and provide perspectives on future research directions for developing multi-stimuli-responsive synergistic nanodelivery systems.

etudes.titre: One-Year Outcomes of Green Laser Endoscopic Cyclophotocoagulation and Factors Associated with Surgical Failure: A Retrospective Observational Study.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Cyclophotocoagulation »; mot du titre : « Surgical »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: We evaluated the 1-year outcomes of green laser endoscopic cyclophotocoagulation (ECP), a newly developed procedure approved in Japan.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 29 eyes of 26 patients who underwent green laser ECP. Intraocular pressure (IOP), glaucoma medication burden, and laser flare were evaluated preoperatively and at 1, 3, 6, 9, and 12 months postoperatively. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis was used to estimate the 12-month success rate. Surgical success was defined as meeting all of the following criteria: IOP ≤21 mmHg, a ≥20% reduction from baseline, and no additional glaucoma surgery. Univariate and multivariable Cox proportional hazards analyses were performed to evaluate factors associated with surgical failure.
RESULTS: The mean IOP decreased from 23.4 ± 8.5 mmHg preoperatively to 17.4 ± 6.9, 16.9 ± 5.2, and 17.5 ± 7.3 mmHg at 1, 3, and 6 months postoperatively, respectively, with significant reductions maintained through 6 months (p < 0.01). However, IOP increased to 21.1 ± 7.9 and 22.3 ± 11.8 mmHg at 9 and 12 months, respectively, with no significant differences from baseline. The glaucoma medication score decreased significantly through 3 months postoperatively (p = 0.02) but returned to baseline levels thereafter. Laser flare increased significantly through 1 month postoperatively (p < 0.01) and decreased numerically through 3 months. The 12-month estimated success rate was 0.36. In multivariable Cox analysis, higher preoperative IOP was significantly associated with a greater risk of surgical failure (HR, 1.10; 95% CI, 1.05-1.15; p < 0.001), whereas age and postoperative laser flare were not significantly associated with failure.
CONCLUSION: Green laser ECP significantly lowered IOP through 6 months postoperatively; however, the estimated 12-month surgical success rate was 36%. Optimization of laser parameters and treatment strategies may be needed to improve long-term outcomes.

etudes.titre: Long-Term Inhaled Corticosteroid Use and the Risk of Open-Angle Glaucoma in Patients with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: The question of whether inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) increase the risk of open-angle glaucoma (OAG) has produced conflicting data on short-term effects, but no study has evaluated their long-term effects. We assessed whether long-term cumulative ICS use is associated with an increased risk of incident OAG among patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).
PATIENTS AND METHODS: The United Kingdom Clinical Practice Research Datalink was used to form a cohort of patients with COPD, aged 40 years or more, who initiated an inhaled maintenance treatment, between September 2013 and March 2021. Subjects were followed until the occurrence of the first OAG diagnosis. Using a nested case-control design, each OAG case was matched with up to 100 concurrently glaucoma-free controls using risk-set sampling. Conditional logistic regression was used to compute the adjusted odds ratio of incident OAG associated with cumulative ICS exposure, as an estimate of the hazard ratio (HR) and its 95% confidence interval (CI).
RESULTS: The COPD cohort included 84,564 subjects, with 732 developing OAG (incidence rate 2.64 per 1000 person-years) and 56% having used an ICS since cohort entry. The adjusted HR of OAG associated with any ICS use since cohort entry, compared with non-use, was 1.14 (95% CI, 0.94-1.38). The HR was 1.11 (95% CI, 0.83-1.48) for total cumulative dose ≥365 mg and 1.23 (95% CI, 0.90-1.68) for over 3 years since ICS initiation.
CONCLUSION: This large cohort study did not observe a statistically significant increase in the risk of OAG with ICS use, including long-term use and higher cumulative doses, among patients with COPD.
etudes.revue: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease

etudes.titre: A New Frontier: Partial Cellular Reprogramming in Plastic Surgery.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Surgery »
etudes.resume: Partial cellular reprogramming employs Yamanaka factors to shift aging cells toward a younger epigenetic state without compromising cellular identity. Over two decades, this Nobel Prize winning breakthrough has advanced from the bench to a first in-human trial in 2026 for optic neuropathy and glaucoma. Here, we outline the foundation of partial cellular reprogramming and delineate its intersection with our field. Defined by innovation, plastic surgery can shape how partial reprogramming is applied in what may prove to be a transformative chapter for our specialty.

etudes.titre: Mastering the eye: Clinical paradigm shifts from optical restoration to genomic correction.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « genomic »

labos.nom: National Natural Science Foundation of China

etudes.resume: Historically, the main operation for cataract was couching, and the interior of the living eye could not be examined until Hermann von Helmholtz introduced the ophthalmoscope in 1851. Since the mid-twentieth century, seven advances have reshaped ophthalmic care. Harold Ridley implanted the first intraocular lens in 1949, and the ophthalmologist Charles Kelman and the engineer Anton Banko developed phacoemulsification, reported in 1967. Robert Machemer performed the first pars plana vitrectomy in 1970, while David Huang and colleagues described optical coherence tomography in 1991. Endothelial keratoplasty, developed by Gerrit Melles and others between 1998 and 2006, replaced only the failing corneal endothelium instead of the full thickness of the cornea. Anti-VEGF therapy followed the purification of VEGF by Napoleone Ferrara and colleagues in 1989 and the approval of ranibizumab in 2006. Minimally invasive glaucoma surgery has spread since 2012, and in 2017 voretigene neparvovec became the first approved gene therapy for an inherited retinal disease. Five of these advances enabled a new type of intervention, whereas endothelial keratoplasty and minimally invasive glaucoma surgery made existing operations safer. For each advance we summarize the best available evidence of benefit to patients and its certainty, which is high for some, such as anti-VEGF therapy, and low for others, such as the effect of imaging on patient outcomes. Each advance created new burdens, from chronic injections to dependence on donor tissue, and routine adoption depended on manufacturing, regulation, cost, reimbursement, and health-system capacity.
etudes.revue: Progress in retinal and eye research

etudes.titre: Trehalose-modulated poloxamer 407 thermosensitive hydrogel: sol-gel transition regulation and sustained low-dose pilocarpine nitrate delivery.
etudes.raison_rubrique: étiquette : produit suivi étudié (rôle suggéré, à vérifier)

labos.nom: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

etudes.resume: Traditional ophthalmic solutions and viscous gels are limited by insufficient precorneal residence time, inaccurate dosing administration, and inconvenient sterile filtration. Pilocarpine, originally a classic muscarinic acetylcholine receptor agonist for glaucoma management, has been recently repurposed for presbyopia treatment. However, its clinical application is greatly restricted by frequent severe ocular adverse reactions, including xerophthalmia and conjunctival hyperemia. Herein, trehalose was adopted to modify poloxamer 407 thermosensitive hydrogel, on the basis of its dual functions of tuning gel physicochemical properties and enhancing cellular desiccation resistance. The incorporation of trehalose lowered the critical gelation threshold concentration of poloxamer 407 without impairing the intrinsic physicochemical properties of the hydrogel. The optimized formulation exists as a low-viscosity aqueous solution (approximately 50 mPa·s) at ambient temperature, which allows convenient sterilization via 0.22 μm filtration, and rapidly undergoes in-situ sol-gel transition on the ocular surface to form isotonic hydrogel. This hydrogel protects loaded pilocarpine against hydrolytic degradation and improves corneal hydration.Both in vitro cell-based assays and in vivo rabbit ocular irritation tests confirmed that the formulation exhibited good ocular safety. Benefiting from excellent thermal stability and industrial processability, this delivery system exhibits promising translational prospects and lays a solid foundation for follow-up clinical research on presbyopia treatment.

etudes.titre: Cost-effectiveness of iStent-based trabecular micro-bypass stenting combined with cataract surgery in mild-to-moderate open-angle glaucoma: a systematic review of analytic perspectives and time horizons.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « stenting »; mot du titre : « surgery »
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: Glaucoma remains a major cause of irreversible blindness and was estimated to affect 64.3 million people worldwide in 2013. Despite growing clinical use of minimally invasive glaucoma surgery (MIGS), reimbursement and uptake remain constrained by uncertainty about long-term cost-effectiveness. iStent-based trabecular micro-bypass implantation is commonly performed at the time of cataract surgery in patients with mild-to-moderate open-angle glaucoma, yet its economic value has not been synthesised systematically across healthcare systems.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the cost-effectiveness of iStent trabecular micro-bypass implantation performed concurrently with cataract surgery for mild-to-moderate open-angle glaucoma, and to examine how the analytic perspective and time horizon adopted in the underlying models relate to the decision the evidence is intended to inform.
METHODS: A systematic review was performed of published model-based economic evaluations. Eligible studies used a formal decision-analytic model, reported quality-adjusted life years (QALYs), and evaluated an iStent device implanted concurrently with cataract surgery. PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library and Web of Science were searched on 27 July 2026 without date, language or publication-type restriction. Incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs), QALYs, analytic perspectives, time horizons, discount rates and probabilistic results were extracted with a page reference for each value. Reporting was appraised item-by-item against CHEERS 2022. Findings were synthesised narratively; no quantitative pooling was attempted. Reporting followed PRISMA 2020.
RESULTS: Of 418 records identified and 293 after de-duplication, eight economic evaluations from eight countries met the eligibility criteria. All eight compared the device added to cataract surgery against cataract surgery alone; seven used a cohort Markov model and one an individual-patient microsimulation. Six adopted a payer or health-system perspective and two a societal perspective; five used a lifetime horizon, one 35 years and two 15 years. No evaluation adopted a provider perspective or a base-case horizon shorter than 15 years. All eight reported a favourable base-case result in the mild-to-moderate target population: reported ratios included €1,154 per QALY in France, €12,676 in Spain, €13,037 in Italy, €10,955 to €15,673 in Germany, JPY 1,430,647 in Japan and A$2,430 in Australia, together with two instances of dominance. Six of the eight were funded by the device manufacturer. Incremental QALY gains were small throughout, between approximately 0.005 and 0.17, so the reported ratios are highly sensitive to small changes in the denominator. One study did not report a price year and for a second it could not be verified; no study reported a pre-specified health economic analysis plan, and none modelled long-term structural change in medication prices, prescribing practice or competing alternatives.
CONCLUSIONS: The included peer-reviewed models generally project that adding an iStent-family device to cataract surgery can be cost-effective over long horizons. That projection depends on sustained medication reduction, on extrapolated glaucoma progression and on local device and treatment costs. Direct evidence that the modelled long-term clinical benefit is realised in practice and offsets the acquisition cost remains limited: the evidence base is small, concentrated in industry-funded analyses of a single device family drawing largely on the same two-year pivotal trial, and built on incremental QALY gains close to zero. All included evaluations adopt a payer, health-system or societal perspective over 15 years or longer, and none addresses whether the marginal cost of adding a stent to an already-scheduled cataract procedure is justified within an annual operating budget. This is a gap in the included QALY-based cost-utility literature; the review was not designed to identify provider-perspective budget-impact analyses outside these eligibility criteria.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable. This study is a systematic review of published economicevaluations; no clinical trial registration was required. The review was not registeredprospectively in PROSPERO.
etudes.revue: Cost effectiveness and resource allocation : C/E

etudes.titre: Interpretable fundus image-based glaucoma classification using aCDR-guided vascular tortuosity analysis.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique

labos.nom: National Natural Science Foundation of China
Industry-Academia-Research Cooperation Project between Hebei-located Universities and Shijiazhuang City

etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to develop and evaluate an interpretable hierarchical auxiliary classification framework for glaucoma-related fundus image analysis, with emphasis on transparent classification rationale for cases with intermediate aCDR values.
METHODS: A MiT-B2-scSE U-Net was employed to jointly segment the optic disc and optic cup from fundus images, and the aCDR was calculated for initial image-level classification. Samples within predefined low- and high-aCDR ranges were directly classified, whereas samples in the intermediate-aCDR group underwent further analysis using peripapillary vessel segmentation and skeleton-based tortuosity quantification. To improve the reliability of vascular morphology assessment, a distance-aware topology-constrained loss function (DATCL) was introduced in the vessel segmentation stage to improve the segmentation accuracy of peripapillary vessels and improve the reliability of subsequent calculations.
RESULTS: On the current REFUGE-based test set, the proposed MiT-B2-scSE U-Net achieved a mean Dice similarity coefficient (Dice) of 0.9254 and a mean Intersection over Union (IoU) of 0.8694 for joint optic cup-disc segmentation. For image-level glaucoma classification, the hierarchical aCDR-plus-vessel strategy achieved an accuracy of 91.25%, compared with 85.0% for the aCDR-only baseline and 66.25% for the vessel-only strategy.
CONCLUSION: The proposed framework suggests that combining optic cup-disc morphology with local vascular tortuosity may provide complementary information for interpretable glaucoma classification in fundus images with intermediate aCDR values. It provides a methodological avenue for deep learning-assisted glaucoma screening.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13755-026-00484-5.

etudes.titre: Hydrus microstent combined with cataract surgery or used alone: cost-utility analysis for UK.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « microstent »; mot du titre : « surgery »
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: Minimally invasive glaucoma surgery (MIGS) has the potential to become standard of care for patients with primary open angle glaucoma (POAG), whether combined with cataract surgery (CS) or as a standalone procedure. This study provides evidence of cost-effectiveness for Hydrus Microstent for both indications in UK healthcare settings.
METHODS: A cohort Markov model simulated the natural history of POAG to assess costs and quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) over a 15-year horizon, comparing Hydrus Microstent + CS with CS alone, and Hydrus Microstent to iStent standalone. Patient progression across glaucoma severity health states was modelled using a rate of progression (RoP) derived from 5-year visual field loss data in HORIZON trial (for mild to moderate POAG) and by trial-based annual number of medications from COMPARE trial (for moderate POAG), respectively. Conducted from the public healthcare payer perspective, model inputs were derived from UK publicly available sources and/or publications. Both deterministic and probabilistic analyses (PA) were performed.
RESULTS: When compared with CS alone, Hydrus + CS was estimated to generate 0.334 more QALYs but £604 higher costs over the 15-year time horizon. When comparing Hydrus to iStent, Hydrus had £534 in projected savings and generated 0.068 more QALYs. The PA showed that the probability of Hydrus + CS being cost-effective compared to CS alone is 87.6%, and about 71.5% when compared to iStent. The results were consistent across scenario analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Hydrus implantation is a cost-effective strategy both in combination with CS (for mild-to-moderate POAG) and as a standalone procedure (for moderate POAG) in UK healthcare settings.

etudes.titre: Association between rheumatic diseases and glaucoma risk: a systematic review and meta-analysis of 5.7 million individuals.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: Some studies suggest that rheumatic diseases (RD) may be associated with the development of glaucoma; however, findings remain inconsistent. We therefore conducted a meta-analysis to estimate the incidence of glaucoma and assess its risk among patients with RD, to inform evidence-based diagnostic decision-making.
METHODS: Following a pre-registered PROSPERO protocol (CRD42024604067), we performed a systematic search of PubMed, the Cochrane Library, and Embase. Pooled incidence estimates, odds ratios (ORs), and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using RevMan 5.4 and STATA 15.0.
RESULTS: Eighteen studies comprising 5,766,143 participants were included. RD was significantly associated with glaucoma. The pooled incidence of glaucoma among patients with RD was 4% (rate = 0.04; 95% CI, 0.03-0.06; P < 0.001). By study design, incidence/prevalence estimates were 3% in cohort studies, 9% in case-control studies, and 8% in cross-sectional studies. Compared with the general population, individuals with RD have a 66% higher risk of developing glaucoma (OR = 1.66; 95% CI, 1.15-2.40; P = 0.007).
CONCLUSION: Both the incidence and risk of glaucoma are elevated in patients with RD. These findings highlight the importance of increased ophthalmologic surveillance in this population.

etudes.titre: Prospective, Multicenter, Single-Arm, Open-Label Study of the Safety and Effectiveness of the Gel Stent in Angle Closure Glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Stent »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the gel stent's intraocular pressure (IOP)-lowering safety and effectiveness in angle closure glaucoma (ACG).
METHODS: Prospective, multicenter, nonrandomized, 12-month, interventional study. Adults with ACG (iridotrabecular contact in ≥2 quadrants, glaucomatous optic disc damage, and visual field loss) and baseline IOP 20-35 mmHg received ab-interno gel stent implantation on Day 1. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients achieving ≥20% IOP reduction from baseline without IOP-lowering medication increase at Month 12.
RESULTS: Of 62 patients/eyes enrolled and implanted, 45 (72.6%) had a history of glaucoma procedures, 50 (80.6%) underwent ≥1 concomitant angle-widening procedure(s) (usually cataract surgery), and 59 (95.2%) completed the study. Baseline IOP was 24.0 mmHg on 2.3 IOP-lowering medications (mean). At Month 12, 80.5% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 68.4-88.8) of patients achieved the primary endpoint, with similar proportions in the presence (81.8%; 95% CI: 67.3-91.8) and absence (83.3%; 95% CI: 51.6-97.9) of concomitant angle-widening procedures. Month 12 mean changes from baseline in IOP and number of IOP-lowering medications were -8.9 mmHg (95% CI: -10.2 to -7.6) and -1.6 (95% CI: -1.9 to -1.2), respectively. Twenty-one eyes (33.9%) required needling. There were no surgical complications. Serious postoperative ocular adverse events occurred in 6 (9.7%) study eyes; all resolved without sequelae.
CONCLUSION: Gel stent implantation had an acceptable safety profile and effectively lowered IOP and the medication burden in ACG.
etudes.revue: Journal of ocular pharmacology and therapeutics : the official journal of the Association for Ocular Pharmacology and Therapeutics

etudes.titre: Psychological distress associated with glaucoma: potential predictors and contributing factors.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: Glaucoma is a chronic, progressive optic neuropathy and one of the leading causes of irreversible blindness worldwide. Beyond visual impairment, the disease can impose a considerable psychological burden. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between glaucoma and psychological distress, and to identify clinical and psychosocial predictors that may contribute to heightened risk, with the aim of informing management strategies to improve patients' quality of life.
METHODS: A cross-sectional quantitative study was conducted involving 107 glaucoma patients treated at the University Eye Clinic Cologne. Data were collected using a standardized questionnaire, including demographic and clinical variables as well as the validated Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9). Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, Spearman correlations, and multiple linear regression to identify predictors of psychological burden.
RESULTS: 25.23% of patients exhibited mild to severe depressive symptoms according to PHQ-9 scores. Significant predictors of higher psychological burden were increased disease preoccupation (β = 0.237, p = 0.007), stronger fear of blindness (β = 0.315, p < 0.001), and poorer self-rated general health status (β = -0.382, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: The findings demonstrate a strong link between glaucoma and psychological distress. These results highlight the need to consider psychosocial factors alongside intraocular pressure in glaucoma management. Interdisciplinary care involving ophthalmologists, psychologists, and nursing staff may improve patient outcomes and quality of life.
etudes.revue: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie

etudes.titre: Predictive baseline thresholds for successful dual blade goniotomy combined with phacoemulsification in glaucoma patients.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « goniotomy »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To define preoperative thresholds of intraocular pressure (IOP) and the number of IOP-lowering eye drops that may predict surgical success following Kahook Dual Blade goniotomy combined with phacoemulsification (Phaco-KDB) in patients with glaucoma and cataract.
METHODS: This retrospective study analysed 307 eyes of 307 patients undergoing Phaco-KDB. Data on demographics, glaucoma type, IOP, number of IOP-lowering medications and complications were collected over 18 months of follow-up. Complete success was defined as IOP ≤ 21, 18, 15 or 12 mmHg without medications; qualified success allowed for ongoing topical IOP-lowering therapy. Logistic regression models were used to determine predictive thresholds.
RESULTS: Mean baseline IOP was 18.6 ± 5.2 mmHg and decreased to 15.0 ± 4.4 mmHg at 18 months. The mean number of IOP-lowering medications was reduced from 2.2 ± 1.1 to 1.7 ± 1.4. For qualified success, the identified preoperative IOP thresholds were 27.2 mmHg for achieving ≤ 21 mmHg (AUC = 0.900, p < 0.001), 25.1 mmHg for ≤ 18 mmHg (AUC = 0.8604, p < 0.001), 19.8 mmHg for ≤ 15 mmHg (AUC = 0.7752, p < 0.001), and 13.5 mmHg for ≤ 12 mmHg (AUC = 0.7772, p = 0.0011). For complete success, the threshold IOP values were 20.6 mmHg for ≤ 21 mmHg (AUC = 0.7893, p < 0.001), 18.1 mmHg for ≤ 18 mmHg (AUC = 0.7365, p < 0.001), and 15.0 mmHg for ≤ 15 mmHg (AUC = 0.5890, p = 0.0109). No significant association was found between the number of preoperative medications and surgical outcome.
CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative IOP is a significant predictor of Phaco-KDB success. Our findings suggest that Phaco-KDB primarily stabilizes IOP at preoperative levels while reducing the need for IOP-lowering therapy, rather than achieving substantial additional IOP reduction.

etudes.titre: Safety and Efficacy of Microhook Ab Interno Trabeculotomy Combined with Cataract Surgery in Older Patients with Glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Trabeculotomy »; mot du titre : « Surgery »
etudes.resume:
INTRODUCTION: Evidence regarding minimally invasive glaucoma surgery in very old patients remains limited, making surgical decision-making challenging in this population. We investigated age-related differences in the safety and efficacy of microhook ab interno trabeculotomy combined with cataract surgery (combined µLOT).
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study in Japan included 67 consecutive glaucomatous eyes of 67 patients who underwent combined µLOT and were followed for at least 6 months. The cohort comprised 27 male and 40 female patients. Patients were divided by median age into younger (< 76 years, n = 32) and older (≥ 76 years, n = 35) groups. Qualified success was defined irrespective of postoperative glaucoma medication use and without the need for additional glaucoma surgery, and was evaluated using three intraocular pressure (IOP) criteria: criterion A, 6 ≤ IOP ≤ 18 mmHg; criterion B, 6 ≤ IOP ≤ 15 mmHg; and criterion C, 6 ≤ IOP ≤ 13 mmHg.
RESULTS: The mean age of the older group was 82.5 years. At 6 months, qualified success probabilities were 94.0%, 82.1%, and 60.0% for criteria A, B, and C, respectively. Although the older group had higher qualified success under criterion C (71.4% vs. 46.9%; nominal P = 0.04) and lower IOP from week 2 to month 6, age was not independently associated with surgical failure in multivariable Cox analyses. Higher preoperative IOP, hypertension, and antithrombotic therapy showed exploratory associations with failure. Postoperative hyphema, transient IOP elevation, corneal endothelial cell loss, and systemic complications were not increased in the older group.
CONCLUSION: Combined µLOT provided favorable short-term IOP control without an increased complication burden in older patients, although baseline medication burden may have confounded the age-group comparison. These real-world findings provide clinically relevant evidence for surgical decision-making in very old patients and may be informative for other aging societies.

etudes.titre: Role of Chromatin-Associated RNAs in Eye Physiology and Pathology.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Noncoding RNAs, including long noncoding RNAs, enhancer RNAs, circular RNAs, and small nuclear and nucleolar RNAs, represent a major, yet still largely uncharacterized, regulatory layer in the eye. A subset of these molecules, chromatin-associated RNAs (caRNAs), physically interacts with DNA and nuclear protein complexes to influence genome organization, transcriptional output, and stress responses. Although caRNAs have emerged as essential regulators of chromatin topology and gene expression in diverse tissues, their identity, dynamics, and mechanisms in the retina and retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) remain elusive. Recent high-resolution genomic studies, disease transcriptomes, and mechanistic studies implicate dysregulated caRNAs in age-related macular degeneration, glaucoma, and diabetic retinopathy, yet causal chromatin-level functions have rarely been demonstrated. In this review, we summarize current understanding of ncRNA-mediated regulation in vision, highlight emerging evidence for caRNA involvement in retinal development, photoreceptor and RPE specialization, and disease-associated epigenetic remodeling, and outline major mechanistic gaps that must be addressed. We then survey the rapidly expanding CRISPR toolbox, including base and prime editors, CRISPRi/a, Cas13 knockdown and editing platforms, and RNA-recruitment and spatial repositioning systems, that now enable targeted perturbation of both caRNA genomic loci and transcripts. These technologies provide the first practical route to move beyond correlative RNA-chromatin maps toward the mechanistic dissection of how caRNAs organize regulatory hubs, modulate enhancer-promoter communication, and shape long-range genome interactions in the eye. As the catalog of pathogenic noncoding variants grows, the ability to decode and engineer caRNA networks will be central to future precision therapeutic strategies for ocular disorders.

etudes.titre: Involvement of ocular angle pigmentation on the effect of 2% topical ganciclovir treatment in patients with cytomegalovirus anterior uveitis.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique

labos.nom: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science

etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: Topical ganciclovir (GCV) reduces intraocular pressure (IOP) in patients with cytomegalovirus (CMV) anterior uveitis. Because increased angle pigmentation may contribute to aqueous outflow resistance, we investigated the relationship between angle pigmentation and the IOP-lowering effects of topical GCV.
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective study.
METHODS: We reviewed the medical records of 31 eyes of 31 patients diagnosed with CMV anterior uveitis using aqueous humor PCR and treated with 2% topical GCV at the University of Tokyo Hospital. The best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), IOP, topical steroids, and glaucoma medication scores were evaluated at baseline, 1, 4, 12, and 24 weeks after GCV initiation. Pre-treatment angle pigmentation was graded and analyzed in relation to IOP. Survival analysis was performed, with failure defined as an IOP > 21 mmHg, or the need for glaucoma surgery.
RESULTS: Topical GCV improved BCVA with gradual reductions in IOP, steroid use, and glaucoma medication. Angle pigmentation was lower in CMV-affected eyes than in fellow eyes in patients with a shorter disease duration. Higher angle pigmentation was significantly correlated with a longer disease duration (ρ = 0.51, p = 0.003). The greater-pigmentation group showed significantly less IOP reduction and lower survival rates than the less-pigmentation group.
CONCLUSION: Angle pigmentation was lower in the affected eyes than in the fellow eyes in patients with a shorter disease duration. In contrast, patients with greater angle pigmentation exhibited longer disease duration and a reduced IOP-lowering response to topical GCV treatment. Therefore, pre-treatment angle pigmentation evaluation may assist in predicting glaucoma outcomes.

etudes.titre: Incidence and Risk Factors of Recurrent Visual Field Progression in Glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Visual Field »
etudes.resume:
IMPORTANCE: A confirmed visual field progression event in glaucoma typically prompts intensification of intraocular pressure (IOP)-lowering therapy, yet the factors associated with recurrent progression after that first event remain poorly characterized.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the incidence of recurrent visual field progression after an initial Guided Progression Analysis (GPA) likely-progression event and the factors associated with a recurrent event.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study was conducted among patients receiving routine ophthalmic care between 1998 and 2025 at a single tertiary academic center (Bascom Palmer Ophthalmic Registry). Data were analyzed from February 2026 to August 2026.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcomes were the cumulative probability of recurrent visual field progression and hazard ratios (HRs) for factors associated with recurrence.
RESULTS: A total of 7457 eyes of 5086 patients with open-angle glaucoma or suspected glaucoma were included, with a mean (SD) follow-up of 12.4 (4.6) years. Mean (SD) patient age was 60.5 (13.1) years, and 4468 eyes (59.9%) were from female patients. By self-reported race and ethnicity, 203 eyes (2.7%) were from Asian patients, 1718 (23.0%) from Black patients, 1677 (22.5%) from Hispanic patients, and 5536 (74.2%) from White patients. A total of 1951 eyes (26.2%) developed initial GPA likely progression; 635 eyes had adequate follow-up after first progression and IOP data. Among those, 167 (26.3%) recurred. Kaplan-Meier cumulative recurrence was 13.8% at 3 years (95% CI, 11.6%-17.1%) and 43.5% at 10 years (95% CI, 35.8%-52.1%). In multivariable Cox analysis, faster mean deviation (MD) loss before first progression (HR, 1.73 per 1 decibel [dB]/y; 95% CI, 1.39-2.15), higher mean IOP after the first event (HR, 1.09 per 1 mm Hg; 95% CI, 1.05-1.13), less negative MD at first progression (HR, 1.08 per 1 dB; 95% CI, 1.04-1.12), and older age (HR, 1.11 per 5 years; 95% CI, 1.03-1.19) were independently associated with recurrence. Each 10% greater IOP reduction was associated with lower hazard (HR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.83-0.94). Among eyes with pre-event MD slopes faster than -1.0 dB/y, recurrence occurred in 42.7% of eyes vs 23.4% in slower-progressing eyes (difference, 19.3%; 95% CI, 8.8%-29.9%).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Findings from this cohort study suggest that recurrent visual field progression after a first GPA progression event is common; eyes at highest risk had faster pre-event visual field loss, less advanced damage at first progression, higher postevent IOP, and older age. These results may help target intensified monitoring and IOP lowering toward higher-risk eyes.

etudes.resume: Glaucomatous optic neuropathy (GON) is the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide, characterized by progressive retinal ganglion cell (RGC) loss. Current clinical treatment relies primarily on IOP-lowering drugs, but a subset of patients continues to experience progressive optic nerve damage. Adjuvant therapies such as antioxidants and calcium channel blockers have limited efficacy. Emerging neuroprotective strategies including NMDA receptor antagonists, neurotrophic factors, and gene therapy remain in preclinical or early-stage trials. This review systematically summarizes the mechanisms, clinical applications, and limitations of these three drug categories, with emphasis on emerging neuroprotective agents, aiming to guide future research directions.

etudes.titre: Fundus camera and artificial intelligence for diabetic retinopathy screening in a São Paulo shelter.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « artificial intelligence »; mot du titre : « screening »
etudes.resume:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to evaluate the applicability of a smartphone-based portable fundus camera for diabetic retinopathy screening in elderly residents of a specialized shelter in São Paulo, Brazil, considering image acquisition by non-ophthalmologist professionals and remote case classification.
METHODS: Prospective pilot interventional study at the Centro de Acolhida Especial para Idosos Morada São João. Thirty-eight participants (76 eyes) underwent retinal imaging using the Eyer® portable fundus camera (Phelcom Technologies, Brazil) by trained non-ophthalmologist professionals. Images were remotely evaluated by a retinal specialist and compared to the EyerMaps® artificial intelligence system.
RESULTS: Mean age was 71.6±7.0 years; 78.9% male. Fifteen participants (39.5%) had confirmed diabetes mellitus. The specialist identified abnormalities in 70 of 76 eyes (92.1%), most frequently glaucoma suspicion, media opacity suggestive of cataract, chorioretinal changes, and age-related macular degeneration signs; no diabetic retinopathy was identified. Against the specialist's assessment of any ocular abnormality as the reference standard, the artificial intelligence system classified 22 eyes as abnormal, yielding sensitivity 25.7% (95%CI 16.9-37.0), specificity 33.3% (95%CI 9.7-70.0), positive predictive value 81.8% (95%CI 61.5-92.7), negative predictive value 3.7% (95%CI 1.0-12.5), and overall accuracy 26.3% (95%CI 17.7-37.2).
CONCLUSION: The Eyer® device demonstrated operational feasibility for ocular screening by trained non-ophthalmologists. The high prevalence of media opacities and non-diabetic retinopathy conditions compromised artificial intelligence performance, highlighting the need for broader screening strategies in elderly and socially vulnerable populations.

etudes.titre: Novel Ab Externo Rescue Technique of a Dislocated Four-point Scleral-Fixated Intraocular Lens.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: The rescue of a dislocated scleral-sutured intraocular lens (IOL) remains surgically challenging. We report a novel, flapless, cornea-based ab externo technique for rescuing a dislocated scleral-fixated Akreos AO60 IOL.
CASE: A 59-year-old male with a history of remote left eye (OS) trauma complicated by glaucoma and retinal detachment status post repair, presented with decreased vision OS following acute blunt ocular trauma. The ocular examination revealed hand motion (LogMAR -2.70) vision and posterior dislocation of a previously scleral-fixated Akreos AO60 IOL. A core and peripheral vitrectomy were performed, and the IOL was relocated to the anterior chamber. Using corneal paracentesis and a 2.4mm main wound, each of the four-lens haptics was externalized and threaded with 8-0 GORE-TEX sutures. The distal suture followed by the proximal suture was passed into the anterior chamber and retrieved through the prior sclerotomies. The IOL was then reposited in the posterior chamber and sutured at sclerotomy sites for fixation. The best-corrected visual acuity improved from hand motion back to baseline of 20/70 (LogMAR 0.54) at follow-up, with no complications observed.
RESULTS: A dislocated Akreos AO60 four-haptic IOL was successfully rescued and re-fixated with stable centration with a novel ab externo approach. This technique provides an effective method with limited manipulation and small wounds.
CONCLUSION: The ab externo technique provides an approach for rescuing dislocated four-haptic lenses, such as the Akreos AO60.

etudes.titre: Association Between Systemic TNF-α Inhibitor Use and Risk of Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Inhibitor »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the association between systemic tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) inhibitor use and the long-term risk of primary open angle glaucoma (POAG), and to compare glaucoma risk among users of different TNF-α inhibitors.
DESIGN: Retrospective, multicenter clinical cohort study.
METHODS: This retrospective, multicenter cohort study compared patients ≥40 years with and without TNF-α inhibitor use (2006-2026) using data from aggregated, de-identified electronic health records across 70 U.S. health care organizations. Patients prescribed TNF-α inhibitors (adalimumab, infliximab, etanercept, certolizumab pegol, or golimumab) were propensity matched (1:1) to controls without TNF-α inhibitor exposure based on demographics and systemic indications for TNF-a. Patients with a history of uveitis and related sequelae were excluded. New POAG diagnosis, identified by ICD-10 codes within 10 years of follow-up, was assessed using Cox proportional hazards models.
RESULTS: Among 12,227 TNF-α inhibitor users and 1,354,651 controls, 11,915 matched pairs were analyzed (mean [SD] age 59 [10] years; 68% female). At 10 years, TNF-α inhibitor users were associated with a lower risk of POAG diagnosis compared to controls (2.0% vs. 3.3%; HR 0.70 [95% CI 0.59-0.82]; P<.001) In agent-specific analysis, adalimumab-users (n=4,962 per cohort) (HR 0.74 [0.57-0.96]) and infliximab users (n=2,134 per cohort; HR 0.68 [95% CI 0.47-0.97) were associated with a lower risk of POAG diagnosis compared to matched controls. No significant differences were observed in pairwise comparisons amongst TNF-α inhibitors.
CONCLUSIONS: Systemic TNF-α inhibitor use, particularly adalimumab and infliximab, was associated with a modest but significant reduction in long-term POAG risk. These findings support a potential role of TNF-α-mediated inflammation in glaucomatous neurodegeneration.

etudes.titre: Prognostic factors and visual outcomes in badminton-related ocular injuries: A retrospective study.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To evaluate a large cohort of eye patients from India for the epidemiology, clinical presentation, and visual outcomes of ocular injuries sustained while playing badminton.
METHODS: Medical records of patients presenting with badminton-related ocular injuries were reviewed to compare the predicted visual outcome with that stipulated by the Ocular Trauma Score (OTS). The patients' data on demographics, mode of injury, clinical evaluation, and treatment modalities were compiled, analysed and interpreted to contrast alongside OTS, the standardised prediction of visual outcomes after indexing the severity of eye injury.
RESULTS: A total of 486 patients were included. Blunt trauma from being hit by badminton shuttlecock was the most common mechanism, followed by racquet injury, and spectacle injury. Closed-globe injury was predominant (97.33%). None of the players were using protective eyewear. Visual prognosis was generally favourable in closed-globe injury (mean final BCVA 0.32 ± 0.56 logMAR) compared to open-globe injury (0.46 ± 0.68 logMAR). Significant predictors of visual outcome included presenting BCVA, early post-injury BCVA, cataract, secondary glaucoma, optic disc involvement, iridodialysis, and OTS. OTS categories 3-5 showed better visual outcomes than predicted by the original OTS model.
CONCLUSION: Closed-globe injury represented the most common injury in badminton-related ophthalmic trauma. Initial visual acuity, lens status, optic disc involvement, secondary glaucoma, eye surgery performed, OTS score and posterior segment injury were statistically significant in predicting final visual outcomes. Additionally, this study emphasizes how important it is to use protective glasses when playing badminton.

etudes.titre: Intraocular Pressure Following Phacoemulsification with Anterior Vitrectomy in the IRIS® Registry (Intelligent Research in Sight).
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To evaluate intraocular pressure (IOP) changes following phacoemulsification with concurrent anterior vitrectomy (AV) using the IRIS® Registry (Intelligent Research in Sight).
DESIGN: Retrospective clinical cohort study SUBJECTS: Eyes in the IRIS Registry that underwent stand-alone phacoemulsification with concurrent AV from 1/1/2013-9/30/2019.
METHODS: Daily mean IOP was compared to baseline IOP through postoperative day 90. An IOP spike was defined as IOP >30 mm Hg and an increase of >10 mm Hg from baseline IOP within the first postoperative week. A linear mixed-effects model was used to determine when the postoperative daily mean IOP stabilized; the final mean IOP was the average of all daily mean IOPs from that timepoint onward. A multivariable logistic regression analysis was used to identify independent risk factors and odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals for an IOP spike.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Postoperative daily mean IOP; incidence and OR of IOP spike RESULTS: Phacoemulsification with AV occurred in 1,811 eyes with a baseline median (interquartile range) IOP of 16.0 (14.0,18.0) mmHg. An IOP spike was observed in 164 (9.1%) eyes. After surgery, daily median IOP for all eyes was elevated to 18.0 (14.0, 23.0) mmHg and generally remained significantly elevated above baseline through postoperative week two. Risk factors for all eyes to have an IOP spike were glaucoma diagnosis (OR 1.71 (1.17-2.5), P=0.005), male sex (OR 1.64 (1.15-2.37), P=0.007), and baseline logMAR visual acuity (OR=1.07 (1.01-1.13) per 0.2 logMAR unit increase, P=0.02). In eyes with glaucoma, risk factors for IOP spike included male sex (OR 2.36 (1.32-4.32), P=0.004), increased age (OR 1.45 (1.08-1.97) per ten years, P=0.02), and Hispanic ethnicity compared to non-Hispanic White patients (OR 2.30 (1.07-4.80), P=0.03). In eyes without glaucoma, only baseline visual acuity was a risk factor (OR 1.09 (1.00-1.18) per 0.2 logMAR unit increase, P=0.04).
CONCLUSIONS: Ophthalmologists can anticipate a postoperative IOP elevation with resolution to baseline IOP by postoperative week two, but IOP is unlikely to decline below baseline, when AV is required during phacoemulsification. Surgeons should closely monitor for IOP spikes when AV is performed for patients with glaucoma, male sex, and worse baseline visual acuity.

etudes.titre: Morgagnian Cataract: Clinical Features, Surgical Management, and Outcomes.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Surgical »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To characterize the clinical features, surgical management, and outcomes of Morgagnian cataracts.
DESIGN: Retrospective clinical cohort study.
SUBJECTS: Fifty eyes of 50 adults diagnosed with Morgagnian cataracts at a tertiary academic referral center in the United States from October 2015 through August 2026.
METHODS: Medical records were reviewed for demographic characteristics, ocular findings, imaging, surgical management, intraoperative complications, intraocular lens (IOL) fixation, postoperative complications, best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), and intraocular pressure (IOP).
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Surgical management, intraoperative complications, postoperative BCVA, and IOP.
RESULTS: Presenting BCVA was hand motions or worse in 43/50 eyes (86%). Mean presenting IOP was 25.8 ± 16.2 mmHg. Lens-induced IOP elevation was present in 24/50 eyes (48%), lens-induced glaucoma in 19/50 (38%), and zonular weakness in 18/43 (42%). Surgery was performed in 40/50 eyes (80%). Phacoemulsification was initially attempted in 30/40 eyes (75%), manual small-incision cataract surgery in 5/40 (13%), and pars plana lensectomy with vitrectomy in 5/40 (13%). Intraoperative complications occurred in 14/40 eyes (35%), including posterior capsule rupture in 8/40 (20%); overall, 16/40 eyes (40%) received an in-the-bag IOL. Mean BCVA improved from 2.39 ± 0.58 logMAR preoperatively to 0.68 ± 0.81 logMAR at the last follow-up (paired analysis; P < 0.001), with 20/40 eyes (50%) achieving 20/40 or better. Mean IOP decreased from 26.0 ± 16.9 mmHg at presentation to 16.7 ± 5.5 mmHg at postoperative month 1 (P = 0.003), although 20/40 eyes (50%) remained on IOP-lowering medications.
CONCLUSIONS: Morgagnian cataracts were associated with profound visual loss, pressure-related complications, and zonular weakness, with substantial intraoperative risk. Despite this complexity, half of the operated eyes achieved BCVA of 20/40 or better. IOP decreased after cataract extraction in the setting of continued medical therapy in many eyes. These findings support careful preoperative assessment, counseling regarding capsular and zonular complications and potential alternative IOL fixation, and an individualized surgical strategy. However, the retrospective design, modest sample size, and variable follow-up limit interpretation, while the tertiary referral setting may limit generalizability.

etudes.titre: Therapeutic efficacy and systemic pharmacokinetics of a dual-drug hydrogel contact lens for sustained glaucoma therapy.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « drug »
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: Conventional topical therapy for glaucoma is limited by poor ocular bioavailability, rapid precorneal drug loss, frequent dosing and systemic absorption through the nasolacrimal pathway, which may reduce therapeutic efficacy and increase the risk of adverse effects. Drug-eluting hydrogel contact lenses have emerged as a promising strategy to overcome these limitations by enabling sustained ocular drug delivery.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy, ocular biocompatibility and systemic pharmacokinetic profile of an optimized dual-drug-loaded HEMA-based hydrogel contact lens delivering timolol maleate (TM) and brimonidine tartrate (BT) for sustained glaucoma management.
METHODS: Optimized hydrogel contact lenses composed of 2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate (HEMA), N, N-dimethylacrylamide (DMA), N-vinylpyrrolidone (NVP) and ethylene glycol dimethacrylate (EGDMA) were fabricated by UV photopolymerization and loaded with TM and BT (4 mg/mL each). Ocular biocompatibility was assessed using the modified Draize irritation test. Therapeutic efficacy was evaluated in a steroid-induced ocular hypertension New Zealand White rabbit model by monitoring intraocular pressure (IOP) for 24 h. Systemic drug exposure was determined by validated high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) analysis of plasma samples, while ocular safety was further confirmed through histopathological examination.
RESULTS: The optimized hydrogel lens exhibited excellent ocular biocompatibility, with a maximum Draize score of 0.33 ± 0.12 that resolved completely within 48 h and no histopathological evidence of ocular tissue damage. In hypertensive rabbits, the dual-drug hydrogel lens maintained normotensive IOP (16.1 ± 0.8 mmHg) for 24 h, representing a 43.5% reduction from baseline and significantly outperforming conventional eye drops beyond 4 h (p < 0.01). Plasma concentrations of both TM and BT remained below the limit of quantification (<2.0 ng/mL) throughout the study, whereas conventional eye drops produced measurable systemic exposure (TM: 18.4 ± 2.1 ng/mL; BT: 8.2 ± 1.2 ng/mL), demonstrating effective minimization of systemic drug absorption.
CONCLUSION: The optimized dual-drug-loaded hydrogel contact lens provided sustained intraocular pressure reduction, excellent ocular biocompatibility and negligible systemic drug exposure compared with conventional topical therapy. These findings highlight its potential as a sustained ocular drug-delivery platform capable of improving therapeutic efficacy, reducing systemic adverse effects and enhancing long-term treatment adherence in glaucoma management. Further long-term preclinical investigations and clinical studies are warranted to support clinical translation.
