etudes.titre: Documented Dry Eye Disease in Patients Receiving Topical Antiglaucoma Therapy: Associations with Treatment Characteristics.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Background/Objectives: Chronic topical antiglaucoma therapy may affect the ocular surface. We assessed documented dry eye disease (DED) and its associations with active-ingredient burden, treatment duration, and preservative exposure. Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 357 adults receiving topical antiglaucoma therapy at a tertiary center who had complete treatment and ocular-surface data. Ocular-surface testing was prompted by symptoms or clinical judgment. The first eligible visit identified during chronological record review was analyzed for each patient. DED was based on the treating ophthalmologist's documented diagnosis. Logistic regression evaluated treatment-related factors. Results: DED was documented in 171/357 patients within this selected sample (47.9%; 95% CI 42.8-53.1%). Prevalence was higher with at least two versus one active IOP-lowering ingredient (60.6% vs. 23.1%; p < 0.001). Each additional ingredient was associated with higher DED odds after adjustment for age, sex, and glaucoma subtype (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.65, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.88-3.74). Longer treatment duration was also associated with higher odds (aOR 1.12 per 12 months, 95% CI 1.05-1.20). In the linear extended model, active-ingredient count was not associated with documented DED (aOR 1.02, 95% CI 0.69-1.51), whereas an exclusively preservative-free regimen was associated with lower odds (aOR 0.011, 95% CI 0.001-0.084) and fixed-combination therapy with higher odds (aOR 3.23, 95% CI 1.74-5.98). However, categorical modeling of ingredient count significantly improved extended-model fit (likelihood-ratio p < 0.001), indicating sensitivity to functional form. Documented DED occurred in 1/91 (1.1%) exclusively preservative-free patients versus 170/266 (63.9%) preserved-exposure patients, with sparse PF events limiting interpretation. Conclusions: Documented DED was common in this selected cohort undergoing ocular-surface assessment. Active-ingredient count was associated with DED in the primary adjusted model, but its interpretation in the extended model depended on the functional form used. The marked inverse association with an exclusively preservative-free regimen requires prospective confirmation because sparse data, limited overlap between treatment groups, treatment selection, and residual confounding preclude causal inference.

etudes.titre: Biological Restoration of Conventional Aqueous Outflow Pathways in Glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Pathways »
etudes.resume: Glaucoma causes progressive damage to the optic nerve, and reducing intraocular pressure is the only clinically proven way to slow the disease. Although current medical, laser, and surgical treatments mainly change aqueous humor dynamics, they do not counteract the cellular and extracellular abnormalities of the conventional outflow pathway. Growing evidence shows that loss and dysfunction of trabecular meshwork cells impair aqueous humor drainage, supporting regenerative approaches that rebuild the outflow system rather than bypass it. In this narrative review, we present novel stem cell-based strategies to regenerate the trabecular meshwork and Schlemm's canal, particularly trabecular meshwork (TM) stem cells, mesenchymal stem cells, pluripotent stem cell-derived TM-like cells, and neural crest-derived progenitors. We review recent evidence suggesting that transplanted cells may restore outflow not just through engraftment and cellular replacement, but also through paracrine signaling, stimulation of endogenous cell proliferation, extracellular matrix modification, and rejuvenation of the trabecular microenvironment. This review discusses advances in lineage specification, cell targeting and delivery, single-cell and transcriptomic characterization, mechanobiology, and bioengineered models of the human aqueous out-flow pathway. New approaches, such as magnetically guided cell delivery and the identification of cells that promote trabecular tissue regeneration and repopulation, show how rapidly this field has developed. We cover key translational barriers, including cell identity, manufacturing standardization, long-term engraftment, tumorigenicity, immune responses, off-target localization, and limited clinical efficacy data. Reconstructing the aqueous outflow pathway using stem cells remains a preclinical endeavor. However, it may shift the focus from chronic pressure control to biologically restoring outflow function in glaucoma.

etudes.titre: Nail-Patella Syndrome in a 76-Year-Old Woman: Multisystem Phenotype, Diagnostic Delay, and Clinical Implications.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Diagnostic »
etudes.resume: Nail-patella syndrome (NPS) is a rare autosomal dominant multisystem disorder characterized by a variable combination of nail abnormalities, patellar hypoplasia or dysplasia, elbow involvement, and iliac horns, with possible renal, ophthalmological, neurological, and skeletal manifestations. Recognition may be substantially delayed when individual abnormalities are assessed separately or attributed to age-related and degenerative musculoskeletal disease. We report the case of a 76-year-old woman evaluated for progressive bilateral knee pain, gait impairment, and chronic multisite musculoskeletal symptoms. Congenital thumbnail abnormalities and long-standing restriction of elbow extension had been present since childhood. Suspicion of NPS was first raised at the age of 43 years after bilateral iliac horns were identified radiographically in one of her grandsons. Clinical examination demonstrated bilateral thumbnail hypoplasia with partial absence of the ulnar nail plate, triangular lunulae, reduced dorsal distal interphalangeal creases, bilateral fifth-finger flexion contractures, marked limitation of elbow extension with restricted pronation and supination, and clinically hypoplastic patellae. Bilateral Lester sign and glaucoma were also documented. Radiographic assessment revealed bilateral patellar hypoplasia, lateral displacement of the left patella, bilateral knee osteoarthritis, and characteristic bilateral iliac horns. Additional findings included bilateral hip osteoarthritis, lumbar degenerative changes, pes planus, a bifid configuration of the left fifth metatarsal, osteopenia, and sensory abnormalities. Walking pain was 70 mm on a 100-mm visual analogue scale, and the WOMAC score was 42/96. Following a 10-day rehabilitation program, walking pain decreased from 70 to 50 mm on the visual analogue scale, while the WOMAC total score improved from 42/96 to 37/96, indicating short-term symptomatic and functional improvement. Routine urinalysis showed no proteinuria or hematuria. Molecular testing for a pathogenic LMX1B variant was not performed. The diagnosis was established on the basis of the highly characteristic integrated clinical and radiographic phenotype. This case illustrates how NPS may remain incompletely recognized for decades despite congenital manifestations and emphasizes the clinical value of pattern recognition across multiple organ systems. In particular, the coexistence of characteristic nail changes, patellar abnormalities, elbow involvement, and bilateral iliac horns should prompt consideration of NPS and appropriate multidisciplinary surveillance.

etudes.titre: Artificial Intelligence in Eye Disease: A Systematic Review of Screening, Diagnosis, Prognosis, Treatment-Response Prediction, and Clinical Decision Support.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Artificial Intelligence »; mot du titre : « Screening »
etudes.resume: Background/Objectives: Artificial intelligence (AI) is expanding eye care beyond image-based detection toward prognosis, treatment-response prediction, monitoring, triage, and clinician-facing decision support. We evaluated AI across eye-disease screening, diagnosis, prognosis, treatment response, and decision support, emphasizing validation, explainability, and clinical readiness. Methods: This PROSPERO-registered review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. Six databases plus supplementary routes identified English-language literature published from 1 January 2015 through 10 August 2026. Included studies underwent design-mapped Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI)/adapted-JBI item-level appraisal; heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis. Results: The evidence base comprised 270 studies. Diabetic retinopathy/diabetic macular oedema was the largest clinical area (82), followed by retinal/multi-disease AI (52), glaucoma (46), and age-related macular degeneration (AMD)/macular disease (29); convolutional neural network (CNN)/convolutional deep learning was the largest primary method group (136). External validation was confirmed in 130 studies, including 95 with a clinical/geographic/prospective/real-world external-validation component (86 clinical-only and nine mixed clinical + technical); 49 had a strict direct clinical comparator and 90 used explainability. Pediatric/pediatric-relevant evidence accounted for 30 studies, while explicit optometry/optometrist involvement appeared in only three. Conclusions: Ophthalmic AI spans diagnosis through clinical management, but translation remains limited by heterogeneous outcomes, incomplete independent validation, few direct comparators, and sparse evaluation of safety, workflow effects, and patient outcomes.

etudes.titre: Patterns and Predictors of Repeated Medication Nonadherence in Glaucoma: A Population-Based Study.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Medication »
etudes.resume: Background/Objectives: We aimed to evaluate nonadherence to topical glaucoma therapy and identify risk factors for repeated prescription fulfillment failure in a large national population-based cohort. Methods: The electronic medical records from a large health maintenance organization were retrospectively reviewed for all patients aged 18 years or older with a diagnosis of glaucoma from 2000 to 2023. Data on patients who had purchased at least one anti-glaucoma medication were retrieved. Compliance was defined as prescription fulfillment within predefined expiration windows of 1, 2, and 3 months. Repeated nonadherence was defined as three unfulfilled prescriptions within a 3-month expiration window. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used to identify risk factors for repeated failure. Results: Among 40,200 treated patients, ≥80% cumulative prescription fulfillment was achieved in 80.3% of the population under a 3-month expiration definition. Under a strict 1-month definition, the incidence rate of the third compliance failure was 335 per 1000 person-years. In multivariable Cox analysis, obesity (HR 1.37, 95% CI 1.29-1.45) and current smoking (HR 1.07, 95% CI 1.04-1.11) were independently associated with increased risk of repeated failure. Older age (≥70 years: HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.62-0.87) and higher baseline intraocular pressure (≥25 mmHg: HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.61-0.68) were associated with reduced risk. Initiation with prostaglandin analogs was associated with lower hazard compared with alpha-2 adrenergic agonists (HR 0.53, 95% CI 0.49-0.57), whereas treatment alterations (≥3 changes) were associated with increased hazard (HR 1.64, 95% CI 1.39-1.95). Conclusions: Repeated nonadherence to topical glaucoma therapy is common and is associated with identifiable behavioral and treatment-related factors. Recognition of patients at elevated risk may support targeted strategies to enhance long-term treatment stability.

etudes.titre: Real-World Treatment Patterns and Persistence of Omidenepag Isopropyl in Korean Patients with Normal-Tension Glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: étiquette : produit suivi étudié (rôle suggéré, à vérifier)
etudes.resume: Background/Objectives: Prostaglandin analogues may cause prostaglandin-associated periorbitopathy (PAP). Omidenepag isopropyl (OMDI), a selective EP2 receptor agonist, may provide an alternative, but real-world data in normal-tension glaucoma (NTG) are limited. We evaluated treatment patterns, persistence, and intraocular pressure (IOP) outcomes of OMDI in Korean patients with NTG. Methods: This retrospective study included 403 eyes of 218 patients with NTG who initiated OMDI and were followed for up to 12 months. Patients received monotherapy, adjunctive therapy, or switching therapy. IOP was analyzed using a three-level linear mixed-effects model, and persistence was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Results: OMDI was prescribed as monotherapy in 88 patients (40.4%), adjunctive therapy in 25 (11.5%), and switching therapy in 105 (48.2%). Among switchers, PAP was the most common reason (68.6%). IOP decreased significantly in all groups (all p < 0.001), with model-estimated 12-month changes of -4.08, -3.37, and -1.40 mmHg, respectively. Twelve-month persistence was 79.8%. OMDI was discontinued in 44 patients (20.2%), most commonly because of visual disturbance or decreased vision (38.6%). Conclusions: OMDI provided sustained IOP reduction and 79.8% 12-month persistence in Korean patients with NTG and was frequently selected as an alternative to prostaglandin analogues in patients with PAP.

etudes.titre: Visual Cortex Activity and Retinal Changes in Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma: An fMRI and OCTA Study.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique

labos.nom: New York Eye and Ear Infirmary of Mount Sinai
Barry Family Center for Ophthalmic Artificial Intelligence and Human Health

etudes.resume: Background and Objectives: Glaucoma is a neurodegenerative disease involving retinal ganglion cell loss, optic nerve damage and alterations within the central visual pathway. We evaluated visual cortex activity using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) in patients with primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) and its associations with retinal structural and microvascular parameters assessed using optical coherence tomography (OCT) and OCT angiography (OCTA). Materials and Methods: This prospective clinical study included 19 patients with POAG and 18 healthy controls. All participants underwent ophthalmological examination, standard automated perimetry (Humphrey 24-2 SITA Standard), swept-source OCT, OCTA of the optic nerve head (ONH) (DRI-OCT Triton, Topcon, Tokyo, Japan), and visual stimulation fMRI (3T Siemens Magnetom Skyra, Siemens Healthineers, Erlangen, Germany). Retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness, vessel density (VD), and visual cortex activity were compared between groups. Associations were assessed using Pearson's or Spearman's correlation according to data distribution, with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction. Unadjusted p and adjusted q values are reported. Results: RNFL thickness was reduced in POAG patients in all four sectors. VD was lower in every sector of the superficial and deep plexus (all q < 0.05), as was outer retinal signal. Choriocapillaris findings were heterogeneous. RNFL thickness correlated with choriocapillaris VD in two of three corresponding nasal sectors, in POAG patients only. Visual cortex activation was lower in POAG patients (p = 0.046; Hedges' g = -0.68, 95% CI -1.34 to -0.01), but not after adjustment for age (p = 0.086). No association between VD and cortical activity survived FDR correction. Conclusions: In POAG, choriocapillaris VD tracked RNFL thickness in corresponding nasal sectors, an association not detected in controls. Reduced cortical activation did not persist after adjustment for age, and no retinal-cortical microvascular association was found. These exploratory findings suggest that distinct retinal vascular layers may carry different pathophysiological information and require confirmation in larger cohorts.

etudes.titre: Clinical Outcomes of Switching from Prostaglandin Analogs to Omidenepag Isopropyl in Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma and Glaucoma Suspect Patients with Prostaglandin-Associated Periorbitopathy: A Prospective, Multicenter Study.
etudes.raison_rubrique: étiquette : produit suivi étudié (rôle suggéré, à vérifier)
etudes.resume: Background/Objectives: Prostaglandin-associated periorbitopathy (PAP) is a common treatment-related burden of prostaglandin analog (PGA) therapy that may compromise long-term glaucoma management. This study evaluated improvement in PAP and changes in intraocular pressure (IOP) after switching from PGAs to omidenepag isopropyl. Methods: This prospective, multicenter study was conducted in Korea over 24 weeks. Adults diagnosed with PAP who had received PGA eye drops for ≥3 months for primary open-angle glaucoma, normal-tension glaucoma, or glaucoma suspect were switched to omidenepag isopropyl. PAP manifestations were evaluated using investigator assessments, independent assessments, and patient-reported outcome measures. Changes in IOP and safety outcomes were also assessed. Results: A total of 96 patients were included in the final analysis. At Week 24, improvement in deepening of the upper eyelid sulcus was observed in 78.16% of patients. Improvements were also observed in flattening of the lower eyelid bag, upper eyelid ptosis, ciliary hypertrichosis, and periorbital hyperpigmentation. Mean IOP was significantly reduced from baseline (-2.14 mmHg), with 42.71% and 27.08% of patients achieving IOP reductions of ≥15% and ≥20%, respectively. Findings were consistent overall across institutional, independent, and subjective assessments. Most adverse events were mild, and no serious adverse events were reported. Conclusions: PAP manifestations improved following transition from PGA therapy to omidenepag isopropyl, while IOP control and favorable tolerability were maintained in glaucoma or glaucoma suspect patients with PAP. These findings may support the clinical feasibility of switching from PGAs to omidenepag isopropyl in patients with PAP.

etudes.titre: Twelve-month outcomes of a tube-in-tube PreserFlo MicroShunt-Baerveldt glaucoma implant connection as a salvage procedure in refractory glaucoma: a pilot series.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « tube »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To report 12-month outcomes of a tube-in-tube connection between an existing PreserFlo MicroShunt (PFMS) and a Baerveldt glaucoma implant (BGI) used as a salvage procedure after PFMS failure or conjunctival/tube-related complications.
METHODS: Retrospective, single-center, consecutive case series of 6 pseudophakic eyes of 6 patients. A 350-mm² BGI was connected to the extraocular segment of the PFMS, which was retained as the anterior chamber entry and flow-restricting conduit while the Baerveldt plate served as a posterior reservoir. Outcome parameters at 12 months were intraocular pressure (IOP), number of topical antiglaucoma medications, surgical success, complications, and reinterventions.
RESULTS: Mean IOP decreased from 29.8 ± 15.0 mmHg preoperatively to 13.7 ± 4.6 mmHg at 12 months. Mean topical medications decreased from 3.0 ± 1.1 to 1.7 ± 1.9; systemic acetazolamide, used in 5 of 6 eyes preoperatively, was discontinued in all eyes. Qualified and complete success were achieved in 2 of 6 (33%) and 1 of 6 eyes (17%), respectively; 4 of 6 eyes were within their individualized target range. No clinically significant hypotony occurred. When the 2 eyes that underwent additional IOP-lowering surgery were excluded, the mean 12-month IOP in the remaining 4 eyes was 13.0 mmHg. Reinterventions comprised bleb revision with device exchange in 1 eye, scleral patch graft for tube exposure in 1 eye, and conjunctival reconstruction followed by micropulse cyclophotocoagulation in 1 eye.
CONCLUSION: The tube-in-tube PFMS-BGI connection lowered IOP and medication burden at 12 months while preserving the original anterior chamber entry, but composite success was modest and conjunctival or tube complications were common. The technique should be reserved for selected salvage cases and is distinct from primary combined PFMS-BGI implantation.
etudes.revue: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie

etudes.titre: Retinal layer structure on optical coherence tomography in post-traumatic stress disorder.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « optical coherence tomography »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To assess individual retinal layer thickness and volume changes on optical coherence tomography (OCT) in individuals with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) compared to controls.
METHODS: Adults ≥18 years with a PTSD diagnosis were identified. Age- and sex-matched controls (±5 years) without PTSD were recruited. Exclusion criteria included any cognitive disorder, brain injury, glaucoma, diabetes, optic nerve or vitreoretinal disease, uncontrolled hypertension, refractive error >±6 diopters, or best corrected visual acuity <20/40. Non-mydriatic OCT macular cube 512x128 images were obtained using Zeiss Cirrus HD-5000 AngioPlex. The Duke Reading Center DRCVisualizer software was used to segment the ganglion cell/inner plexiform (GC-IPL), inner nuclear (INL), outer plexiform (OPL), outer nuclear (ONL), photoreceptor, and retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) layers. Mean retinal thickness and volume were calculated for all layers within the central 1-mm subfield and 3- and 6-mm ETDRS rings, further divided into nasal, superior, temporal, and inferior quadrants.
RESULTS: 81 eyes of 42 PTSD patients and 81 eyes of 42 controls were analyzed. Average ages were 48 ± 15 years for PTSD and 51 ± 19 years for controls. Groups were 36% male. PTSD eyes showed significantly decreased photoreceptor thickness and volume and increased RPE thickness/volume across all ETDRS rings and quadrants (all p < 0.05). OPL thicknesses were decreased in PTSD eyes versus controls for temporal 3-mm (25.29 ± 1.36 µm vs. 26.64 ± 3.80µm) and temporal 6-mm (23.47 ± 0.88µm vs. 24.00 ± 1.54µm) rings (p < 0.05). OPL inferior 6-mm thickness was decreased in PTSD eyes (23.98 ± 1.58 µm vs. 24.78 ± 2.34 µm) versus controls (p < 0.05). The ONL nasal 6-mm thickness was decreased in PTSD versus controls (55.96 ± 7.90 µm vs. 56.74 ± 7.47µm) (p < 0.05). After adjusting for multiple testing, RPE differences remained significant across all evaluated regions, while photoreceptor differences remained significant within the central 1-mm and 3-mm ETDRS regions.
CONCLUSIONS: PTSD eyes demonstrated decreased photoreceptor layer and increased RPE thickness and volume.

etudes.titre: Autologous Anterior Lens Capsule as an Intrascleral Spacer in Deep Sclerectomy: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
OBJECTIVE: To compare deep sclerectomy (DS) combined with phacoemulsification (PE), with versus without an autologous anterior lens capsule spacer.
DESIGN: Prospective, randomized, parallel-group clinical trial.
METHODS: Sixty eyes of 60 adults with medically uncontrolled glaucoma and visually significant cataracts underwent PE-DS with an autologous anterior capsule spacer (Spacer group) or PE-DS alone (Control group). Follow-up was at least 12 months. The primary outcome was change in intraocular pressure (IOP) from baseline through 12 months. Secondary outcomes included glaucoma medication use, surgical success according to prespecified IOP-based criteria, and adverse events.
RESULTS: Baseline IOP was similar (25.14 ± 9.62 vs 23.77 ± 5.18 mmHg) and both study groups had significant IOP reduction at all visits. IOP was significantly lower in the spacer group at month 6 (11.90 ± 1.82 vs 13.13 ± 2.20 mmHg; P = 0.022) and month 12 (12 ± 2.20 vs 13.29 ± 2.68 mmHg; P = 0.042). Medication use was lower in eyes with an autologous spacer at months 6 (0.14 ± 0.45 vs 0.48 ± 0.85; P= 0.063) and 12 (0.29 ± 0.66 vs 0.68 ± 1.04; P =0.094). Under stringent success definitions, survival favored the spacer (e.g., Definition C: IOP≤12 mmHg: 47.5% vs 15.5%; log-rank test P = 0.025).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Adding an autologous anterior capsule spacer during PE-DS was associated with lower IOP at 6 and 12 months and higher cumulative success under stringent IOP thresholds. Medication use was lower in the spacer group, although the between-group differences showed a trend toward statistical significance.

etudes.titre: Delayed presentation of intraocular pentastomiasis resulting in unilateral blindness in a Congolese child.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: We report the case of a 6-year-old girl who presented with a motile larva in the anterior chamber of the right eye, associated with anterior uveitis, secondary glaucoma, and blindness. The larva was identified macroscopically as Armillifer grandis, a pentastomid parasite with snakes and other reptiles as definitive hosts. Intraocular pressure normalized and intraocular inflammation resolved within days following removal. This case is reported because ocular pentastomiasis is exceptionally rare compared with visceral pentastomiasis. It underscores the vision-threatening potential of intraocular pentastomiasis and the importance of early recognition and prompt surgical extraction to prevent visual impairment. Ocular pentastomiasis is a rare parasitic infection of the eye caused by larval stages of pentastomid arthropods, most commonly Armillifer and less frequently Linguatula species. Although pentastomiasis has historically been considered an endemic zoonosis in some areas of Africa, Asia, and the Middle East, imported cases have been reported in nonendemic regions (Europe and North America) as a result of increased travel and migration.1-4.
etudes.revue: Journal of AAPOS : the official publication of the American Association for Pediatric Ophthalmology and Strabismus

etudes.titre: Lens particle-induced pediatric glaucoma following congenital cataract surgery: a case report.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « surgery »
etudes.resume: A 13-year-old boy with a history of bilateral lens extraction for congenital cataract at 4 months of age presented with nausea and vomiting. Tafluprost had been administrated once daily to both eyes since the age of 7 years, and intraocular pressure (IOP) in both eyes remained around 20 mm Hg before this visit. On examination, IOP was 21 mm Hg in the right eye and 52 mm Hg in the left eye. The next day, the IOP in the left eye decreased to 10 mm Hg. No significant floaters were seen in the anterior chamber of either eye. Multiple lens fragments were present in the left angle. Four days later, the left eye IOP had increased to 60 mm Hg, and lens fragments were observed floating in the left anterior recess. Based on the course and findings, lens-induced glaucoma was considered the most reasonable cause for the elevated IOP; therefore, anterior chamber washout was performed. Eighteen months postoperatively, no fragments remained in the anterior chamber, and IOP remained 17-19 mm Hg. In this case, gonioscopy was useful in establishing the cause of IOP elevation.

etudes.titre: Real-World Safety Profile of Mirvetuximab Soravtansine: A Population-Based Pharmacovigilance Study Leveraging FAERS and EudraVigilance Databases.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: Mirvetuximab soravtansine (MIRV) is the first FDA-approved antibody-drug conjugate targeting folate receptor-α (FRα)-positive platinum-resistant ovarian cancer. Despite its clinical adoption, comprehensive post-marketing real-world evidence regarding its safety profile remains limited. This study aimed to systematically characterize the adverse event (AE) profile of MIRV in real-world settings and to identify potential safety signals using large-scale pharmacovigilance databases.
METHODS: A retrospective pharmacovigilance analysis was conducted using adverse event reports from the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS, 2022-2025). We excluded all reports submitted for male patients. Safety signals were assessed at the system organ class (SOC), standardized MedDRA query (SMQ), and preferred term (PT) levels. Disproportionality analyses were performed using 4 algorithms: reporting odds ratio (ROR), proportional reporting ratio (PRR), Bayesian confidence propagation neural network (BCPNN), and multi-item gamma Poisson shrinker (MGPS). Time-to-onset (TTO) analysis was conducted to evaluate onset patterns. External validation was performed using the EudraVigilance database.
FINDINGS: A total of 1,249 MIRV-related reports corresponding to 2,577 AEs were identified in FAERS. At the SOC level, eye disorders were the most frequently reported AEs (n = 593) and demonstrated the strongest disproportionality signal (ROR: 13.79, 95% CI: 12.58-15.12). At the PT level, the 3 most frequently reported AEs were vision blurred (n = 97), neuropathy peripheral (n = 95), and cataract (n = 75). Among detected safety signals, the strongest disproportionality signals (ranked by IC025 value) were observed for keratitis (ROR: 390.64, PRR: 383.08, EBGM05: 269.06, IC025: 5.06), keratopathy (ROR: 487.9, PRR: 479.78, EBGM05: 323.68, IC025: 4.87), and pneumonitis (ROR: 56.93, PRR: 55.37, EBGM05: 43.35, IC0254.64). Overall, 44 positive PT-level signals were identified. Common labeled AEs included blurred vision, peripheral neuropathy, cataract, diarrhoea, and abdominal pain. Potentially novel (unlabeled) signals included blindness, colitis, pulmonary fibrosis, glaucoma, intestinal perforation, and astigmatism. Time-to-onset analysis showed that 42.9% of AEs occurred within the first month after treatment initiation, indicating an early-onset pattern. In the EudraVigilance database, 527 MIRV-related reports were identified. At the SOC level, eye disorders again demonstrated the strongest disproportionality signal, consistent with the findings from FAERS. At the PT level, the most frequently reported AEs were pneumonitis (n = 47), peripheral neuropathy (n = 45), and vision blurred (n = 43), whereas keratitis, keratopathy, and pneumonitis exhibited the strongest disproportionality signals. A total of 29 overlapping positive signals were identified between FAERS and EudraVigilance, further supporting the robustness of the observed safety signals.
IMPLICATIONS: This dual-database pharmacovigilance study provides consistent real-world evidence supporting the established ocular toxicity profile of MIRV and identifies additional potential safety signals requiring further clinical attention. These findings may assist clinicians in optimizing risk assessment and monitoring strategies for patients receiving MIRV.

etudes.titre: Topographic and layer-specific mapping of anterior scleral complex thickness using anterior segment OCT: an anatomical reference with potential surgical relevance.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « surgical »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To provide a layer-specific surgical atlas of the anterior scleral complex and link the AS-OCT anatomy to the tissue planes and entry zones used during glaucoma filtration surgery, scleral-fixated IOL implantation, intravitreal injection and ocular surface surgery.
METHODS: This prospective cross-sectional study included 120 healthy Turkish volunteers. Thicknesses of the scleral stroma, episclera, Tenon's capsule and conjunctiva were measured at 1, 2, 3 and 4 mm from the scleral spur in four quadrants using wide-angle anterior segment optical coherence tomography with rectus muscle visualization. Measurement reliability was assessed using the ICC, SEM, TEM and repeatability coefficient.
RESULTS: The mean age of participants was 42.74 ± 15.31 years; 72.5% were female. Layer-specific boundaries of all four tissues were feasible, with most parameters demonstrating good to excellent reliability. Notably, certain measurements of the thickness of the medial Tenon's capsule were significantly greater in females. Scleral stromal and episcleral thickness generally increased with age across most quadrants. The thickness of Tenon's capsule generally decreased with age. Conjunctival thickness changes were quadrant-specific, with a significant increases in the inferior and medial quadrants with age. Topographical analysis revealed that scleral stromal thickness progressively decreased toward the periphery, whereas episcleral thickness generally increased.
CONCLUSION: Beyond establishing normative AS-OCT measurements, this study introduces anterior scleral anatomy into a potential clinically relevant surgical reference framework. The layer-specific topographical atlas and age-related remodeling patterns describe the tissue characteristics encountered at commonly used surgical locations and may inform surgeons in selecting flap depth, fixation sites, dissection planes and injection zones according to patient age and quadrant-specific anatomy.

etudes.titre: Optic disc and cup segmentation using Vision Mamba UNet with enhanced edge-guided attention in fundus images.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: Glaucoma is an irreversible blinding disease for which early detection is essential. Precise segmentation of the optic disc (OD) and optic cup (OC) enables accurate cup-to-disc ratio (CDR) calculation, which serves as an important reference for glaucoma evaluation. However, the ambiguous boundaries between these structures make manual segmentation time-consuming and highly subjective.
METHODS: This study proposes a hybrid framework for OD and OC segmentation in fundus images. The framework first adopts YOLOv10 to achieve coarse localization and extraction of the OD region, followed by fine-grained segmentation using the proposed EEGA-VMUNet network. Based on a Vision Mamba-UNet backbone, we design an enhanced edge-guided attention (EEGA) module to adaptively integrate multi-scale contextual information. This module strengthens the representation of edges and fine structural features. A multi-scale loss function is also used to improve robustness to scale variations.
RESULTS: Experiments on four benchmark datasets demonstrate that EEGA-VMUNet achieves competitive segmentation performance. On the same-domain test sets, OD Dice coefficients range from 95.20% to 97.65% and OC Dice coefficients range from 87.51% to 89.95%. Zero-shot cross-domain experiments achieve an OD Dice of 95.18% and an OC Dice of 85.13%.
CONCLUSION: The proposed model achieves competitive performance in both OD and OC segmentation tasks. Bland-Altman analysis suggests that the derived vertical cup-to-disc ratio (VCDR) holds potential as a diagnostic aid for glaucoma screening, although its precision may require further improvement for longitudinal monitoring.

etudes.titre: Periocular morphology during long-term topical ophthalmic treatment: associations with prostaglandin analogs, preservatives, and eyelid manipulation.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: This cross-sectional study characterized periocular morphology in long-term users of topical ophthalmic medications and examined its associations with current prostaglandin analog use, preservative exposure, estimated cumulative eyelid-manipulation exposure, and eyelid manipulation during eye-drop instillation.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 115 patients receiving long-term topical ophthalmic treatment (50 receiving antiglaucoma [AG] treatment, 35 receiving artificial tear [AT] treatment, and 30 receiving both AG and AT treatment) and 50 healthy controls. Levator function (LF), margin reflex distance (MRD1 and MRD2), inferior scleral show, and the lower eyelid pinch test were assessed, while standardized photographs were used to evaluate upper and lower eyelid herniation, upper eyelid atrophy, and malar festoons. Associations between study groups, treatment-related exposures, and periocular outcomes were examined using multivariable linear, binary logistic, and ordinal logistic regression models adjusted for age, sex, and study-specific covariates, with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction.
RESULTS: After adjustment for age and sex, the AG group had lower LF (q = 0.016), whereas all treatment groups showed lower MRD1 values (all q ≤ 0.005) and higher frequency and severity of upper eyelid atrophy (all q < 0.05) than controls. No clear associations were identified between estimated cumulative eyelid-manipulation exposure or eyelid manipulation and the evaluated periocular outcomes after FDR correction. Current prostaglandin analog use was associated with higher odds of upper eyelid atrophy (OR 4.30, 95% CI 1.52-12.13; q = 0.016) together with lower odds of upper (OR 0.21, 95% CI 0.06-0.72; q = 0.029) and lower eyelid herniation (OR 0.13, 95% CI 0.04-0.43; q = 0.004), with an additional association with higher upper eyelid atrophy stage. Preservative-containing treatment was associated with higher odds of lower eyelid herniation (OR 5.46, 95% CI 1.76-16.94; q = 0.018) and its ordinal stage (q = 0.018). These associations remained significant after mutual adjustment for prostaglandin analog and preservative exposure.
CONCLUSION: Current prostaglandin analog use was associated with a periocular morphologic pattern characterized by increased upper eyelid atrophy and reduced visible upper- and lower-eyelid herniation. Preservative-containing treatment showed an exploratory association with lower eyelid herniation, whereas no clear associations were identified for estimated cumulative eyelid-manipulation exposure or eyelid manipulation. These findings reflect cross-sectional exposure-phenotype associations rather than causal effects.

etudes.titre: Comparative Study on the Efficacy of Intravitreal and Subconjunctival Simultaneous Injection of Conbercept Followed by Trabeculectomy Versus Intravitreal Injection of Conbercept Followed by Trabeculectomy Combined With 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) in the Treatment of Neovascular Glaucoma (NVG).
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Trabeculectomy »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To compare the efficacy of trabeculectomy preceded by simultaneous intravitreal and subconjunctival conbercept administration with that of trabeculectomy combined with 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) following intravitreal conbercept injection in patients with neovascular glaucoma (NVG).
METHODS: In this comparative study, 120 patients with NVG were enrolled and allocated to two treatment groups. Regression of neovascularization of the iris (NVI) and neovascularization of the angle (NVA) following conbercept administration was assessed. Additional outcome measures included intraocular pressure (IOP), visual acuity, filtering bleb morphology, use of antiglaucoma medications, surgical success rate, and postoperative complications before and after trabeculectomy.
RESULTS: On day 1 after conbercept injection, the group receiving simultaneous intravitreal and subconjunctival conbercept demonstrated significantly greater regression of NVI (p = 0.001) and NVA (p = 0.003) than the comparator group. Across follow-up visits, significant reductions in IOP were observed within both groups (time effect: F = 352.42, p = 0.001). Improvement in visual acuity did not differ significantly between groups (p > 0.05). Significant between-group differences in bleb height were observed at 1, 3, and 6 months after trabeculectomy (p = 0.008, p = 0.001, and p = 0.001, respectively). No significant difference in bleb extent was detected at any postoperative timepoint (F = 2.546, p = 0.080). Bleb vascularity differed significantly between groups throughout follow-up (F = 3.297, p = 0.021). Rates of postoperative complications, antiglaucoma medication use before surgery and within 6 months after injection, and overall surgical success did not differ significantly between groups (all p > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: In patients with NVG undergoing trabeculectomy, simultaneous intravitreal and subconjunctival administration of conbercept was associated with more rapid regression of anterior-segment neovascularization and more favorable postoperative bleb characteristics. However, no significant between-group differences were observed in 6-month IOP control or surgical success. The potential benefits of the combined administration strategy appear to be mainly related to early neovascular regression and bleb morphology, and their significance for long-term surgical outcomes remains to be determined.

etudes.titre: Thirty-year follow-up of retinal vasculitis at a tertiary eye care center in India.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To describe the clinical course of patients with retinal vasculitis over a three-decade follow-up.
METHODS: Retrospective chart review of patients with a minimum follow-up of 30 years at a tertiary eye care institute in India.
RESULTS: A total of 37 patients were included. The mean follow-up duration was 34.3 ± 2.9 years (range: 30-44 years). The mean age of the patients at presentation was 31.05 ± 15.6 years, and 97% of them were male. In 54% of the patients, the involvement was bilateral. Five patients who initially presented with unilateral involvement subsequently developed involvement in the other eye. Presumed tuberculosis was diagnosed in five patients. None of the remaining patients developed ocular or extraocular manifestations of tuberculosis during the 30-year follow-up. Common investigations done for all patients were antinuclear antibody, Venereal Disease Research Laboratory test, Mantoux test, chest radiography, and serum angiotensin-converting enzyme levels. The use of immunosuppressives was low (2), as was the use of intravitreal anti-Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) (1). The primary modalities of treatment were oral corticosteroids and photocoagulation. The most common complications were glaucoma (35, 56.5%), vitreous hemorrhage (30, 48.4%), and optic neuropathy (10, 16.1%). Recurrence of inflammation was seen in 30.6% of eyes in three decades of follow-up. Nineteen eyes required vitrectomy, and five eyes underwent scleral buckling for retinal detachment. The mean visual acuity in logarithm of the minimum angle of resolution at presentation was 0.8, and at the final visit, after 30 years of follow-up was 0.66. It was observed that 41.9% of eyes had visual improvement, 24.2% of eyes remained visually stable, and vision deteriorated in 33.9% of eyes.
CONCLUSION: Retinal vasculitis has a chronic and unpredictable course, warranting long-term follow-up to detect late bilateral involvement and recurrence. While recurrence becomes less frequent over time, it may still occur after many years. Most patients continue to have idiopathic disease without subsequent identification of a systemic cause.

etudes.resume: The corneal endothelium plays a pivotal role in maintaining corneal clarity, and its damage leads to a hydration dysfunction and secondary glaucoma. We previously identified XMU-MP-1, a Hippo pathway inhibitor, as a potent stimulator of corneal endothelial cell proliferation in nonhuman primate models. However, its therapeutic potential is limited by poor intraocular permeability and low bioavailability. Herein, we report an engineered perfluoropentane (PFP)-cored lipid microbubble (MB) platform for the buoyancy-mediated targeted delivery of XMU-MP-1. Post intracameral injection, drug-loaded microbubbles (D@MB) undergo spontaneous in situ liquid-to-gas phase transition at physiological temperature, which grants them buoyancy-driven upward movement in aqueous humor to maintain continuous direct contact with the endothelial layer, achieving an extended retention of over 72 h in the anterior chamber. Finally, the D@MB drug delivery platform accelerates regenerative processes and restores both the corneal ultrastructure and physiological function. This study highlights a minimally invasive approach that bypasses traditional surgical interventions to stimulate the repair of the damaged corneal endothelium.

etudes.titre: Neuroprotectant development from small molecule inhibitors of CHOP/ATF4 expression.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « inhibitors »
etudes.resume: Glaucoma is a neurodegenerative disease that is in urgent need of neuroprotective therapies. We previously revealed the critical role of neuronal endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress induced by optic nerve injury in glaucomatous neurodegeneration. We also demonstrated that modulation of the ATF4-CHOP branch of ER stress provides significant neuroprotection. Here, we present multiple new chemical series identified by high-throughput screening that inhibit ER stress-induced C/EBP homologous protein (CHOP) expression. We perform a structure-activity relationship analysis of one "hit" compound and establish two analogs with potent activities on inhibiting the expression of CHOP and activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4). We further demonstrate their neuroprotective efficacy in two optic neuropathy models; in both models, they increase survival of retinal ganglion cell somata and axons and preserve visual function. Together, this proof-of-concept evidence establishes the new ER stress modulators as promising candidates for further drug development to provide neuroprotective therapy for glaucoma and other optic neuropathies, and potentially for diverse CNS axonopathies.

etudes.titre: Glaucoma Treatment Trends in Australia Over a 10-Year Period.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To characterise trends in the use of selective laser trabeculoplasty (SLT), glaucoma surgery and medication prescribing in Australia between 2015 and 2024.
STUDY DESIGN: Nationwide, population-based cross-sectional analysis.
METHODS: Medicare Benefits Schedule (MBS) procedure claims and Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS)/Repatriation PBS dispensing data were analysed from 2015 to 2024. Procedure and prescription rates were expressed per 100,000 Australian residents using Australian Bureau of Statistics population estimates.
RESULTS: Between 2015 and 2024, 344,370 SLT procedures were recorded. Rates rose from 127 to 150 per 100,000 (β = 1,335 procedures/year; 95% CI 969-1,701; p < 0.001). Annual glaucoma medication prescriptions decreased from 4,167,417 to 3,390,394 (17,498 to 12,466 per 100,000), without a statistically significant linear trend (β = -52,005/year; 95% CI - 104,373-363; p = 0.051). Overall, 113,466 glaucoma surgeries were recorded: annual procedures increased from 4,953 (20.8 per 100,000) to 15,334 (56.4 per 100,000). Minimally invasive glaucoma surgeries (MIGS) increased from 2,177 in 2017 to 10,501 in 2024, compared with 4,080 to 4,386 filtration procedures and 292 to 409 drainage device procedures. Negative binomial regression found no significant annual rate trends for MIGS (IRR 1.16; 95% CI 0.86-1.57; p = 0.34), filtration procedures (IRR 1.00; 95% CI 0.81-1.24; p = 0.97), or drainage devices (IRR 1.03; 95% CI 0.83-1.28; p = 0.79). Optometrists' share of glaucoma prescriptions increased from 1.25% to 5.63%.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings demonstrate changing glaucoma treatment trends in Australia. SLT and MIGS procedure volumes increased as medication prescriptions declined, while optometrists accounted for an increasing proportion of medication prescribing.

etudes.titre: Comparative Outcomes of Systemic Immunomodulatory Therapy Versus Local Corticosteroid Therapy in Chronic Noninfectious Uveitis.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: Chronic uveitis is a significant cause of visual impairment. Although initial therapy relies on corticosteroids, patients with chronic inflammation often require systemic immunomodulatory therapy (IMT) or local sustained-release steroids. However, comparative long-term outcomes of these treatment approaches remain unclear.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used the TriNetX Network to identify adults (ages ≥ 18 years) with chronic uveitis treated with systemic IMT or local corticosteroid therapy. Baseline characteristics were balanced using propensity score matching (PSM). Incidence of ocular outcomes including intraocular pressure (IOP)-lowering medication use, glaucoma, incisional glaucoma surgery, cataract surgery, cystoid macular edema (CME), and epiretinal membrane (ERM) were assessed at 1, 2, and 3 years. Outcome proportions were compared between groups using risk ratios (RR), with p < 0.05 considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Of 4,683 patients meeting inclusion criteria (1,273 on local therapy; 3,410 on systemic IMT), 1,087 patients remained per group after PSM. By 3 years, patients treated with local therapy had a higher cumulative incidence of IOP-lowering medication use (12.9% vs 6.9%; RR 1.88, p < 0.001), glaucoma (8.2% vs 3.1%; RR 2.60, p < 0.001), incisional glaucoma surgery (2.3% vs 1.1%; RR 2.19, p = 0.03), and cataract surgery (7.7% vs 3.5%; RR 2.24, p < 0.001) compared with systemic IMT. Rates of newly diagnosed CME (8.3% vs 2.5%; RR 3.37, p < 0.001) and ERM (8.9% vs 4.4%; RR 2.04, p < 0.001) were likewise higher in the local therapy group.
CONCLUSION: Local corticosteroid therapy was associated with a higher cumulative incidence of complications compared to systemic IMT in patients with chronic uveitis.
