etudes.titre: Demographic and Clinical Factors Associated with Fuchs Endothelial Corneal Dystrophy: A Nationwide Population-Based Study.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To identify demographic and clinical factors associated with Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy (FECD) in Israel.
METHODS: We conducted a population-based nested case-control study using data from Israel's largest healthcare provider covering the years 2005 to 2023. FECD patients were identified and compared with ten age and sex-matched controls per case, selected using risk-set sampling. Demographic factors and comorbidities were analyzed using conditional logistic regression.
RESULTS: We identified 591 FECD patients. The mean age at diagnosis was 64.35 ± 11 years; 198 (33.5%) were male. Multivariable analysis revealed several factors significantly associated with FECD: Medium and high SES (OR = 1.308, p = 0.014) and (OR = 1.456, p = 0.017), cataract (OR = 4.836, p < 0.001), skin cancer (OR = 1.362, p = 0.01), keratoconus (OR = 4.349, p = 0.002), hypermetropia (OR = 1.839, p < 0.001), glaucoma (OR = 1.726, p = 0.003) and uveitis (OR = 3.082, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: This population-based study identifies several factors significantly associated with FECD, including medium and high SES, cataract, skin cancer, keratoconus, hypermetropia, glaucoma and uveitis. These findings improve understanding of the demographic and clinical context associated with FECD and inform future longitudinal and mechanistic studies.

etudes.titre: Mishel theory-based perioperative nursing after trabeculectomy for primary glaucoma: effects on illness uncertainty, self-management, and quality of life.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « trabeculectomy »
etudes.resume:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effects of a perioperative nursing intervention based on Mishel's Uncertainty in Illness Theory in patients with primary glaucoma undergoing trabeculectomy.
METHODS: This single-center, two-arm, parallel-group randomized controlled study enrolled 198 patients undergoing first trabeculectomy at The First Affiliated Hospital of Suzhou University between February 2024 and December 2025. Participants were randomly allocated 1:1 to routine perioperative ophthalmic nursing or routine care plus a structured Mishel theory-based nursing intervention. Assessments were conducted 1 day before surgery (T0), at discharge (T1), and at 1 month (T2) and 3 months (T3) after surgery. The primary outcome was illness uncertainty measured using the Mishel Uncertainty in Illness Scale. Secondary outcomes included psychological status, discharge readiness, self-management, medication adherence, sleep quality, vision-related quality of life, satisfaction with nursing care, postoperative ophthalmic outcomes, and complications. All randomized participants completed follow-up and were analyzed according to their assigned groups.
RESULTS: After Holm adjustment, the intervention group had lower illness-uncertainty scores at T1, T2, and T3; lower anxiety scores at T1 and T3 and lower depression scores at T2 and T3; higher discharge-readiness and satisfaction-with-nursing-care at T1; higher self-management and medication-adherence scores and lower sleep-quality scores at T2 and T3; and lower GQL-15 scores at T3. At T3, the model-estimated between-group differences were -8.13 points for illness uncertainty (95% CI, -10.74 to -5.53), 5.64 points for self-management (95% CI, 4.08-7.19), 6.05 points for medication adherence (95% CI, 2.98-9.12), and -3.71 points for GQL-15 (95% CI, -5.41 to -2.00). At discharge, the between-group difference in discharge readiness was 1.23 points (95% CI, 0.99-1.47). No statistically significant between-group differences were detected in postoperative intraocular-pressure trajectories, visual-acuity recovery, medication-free status, postoperative procedures, or complications within 3 months.
CONCLUSION: In this single-center randomized study, Mishel theory-based perioperative nursing was associated with greater improvements in illness uncertainty and several psychological, behavioral, and recovery-related patient-reported outcomes after trabeculectomy. No statistically significant differences were detected in short-term objective ophthalmic outcomes or postoperative complications.

etudes.titre: Occult Optic Disk Pit Maculopathy Masquerading as Exudative Age-Related Macular Degeneration in an Elderly Patient: A Case Report.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
INTRODUCTION: Occult optic disk pit maculopathy (ODPM) is a rare cause of macular retinoschisis in which no pit is visible on funduscopic examination. Optic disk pits are congenital cavitary anomalies thought to arise from incomplete closure of the embryonic fissure during ocular development.
CASE PRESENTATION: This report presents an 83-year-old woman with a history of exudative AMD of the left eye (OS) and low-tension glaucoma having received 11 intravitreal anti-VEGF injections over approximately 18 months without resolution of macular fluid. Fluorescein angiography demonstrated no macular leakage and no macular neovascularization. Spectral-domain optical coherence tomography revealed multilayered peripapillary retinoschisis with fluid extending from the optic disk to the fovea. Dedicated optic disk OCT confirmed a deep crater-like excavation consistent with an occult optic disk pit. Anti-VEGF therapy was discontinued, and the patient was observed. At approximately 10 months after the last injection, best-corrected visual acuity was stable at 20/25 OS with stable nasal macular cysts on OCT.
CONCLUSION: Occult ODPM can closely mimic exudative AMD and may go unrecognized for many months in elderly patients with coexisting retinal disease, resulting in repeated unnecessary anti-VEGF treatment.

etudes.titre: Evaluation of the Perimouse Online Suprathreshold Visual Field Test for Glaucoma Screening in a Chinese Population: A Comparison with the Humphrey Field Analyzer.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Screening »; mot du titre : « Visual Field »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the diagnostic performance and spatial agreement of an online suprathreshold perimeter (Perimouse) compared with the Humphrey Field Analyzer (HFA) for detecting glaucomatous visual field defects.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this prospective comparative study, 174 participants (283 eyes with open-angle glaucoma or healthy controls) underwent Perimouse suprathreshold program and HFA. Abnormal points (missed stimuli in Perimouse; points with P<0.5% on HFA total deviation map) were compared. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Point-wise performance used neural network-derived area under the curve (AUC) and Cohen's κ.
RESULTS: Perimouse abnormal-point counts were correlated with HFA abnormal-point counts (r = 0.88, P < 0.001) and negatively correlated with HFA mean deviation (r = -0.80, P < 0.001). The intraclass correlation coefficient for abnormal-point counts between Perimouse and HFA was 0.93, and Bland-Altman analysis showed a mean bias of 0.73 abnormal points, with 95% limits of agreement ranging from -10.70 to 12.17. A cutoff of five abnormal points achieved 85.9% sensitivity and 97.9% specificity (AUC = 0.97), with performance improving with disease severity. Point-wise κ values ranged from 0.32 to 0.78 (AUC, 0.67-0.96). The test duration for Perimouse was 2.64 ± 1.83 minutes.
CONCLUSION: Perimouse demonstrated reasonable overall diagnostic accuracy for detecting HFA-defined visual field defects. Diagnostic performance was higher for moderate and advanced glaucomatous defects than for early defects, with variable point-wise agreement with HFA. Perimouse may serve as a rapid, adjunctive tool for preliminary functional screening of glaucomatous visual field loss.

etudes.titre: Endothelin 2-Mediated Neuroinflammation Drives Hypertensive Retinal Dysfunction.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique

labos.nom: National Natural Science Foundation of China

etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: Systemic hypertension is a risk factor for glaucoma, a leading cause of irreversible blindness, yet the mechanistic basis connecting the 2 conditions remains elusive.
METHODS: A longitudinal assessment of blood pressure, intraocular pressure, retinal function, structure, and perfusion was conducted in spontaneously hypertensive rats and Wistar-Kyoto rats. Transcriptomic analyses and immunofluorescence staining were performed to investigate hypertension-associated retinal biochemical changes. AAV-mediated knockdown of endothelin 2 was used to investigate its mechanistic role.
RESULTS: Hypertensive rats develop accelerated retinal degeneration marked by retinal thinning, functional impairment, reduced perfusion, and progressive neuroinflammation. Critically, these changes occur despite persistently low intraocular pressure, indicating an intraocular pressure-independent mechanism underlying the pathology. Biochemical analyses identified robust activation of the retinal endothelin system, with endothelin 2 the most significantly upregulated component. AAV-mediated retinal endothelin 2 knockdown substantially restored retinal function, ameliorated neuroinflammation, and enhanced retinal blood flow in hypertensive rats. Pharmacological blockade of endothelin receptor type A, but not type B, replicated these protective effects without altering intraocular pressure.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings establish endothelin 2 as an important, intraocular pressure-independent contributing factor to hypertension-associated retinal neurodegeneration and identify the endothelin-endothelin receptor type A axis as a potential therapeutic target to prevent vision loss in patients with hypertension.

etudes.titre: Secure Patient Messaging in Ophthalmology: Retrospective Natural Language Processing Study.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique

labos.nom: National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases

etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: The rapid rise of secure patient messaging has transformed ophthalmic communication, with text volumes now exceeding prepandemic levels across health care systems. Our study uses a natural language processing (NLP) model to explore patterns in over 30,000 secure messages and identify common ocular complaints and differences by patient demographics.
OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study is to characterize the clinical and administrative concerns communicated through secure ophthalmology messaging and to assess differences in message content across patient sociodemographic groups.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study of deidentified, patient-initiated secure messages sent between June 2014 and July 2024. Patients with ophthalmic conditions who initiated secure electronic health record (EHR) portal messages were included. Of the 52,388 extracted message threads, 30,390 (58%) patient medical advice request (PMAR) messages routed solely to the Department of Ophthalmology from 4817 unique patients were assessed after the exclusion of questionnaires, courtesy messages, clinician responses, and messages routed to other health care departments. Of these unique patients, 2673 (55.5%) were female, 2740 (56.9%) were aged 50 years or older, 2346 (48.7%) were White, 4392 (91.2%) were non-Hispanic, and 2774 (57.6%) were married. NLP and large language model (LLM)-assisted topic classification were used to categorize message content. The distribution of message topics and frequency of clinical concerns were assessed and stratified by age, sex, race, ethnicity, and marital status. Differences in message frequency by demographic subgroup were assessed using 2-proportion z-tests.
RESULTS: Following preprocessing and topic modeling, 14,284 (47%) of the 30,390 messages could be predefined in relation to a topic cluster and were included in the final analysis. Nearly half of all 14,284 predefined messages addressed administrative issues, including 4166 (29.2%) scheduling-related inquiries, 1352 (9.5%) pharmacy and medication refill requests, and 581 (4.1%) insurance document issues. Among clinical concerns, of the total 14,284 predefined messages, 2975 (20.8%) messages involved vision disturbances, 1241 (8.7%) involved glaucoma-related symptoms, 1074 (7.5%) involved tumor-related questions, and 1064 (7.4%) involved surgery-relevant concerns. Message content differed significantly by demographic characteristics. Non-White patients more frequently raised issues related to pharmacy refills, insurance, glaucoma, and disability documentation, whereas White patients more often reported surgical concerns. Older patients more frequently messaged about glaucoma, surgery, and tumor-related issues, while female patients more often reported complications and swelling or infection.
CONCLUSIONS: Secure patient messages frequently include clinically relevant symptoms with potential triage implications and demonstrate demographic differences in care-seeking behavior. Systematic analysis of message content may support safer triage, improved workflow efficiency, and more equitable delivery of ophthalmic care.

etudes.titre: [The perimetry ant tonometry in real clinical practice of managing patients with glaucoma: facilities and possibilities].
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « tonometry »; mot du titre : « perimetry »

labos.nom: Ministry of Health of the Russian Federation

etudes.resume: The anonymous survey of 107 ophthalmologists was carried out to assess facilities and practical application of diagnostic equipment in detection and management of glaucoma patients. It is established that main load of dispensary monitoring lies upon out-patient sector (81.8% of interrogated physicians of this level). However, only 12.5% of them have dedicated hours for glaucoma patients as compared to 35.3% of in-patient physicians (p=0.03). This indicates at time deficiency for full-value management of glaucoma patients at the primary care level that may negatively affect quality of dispensary monitoring. The significant deficiency of modern equipment is established. Only 46.4% of institutions are equipped with computerized perimeters. At that, outdated and law informative Förster perimeter remains the only method to assess visual field for 37.4% of specialists. The standard automated perimetry is applied by only 45.4% of physicians, and 9.1% of ophthalmologists in polyclinics apply no perimetry at all. The Maklakov tonometry (78.5%) and pneumotonometry (62.6%) dominate among methods measuring intraocular pressure, while Goldmann tonometry is practically unavailable (2.8%). The study results testify significant gap between Russian clinical practice and international standards requiring comprehensive measures on technical re-equipment and optimization of organization of ophthalmological care.
etudes.revue: Problemy sotsial'noi gigieny, zdravookhraneniia i istorii meditsiny

etudes.titre: Visual Field and RNFL OCT Testing Among Rural and Urban Residents With Glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « OCT »; mot du titre : « Visual Field »
etudes.resume:
IMPORTANCE: Rural populations face disparities in eye care; therefore, understanding the utilization of structural imaging and visual field (VF) testing for glaucoma monitoring among rural compared with urban patients is important.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether rural residence and sociodemographic factors are associated with patterns of VF testing and retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) optical coherence tomography (OCT) in patients with glaucoma.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective longitudinal cohort study used data from the Sight Outcomes Research Collaborative (SOURCE) consortium, a multi-institutional repository of US academic ophthalmic clinical data, from May 2012 to January 2025. Included patients had at least 2 separate dates of glaucoma billing codes, at least 3 years of follow-up data, and at least 1 VF or RNFL OCT test.
EXPOSURE: Rural vs urban residence, categorized by Rural-Urban Commuting Area codes.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcomes were utilization frequency (tests per year) and regular monitoring (≥1 test every 18 months) for VF and RNFL OCT. Testing frequency was analyzed using multivariable negative binomial regression, and regular monitoring was analyzed using logistic regression adjusted for sociodemographic characteristics and baseline visual acuity.
RESULTS: Among 48 196 patients, 45 843 (95.1%) lived in urban areas (25 613 [55.9%] female; mean [SD] age, 67.78 [12.71] years) and 2353 (4.9%) lived in rural areas (1272 [54.1%] female; mean [SD] age, 67.3 [12.03] years). Mean (SD) VF testing frequency was 0.91 (0.52) tests per year among rural patients and 0.91 (0.56) among urban patients; rural residence was not associated with regular VF monitoring (adjusted odds ratio [AOR], 0.95; 95% CI, 0.88-1.04; P = .28). Rural residence was associated with lower RNFL OCT frequency (mean [SD], 0.57 [0.45] vs 0.63 [0.47] tests per year; difference, -0.06 [95% CI, -0.08 to -0.04] tests per year; adjusted incidence rate ratio, 0.93 [95% CI, 0.88-0.98]; P = .004) and lower odds of regular RNFL OCT monitoring (AOR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.74-0.90; P < .001). Medicaid insurance was associated with lower odds of regular monitoring with VF (AOR, 0.35; 95% CI, 0.30-0.40; P < .001) and RNFL OCT (AOR, 0.62; 95% CI, 0.52-0.74; P < .001).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study, rural residence was associated with lower utilization of RNFL OCT but not VF testing, while Medicaid insurance was associated with lower odds of monitoring for both modalities. The findings suggest that ophthalmologists should be aware that rural patients with glaucoma may require additional attention to continuity of structural imaging.

etudes.titre: Ophthalmic Encounters After Tamoxifen Initiation.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
IMPORTANCE: Tamoxifen can cause retinal toxicity and vision loss, yet no formal screening guideline exists in the US.
OBJECTIVE: To characterize ophthalmic use after tamoxifen initiation, identify predictors, and compare 12-month use between those with breast cancer taking tamoxifen and those taking aromatase inhibitors.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a retrospective cohort study conducted May to June 2026 using All of Us data with 365-day minimum follow-up. The setting was a US multisite research program. Participants included adults with a first tamoxifen prescription recorded in All of Us, excluding those taking hydroxychloroquine. The comparator included those with breast cancer taking aromatase inhibitors.
EXPOSURES: Tamoxifen or aromatase inhibitor initiation.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was any ophthalmic encounter within 12 months, identified from eye examination, retinal procedure, and eye visit codes. Retinal optical coherence tomography (OCT) or fundus photography was secondary. Logistic regression assessed predictors and compared treatment groups after adjustment for demographics, preexisting conditions, preindex health care use, region, and initiation year.
RESULTS: Among 2327 individuals taking tamoxifen (mean [SD] age, 53.8 [10.6] years; 2232 [95.9%] female), 162 (7.0%) had an ophthalmic encounter within 12 months, and 39 (1.7%) underwent retinal OCT or fundus photography. Among participants with preexisting glaucoma or diabetic retinopathy, 22 of 88 (25.0%) had an encounter vs 140 of 2239 (6.3%) without either condition (difference, 18.7 percentage points; 95% CI, 10.8-28.8 percentage points; P < .001). Preexisting glaucoma (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 3.87; 95% CI, 2.12-7.06; P < .001), greater preindex health care use (aOR, 1.43; 95% CI, 1.24-1.63; P < .001), and older age (aOR per 10-year increase, 1.21; 95% CI, 1.04-1.42; P = .02) were associated with greater use. Among participants with breast cancer, 126 of 1886 individuals taking tamoxifen (6.7%) had an encounter vs 240 of 2809 individuals taking aromatase inhibitors (8.5%; difference, -1.9 percentage points; 95% CI, -3.4 to -0.3 percentage points; P = .02). After adjustment, tamoxifen use was not associated with greater ophthalmic use (aOR, 1.10; 95% CI, 0.85-1.42; P = .46).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Results of this cohort study suggest that ophthalmic use after tamoxifen initiation was uncommon, and retinal-specific testing was rare. Tamoxifen use was not associated with greater adjusted 12-month use than aromatase inhibitor use. Additional evidence on retinopathy incidence, natural history, screening strategies, and clinical benefit is needed to inform guidance.

etudes.titre: Archetypal analysis of visual field patterns in an African population: a data-driven approach.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « visual field »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: Visual field (VF) testing is essential for the evaluation of glaucoma, neurological, and retinal diseases. Interpretation, however, is subject to interindividual variability. Archetypal analysis, a type of machine learning, enables quantitative characterization of VFs. While prior studies have focused on predominantly Caucasian populations, no comparable investigation exists for an African population.
METHODS: We conducted an archetypal analysis of 8,766 VF measurements obtained with a Humphrey field analyzer (HFA) from 4,096 patients attending an ophthalmic imaging referral center in Kumasi, Ghana. Patients were referred for glaucoma, neuro-ophthalmic, retinal, or other perimetry-requiring examinations. Measurements with > 33% fixation losses or > 15% false-positive rates were excluded. Left-eye fields were mirrored to align with right-eye orientation. The optimal number of archetypes was determined using 10-fold cross-validation and Bayesian Information Criterion.
RESULTS: Patients had a mean age of 42.9 ± 19.6 years, with 56.7% female. Sixteen archetypes were identified (ordered by frequency), representing diverse VF patterns: normal VF, total scotoma, enlarged blind spot (superior/temporal), central scotoma, peripheral inferior arcuate defect, nasal hemianopia, upper eyelid artifact, peripheral circular paracentral scotoma, broad inferior defect, narrow inferior and superior arcuate defects, thin peripheral circular scotoma, temporal hemianopia, broad superior arcuate defect, and an artifactual defect without clinical correlate.
CONCLUSION: Archetypal analysis facilitates objective, data-driven extraction of prototypical VF patterns. Comparison with a North American HFA dataset showed substantial overlap (13/16 archetypes at cosine similarity > 0.7), alongside distinct differences that should be interpreted cautiously given differences in age distribution, referral characteristics, and clinical context between cohorts.
etudes.revue: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie

etudes.titre: Development of a Corneal Biomechanical Risk Score for Visual Field Progression in Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Visual Field »; mot du titre : « Biomechanical »

labos.nom: Program for Zhejiang Leading Talent of S&T Innovation
Key Research and Development Projects of Zhejiang Province

etudes.resume:
PRECIS: This study developed and internally validated an exploratory risk score model based on four Corvis-ST parameters to predict visual field progression in POAG. The model demonstrated acceptable predictive and risk-stratification performance.
PURPOSE: To develop a risk score model based on corneal biomechanical properties for predicting visual field (VF) progression in patients with primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG).
METHODS: This prospective clinical cohort study included POAG patients with a follow-up period exceeding 18 months and at least six reliable visual field examinations. The initial screening of relevant factors was identified using a dual-screening strategy that combined LASSO-Cox regression model and univariate Cox regression models. Then staged Cox regression models and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis were applied to evaluate the association between these factors and VF progression. Based on these analyses, a weighted integer risk score model was developed, and patients were stratified into low-risk, medium-risk, and high-risk groups.
RESULTS: A total of 129 patients were included, 46.5% of eyes showed progression, with a median progression time of 45 months. The final model incorporated velocity of applanation 1 (A1V), length of applanation 2 (A2L), time of applanation 2 (A2T), and pachymetry-adjusted intraocular pressure (IOP pachy). The risk score model predicted the outcome with a C-index of 0.701 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.620 - 0.760). It successfully stratified patients into groups with markedly different progression rates (Low: 17.2%, Medium: 45.7%, High: 76.7%; P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: This internally validated, exploratory risk score based on four corneal biomechanical parameters stratified POAG patients by risk of VF progression. Further validation is needed to determine its clinical utility.

etudes.titre: Longitudinal OCT Angiography Versus Structural OCT for Predicting Visual Field Progression in Glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « OCT »; mot du titre : « Visual Field »
etudes.resume:
PRCIS: In this longitudinal study, the rate of OCT angiography vessel density loss was an independent predictor of visual field progression in glaucoma, whereas the rate of structural OCT thinning was not.
PURPOSE: To compare longitudinal OCT angiography vessel density and structural OCT changes as predictors of visual field (VF) progression in open-angle glaucoma (OAG).
METHODS: This prospective study included 333 OAG eyes (110 normal-tension) followed quarterly for 4.1±0.9 years and 60 age-matched healthy controls examined at baseline and 6 months. Peripapillary capillary vessel density (pcVD), macular vessel density (mVD), peripapillary retinal nerve fibre layer thickness (pRNFLT) and macular ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer thickness (mGCIPLT) were measured. VF progression was defined by combined event- and trend-based criteria. Linear mixed-effects models compared rates of change; Cox models used cumulatively updated rates as time-dependent predictors.
RESULTS: Controls showed minimal change, with small statistically detectable declines in some parameters. Ninety-eight eyes (29.4%) progressed. Progressors showed faster pcVD (-0.73 vs. -0.56%/year, P=0.022) and parafoveal mVD loss (-1.12 vs. -0.40%/year, P<0.001). In advanced glaucoma, mVD loss remained associated with progression (P<0.001), whereas mGCIPLT (P=0.104) and pRNFLT (P=0.118) changes did not. In multivariable Cox analysis, parafoveal mVD rate (HR 2.15 per 1%/year faster loss, 95% CI 1.52-3.04) and pcVD rate (HR 1.82, 95% CI 1.34-2.47) were independent predictors (both P<0.001), whereas pRNFLT (HR 1.28 per 1 μm/y, P=0.158) and mGCIPLT (HR 1.41, P=0.071) were not.
CONCLUSION: Vessel density loss independently predicted VF progression, whereas structural OCT thinning was not; in advanced glaucoma, vessel density loss remained associated with progression in mixed-model analyses. Formal head-to-head comparisons were not performed.

etudes.titre: Interocular Asymmetry in Normal-Tension Glaucoma: Risk Factors for Unilateral Disease and Asymmetric Progression.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique

labos.nom: the Program for Zhejiang Leading Talent of S&T Innovation
the Key Research and Development Projects of Zhejiang Province

etudes.resume:
PRCIS: This prospective cohort identifies clinical features linked to unilateral presentation and different progression risk in NTG.
PURPOSE: This study aimed to identify determinants of asymmetric progression in bilateral normal-tension glaucoma (NTG) and compare interocular differences in patients with unilateral NTG.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This prospective cohort study enrolled 119 patients with NTG (238 eyes), including 48 bilateral (96 eyes) and 71 unilateral cases (142 eyes). Using a stratified grouping approach, eyes in the unilateral NTG group were categorized as affected eyes versus contralateral unaffected eyes based on diagnostic criteria. For the bilateral NTG group, eyes were stratified into high- and low-risk progression subgroups according to visual‑field progression rates. Interocular differences within each patient were compared.
RESULTS: In the unilateral NTG group, affected eyes exhibited higher baseline intraocular pressure (IOP; 15.13±3.35 mm Hg vs. 14.47±2.87 mm Hg, OR=1.56, 95% CI: 1.11-2.20, P=0.010) and larger optic disc area (2.12±0.42 mm² vs. 2.05±0.39 mm², OR=1.04, 95% CI: 1.00-1.07, P=0.048) than contralateral unaffected eyes. In bilateral NTG, high-risk eyes exhibited less negative spherical equivalent (SE; -1.40±3.17 D vs. -1.79±3.69 D, OR=2.34, 95% CI: 1.08-5.35, P=0.032), shorter axial length (AL; 24.10±1.52 mm vs. 24.21±1.38 mm, P=0.012), and higher disc hemorrhage prevalence (27.1% vs. 4.1%, OR=12.00, 95% CI: 1.53-93.99, P=0.018).
CONCLUSIONS: Larger optic disc area and higher baseline IOP are associated with unilateral manifestation in NTG. Disc hemorrhage and less negative SE are correlated with high-risk progression in bilateral NTG.

etudes.titre: The Associations of Plasma Brain-derived Neurotrophic Factor with Macular Structure and Visual Function in Open-angle Glaucoma: A Cross-sectional Study.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PRCIS: Plasma BDNF differed across glaucoma severity stages and was cross-sectionally associated with visual and structural parameters; in exploratory age-stratified analyses, the fitted csGCCT-BCVA relationship differed between younger and older patients.
PURPOSE: To compare the plasma level of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) in open-angle glaucoma (OAG) patients across disease stages and to examine its associations with visual and structural parameters.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 167 control (cataract) patients and 800 patients with OAG. Plasma BDNF level was measured using a bead-based immunoassay (Luminex). Clinical variables included best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), Humphrey Field Analyzer 24-2 indices, and swept-source optical coherence tomography measurements of superior, central, and inferior papillomacular central-strip ganglion cell complex thickness (csGCCT). Glaucoma severity was classified with the Anderson-Patella criteria. Exploratory generalized additive models characterized the central csGCCT-BCVA relationship by age group and by lowest versus highest quartile.
RESULTS: Plasma BDNF was lower in early and moderate glaucoma patients than in controls (P=0.006, 0.001) but higher in advanced than in early or moderate glaucoma patients (P=0.040, 0.006). The highest-BDNF-quartile glaucoma patients had worse BCVA and mean deviation (MD) than the lowest-quartile patients, with significantly lower central csGCCT. Among patients aged <60 years, the fitted central csGCCT-BCVA relationship differed between the highest and lowest BDNF quartiles, with higher fitted logMAR in the highest-quartile group at lower csGCCT values.
CONCLUSIONS: Plasma BDNF level differed across OAG disease stages and was associated with visual and structural parameters. Among younger patients, plasma BDNF quartile was associated with the fitted csGCCT-BCVA relationship. These cross-sectional findings do not establish temporal or causal relationships.

etudes.titre: Analysis of risk factors for glaucoma associated with environmental persistent pollutant exposure based on the NHANES database: Construction of a machine learning prediction model and exploratory pathway decomposition.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « machine learning »
etudes.resume:
OBJECTIVE: Glaucoma, an irreversible blinding eye disease, may be influenced by environmental pollutant exposure. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the associations between exposure to environmental persistent pollutants and glaucoma risk, and to explore the underlying pathogenic mechanisms.
METHODS: A cross-sectional analysis was performed using data from the U.S. National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), including 2272 participants. Baseline characteristics were summarized, and serum concentrations of 12 PFAS compounds and 4 heavy metals were measured. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline analysis, and subgroup interaction tests were used to examine associations between exposure levels and glaucoma risk. Exploratory pathway decomposition was conducted for key exposure factors nominally associated with glaucoma. Additionally, multiple machine learning models were constructed, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was applied for model interpretability. Glaucoma was defined by self-report, which may underestimate true prevalence and cannot distinguish glaucoma subtypes.
RESULTS: Participants with glaucoma had a higher prevalence of diabetes and hypertension, as well as higher blood lead and MPAH levels. In the primary analysis, inorganic mercury showed a nominal inverse association with glaucoma, whereas higher quartiles of MPAH and blood lead showed nominal positive associations. However, none of these associations remained statistically significant after Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction (minimum *q* = 0.128). Restricted cubic spline models indicated nonlinear dose-response relationships between some exposures and glaucoma risk. Multiple machine learning models achieved satisfactory performance in predicting glaucoma. Exploratory pathway decomposition suggested that the nominal association between MPAH and glaucoma risk might be partly mediated by pathways involving age, race/ethnicity, and blood pressure; however, these results should be interpreted with caution given the cross-sectional design and the lack of FDR-corrected significance.
CONCLUSIONS: Nominal associations were observed between certain PFAS compounds and heavy metals and glaucoma prevalence, but none survived FDR correction. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger studies. Interpretable machine learning achieved modest discrimination (AUC 0.62-0.74) for glaucoma risk, which may be adequate for population-level signal detection but not for individual diagnostic use. These findings provide epidemiological evidence and methodological support for identifying environmental risk factors, screening susceptible populations, and guiding early prevention of glaucoma.

etudes.titre: Adjunctive sub-tenon triamcinolone with Susanna glaucoma drainage device: a randomized clinical trial.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « drainage device »

labos.nom: Coordenação de Aperfeiçoamento de Pessoal de Nível Superior
Coordenacao de Aperfeicoamento de Pessoal de Nivel Superior

etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of Adjunct Triamcinolone (TA) with the Susanna drainage device for refractory primary open-angle glaucoma, to our knowledge, the first such evaluation with a non-valved glaucoma drainage device.
METHODS: This prospective, multicenter, randomized, double-blind (patient and outcome assessor) trial included 39 eyes with refractory primary open-angle glaucoma, divided into a control (n = 20) and a triamcinolone group (n = 19). Primary outcome was mean Intraocular Pressure (IOP) at six months. Secondary outcomes included success rates and postoperative complications.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics and mean preoperative IOP were similar (24.45±8.03 mmHg control vs. 24.95±6.80 mmHg TA, p = 0.83). At six months, both groups showed similar mean IOP reduction (14.05±3.99 mmHg control vs. 14.33±4.70 mmHg TA, p > 0.99), with percentage reductions of 42.53% and 42.56%, respectively. Hypotensive eyedrop use also decreased similarly (1.57 control vs. 1.16 TA, p = 0.95). Qualified success (IOP 5‒21 mmHg) was 90% (control) and 89.47% (TA) (p > 0.05). However, the triamcinolone group had a significantly higher incidence of late-onset hypotony (52.6%vs. 0%, p < 0.001). Clinically significant hypotony requiring surgical re-intervention occurred in 36.8% of the TA group versus 0% in the control group (p = 0.003).
CONCLUSION: In patients undergoing Susanna GDD implantation, adjunctive sub-Tenon triamcinolone provided no additional IOP-lowering benefit but was associated with a significantly increased risk of serious hypotony-related complications. Our findings do not support the use of sub-Tenon triamcinolone (20 mg) as an adjunct to non-valved GDDs in this setting.

etudes.titre: Macular Retinal Ganglion Cell Counts and Central Visual Field Sensitivity in Glaucoma: A Comparison of Logarithmic and Linear Scales.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Visual Field »
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND/AIM: To evaluate the structure-function relationship between mean central differential light sensitivity, scaled in decibels (dB) and linear units (1/L), and estimated macular retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) counts derived using Medeiros' integrated algorithms in glaucoma patients.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this study of 55 eyes, peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness was measured via spectral domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT), and functional sensitivity was assessed using 24-2 standard automated perimetry. Macular RGC counts were calculated from temporal sectors using Medeiros' formulas. Functional data averaged the 16 central perimetric points. Regression models and Pearson coefficients (r) compared both scaling methods.
RESULTS: Macular RGC count averaged 465,939.5±213,096.2. The logarithmic model (dB) demonstrated an exceptional fit [y=-47.96+5.86ln(x); adjusted R2=0.8891; r=0.9440; p<0.0001]. The linear model (1/L) showed a strong correlation (y=-133.62+0.0019x; adjusted R2=0.7647; r=0.8770; p<0.0001), explaining 12% less variance overall.
CONCLUSION: While the logarithmic scale offers superior overall fit, the linear scale (1/L) is clinically critical for detecting early, "silent" neural loss masked by perimetric data compression. These findings support optimizing the standard 24-2 grid through localized "macular cluster indices" to improve pre-perimetric glaucoma detection.

etudes.titre: Biobank analysis of canine eye disease variants identifies new breed associations and a potential X-linked Retinoschisin 1 disease model.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique

labos.nom: Mary och Georg C Ehrnrooths Stiftelse

etudes.resume: Canine inherited ocular diseases exhibit significant genetic heterogeneity, mirroring many human ophthalmic conditions. This study conducted an extensive screening of 90 OMIA-listed disease-associated variants across 192 affected dogs from 71 breeds to evaluate diagnostic utility and identify novel disease models. This screening identified previously reported variants in 35% of cases, while most cases remained unexplained, prompting whole-genome sequencing of a variant-negative case. This led to the identification of a novel candidate duplication c.442dupC in the X-linked Retinoschisin 1 (RS1) gene, located in the conserved discoidin domain of RS1. If validated, this variant may establish the first spontaneous canine model for human X-linked retinoschisis that may provide a new model for studying pathogenesis and therapeutic approaches. Our analysis also supported the expansion of the known breed distributions for several variants, including progressive retinal atrophy (PRA) variant IFT122 c.3176G>A in Finnish Lapphunds, PRA variant PDE6A c.1847del in Pomeranians, glaucoma variant ADAMTS10 c.1981G>A in East Siberian Laikas, and microphthalmia variant RBP4 c.90_92del in Jack Russell Terriers. The RPGRIP1 c.142_143ins[A[29]; GGAAGCAACAGGATG] PRA variant was observed in four new breeds; however, the reported phenotype was not sufficient to confirm the causative nature. Additionally, our data reclassified the JPH2 c.452A>C PRA variant as a common, benign polymorphism rather than a causal variant in Shih Tzus, emphasizing the need for large-scale genomic validation of published markers. Collectively, these results illustrate the extensive genetic heterogeneity underlying canine eye diseases and underscore the potential for identifying novel preclinical models that advance both veterinary medicine and human vision research.

etudes.titre: Ultrasound cycloplasty: dynamic efficacy and long-term safety in glaucoma patients from northwest China.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique

labos.nom: National Natural Science Foundation of China

etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To comprehensively evaluate the dynamic efficacy of UCP in treating different types of glaucoma patients in Northwest China, systematically analyze treatment outcome variations across follow-up time points, and assess long-term safety profiles.
METHODS: In a 1-year follow-up study, 24 patients (30 eyes) with various types of glaucoma were enrolled and underwent UCP treatment (10 sectors or 8 sectors). Follow-up visits were conducted at different postoperative time points (1 day, 1 week, 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, and 1 year). Follow-up assessments consisted of IOP measurements, IOP reduction from baseline, surgical success rate, 24-hour IOP fluctuation, pain score improvement, and complications. Furthermore, the correlation between IOP at the final follow-up and baseline IOP was evaluated.
RESULTS: 1. The overall IOP in all patients significantly decreased after UCP compared to preoperative levels (P < 0.01). 2. UCP demonstrated significant long-term IOP-lowering effects in patients with various types of glaucoma, with a 59.91% reduction at 1 year postoperatively. The efficacy was particularly notable in patients with primary angle-closure glaucoma, achieving a surgical success rate of 96.67% at 1 year. 3. Preoperative baseline IOP showed a positive correlation with IOP reduction at 1 year postoperatively (r s = 0.641, P < 0.01), indicating that higher baseline IOP was associated with greater IOP reduction. 4. UCP significantly improved IOP fluctuation, with the mean 24-hour IOP fluctuation decreasing from 10.6 preoperatively to 5.3 postoperatively (P = 0.001). 5. UCP exhibited acceptable safety, with significant reductions in pain scores (P < 0.05) and no severe complications such as hypotony or macular edema observed during follow-up.
CONCLUSION: 1. In glaucoma patients in the Northwest population, UCP demonstrates significant long-term and dynamic efficacy-the higher the baseline IOP, the more pronounced the IOP-lowering effect, with outstanding performance in stabilizing IOP fluctuations. 2. UCP exhibits acceptable safety and controllable complications. Postoperative IOP stabilizes by 3 months, allowing for gradual withdrawal of medications, making it a reliable treatment option for glaucoma.

etudes.titre: Transcriptomic profiling of normal and glaucomatous trabecular meshwork cells in a tissue-like soft ECM environment.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Transcriptomic »

labos.nom: State University of New York Upstate Medical University

etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: Trabecular meshwork (TM) dysfunction contributes to the elevated intraocular pressure in primary open-angle glaucoma. To better understand the "molecular signature" distinguishing glaucomatous from normal TM cells, we interrogated their genome-wide transcriptomic differences in a tissue-like soft extracellular matrix (ECM) microenvironment.
METHODS: Primary human glaucomatous and normal TM cell strains (N = 5 each) from three independent laboratories were plated on bioengineered collagen type I/hyaluronic acid/elastin-like polypeptide ECM hydrogels in 10% FBS media for 4-5 days, then serum-free media for 2 days. Cell-laden hydrogels were homogenized in TRIzol for RNA isolation, quality assessment, and library preparation, followed by paired-end 100-bp Illumina sequencing. Differential expression was assessed using DESeq2, including glaucoma status, originating laboratory, and donor age/sex in the model. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were defined as p < 0.05 and |fold change| ≥ 2, followed by Gene Ontology (GO) enrichment and QIAGEN Ingenuity Pathway Analysis (IPA).
RESULTS: In total, 588 DEGs distinguished the glaucomatous from the normal TM transcriptome (393 up-regulated in glaucomatous TM; 195 up-regulated in normal TM, i.e., down-regulated in glaucomatous TM). GO and IPA causal analyses revealed three coordinated disease programs: (i) TGF-β/Wnt-driven ECM remodeling and fibrosis, (ii) NF-κB-associated inflammation, and (iii) a hypoxia/metabolic-stress program linked to p300/CREBBP chromatin co-activation.
CONCLUSIONS: These data define a transcriptomic signature of glaucomatous TM cells when cultured in a soft physiologic ECM microenvironment, independent of the originating laboratory, with three mechanistic axes (ECM/fibrosis, inflammation, hypoxia/metabolism), and nominate p300 (encoded by EP300) as a candidate upstream node integrating these programs.

etudes.titre: Compatibility of 24-2C central extra test points with OCT and OCTA parameters in early-stage glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « OCT »
etudes.resume:
AIM: To facilitate structure-function analysis by evaluating the compatibility of newly added 10 extra test points in early-stage glaucoma cases with optical coherence tomography (OCT) and OCT-angiography (OCTA) glaucoma parameters in clinical practice.
METHODS: Cases diagnosed with primary open angle glaucoma underwent Humphrey 24-2C visual field (VF) test, OCT, and OCTA tests on the same day. The arithmetic average of the central 10 extra points in the 24-2C VF was calculated, and its compatibility with OCT and OCTA parameters was assessed. Patients with low signal strength OCT and OCTA images, high fixation losses in VF, intraocular pressure of 25 mm Hg and above, systemic vascular diseases [diabetes mellitus (DM), hypertension (HT)] were excluded from the study.
RESULTS: Totally 68 early-stage glaucoma cases (68 right eyes, 37 males) were included with the mean age of 64.52±8.89y. In the Spearman correlation test, all OCT and OCTA parameters except inside disc vascular density showed a positive correlation with the mean of additional VF test points (P<0.05 for all parameters, P=0.114 for inside disc vascular density). In multiple linear regression analysis, superior hemifield vessel density and whole image vessel density percentages were found to be significantly associated with additional points (P=0.029, 0.039, respectively).
CONCLUSION: It is known that specific regions of the macula may be sensitive to early-stage glaucomatous damage. This suggests that in early-stage glaucoma, attention should be paid to central points in addition to peripheral findings on VF. The compatibility of the mean of 24-2C SITA-Faster VF central extra points with the defined OCTA parameters may demonstrate the value of OCTA in diagnosis and follow-up in early stages for clinics without access to the new software VF devices.

etudes.titre: Glaucoma neurodegeneration: targeted modulation of intraocular immune pathways - a review of novel therapeutic advances.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « pathways »; mot du titre : « neurodegeneration »
etudes.resume: Glaucoma is the leading global cause of irreversible blindness, with its pathogenesis extending far beyond elevated intraocular pressure. Dysregulation of the intraocular immune system plays a central role in the progressive death of retinal ganglion cells. This review systematically examines the research progress on key intraocular immune pathways in glaucomatous neurodegeneration, with a primary focus on immune-inflammatory responses mediated by microglia, astrocytes, and T cells. It delves into the molecular mechanisms of various immunoregulatory networks, including the TLR4/nuclear factor kappa B (TLR4/NF-κB), Janus kinase/signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK/STAT), mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), complement, and T-cell receptor signaling pathways. The review analyzes potential therapeutic strategies targeting these pathways. By integrating the latest evidence from basic research and translational medicine, this article aims to provide a theoretical foundation and directional guidance for developing neuroprotective immunomodulatory therapies that go beyond intraocular pressure reduction.

etudes.titre: The 1-2-3 Rule: When to "Consider" Glaucoma Surgery and Discuss It With Patients.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Surgery »
etudes.resume: Earlier intervention is gaining momentum in glaucoma care, yet delayed referral and delayed consideration of surgery remain concerns in clinical practice. A simple clinical rule may help general ophthalmologists recognize when to discuss procedural options with patients. We propose the Shimane University 1-2-3 rule (SU1-2-3), comprising three prompts: intraocular pressure (IOP) >12 mmHg in progressive advanced glaucoma, with advanced glaucoma defined for this rule as visual field mean deviation ≤ -10 dB or glaucomatous visual field defects within the central 10°; IOP >20 mmHg despite topical treatment in perimetric glaucoma; or use of ≥3 bottles of IOP-lowering eye drops. Oral acetazolamide use is an additional, independent prompt. Meeting any criterion should initiate consideration of surgical options, shared decision-making, and specialist consultation when appropriate, rather than constitute an automatic indication for surgery. SU1-2-3 draws on evidence supporting IOP lowering, treatment-burden assessment, and procedural intervention, but its thresholds and clinical utility have not been prospectively validated. Because its components rely on readily available clinical information, SU1-2-3 may also facilitate consultation when glaucoma subtype classification remains incomplete. It is intended as a minimum safeguard against delayed consideration of surgery, while allowing earlier laser or surgical intervention according to individual needs. SU1-2-3 may serve as a practical clinical and educational reminder for ophthalmologists without glaucoma subspecialty training, general ophthalmologists, and ophthalmology residents.

etudes.titre: Integration of biomarkers in common retinal neurodegenerative diseases: a comprehensive review.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « biomarkers »
etudes.resume: Retinal neurodegenerative diseases (RNDs) are major causes of irreversible vision loss worldwide. RNDs majorly include age-related macular degeneration (AMD), diabetic retinopathy (DR), and glaucoma. Despite their distinct etiologies, these conditions share convergent mechanisms of retinovascular ischemia, neuronal apoptosis, and chronic inflammation. Physiologically, the retina and optic nerve are direct extensions of the central nervous system, sharing embryological origin, glial architecture, and neurodegenerative mechanisms with the brain, positioning them as an accessible model system for studying both ocular and systemic neurodegeneration. The growing field of ocular biomarkers thus offers objective, quantifiable endpoints for early detection, disease monitoring, and therapeutic evaluation of RNDs by bridging structural, functional, molecular, and genetic dimensions of retinal health. This narrative review synthesizes peer-reviewed literature published between January 2015 and May 2026, identified through PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science, on ocular biomarkers in AMD, DR, and glaucoma. Eligible studies reported original clinical or translational research assessing imaging, functional, molecular, or genomic biomarkers with quantitative associations to disease diagnosis, prognosis, or treatment response. Biomarker evidence is organized by domain to enable cross-disease comparison and integration, and each major biomarker is graded by clinical maturity, distinguishing routine clinical use, research validation, use as a clinical trial endpoint, and regulatory acceptance. Optical coherence tomography-derived retinal nerve fiber layer thickness in glaucoma and geographic atrophy area on fundus autofluorescence in AMD are the most established biomarkers in clinical care and trials, whereas disorganization of retinal inner layers and vessel density in DR, and dark adaptation and ellipsoid zone integrity in AMD, are well supported in research settings but not yet standardized for routine clinical use. Ocular biomarkers are reshaping precision ophthalmology, offering reproducible measures for diagnosis, prognosis, and therapeutic monitoring across retinal diseases. While several structural and functional biomarkers are nearing clinical adoption, standardized acquisition protocols, external validation, and regulatory qualification remain critical next steps. Integration of multimodal imaging, molecular analytics, and artificial intelligence-driven modeling holds promise for a unified, biomarker-based framework for early detection and individualized management of retinal neurodegeneration. Retinal biomarkers therefore carry dual relevance: they characterize disease within the eye and increasingly serve as accessible surrogates for central nervous system neurodegenerative processes, with broader implications for the field of neurodegenerative disease research.

etudes.titre: Bilateral same-day minimally invasive glaucoma surgery: single-centre review of safety and outcomes.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « minimally invasive glaucoma surgery »; mot du titre : « surgery »
etudes.resume:
OBJECTIVE: To report the efficacy and safety of bilateral same-day glaucoma surgery (BSDGS), specifically with minimally invasive glaucoma surgery (MIGS) procedures.
DESIGN: Single university centre longitudinal, consecutive case series.
PARTICIPANTS: A total of 63 patients (126 eyes) were included.
METHODS: This study reviewed all patients undergoing BSDGS between February 2022 and February 2025 at a university hospital in Montreal, Quebec. MIGS procedures included iStent trabecular microbypass, Hydrus Microstent, and bent ab interno needle goniotomy. All surgeries were performed by a single glaucoma specialist. Inclusion criteria included (i) bilateral glaucoma, (ii) need for intraocular pressure (IOP) or medication reduction, (iii) candidate for angle-based MIGS, and (iv) minimum 1 month follow-up. Exclusion criteria included (i) bleb-forming MIGS, (ii) gonioscopy-assisted transluminal trabeculoplasty, (iii) rapid progression, and (iv) less than 1 month follow-up. Outcome measures included changes in IOP, topical medication use, and visual acuity. All perioperative complications were recorded.
RESULTS: IOP and topical glaucoma medication use were significantly reduced (P < 0.05) at various follow-up visits. Adverse events occurred in 44 eyes (34.9%). Clinically significant adverse events occurred in 13 eyes (10.3%). Bilateral simultaneous adverse events were observed in 11 patients (17.4%). Bilateral complications included transient IOP spikes, hyphema or microhyphema, cystoid macular edema, and rebound uveitis. Overall, 9 eyes (7.1%) required anterior-chamber paracentesis for acute IOP control in the postoperative period. There were no cases of vision-threatening adverse events.
CONCLUSIONS: this is the first study to report safety outcomes of BSDGS using MIGS procedures. The intervention appears safe and effective relative to both unilateral MIGS and immediately sequential bilateral cataract surgery.
etudes.revue: Canadian journal of ophthalmology. Journal canadien d'ophtalmologie

etudes.titre: Pupilloplasty for glaucoma in CNA2-related cornea plana.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: A 7-year-old boy presented with progressive visual decline. On examination, visual acuity was no light perception in the left eye and 20/60 in the right eye. Examination showed bilateral microcornea, marked corneal flattening, shallow anterior chambers, abnormal iris configuration, and elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) in both eyes. The right eye had a slit-like pupil of 1 mm, and the left eye showed a closed pupil with very shallow anterior chamber and superior intercalary staphyloma. Keratometry values were significantly reduced, suggestive of cornea plana, which was subsequently confirmed by identification of a homozygous intronic variant in the KERA gene. These findings suggested pupillary block as the primary mechanism of glaucoma due to a functionally imperforate pupil. Pupilloplasty was performed in the right eye to create a functional pupillary aperture and relieve pupillary bock, and transscleral cyclophotocoagulation was performed in the left eye in view of the guarded prognosis. Following the interventions, IOP was controlled in both eyes with two antiglaucoma medications. This case highlights the tailored surgical approach because of complex anterior segment anatomy.
etudes.revue: Journal of AAPOS : the official publication of the American Association for Pediatric Ophthalmology and Strabismus

etudes.titre: Pediatric Endothelial Keratoplasty: A Modified Delphi Consensus by the EKLG Study Group on Indications, Surgical Techniques, and Postoperative Care.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Surgical »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To identify areas of consensus among global experts on the clinical management of pediatric endothelial keratoplasty (EK), including patient selection, timing, preoperative evaluation, technique selection, intraoperative standards, and postoperative care, and to provide a practical framework for surgeons earlier in their pediatric EK learning curve.
DESIGN: Modified Delphi-based global consensus study.
PARTICIPANTS: International ophthalmologists with expertise in endothelial keratoplasty and pediatric corneal diseases.
METHODS: A series of consensus statements on pediatric EK were developed from iterative rounds of structured questions and statements posed to a panel of experts. Two rounds of asynchronous electronic questionnaires were followed by a structured hybrid discussion of unresolved items. Experts responded anonymously to statements assessing consensus and to revised items addressing indications, contraindications, timing, preoperative workup, technique selection, intraoperative standards, and postoperative management. Results are reported using item-specific denominators because occasional non-response occurred across the survey items.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Consensus was defined as ≥70% agreement among the experts. Agreement between 60% and 69.9% was considered to be near consensus.
RESULTS: The consensus supported pediatric EK for congenital hereditary endothelial dystrophy, aphakic or pseudophakic corneal edema, persistent corneal edema in congenital glaucoma, X-linked endothelial corneal dystrophy, iatrogenic endothelial decompensation, and trauma-related decompensation. EK was inappropriate for severe anterior segment dysgenesis with keratolenticular or extensive iridocorneal adhesions. In Round 2, experts further endorsed EK for failed penetrating keratoplasty due to endothelial failure, congenital glaucoma with visually significant Haab's striae, and forceps injury involving the visual axis. There was a consensus that the timing of intervention should be guided primarily by amblyopia risk rather than by a specific age cut off. Essential preoperative assessments included examination under anesthesia, B-scan ultrasonography, anterior segment optical coherence tomography, intraocular pressure measurement, ultrasound biomicroscopy, and refraction. Experts agreed that ultrathin-DSAEK and DSAEK are the predominant techniques, whereas DMEK is currently selectively reserved, usually for older children with uncomplicated anterior segment anatomy. Preferred intraoperative principles included air tamponade, anterior chamber maintenance, and donor graft under-sizing relative to the corneal diameter. Postoperative recommendations included early intraocular pressure assessment, topical corticosteroid therapy for > 6 months, regular monitoring for steroid response, selective contact lens use, and individualized long-term follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: The consensus statements provide globally endorsed recommendations for the clinical management of pediatric EK. These guidelines are relevant for corneal specialists providing a practical framework to benchmark practice, reduce variability, and guide future multicenter investigations.

etudes.titre: A Retrospective Study of Ophthalmic Diseases in Companion Rabbits (Oryctolagus cuniculus): 297 Eyes From 205 Rabbits (2007-2022).
etudes.phase: Stade : Vétérinaire (animaux soignés) — hors veille principale
etudes.raison_rubrique: étiquette vétérinaire (revue vétérinaire (Veterinary ophthalmology))

labos.nom: Japan Agency for Medical Research and Development

etudes.resume:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the incidence of ophthalmological diseases in companion rabbits and the factors affecting incidence.
ANIMALS STUDIED: Client-owned rabbits (205 rabbits and 297 eyes).
PROCEDURES: We retrospectively investigated the incidence of ophthalmic diseases in companion rabbits of varied breed, age, and sex at a referral ophthalmology section in a single veterinary clinic.
RESULTS: The incidences of cataracts, glaucoma, uveitis, and corneal ulcers were relatively high. Multiple diseases occurred in one eye in 65 rabbits (31.7%) and 80 eyes (26.9%), overall; the most common combination was cataracts and uveitis. Glaucoma incidence increased with age (odds ratio (OR): 1.010, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.000-1.020; p = 0.007) and was less frequent in intact males (OR: 0.295, 95% CI: 0.094-0.927; p = 0.037) and spayed females (OR: 0.163, 95% CI: 0.042-0.638; p = 0.009) compared with neutered males. Uveitis incidence decreased with age (OR: 0.970, 95% CI: 0.958-0.982; p < 0.001; median: 1 year), and corneal ulcer incidence increased with age (OR: 1.010, 95% CI: 1.000-1.020; p = 0.007; median: 4 years). Holland Lops (73 rabbits, 116 eyes) and Netherland Dwarfs (63 rabbits, 82 eyes) were the two most frequently represented breeds. In Holland Lops, glaucoma and cataracts accounted for more than half of the ophthalmic diseases. In Netherland Dwarfs, the most common diseases were uveitis, corneal ulcers, tarsal plate abnormality, and glaucoma.
CONCLUSIONS: The incidence of some eye diseases in rabbits may be influenced by factors such as sex, age, and breed. These results can be useful in predicting ophthalmic diseases that are influenced by age, sex, and breed.

etudes.titre: Seasonal intraocular pressure variation in patients with primary open-angle or exfoliation glaucoma: a bidirectional encoder representations from transformers -based natural language processing analysis.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: Seasonal variations in intraocular pressure (IOP) are reported in glaucoma, but differences between subtypes and the influence of filtration surgery remain unclear. This study examined seasonal IOP patterns in primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) and exfoliation glaucoma (EXG) using electronic medical records analyzed with a Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT)-based natural language processing system.
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective observational study.
METHODS: We analyzed 1,679 visits from 352 patients (238 with POAG and 114 with EXG) at a Japanese university hospital between August 2020 and May 2023. Clinical parameters were extracted from electronic medical records using a validated BERT-based natural language processing model. Seasonal IOP differences between winter and summer and factors associated with IOP were evaluated using mixed-effects regression analysis.
RESULTS: Both POAG and EXG patients demonstrated significantly higher IOP in winter than in summer (POAG: 12.4 ± 3.3 mmHg vs. 12.0 ± 3.1 mmHg, p < 0.001; EXG: 12.4 ± 5.4 mmHg vs. 11.8 ± 4.2 mmHg, p < 0.001). The magnitude of seasonal IOP variations did not differ between glaucoma subtypes (p = 0.833); approximately 70% of patients in both groups exhibited higher winter IOP. Seasonal IOP elevation persisted regardless of filtration surgery history. Multivariate analysis identified age, systolic blood pressure, season, filtration surgery history, and medication score as independent predictors of IOP (all p < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: Intraocular pressure is higher in winter, regardless of glaucoma subtype or filtration surgery status. Filtration surgery lowers baseline intraocular pressure but does not eliminate season-related physiological influences.

etudes.titre: A quantum-inspired cross-attention fusion network for multi-class eye disease classification from retinal fundus images.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Automated screening of blinding eye diseases from colour fundus photographs is an active area of medical image analysis, yet many reported systems are validated on a single dataset and offer limited insight into their internal decision process. This study introduces QICAF-Net, a dual-branch deep learning framework that couples a Swin Transformer global-context branch with an EfficientNet local-lesion branch and fuses their representations through a novel Quantum-Inspired Cross-Attention Fusion (QICAF) module. The QICAF module reformulates cross-attention using the mathematical formalism of quantum states: token features are amplitude-encoded as complex unit vectors, transformed by a learnable norm-preserving unitary gate, compared through a fidelity-inspired similarity, normalised by a Born-rule measurement rule, and combined through an entanglement-inspired bilinear interaction. All operations are executed as classical linear algebra on conventional graphics hardware; no physical quantum computer and no quantum speed-up are claimed. The model was trained and evaluated on a balanced four-class retinal dataset of 4,217 fundus images spanning cataract, diabetic retinopathy (DR), glaucoma and normal categories. Under stratified five-fold cross-validation with six-view test-time augmentation (TTA), QICAF-Net attained a macro-F1 of 0.9358 ± 0.0113, an accuracy of 0.9367 ± 0.0112 and a macro one-versus-rest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.9914 ± 0.0023; a three-seed evaluation of the full model gave a macro-F1 of 0.9420 ± 0.0071. An 18-run multi-seed component ablation (six fusion configurations × three seeds) confirmed that the quantum-inspired components achieve accuracy statistically indistinguishable from strong classical fusion baselines, and a paired three-seed significance test between QICAF-Net and a matched dual-branch concatenation model returned no statistically significant accuracy difference (paired t-test p = 0.887; Wilcoxon p = 1.000). Against five single-backbone baselines under an identical preprocessing and TTA protocol, QICAF-Net was competitive but did not exceed the strongest backbones (Swin-Tiny 0.9583, ViT-Small 0.9487). The principal contribution of the module is therefore a novel and interpretable formulation rather than a raw accuracy gain. External validation on a heterogeneous independent cohort (N = 3,907) showed heterogeneous cross-dataset transfer - better preserved for cataract and normal and substantially degraded for glaucoma; under an observed external-domain shift the diabetic-retinopathy sensitivity fell to 39.61%, and under colour-constancy correction with six-view TTA the external accuracy was 0.8741 (95% CI 0.8633-0.8841) and the macro-F1 0.7188 (95% CI 0.6969-0.7398). Two complementary explainability methods together with visualisation of the QICAF attention indicated that the model attends to clinically plausible regions, most strongly the optic nerve head for glaucoma. Calibration, quantitative explanation-faithfulness (deletion/insertion) and profiler-based computational analyses were additionally performed. QICAF-Net is thus presented as an interpretable and transparently evaluated framework whose accuracy is on par with established fusion strategies while contributing a new attention formulation to the retinal imaging literature.

etudes.titre: Clinical Profile, Management Strategies, and Outcomes of Ocular Sarcoidosis: An Egyptian Multicenter Retrospective Study.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To characterize the clinical spectrum, investigations, management, and outcomes of ocular sarcoidosis in Egyptian tertiary referral centers.
METHODS: A retrospective multicenter review included 170 patients presenting to 10 tertiary centers diagnosed with definite, presumed, or probable ocular sarcoidosis according to the 2019 International Workshop on Ocular Sarcoidosis criteria between 2020 and 2024. Demographic, clinical data, imaging/investigations, treatment, and visual and treatment outcome data were analyzed.
RESULTS: Mean age was 37.2 ± 16.8 years, and 74.1% were female. Thirteen patients had definite sarcoidosis (7.6%), 53 patients presumed sarcoidosis (31.2%), and 104 probable sarcoidosis (61.2%). Bilateral disease occurred in 88.2% of patients. Uveitis was the predominant presentation, with panuveitis (43.4%) and intermediate uveitis (24.1%) being the most common. Cataract (46.5%), posterior synechiae (42.9%), cystoid macular edema (28.8%), and glaucoma (21.8%) were frequent complications. Serum ACE was elevated in 27% of patients, while chest imaging demonstrated hilar/mediastinal lymphadenopathy in 44%. Among 102 patients with available tuberculosis screening, 13.7% tested positive. Most patients received systemic corticosteroids with steroid-sparing immunosuppressive therapy. Categorical analysis of visual-loss severity demonstrated a significant shift, with 42 eyes improving by at least one category and 5 eyes worsening (p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Ocular sarcoidosis in Egypt commonly presents as bilateral panuveitis in young women. The variable findings on serum ACE, chest imaging, and tuberculosis screening highlight the need for an integrated clinical, ocular, and systemic evaluation when diagnosing ocular sarcoidosis. Early immunomodulatory therapy was associated with improved inflammatory control.

etudes.titre: Cognitive decline: A 10-year prospective study in glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy, and age-related macular degeneration.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the longitudinal association of glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy (DR), and age-related macular degeneration (AMD) with 10-year cognitive impairment, defined as a Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score <26, as well as to determine the predictive value of self-perceived visual function and retinal structural biomarkers for cognitive impairment. The 25-item Visual Function Questionnaire (VFQ-25) assesses self-perceived visual functioning and its impact on vision-related activities and quality of life. The Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) is a global cognitive screening test assessing domains including orientation, registration and recall, attention/calculation, and language, whereas the MoCA assesses a broader range of cognitive domains, including executive functions, visuospatial abilities, attention, memory, language, and orientation. Because some MMSE and, particularly, MoCA tasks involve visual or visuospatial components, performance may be influenced by visual impairment; both tests may also be influenced by educational level.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This monocentric prospective observational study included 360 adults aged ≥60 years (90 participants per group and 90 matched controls) followed for 10 years. Demographic, vascular, and psychosocial variables, best-corrected binocular visual acuity, VFQ-25 (25-item Visual Function Questionnaire), MMSE (Mini-Mental State Examination), and MoCA scores were collected. Retinal structure was assessed using swept-source OCT, including retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) and ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GCIPL) measurements. Evaluations were performed at baseline, 5 years, and 10 years. Adjusted Cox models, multivariate logistic regression, and longitudinal mixed-effects models were applied. No stratification of glaucoma or diabetic retinopathy according to clinical severity or stage was performed.
RESULTS: Cognitive impairment was more frequent in DR (54%), glaucoma (52%), and AMD (49%) compared with controls (27%) (P < .001). All ocular diseases remained independently associated with cognitive impairment after multivariate adjustment, with the highest risk observed in DR (HR 2.05). Higher VFQ-25 scores were associated with a lower risk of cognitive impairment, whereas GCIPL thinning showed an independent association with increased risk. However, participants with ocular disease had lower educational attainment, a higher prevalence of depression, and a higher comorbidity index at baseline than controls, and these baseline differences may contribute to the observed associations.
CONCLUSIONS: Chronic ocular diseases are associated with a higher 10-year risk of cognitive impairment. These findings should nevertheless be interpreted cautiously because of baseline imbalances in education, depression, and comorbidity, the potential influence of visual impairment on cognitive testing, the lack of severity stratification for glaucoma and DR, and the possibility of residual confounding and reverse causality. Self-perceived visual function and retinal structural biomarkers may represent indicators of neurocognitive vulnerability in aging.
