etudes.titre: Psychiatry of ophthalmology: proposing the ophthalmo-psychiatric disorders framework.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: We propose the ophthalmo-psychiatric disorders (OPD) framework as an organizing clinical and research model at the interface of vision science and mental health, and to synthesize, with wording calibrated to evidence strength, bidirectional relationships between ophthalmic disease, visual function, and psychiatric states. Visual impairment and common mental disorders co-distribute globally, with adults with vision loss showing roughly two-to three-fold higher prevalence of depressive and anxiety symptoms than visually normal peers. Elevated psychiatric comorbidity across glaucoma, dry eye disease, and age-related macular degeneration is supported by systematic reviews and meta-analyses, as is the benefit of psychological and stepped-care intervention. Mechanistic claims are weaker: hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal and autonomic dysregulation, inflammation, circadian disruption, central sensitization, and retinal neurodegeneration remain candidate pathways resting largely on cross-sectional data, and retinal findings in severe mental illness are group-level associations confounded by lifestyle, metabolic, medication, and imaging factors. The eye and the mind are anatomically and physiologically connected. The concept of OPD provides a pragmatic biopsychosocial framework that moves beyond an "organic versus non-organic (functional)" dichotomy and highlights the clinical intersection of the 2 fields. Progress will depend on interdisciplinary training, longitudinal research with harmonized definitions, and culturally sensitive implementation of eye-mind care.

etudes.titre: Outcomes of the Paul Glaucoma Implant for Refractory Glaucoma in an Indonesian Population.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PRECIS: The Paul Glaucoma Implant demonstrated favorable short- to mid-term outcomes in patients with refractory glaucoma in the Indonesian population. Low rates of postoperative hypotony following implantation were observed with the use of intraluminal 6/0 prolene stent.
PURPOSE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of the Paul Glaucoma Implant in managing refractory glaucoma in the Indonesian population.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective study reviewed patients who underwent implantation of the Paul Glaucoma Implant at the Kedoya and Menteng branches of the Jakarta Eye Center between September 2022 and January 2025.
RESULTS: 121 implantations from 113 patients were included, with a median follow-up of 12.00 (12.00 - 24.00) months. Median intraocular pressure decreased from 35.00 (28.25 - 43.00) mmHg preoperatively to 15.00 (11.00 - 18.00) mmHg at one year and 15.00 (12.00 - 18.00) mmHg at two years. Median glaucoma medication use decreased from 3.00 (3.00 - 4.00) to 1.00 (0.00 - 1.00). Median best-corrected visual acuity improved from 0.30 (0.02 - 1.47) logarithm of the minimum angle of resolution preoperatively to 0.15 (0.00 - 1.00) at one year and 0.10 (0.00 - 0.60) at two years. Overall success rate of the Paul Glaucoma Implant was 98.08% at one year and 92.68% at two years. Four implantations (3.30%) failed, including two requiring explantation and two failing to achieve the target intraocular pressure reduction. Hypotony occurred in six eyes (4.96%), all self-resolving. An intraluminal 6/0 prolene stent was employed for implantations and removed in 81 eyes (66.94%), with a median removal time of 3.00 (2.00 - 4.00) weeks.
CONCLUSION: The Paul Glaucoma Implant demonstrated favorable short- to mid-term outcomes, with substantial reductions in intraocular pressure and glaucoma medication use and a low rate of postoperative hypotony.

etudes.titre: The risk of rhegmatogenous retinal detachment associated with topical pilocarpine: a systematic review.
etudes.raison_rubrique: étiquette : produit suivi étudié (rôle suggéré, à vérifier)
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the risk of developing rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD) in patients treated with topical pilocarpine.
DESIGN: Systematic review.
METHODS: In October 2024 and March 2026, we searched six electronic databases (PubMed, EMBASE, CENTRAL, SCOPUS, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar) for comparative studies published through March 2026 to evaluate the risk of RRD in patients treated with topical pilocarpine. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials, cohort studies, and case-control studies comparing patients aged ≥ 40 years who received any dose, frequency, or duration of topical pilocarpine (for any indication) with an appropriate control group (placebo or an alternative topical ophthalmic therapy). We excluded non-randomized trials, case reports, case series, non-original articles, non-English studies, abstracts, non-human studies, studies without a control group, single-dose pilocarpine administration, pilocarpine as part of multi-drug regimens, non-topical non-ophthalmic routes of administration, participants < 40 years, and studies in which the control group also received pilocarpine. We conducted methodological quality and risk-of-bias assessments using the National Institutes of Health (NIH) quality assessment tools. Subsequently, a structured qualitative synthesis was conducted, summarizing key study characteristics, exposure parameters (e.g., pilocarpine dosing, formulation, and exposure duration), and RRD incidence. Study Methods are detailed in the full protocol developed prospectively and uploaded to PROSPERO (CRD420261305829).
RESULTS: We included 10 studies, with 5,421 patients in the pilocarpine groups and 5,443 in the non-pilocarpine groups, with some overlap due to one pooled analysis. Study designs were heterogeneous, with varying pilocarpine dosing regimens (0.2-4%, 1-4 times daily), sample sizes (13-4,494 patients per group), and mean participant ages (49-70.5 years). Exposure durations ranged from 14 to 30 days (short-term) to 24 months (long-term), and follow-up times ranged from 14 days to 24 months. RRD was rare, with no events reported in nine studies (1,876 participants). In one large retrospective cohort (8,988 participants), RRD occurred in 35 pilocarpine-exposed eyes compared with 15 controls, with a 3.14-fold increased risk (adjusted HR 3.14, 95% CI 1.66-5.93, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Because all reported RRD events derived from a single retrospective cohort and the remaining nine studies were event-free, quantitative pooling was not feasible and this review functions as a structured narrative around one dataset. The available evidence suggests a possible association between pilocarpine use and RRD, particularly in predisposed patients, but its low certainty means the finding should be considered hypothesis-generating, and larger prospective studies are needed to confirm it.

etudes.titre: Risk of Obstructive Sleep Apnea in Open-Angle Glaucoma: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PRECIS: In this retrospective population-based cohort study, patients with open-angle glaucoma were more likely to develop obstructive sleep apnea than matched controls from the general population of Olmsted County, Minnesota.
PURPOSE: To investigate the risk of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) in patients with open-angle glaucoma (OAG) compared to the risk of OSA in matched controls from a general population.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Retrospective population-based case-control study comparing the incidence of OSA with a diagnosis of OAG (cases) to the incidence of OSA in matched patients without OAG (controls) from Olmsted County, Minnesota between January 1, 1980 and December 31, 2018. Patients were identified using the Rochester Epidemiology Project. Medical records were reviewed to confirm OAG diagnoses. OSA diagnoses were based on sleep study data and polysomnography parameters. Cumulative probability of OSA was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method.
RESULTS: This cohort had 7,000 patients: 3,500 case patients with OAG diagnosed at any time point, and 3,500 matched control subjects without OAG, with all OAG and OSA diagnoses manually confirmed. There was no statistically significant difference of OSA frequency prior to index date in cases versus controls (P=0.52). There were 371 (12.5%) cases who developed OSA after glaucoma diagnosis compared to 297 (10.2%) patients who were diagnosed with OSA after the index date (P=0.0068). The multivariate hazard ratio for diagnosis of OSA after OAG diagnosis was 1.17 (P=0.047, 95% CI: 1.00, 1.36). The 10-year absolute risk of OSA after OAG diagnosis was 12.5%, and risk of OSA increased with time.
CONCLUSION: In this population-based study, patients with OAG were more likely to be diagnosed with OSA compared to patients without OAG, suggesting a possible association that may justify increased clinical awareness.

etudes.titre: Feasibility and Early Outcomes of Gonioscopy-Assisted Transluminal Trabeculotomy for Neovascular Glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Trabeculotomy »
etudes.resume: This retrospective observational case series evaluates the clinical outcomes of gonioscopy-assisted transluminal trabeculotomy (GATT) in 6 consecutive eyes with neovascular glaucoma (NVG) treated at a tertiary referral center. NVG was defined as secondary glaucoma associated with retinal ischemia, characterized by elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) and prior presence of iris and/or angle neovascularization. All patients had previously undergone pan-retinal photocoagulation and intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor therapy and were receiving maximally tolerated medical treatment at presentation. Circumferential GATT was successfully completed in all cases. At final follow-up, IOP control was achieved in 3 eyes with topical therapy, while the remaining 3 eyes required subsequent Ahmed glaucoma valve implantation due to early surgical failure. All eyes that met failure criteria demonstrated circumferential peripheral anterior synechiae formation during early postoperative follow-up and were observed in patients with poorly controlled diabetes mellitus. Two cases required anterior chamber washout for persistent hyphema. In this small case series, our observations suggest that clinical role of GATT remains uncertain and the present data do not allow identification of patient subgroups that may benefit or support definition of clinical indications.

etudes.titre: Comparative Accuracy and Safety of Large Language Models in Glaucoma Knowledge Assessment.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PRCIS: Across glaucoma MCQs, GPT-5.2, Gemini 3 Pro, and Claude Opus 4.5 were highly accurate, whereas DeepSeek-V3.2 underperformed; potentially harmful wrong answers were uncommon.
PURPOSE: To compare the accuracy and potential patient-safety risk of four large language models (LLMs) on glaucoma multiple-choice questions (MCQs).
METHODS: DeepSeek-V3.2, GPT-5.2 (via ChatGPT), Gemini 3 Pro, and Claude Opus 4.5 were tested on two American Academy of Ophthalmology datasets: 129 text-only AAO ONE Network glaucoma self-assessment questions and 32 text-only Basic and Clinical Science Course (BCSC) glaucoma study questions. Each item was queried once per model using a standardized prompt in a fresh session. Accuracy was compared using Cochran's Q and pairwise exact McNemar tests with Holm adjustment. Potentially harmful wrong answers (HW2) were coded using a prespecified rubric.
RESULTS: In AAO ONE, accuracy was 69.0% for DeepSeek-V3.2, 93.0% for GPT-5.2, 92.2% for Gemini 3 Pro, and 96.1% for Claude Opus 4.5 (Q=65.17, P<0.0001). DeepSeek-V3.2 was significantly less accurate than the other three models; differences among the other models were not significant. In BCSC, accuracy was 65.6%, 93.8%, 84.4%, and 87.5%, respectively (Q=18.00, P=0.0004); GPT-5.2 outperformed DeepSeek-V3.2 after correction. A post hoc item-level screen classified 38/161 questions (23.6%) as directly HW2-eligible; four HW2 events occurred and did not differ significantly across models.
CONCLUSIONS: GPT-5.2, Gemini 3 Pro and Claude Opus 4.5 achieved high accuracy on text-only glaucoma MCQs, whereas DeepSeek-V3.2 underperformed. Harmful errors were uncommon but present, underscoring the need for clinician oversight.

etudes.titre: Cerebrovascular Function in Glaucoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PRCIS: Glaucoma patients appear to exhibit variable cerebrovascular differences, including reduced MCA blood velocity and heterogeneous cerebral blood flow and neurovascular coupling responses.
PURPOSE: Glaucoma is associated with neurodegenerative and cerebrovascular diseases, such as dementia, migraine, and stroke, indicating a possible shared underlying pathophysiology of cerebrovascular dysfunction. However, no previous systematic review or meta-analysis has investigated whether people with glaucoma have poorer cerebrovascular function than those without. This study aimed to compare cerebrovascular function in glaucoma patients to healthy controls.
METHODS: Five electronic databases (Embase, Medline, PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science) were systematically searched until 28 October 2025 for full-text studies comparing measures of cerebrovascular function in people with glaucoma to controls. Meta-analyses were performed, where applicable, using mean differences (MD) and confidence intervals (CI) between glaucoma and control groups.
RESULTS: Qualitative analysis of sixteen observational studies revealed that glaucoma patients exhibited varying neurovascular coupling responses (both higher and lower than controls) across frontal, occipital, and parietal regions along with varying cerebral blood flow differences. Cerebral blood flow tended to be lower within the occipital and parietal lobes, and higher within the frontal lobe. Data from six observational studies were included in meta-analyses, which revealed glaucoma patients had lower systolic (MD = -16.38, 95% CI -27.96 to -4.80, P=0.006) and mean (MD = -6.50, 95% CI -11.99 to -1.02, P=0.02) blood velocities in the middle cerebral artery than controls. Sensitivity analyses indicated findings were sensitive to the inclusion of individual studies.
CONCLUSION: Glaucoma patients show heterogeneous cerebrovascular differences compared to controls, without a consistent directional or global pattern of dysfunction. Future longitudinal studies are needed to further characterise cerebrovascular measures in glaucoma.

etudes.titre: Defining the optimal duration of remote home tonometry for accurate characterization of intraocular pressure fluctuation.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « tonometry »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To determine the minimal duration of remote intraocular pressure (IOP) monitoring needed to yield accurate IOP fluctuation metrics in patients.
DESIGN: Secondary modeling analysis of retrospective data, validated with a large national database.
PARTICIPANTS: 397 patients from the Moran Eye Center and/or Wilmer Eye Institute and 1,579 patients from a MyEyes CorporationTM database who utilized an iCare HOME/HOME2 tonometer and recorded ≥3 measurements throughout each day over several consecutive days.
METHODS: Bootstrapped progressive day-censorship analyses and exponential decay modeling were used to estimate the number of monitoring days required to achieve 95% of the maximal model-based reduction in error for IOP metrics, including mean, maximum, range, and standard deviation (SD). Ground truth for each metric was defined using all available measurements within each eye-specific monitoring period. Sensitivity analyses assessing the effects of diagnosis, treatment, and three daily IOP measurements were also completed.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Mean absolute error (MAE) and mean relative error (MRE) for IOP mean, maximum, range, and SD; the number of monitoring days required to achieve 95% of the maximal model-based reduction in error.
RESULTS: Across both datasets, approximately 6-7 monitoring days were required to achieve 95% of the modeled reduction in error for daily mean, maximum, range, and SD of IOP in the primary analysis. Sensitivity analyses demonstrated longer monitoring requirements in primary open-angle glaucoma (9.1-10.0 days) compared with glaucoma suspects (5.5-6.7 days), secondary open-angle glaucoma (6.4-8.0 days), and primary angle-closure glaucoma (7.8-8.3 days). Monitoring durations remained relatively consistent before and after selective laser trabeculoplasty (8.4-9.0 days) and Hydrus microstent implantation (6.0-6.8 days). Restricting measurements to only three daily IOP recordings throughout the day extended monitoring duration to approximately 10 days in the Moran/Wilmer dataset and longer in the MyEyes dataset. Additionally, 74.1% of peak IOP measurements occurred outside typical clinic hours.
CONCLUSIONS: Remote tonometry provides clinically meaningful characterization of IOP metrics beyond traditional office-based measurements. Depending on the clinical context, seven to ten consecutive monitoring days consisting of measurements across each day are needed to represent a patient's true IOP pattern.

etudes.titre: External validation of a deep-learning algorithm for perimetric glaucoma detection on color fundus photographs in the Rotterdam Study.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « deep-learning »; mot du titre : « detection »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To externally validate a deep-learning (DL) algorithm detecting perimetric glaucoma on color fundus photographs (CFPs) in a population-based cohort.
DESIGN: External validation in a prospective population-based cohort.
PARTICIPANTS: Participants aged 50-80 years from three Rotterdam Study cohorts.
METHODS: We applied the winning Artificial Intelligence for Robust Glaucoma Screening (AIROGS) challenge algorithm, trained on 101,442 macula-centered CFPs to detect referable presumed perimetric glaucoma. Performance was assessed at eye and participant level, with participant-level cluster bootstrap confidence intervals. Misclassified cases underwent qualitative review. Longitudinal detection was evaluated by Kaplan-Meier analysis. Additionally, paired analyses compared macula- with disc-centered CFPs. A post-hoc analysis examined the effect of image quality on positive predictive value (PPV).
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Sensitivity at 95% specificity, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC), partial AUC (pAUC) for 90-100% specificity, PPV, and precision-recall AUC (PR-AUC).
RESULTS: Among 19,088 eyes (9,837 participants), 201 eyes (1.1%) had perimetric glaucoma. At eye level, sensitivity at 95% specificity was 70.6% (95% CI: 63.8-76.8), with an ROC-AUC of 0.911 (95% CI: 0.887-0.934) and a PR-AUC of 0.343 (95% CI: 0.274-0.427). At participant level, sensitivity was 68.8% (95% CI: 61.8-75.9) and ROC-AUC 0.909 (95% CI: 0.882-0.934). Overall, this resulted in 5.1 referrals per detected glaucoma case. True positives showed more advanced visual field damage than false negatives (median mean deviation -10.8 vs -5.8 dB; P < 0.001). Among true positives with prior imaging, 33 of 61 (54%) were flagged before conversion, typically 4-7 years before diagnosis. Discrimination in the 90-100% specificity range was higher for disc- than macula-centered CFPs (pAUC 0.860 vs 0.802; P = 0.003). PPV improved substantially after excluding CFPs with incomplete optic nerve head (ONH) visibility.
CONCLUSIONS: The DL-algorithm achieved meaningful discrimination for perimetric glaucoma in an external population-based dataset. Correctly identified cases were frequently flagged at an earlier examination, years before the perimetric diagnosis. Despite having been trained exclusively on macula-centered CFPs, the DL-algorithm showed no loss of discriminative performance on disc-centered CFPs. Incomplete ONH visibility was an important source of false positives. These findings support CFP-based deep learning as a scalable triage tool for glaucoma screening and highlight image acquisition standards for implementation.

etudes.titre: Topical Cyclosporine in Ophthalmology: Current Formulations, Clinical Applications, Advantages, and Limitations.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Cyclosporine A (CsA) is a calcineurin-inhibiting immunomodulator that suppresses T cell-mediated inflammation, a central mechanism in the pathogenesis of many ocular surface diseases. Following the systemic use of CsA in ophthalmology, topical formulations were developed to provide local immunomodulation at the ocular surface while keeping systemic absorption negligible. Since the approval of the first commercial ophthalmic emulsion in 2002, topical CsA has become a cornerstone disease-modifying therapy. Unlike corticosteroids, topical CsA provides sustained anti-inflammatory control without the long-term risks of glaucoma and cataract. Its highly lipophilic and poorly water-soluble nature, however, has posed a persistent formulation challenge, driving the development of diverse delivery platforms, including anionic and cationic oil-in-water emulsions, aqueous nanomicellar and nanoemulsion solutions, and water-free semifluorinated alkane vehicles. Despite sharing the same active molecule, these formulations differ in concentration, ocular surface retention, bioavailability, and tolerability. This review comprehensively evaluates these formulations in terms of their pharmaceutical delivery systems, concentrations, and clinical applications, together with comparative data on efficacy and safety across dry eye disease, vernal and atopic keratoconjunctivitis, Sjögren's-associated dry eye, ocular graft-versus-host disease, and high-risk keratoplasty. Topical CsA demonstrates a consistently favorable systemic safety profile, with ocular tolerability and a slow onset of action remaining its principal practical limitations. Individualized formulation selection, together with standardized head-to-head trials and biomarker-based approaches, will be key to optimizing the clinical use of topical CsA.

etudes.titre: Making better use of patients' time: feasibility of performing self-administered vision assessments in waiting rooms.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: Patients often spend significant time in clinic waiting rooms. This study assessed the feasibility of using this "wasted" time to perform self-administered vision assessments directly within the waiting area.
METHODS: Glaucoma patients attending routine appointments were asked to complete either a pen-and-paper (SpotChecks) or digital (PopCSF) contrast sensitivity (CS) test. Ambient illuminance, background noise, and crowd levels were recorded to assess potential environmental confounds. Test durations and patient feedback were recorded. Visual-Functioning Index-7 (VF-7) and Pelli-Robson CS (reference) test results were collected for comparison.
RESULTS: Of 173 patients approached, 155 (89.6%) agreed to participate, and 151(97.4%) participants completed testing before their appointment (77/78 pen-and-paper; 74/74 digital). Environmental factors had no significant impact (all P > 0.05). Median completion times were 3.0 {2.6-4.5} minutes (pen-and-paper) and 2.5 {2.0-3.5} minutes (digital). Age did not impact the pen-and-paper test duration (P = 0.944) but weakly correlated with the digital test duration (rdigital = 0.27, P = 0.020). Functional CS scores correlated with Pelli-Robson reference measurements (rpen-and-paper = 0.81; rdigital = 0.62), age (rpen-and-paper = -0.58; rdigital = -0.37), logMAR visual acuity (rpen-and-paper = -0.42; rdigital = -0.44), and visual field mean deviation scores (rpen-and-paper = -0.54; rdigital = -0.63). Both tests were highly acceptable to patients ( > 80% on all questions). Visit durations were longer for participants (109 vs 88 min, P = 0.007), but this was attributed to consenting and related research activities rather than the tests themselves.
CONCLUSIONS: This proof-of-concept study demonstrates that it is feasible for patients to self-administer portable vision tests in clinic waiting rooms. Using CS as a representative example, this approach may enable additional data collection, potentially improving patient management, clinic flow, and/or patient satisfaction.

etudes.titre: The Royal College of Ophthalmologists' National Ophthalmology Database: report 15, severe vision loss following cataract surgery.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « surgery »
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: To investigate rates of severe vision loss post-cataract surgery.
SUBJECTS/METHODS: Post-cataract severe vision loss (SVL) was defined as a loss of ≥0.60 LogMAR between preoperative presenting visual acuity and postoperative visual acuity. The term 'legally blind' was used for eyes with a corrected visual acuity worse than 1.30 LogMAR. Between 2010 and 2024, there were 1,750,553 eligible operations performed on 1,217,267 patients by 3766 surgeons from 132 centres supplying data to the Royal College of Ophthalmologists National Ophthalmology Database Cataract Audit.
RESULTS: Severe vision loss was recorded in 3723 (0.21%) eyes, including 3 eyes (2 patients) from 2 718 immediate sequential bilateral cataract surgery (ISBCS) eyes. The highest observed SVL rate was 10.68% for eyes recorded as left aphakic after surgery and the second highest observed SVL rate (3.32%) was when posterior capsular rupture occurred. The SVL rate was higher than the overall rate for eyes with previous intravitreal injections (0.76%), eyes with optic nerve or central nervous system problems (0.74%), age-related macular degeneration (0.52%), previous vitrectomy surgery (0.49%), diabetic retinopathy (0.45%), glaucoma (0.42%) or corneal pathology (0.33%). Of 1,642,386 (93.8%) eyes that were not preoperatively legally blind, 2731 (0.2%) were postoperatively legally blind. Of these, 2294 (84.0%) eyes experienced severe vision loss.
CONCLUSIONS: Severe vision loss from any cause following cataract surgery occurs infrequently. However, it has a higher prevalence in eyes left aphakic, when PCR occurs and for certain ocular comorbidities.

etudes.titre: Dislocated crystalline lens into the suprachoroidal space after blunt ocular trauma: a case report and diagnostic challenge.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « diagnostic »
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: The posterior dislocation of the crystalline lens into the suprachoroidal space after closed-globe trauma is an exceptionally rare entity. Lens preservation is one of the treatment strategies.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 55-year-old male presented with severe visual impairment three days after a closed-globe injury to his right eye. Clinical examination revealed corneal edema, total hyphema, and ocular hypertension. B-scan ultrasonography suggested vitreous hemorrhage and choroidal detachment, while orbital computed tomography (CT) confirmed an intact ocular wall and lens dislocation. Surgical exploration via vitrectomy unexpectedly revealed a superotemporal ciliary body detachment and the crystalline lens incarcerated within the nasal suprachoroidal space. The patient was managed with ciliary body suturing and silicone oil tamponade without lens extraction, achieving favorable anatomical and functional outcomes at follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: Lens preservation is a feasible strategy in cases of posterior dislocation of the crystalline lens into the suprachoroidal space after closed-globe trauma, provided that the lens capsule remains intact and there is no evidence of inflammation or elevated intraocular pressure.

etudes.titre: Axon Content of the Circumpapillary Nerve Fiber Layer in Experimental Glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: étiquette : stade préclinique (indexation PubMed)
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To determine axonal content from optical coherence tomography (OCT)-derived circumpapillary retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) measures using histologically informed models in a non-human primate experimental glaucoma model.
METHODS: Unilateral experimental glaucoma was induced in 22 animals (mean age, 6.1 ± 1.9 years; 10 females) who were monitored with OCT. At varying stages of neuropathy, animals were euthanized and perfusion fixed. For RNFL histology, circumpapillary tissue (∼0.75 × 0.75 mm) from six equally spaced regions was obtained and processed for serial block face scanning electron microscopy in five animals. A single high-resolution image of the block face was used to quantify axon size (cross-sectional area) and non-axonal tissue area within the RNFL. Using the 95% limits of the histological data as a starting point, models for estimating axon count from OCT RNFL area were optimized and compared to total retrobulbar optic nerve axon counts in 22 animals.
RESULTS: The mean circumpapillary RNFL thickness of control eyes was 112 ± 6 µm, and it was 70 ± 24 µm in eyes with experimental glaucoma. Axon size and non-axonal area varied across the circumpapillary regions (F5, 31 = 9.06 and F5, 36 = 3.94, respectively; both P < 0.01), but did not differ between the two eyes (F1, 22 = 0.59, P = 0.45 and F1, 15 = 2.10, P = 0.17). The optimized model for estimating axon content from the circumpapillary RNFL profile had good agreement with the retrobulbar axon count (mean difference = 25; 95% limits of agreement, -334,239 to 334,289).
CONCLUSIONS: The axon size distribution and non-axonal area in the circumpapillary RNFL are similar between healthy and stable glaucomatous eyes. Building on this, a location-specific model is proposed that estimates axon content from the circumpapillary RNFL profile after accounting for regional variability in axonal and non-axonal components.

etudes.titre: Reading disability in glaucoma: A neglected dimension of visual disability.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Reading disability is a common and clinically relevant, yet under-recognized, functional impairment in glaucoma, with significant impact on independence, daily activities, and quality of life, particularly in an increasingly digital environment. Reading performance is influenced by a complex interplay of visual field loss, reduced contrast sensitivity, oculomotor dysfunction, and cognitive load. Patients typically exhibit reduced reading speed, increased fixation instability, and altered saccadic patterns, even in the presence of preserved visual acuity. The severity and spatial distribution of visual field defects play a key role in determining impairment, as central and paracentral defects may disrupt fixation and letter recognition, while peripheral loss can impair text navigation and eye movement guidance. Additionally, glaucoma therapies may indirectly contribute to reading impairment through detrimental effects on ocular surface health and overall visual quality. Assessment remains challenging due to the lack of standardized, glaucoma-specific tools. Available tests capture complementary aspects of reading function, while patient-reported outcomes provide insight into perceived disability but only partially address reading. Evidence on interventions is heterogeneous. Assistive devices show the most consistent benefits, whereas rehabilitation strategies and emerging technologies remain insufficiently validated, with particularly limited evidence in glaucoma-specific populations. Reading disability represents a rapid and clinically accessible measure of functional impairment that may complement structural and perimetric assessment in glaucoma. Given its impact on quality of life, independence, and near-vision demands in an increasingly digital world, reading performance should be more regularly evaluated in clinical practice, while a better understanding of the underlying mechanisms may help guide targeted rehabilitation strategies.

etudes.titre: Clinical and ocular factors associated with visual field progression following optic disc haemorrhage in glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « visual field »
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: To investigate the structural and clinical factors linked to visual field (VF) progression in glaucomatous eyes after the initial detection of optic disc haemorrhage (DH) in patients with primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG).
METHODS: This study included 92 eyes of 92 patients who presented with at least one optic DH on stereoscopic optic disc and red-free photography. The included patients had a minimum follow-up of 3 years after initial detection of DH and at least 5 reliable standard automated perimetry investigations. VF progression was assessed using event-based guided progression analysis (GPA). Baseline demographic, clinical, and ocular parameters were examined using Cox proportional hazards regression to identify the independent predictors of functional deterioration.
RESULTS: Among the patients, 32 (34.8%) showed VF progression and 60 (65.2%) remained stable. In univariate analysis, recurrent DH, longer axial length, thinner central corneal thickness (CCT), and intraocular pressure (IOP) fluctuation were significantly associated with VF progression. In multivariate analysis, recurrent DH (HR 4.008, p < 0.001), longer axial length (HR 1.287, p = 0.005), thinner CCT (HR 0.865, p = 0.005), and greater IOP fluctuation (HR 1.997, p = 0.032) remained independently associated with VF progression.
CONCLUSIONS: Recurrent DH, longer axial length, thinner CCT, and greater IOP fluctuation were independently associated with VF progression following optic DH. These factors may help identify glaucomatous eyes at higher risk of progression and support closer clinical monitoring after the initial detection of DH.

etudes.titre: Ocular Considerations for the Department of War's New Testosterone Initiative.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: On 15 July 2026, the Secretary of War announced that the Department of War will begin annual testosterone deficiency screening for male Active Duty and Reserve Component personnel aged 30 and older as part of the periodic health assessment, with screening available on request to younger servicemembers. This policy will increase testosterone testing and may increase testosterone replacement therapy (TRT). Primary care, flight, and operational medicine providers will be on the front line of a hormonal intervention with possible ocular implications. This Commentary summarizes the ophthalmic manifestations of low and elevated testosterone states relevant to a military population and proposes pragmatic recommendations for providers implementing this initiative. Screening identifies testosterone concentrations, not symptoms of deficiency, and should not be equated with an indication for treatment. Androgen deficiency is associated with meibomian gland dysfunction and evaporative dry eye, but benefit from replacement remains unproven. The evidence linking testosterone exposure to central serous chorioretinopathy, retinal vascular occlusion, and intracranial hypertension is real but heterogeneous. Cohort findings, case reports, and observations in transgender patients do not establish a common risk in hypogonadal male servicemembers. Glaucoma findings are similarly mixed. We propose a brief, targeted ocular history, symptom counseling and inquiry during TRT follow-up and periodic health assessments, and referral according to clinical urgency. For vision-critical specialties, baseline dilated examination should be coordinated through existing occupational clearance processes when an adequate recent examination is unavailable. These measures are precautionary; screening benefit and an optimal repeat-examination interval have not been established. The Military Health System is uniquely positioned to prospectively answer the ocular questions this literature has only partially resolved.

etudes.titre: Prevalence and OCT Characteristics of Glaucoma-Like Optic Neuropathy in a Real-World Population.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « OCT »
etudes.resume:
PRCIS: Based upon a real-world data set, the prevalence of subtle glaucoma-like defects in the macula is underestimated.
PURPOSE: To understand the prevalence and characteristics of glaucoma-like defects in a large real-world data set using optical coherence tomography (OCT) and an OCT-based Reading Center (OCT-RC) approach.
METHODS: OCT scans were analyzed from 6184 individuals tested at optometric sites involved in refractive care. Based on commercial widefield OCT reports, foveal B-scans, and a previously published OCT-RC method, 361 individuals had evidence of optic neuropathy consistent with glaucoma in 1 or both eyes [ON-G (RC)]. Using the Columbia University (CU) OCT method, 2 experienced graders also labeled eyes as "ON-G (CU)" and "Not ON-G (CU)," based only upon the OCT report.
RESULTS: As expected, prevalence of pathology increased with age: 2.9% aged 50 years or older to 27.5% ≥70 years or older, with ON-G increasing from 2.1% (<50 y) to 14.2% (≥70 y). 320 (88.6%) of 361 ON-G eyes had macular damage, and 59 (16.3%) had thin arcuates largely restricted to the thick ganglion cell layer (GCL) region of the central macula. ON-G severity increased with age as indicated by central macular involvement. Using the CU method, 18% of ON-G individuals were judged as "Not ON-G (CU)."
CONCLUSIONS: Glaucoma-like optic neuropathy was common in this real-world population and was characterized by frequent macular involvement, including early central GCL arcuate defects. These findings support the value of careful macular OCT assessment for identifying early glaucomatous structural damage.

etudes.titre: INDIVIDUAL ARTICLE: Topical Corticosteroid Approved Labeling in the US: A Modern Inter- and Intra-Product Analysis.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: A wide variety of prescription-strength topical corticosteroids (TCS) have been commercially available for many decades. Product labels often vary, reflecting inconsistent guidance for dosing, duration of use, and safety.
OBJECTIVE: This study was designed to analyze and compare dosing and safety information among TCS product labels approved by the United States (US) Food and Drug Administration (FDA).
METHODS: The FDA's openFDA Public Label API was used to collect US TCS labels. The content of each label was searched for safety terminology and quantitative use limits. These data were assessed for consistency across products.
RESULTS: Warnings for a variety of adverse events (AEs) were found in TCS labels including, but not limited to, allergic contact dermatitis, skin infections, hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis suppression and Cushing syndrome, cataracts and glaucoma, and carcinogenesis. However, none of these warnings were included in all labels and were inconsistent among labels for the same active ingredient. Recommended limits on treatment duration and total weekly dose were included in some labels (35% and 22%, respectively) but many had no limits. If TCS are applied as described in the labels, patients with ~15% or greater affected body surface area will exceed weekly dose limits for HPA axis suppression.
CONCLUSIONS: FDA-approved product labels are intended to inform clinical decision support systems. TCS product labels unfortunately do not contain warnings for known AEs and have inconsistent or absent dosing recommendations. Lack of guidance and inconsistent safety information diminish awareness of the risks associated with long-term use and/or overuse of these medications and can impact access. TCS label review and revision are warranted to eliminate inconsistency, modernize language around warnings and precautions, and provide clear dosing instructions and exposure limits to better inform clinicians, patients, and caregivers about safe use of these medications.

etudes.titre: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists and the Eye: Ocular Safety, Retinal Outcomes, and Clinical Implications.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Agonists »
etudes.resume: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists have transformed the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, but rapidly expanding use has generated concern about ocular adverse events. In Korea, newly established national health insurance reimbursement criteria for injectable semaglutide (Ozempic prefilled pen) took effect on February 1, 2026; as use among eligible patients may expand, proportionate ophthalmic preparedness is timely. This structured narrative review evaluates randomized trials, systematic reviews, large pharmacoepidemiologic studies, mechanistic investigations, and regulatory assessments through June 30, 2026. The evidence does not support a single class-wide syndrome of ocular toxicity. The most coherent retinal signal is early worsening of diabetic retinopathy during rapid glycemic improvement, particularly in eyes with substantial pre-existing disease; available trial and real-world evidence does not demonstrate a uniform sustained toxic effect. Nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy is a rare but clinically important semaglutide safety signal. Multiple observational studies and regulatory action justify vigilance, although effect estimates remain heterogeneous and the absolute risk is low. Evidence for neovascular age-related macular degeneration is conflicting, whereas reported associations with retinal vein occlusion and glaucoma remain exploratory. For retina specialists, management should be phenotype based: identify active or advanced diabetic retinopathy, avoid delaying indicated retinal treatment, document the timing and trajectory of metabolic change, and urgently evaluate sudden painless visual loss or field defects. This approach preserves the substantial systemic benefits of incretin therapy while improving recognition of uncommon but consequential ocular events.

etudes.titre: Exploring Elimination Profiles and Metabolite Patterns of Brinzolamide and Dorzolamide After Transdermal Exposure for Doping Control Purposes.
etudes.raison_rubrique: étiquette : produit suivi étudié (rôle suggéré, à vérifier)

labos.nom: Manfred Donike Institute for Doping Analysis e V
Federal Chancellery of the Federal Republic of Germany

etudes.resume: Brinzolamide (BA) and dorzolamide (DA) are carbonic anhydrase inhibitors (CAIs), commonly used for glaucoma treatment via topical application. Under the World Anti-Doping Agency Prohibited List, both substances are prohibited in- and out-of-competition, except when administered ophthalmically. In anti-doping testing, adverse analytical findings (AAFs) may arise not only from intentional misuse but also from unintentional exposure or contamination. Although elimination characteristics after oral or ocular administration have been described, little is known about the systemic uptake and metabolic behaviour of these substances following dermal exposure. Therefore, the present study investigates the transdermal absorption of BA and DA under controlled conditions to characterize elimination profiles and metabolite patterns. Two groups of 12 volunteers received dermal applications of AZOPT brinzolamide (10 mg/mL) and TRUSOPT dorzolamide (20 mg/mL) at doses of 1 and 6 mg per substance, applied to the lower forearm skin. Urine samples were collected before application and up to 168 h post-application, and dried blood spot (DBS) samples were collected for up to 3 weeks. Samples were analysed by liquid chromatography-high-resolution tandem mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS/MS) for parent compounds and selected metabolites. Concentrations in DBS and urine samples were corrected for haematocrit (Hct) and urine specific gravity (SG), respectively. Subsequently, relative metabolite-to-parent ratios were calculated to describe matrix-dependent metabolic profiles after dermal exposure. BA and DA were detectable in both urine and DBS after transdermal application, with detection windows increasing in a dose-dependent manner. In the low-dose group, only four participants showed detectable urinary concentrations within the first 2 days post-application, whereas both compounds remained detectable in DBS for up to 3 weeks. High doses resulted in greater peak concentrations and prolonged detectability. Parent compounds and N-desethyl metabolites were identified, with matrix-dependent differences in detectability and relative abundance. Systemic absorption was confirmed at concentration levels that may lead to AAFs in routine doping controls.

etudes.titre: Clinical value evaluation of MEG3/miR-144-3p as a biomarker for the early diagnosis of glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « diagnosis »; mot du titre : « biomarker »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: LncRNA MEG3 and miR-144-3p have been confirmed to be related to ocular pathological processes, but their roles as early diagnostic biomarkers for Primary open angle glaucoma (POAG) and the underlying regulatory mechanisms remain unclear.
METHODS: The targeting relationship between MEG3 and miR-144-3p was verified by the dual luciferase reporter gene assay. MEG3 and miR-144-3p expression were detected by real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). ROC curves and correlation analysis were used to evaluate the diagnostic value and correlation of MEG3 and miR-144-3p. NaIO3 was used to treat retinal ganglion cells (RGCs), CCK-8 was used to measure cell proliferation and survival rate, and ELISA was used to detect levels of CAT, MDA, and inflammatory factors (IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β).
RESULTS: MEG3 and miR-144-3p have a targeting relationship. Compared with the healthy control group, the expression of MEG3 in tears and serum of patients with early POAG was significantly increased, while the expression of miR-144-3p was decreased. ROC analysis showed that MEG3 (serum AUC = 0.899; tears AUC = 0.894) and miR-144-3p (serum AUC = 0.877; tears AUC = 0.873) had excellent diagnostic efficacy for early POAG. In RGCs, silencing MEG3 or overexpressing miR-144-3p could alleviate NaIO3-induced cell damage, inflammation, and oxidative stress.
CONCLUSION: MEG3 and miR-144-3p form a regulatory axis involved in glaucoma pathogenesis. Their abnormal expression in tears and serum makes them promising non-invasive biomarkers for early POAG diagnosis. The aqueous humor samples used in the study were solely for the analysis of the correlation of regulatory mechanisms.

etudes.titre: Blood pressure and intraocular pressure in the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging: a bidirectional Mendelian randomization analysis.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To investigate the association of blood pressure (BP) with intraocular pressure (IOP), determine whether these associations are modified by genetic susceptibility to elevated IOP, and assess potential causality using Mendelian randomization (MR).
METHODS: Cross-sectional analyses were conducted using baseline data from the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging (CLSA) Comprehensive Cohort. Non-closely related participants of European descent with complete data for IOP and BP were eligible for individual-level data analyses (N = 21,633). Associations of systolic BP (SBP), diastolic BP (DBP) and pulse pressure (PP) with corneal-compensated IOP were assessed using multivariable linear regression. An IOP polygenic risk score (PRS) was used to measure genetic susceptibility to elevated IOP. One-sample and two-sample MR analyses were conducted to evaluate potential causality.
RESULTS: Multivariable linear regression found SBP, DBP, and PP to be positively associated with IOP after adjustment for relevant covariates (P ≤ 3.82 × 10-17). Interaction analyses did not find the IOP PRS to influence these associations (P ≥ 0.122). One-sample MR found genetically predicted SBP to be positively associated with IOP (β = 0.227 mm Hg per 10 mmHg increase in SBP, 95% confidence interval (CI) [0.074, 0.381], P = 0.004). Reverse one-sample MR did not provide evidence of IOP having a causal effect on BP (P ≥ 0.103). Similar results for the observational and bidirectional one-sample MR analyses were obtained after excluding participants taking IOP-lowering or antihypertensive medications. Two-sample MR provided some evidence of a positive causal effect of SBP on IOP. Significant positive associations were observed using the inverse-variance weighted multiplicative random-effects (IVW-MRE; β = 0.216 mmHg per 10 mmHg increase in SBP, 95% CI [0.043, 0.390], P = 0.015), MR contamination mixture (MR-ConMix; β = 0.314 mmHg per 10 mmHg increase in SBP, 95% CI [0.134, 0.565], P = 0.001), and MR Pleiotropy RESidual Sum and Outlier (MR-PRESSO; β = 0.239 mmHg per 10 mmHg increase in SBP, 95% CI [0.075, 0.402], P = 0.004) methods. However, there was evidence of directional pleiotropy based on the MR-Egger intercept test (P = 0.049). Similar two-sample MR results were obtained using IOP summary statistics from that CLSA after excluding participants taking IOP-lowering medications, although the MR-Egger intercept test was non-significant (P = 0.062). Analyses using Steiger-filtered genetic instruments provided some support for the primary two-sample MR results, but not the primary one-sample MR results.
CONCLUSION: SBP, DBP, and PP are positively associated with IOP and genetic susceptibility to elevated IOP does not appear to modify these associations. One-sample and two-sample MR analyses provided some evidence of a potential causal effect of SBP on IOP. If confirmed, a causal effect of BP on IOP could lead ophthalmologists treating elevated IOP to encourage their patients to also have their BP under control.

etudes.titre: Clinical Features and Outcomes of Glaucoma Surgery-Associated Bullous Keratopathy: A Subanalysis of the Japanese National Survey on Corneal Transplantation.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Surgery »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: The purpose of this study was to investigate clinical characteristics and 1-year outcomes of glaucoma surgery-associated bullous keratopathy (BK), comparing eyes with prior incisional glaucoma surgery (IGS-BK) and laser iridotomy (LI-BK), using data from the Japanese National Survey on Corneal Transplantation.
METHODS: Among 1941 BK eyes, 404 IGS-BK and 353 LI-BK eyes were analyzed. Clinical parameters and 1-year graft clarity were compared. Within IGS-BK, glaucoma subtypes were examined. Univariate (n = 382) and multivariable (n = 371, excluding cytomegalovirus and pediatric glaucoma) logistic regression identified predictors of graft failure.
RESULTS: IGS-BK patients were younger (72.8 vs. 77.2 years, P <0.001) and predominantly male (64.6% vs. 18.4%). Primary open-angle/normal-tension glaucoma (34.7%) and exfoliation glaucoma (XFG) (30.0%) were most common. Descemet stripping automated endothelial keratoplasty was the predominant procedure (81.7% IGS-BK; 78.2% LI-BK). One-year graft clarity was lower in IGS-BK (82.2% vs. 90.5%, P = 0.002), with XFG showing the poorest outcomes (73.0%). Univariate analysis identified male sex [odds ratio (OR) = 1.83, P = 0.046], younger age (OR = 0.75 per 10-year increase, P = 0.008), and XFG (OR = 2.63, P = 0.004) as predictors of graft failure. After multivariable adjustment, XFG remained an independent risk factor (OR = 3.00, 95% confidence interval: 1.50-5.99, P = 0.002), as did younger age (OR = 0.72, P = 0.019). Complication profiles differed between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: XFG independently predicts poor outcomes in IGS-BK, underscoring the importance of glaucoma subtype stratification. Patients with XFG require intensified perioperative management and postoperative monitoring to optimize graft survival.

etudes.titre: Adverse Events Associated with Trabecular Meshwork Bypass Devices from 2020-2025.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PRCIS: Analysis of the Manufacturer and User Device Experience database identified a low number of adverse events reported for trabecular meshwork bypass devices, with stent malposition, inflammation, and break most common.
PURPOSE: To characterize adverse event (AE) complications with Hydrus Microstent (HM), iStent inject W (ISW), and iStent infinite (ISI) using the Manufacturer and User Device Experience (MAUDE) database.
METHODS: HM, ISW, and ISI patient AEs in MAUDE from 2020-2025 were categorized by keywords: Inflammation, bleeding, hypotony, endophthalmitis, or adhesions. Device AEs were categorized as malposition or break.
RESULTS: 426 reports containing 511 AEs of interest were identified: HM 215, ISW 237, and ISI 59. Most common AEs were stent malposition (168/511 [32.9%]), inflammation (93/511 [18.2%]), break (90/511 [17.6%]), and bleeding (88/511 [17.2%]). For HM and ISI, the most common AEs were stent malposition (HM 75/215 [34.9%], ISI 20/59 [33.9%]), inflammation (HM 53/215 [24.7%], ISI 13/59 [22.0%]), and bleeding (HM 41/215 [19.1%], ISI 10/59 [16.9%]). Common ISW AEs were break (80/237 [33.8%]), stent malposition (73/237 [30.8%]), and bleeding (37/237 [15.6%]). Rate of breaks were 2/215 (0.9%) for HM and 8/59 (13.6%) for ISI. 98.8% of ISW breaks and 100% of ISI breaks were injector breaks; 100% of HM breaks were device breaks. Reports of hypotony (HM 14/215 [6.5%], ISW 5/237 [2.1%], ISI 0/59 [0%]) and endophthalmitis (HM 2/215 [0.9%], ISW 5/237 [2.1%], ISI 1/59 [1.7%]) were low.
CONCLUSIONS: A low number of AEs were submitted for HM, ISW, and ISI in MAUDE from 2020-2025. Common complications were stent malposition, inflammation, break, and bleeding, with more frequent inflammation with HM and injector breaks with ISW. Similar AE numbers were described for HM and ISW, with approximately double the estimated sales for ISW.

etudes.titre: Outcomes of Primary Trabeculectomy in Secondary Glaucoma with Cytomegalovirus Anterior Uveitis.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Trabeculectomy »
etudes.resume:
PRCIS: In eyes with CMV anterior uveitis-associated glaucoma, primary trabeculectomy with mitomycin C achieved a 92% success rate over a 4-year follow-up, providing sustained intraocular pressure control and reducing the frequency of uveitic attacks.
PURPOSE: To evaluate long-term efficacy, safety, and complications of mitomycin C (MMC)-augmented trabeculectomy (TRAB) in eyes with cytomegalovirus anterior uveitis (CMV AU)-associated secondary glaucoma.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 25 eyes of 25 patients with CMV-AU undergoing primary TRAB with MMC. Success was defined as IOP 5-21 mmHg without systemic acetazolamide or further surgery. Complete success required no topical medication, while qualified success allowed it. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis was used to evaluate success rates.
RESULTS: Mean follow-up was 45.7±17.8 months. Preoperative IOP (36.0±9.0 mmHg) decreased significantly to 12.2±4.7 mmHg at the final visit (P<0.001); topical medications reduced from 3.7±0.5 to 0.7±1.1. Visual acuity was preserved (P>0.05). Postoperatively, uveitic episodes and antiviral use significantly decreased (P<0.001). Early hypotony occurred in 24% (n=6) of eyes. Late complications included bleb failure (24%) and hypotony (20%), mostly managed by needling or resuturing. Two eyes required secondary glaucoma surgery. At the final visit, complete success was achieved in 84% (n=21) and qualified success in 8% (n=2). The primary TRAB success rate was 92% but dropped to 60% when postoperative interventions (needling/resuturing) were treated as failures (P=0.007).
CONCLUSIONS: Primary TRAB with MMC is a safe and effective strategy for CMV-AU associated glaucoma, reducing IOP and medication burden while preserving visual acuity. However, vigilance is required regarding early hypotony and the potential need for additional postoperative interventions.

etudes.titre: Macular Structural Progression Before and After Trabeculectomy in Glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Trabeculectomy »
etudes.resume:
PRCIS: In this retrospective study, trabeculectomy significantly slowed macular thinning in glaucomatous eyes, with structural preservation most evident in RNFL, GCL+IPL, and CC+CS layers.
PURPOSE: To evaluate the thickness change rates in total and segmented macular structures in glaucomatous eyes before and after trabeculectomy (TE).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: For this retrospective, observational, longitudinal study records of glaucoma patients who underwent TE between 2012 and 2022 were reviewed. Sixty-four eyes from 59 patients were included for rate of change analysis. Postoperative follow-up examinations were typically scheduled at 1 and 2 weeks, and at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months, followed by annual visits. For the rate of change analysis, at least two scans before and after surgery were needed. Measurements were taken from the retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL), ganglion cell layer and inner plexiform layer (GCL+IPL), inner nuclear layer and outer plexiform layer, outer nuclear layer, photoreceptor layer and retinal pigment epithelium layer, choriocapillaris and choroidal stroma (CC+CS), and total retinal thickness. Thickness rates of change of macular structures before and after TE were determined using linear least squares regression.
RESULTS: Mean follow-up was 65.7±4.9 months. After TE, the rate of change for macular RNFL (P<0.001) and GCL+IPL (P=0.04) increased significantly after surgery. When stratified by surgical outcome, the success group showed significantly increased rates of change for RNFL (P<0.001), GCL+IPL (P=0.03), and CC+CS (P=0.04).
CONCLUSIONS: Successful trabeculectomy was associated with significantly slower rates of macular structural progression.

etudes.titre: Secondary Glaucoma Incidence Following Ischemic Retinal Disease and Anti-Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Utilization.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PRECIS: This large real-world cohort study demonstrates reduced one-year secondary glaucoma incidence following ischemic retinal disease in the later anti-VEGF era, alongside increased anti-VEGF utilization and declining panretinal photocoagulation use.
PURPOSE: Compare one-year incidence of secondary glaucoma following ischemic retinal disease between early and later anti-vascular endothelial growth factor treatment eras.
METHODS: In this retrospective study using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network, adults with proliferative diabetic retinopathy, central retinal vein occlusion, or branch retinal vein occlusion were categorized into an early (2010-2014) or later (2015-2024) anti-vascular endothelial growth factor era based on index diagnosis date. The primary outcome was incident secondary glaucoma within one year. 1:1 propensity score matching balanced baseline demographics, comorbidities, and hemoglobin A1c testing. Time-to-event associations used Kaplan-Meier and Cox models. Exploratory analyses were performed separately by ischemic etiology.
RESULTS: Each era included 36,137 matched patients. Within one year, secondary glaucoma occurred in 773/34,441 patients (2.2%) in the early era and 669/34,155 patients (2.0%) in the later era (risk difference, 0.3%; 95% CI, 0.1%-0.5%; P=0.009; risk ratio, 1.15; 95% CI, 1.04-1.27). Anti-vascular endothelial growth factor utilization increased from 10.3% to 13.7% (P<0.001), while panretinal photocoagulation utilization declined from 12.3% to 9.7% (P<0.001). Exploratory analyses demonstrated a significant era-related difference for central retinal vein occlusion.
CONCLUSION: The later era was associated with lower incidence of secondary glaucoma following ischemic retinal disease, concurrent with increased anti-vascular endothelial growth factor utilization and declining laser use. These findings describe temporal associations between evolving treatment patterns and secondary glaucoma incidence, underscoring the need for continued vigilance and individualized management.

etudes.titre: The Association Between Marijuana Use and Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma Using the All of Us Research Program: A Case-Control Study.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PRCIS: In this multi-racial, multi-ethnic nationwide cohort study using the All of Us Research Program, we report that daily marijuana use was associated with lower odds of POAG in a dose-response manner.
PURPOSE: To investigate the association between marijuana use and primary open angle glaucoma (POAG) in a nationwide US cohort using the All of Us Research Program.
METHODS: 5096 patients with primary open angle glaucoma and 20,384 control patients were included. Electronic health records and survey data from was analyzed, and multivariable regression were performed to test the associations between marijuana use frequency and POAG.
RESULTS: Among 5096 POAG patients, 2063 (40%) answered yes to any marijuana use, and marijuana use frequency was significantly associated with non-POAG status (P<0.001). On bivariate analysis, marijuana use frequencies were associated with reduced odds of POAG when compared to non-users (P<0.05). In multivariable regression, more frequent marijuana use was also associated with lower odds of POAG, with daily marijuana use significantly associated with decreased odds of POAG when compared to no use (OR=0.61, 95% CI: 0.38-0.95, P=0.035).
CONCLUSIONS: The relationship between marijuana use and glaucoma is controversial with limited validation using real-world, population-level data. We identified an inverse dose-response association between marijuana use frequency and POAG. Daily marijuana use was significantly associated with reduced odds of POAG, especially in White patients. Our results suggest the therapeutic use of marijuana and its components for POAG warrants further research, particularly prospective studies for assessing causality.

etudes.titre: Selective Laser Trabeculoplasty versus Latanoprost: A Randomized OCT Angiography Study of Retinal Microvascular Changes in Glaucoma and Ocular Hypertension.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Trabeculoplasty »; mot du titre : « Laser »
etudes.resume:
PRCIS: SLT and latanoprost achieved significant IOP reduction, while macular and peripapillary OCT-A-derived vascular parameters remained largely stable over 6 months in treatment-naïve patients with early-stage POAG and OHT.
PURPOSE: To compare the effects of selective laser trabeculoplasty (SLT) and topical latanoprost 0.005% treatments on macular and optic nerve head (ONH) microvascular parameters in patients with newly diagnosed early-stage primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) and ocular hypertension (OHT), using optical coherence tomography angiography (OCT-A).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Sixty eyes of 60 patients with POAG (n=33) and OHT (n=27) were included and randomized into SLT (n=30) and latanoprost (n=30) groups. OCT-A measurements were obtained at baseline, week 2, and months 1, 3, and 6. Macular superficial capillary plexus vessel density (VD) was assessed using 6×6 mm scans, and radial peripapillary capillary (RPC) VD was evaluated using 4.5×4.5 mm ONH scans. Intra- and inter-group comparisons were performed.
RESULTS: At week 2, intraocular pressure (IOP) levels were significantly lower in the SLT group than in the latanoprost group (P=0.033), with greater IOP reduction from baseline (P=0.031). Both groups showed significant IOP reductions at months 1, 3, and 6 (all P<0.001). At month 3, the increase in inferior hemisphere RPC VD was significantly greater in the SLT group (P=0.028), whereas at month 6, the increase in inferior hemisphere perifoveal VD was greater in the latanoprost group (P=0.028). Baseline IOP was strongly negatively correlated with 6-month IOP change in both groups (P<0.001), indicating greater IOP reduction in eyes with higher baseline IOP.
CONCLUSION: Both treatments provided significant IOP reduction, while macular and ONH microvascular parameters remained largely stable over the 6-month follow-up. The clinical significance of this vascular stability requires further investigation in longer-term studies.

etudes.titre: Surgical Outcomes and Predictors of Success Following Gonioscopy-Assisted Transluminal Trabeculotomy for Primary Congenital and Juvenile Open-Angle Glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Trabeculotomy »; mot du titre : « Surgical »

labos.nom: National Key Research and Development Program of China
National Key Research and Development Program of China

etudes.resume:
PRECIS: GATT is effective and safe in PCG and JOAG, with a higher success rate in PCG. Prior glaucoma surgery predicts surgical failure. IOP spike in one eye predicts fellow-eye spike in PCG.
PURPOSE: To compare the efficacy and safety profiles of gonioscopy-assisted transluminal trabeculotomy (GATT) in primary congenital glaucoma (PCG) and juvenile open-angle glaucoma (JOAG), and to identify predictors for prognosis and intraocular pressure (IOP) spikes.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This is a retrospective cohort study of 27 PCG and 108 JOAG eyes undergoing suture GATT. Surgical outcomes including IOP reduction, number of anti-glaucoma medications, success rates, and adverse events were compared longitudinally and between groups.
RESULTS: GATT decreased IOP significantly at all postoperative follow-ups in both groups (P<0.001) with no intergroup differences (P > 0.05). GATT also reduced the requirement of anti-glaucoma agents in both groups. The PCG group required fewer medications than the JOAG group except for the 24-month time point (P<0.05). PCG had higher cumulative partial and complete success probabilities than JOAG eyes (P=0.011 and 0.002, respectively). Prior glaucoma surgery predicted surgical failure. No vision-threatening events were recorded with transient hyphema and IOP spike being the most common complications. IOP spike in one eye had predictive value for the fellow eye in PCG, but not in JOAG.
CONCLUSIONS: GATT is effective and safe in our PCG and JOAG cohorts, with superior outcomes in younger, surgery-naïve eyes. In PCG, an IOP spike in the first-operated eye predicts that in the fellow eye.

etudes.titre: On-going retinal neuronal degeneration despite clinical stability in glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Glaucoma, a leading cause of irreversible blindness, involves progressive retinal ganglion cell loss. Early detection of this neurodegeneration is critical, yet current clinical methods often identify disease only after substantial damage has occurred. This preliminary study used high-resolution adaptive optics-optical coherence tomography (AO-OCT) to track individual retinal ganglion cells in patients and healthy volunteers over 3 to 5 years. Results revealed higher neurodegeneration in glaucoma compared to normal aging. We observed 4.16 to 6.86% annual decrease in cell density in glaucoma, far exceeding the 0.27% cell loss rate observed in the healthy volunteer group. Critically, AO-OCT detected progression significantly earlier, identifying cell loss 0.74 years before conventional OCT and 1.49 years before visual field testing. These findings demonstrate AO-OCT as a more sensitive tool capable of monitoring glaucomatous damage with superior precision, potentially representing a major advancement over current clinical imaging.
