etudes.titre: Early diagnosis program for multimodal primary open-angle glaucoma based on clinical process.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « diagnosis »

labos.nom: National Natural Science Foundation of China

etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: Glaucoma is among the leading causes of blindness. It is important to detect glaucoma at early stages. Using structural and functional examinations to identify primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) is critical. Computer-aided diagnosis of glaucoma requires multimodal data to identify an accurate and explainable model for early glaucoma diagnosis.
METHODS: In this study, 301 multimodal data points were collected from the ophthalmology department at the Second Affiliated Hospital of Harbin Medical University. Data regarding fundus photography (FP), retinal nerve fiber layer thickness (RNFLt), intraocular pressure (IOP) values, visual field examination parameters and age were obtained. A powerful deep learning network was used to segment the optic nerve head obtained from the FPs. Machine learning classifiers (MLCs) were adopted to obtain the final classification results using 3 datasets: early glaucoma eyes, suspected glaucoma eyes, and healthy eyes; moreover, the diagnostic results of glaucoma specialists and general nonglaucoma ophthalmologists were collected.
RESULTS: The overall area under the curve was 0.9858. The accuracy values of the deep learning- machine learning system, the glaucoma specialist group, the general ophthalmologist group were 0.9478, 0.9493, 0.8725, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: The algorithm delivers superior results in the early diagnosis of POAG. This study's hybrid deep learning-machine learning framework can effectively assist with clinical decision-making for early POAG.

etudes.titre: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis masquerading as lung cancer with meningeal metastasis: a case report and literature review.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique

labos.nom: National Natural Science Foundation of China
Natural Science Foundation of Fujian Province

etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA) is an anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated small-vessel vasculitis classically presenting with upper and lower respiratory tract and renal involvement. Central nervous system (CNS) involvement in GPA is rare and is highly prone to being misdiagnosed as intracranial tumor metastasis or intracranial infection.
CASE REPORT: We report a 60-year-old female who presented with recurrent headache and conjunctival injection. She had undergone two surgical procedures for "glaucoma" at an outside hospital without headache relief. Upon admission to our hospital, chest CT revealed multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules, highly suspicious for lung cancer; brain MRI showed dural thickening with subdural effusion; lumbar puncture revealed an intracranial pressure (ICP) of 270 mmH₂O, with negative CSF cultures and no tumor cells. The initial diagnosis was leptomeningeal metastasis from lung cancer. However, percutaneous lung biopsy showed no evidence of tumor or infection, and serology revealed positive c-ANCA/PR3-ANCA, leading to a final diagnosis of GPA with clinicoradiologically supported GPA-related pachymeningitis. After glucocorticoid therapy, the patient's headache and other symptoms resolved rapidly.
LITERATURE REVIEW: We reviewed 33 published cases of GPA with cranial involvement and summarized their clinical features. Hypertrophic pachymeningitis (HP) was the most common cranial manifestation (51.5%). Serum ANCA positivity was 87.9% (29/33). Among all 33 cases, c-ANCA/PR3-ANCA was reported in 23 (69.7%); among the 29 ANCA-positive cases, c-ANCA/PR3-ANCA accounted for 79.3% (23/29). After immunosuppressive or immunomodulatory therapy, approximately 90.9% of patients improved or stabilized. These features may serve as clues that should prompt clinicians to consider GPA in the differential diagnosis of pulmonary nodules with pachymeningeal disease and raised intracranial pressure, rather than as established discriminators from lung cancer brain metastasis.
CONCLUSION: GPA can present with multiple pulmonary masses, headache, and pachymeningitis, closely mimicking leptomeningeal metastasis of lung cancer. When imaging and clinical presentation are atypical, serum ANCA testing and pathological biopsy are key to differential diagnosis. Clinicians should be alert to this "mimic of malignancy" to avoid unnecessary surgery or radiotherapy.

etudes.titre: Case Report: Bilateral vision-threatening anterior segment injury following periocular cosmetic high-intensity focused ultrasound.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: High-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) is widely used for noninvasive cosmetic rejuvenation, including periocular procedures. However, when performed near the globe, focused thermal energy may injure multiple anterior segment structures. We report a 38-year-old woman who developed acute bilateral ocular pain, redness, and blurred vision shortly after periocular cosmetic HIFU for eyelid fat reduction and facial rejuvenation. The right eye was more severely affected. At presentation, best-corrected visual acuity was counting fingers at 0.5 m in the right eye and 20/40 in the left eye, with intraocular pressures of 30 and 26 mmHg, respectively. Slit-lamp examination showed bilateral anterior uveitis, corneal edema, keratic precipitates, endothelial pigment deposits, diffuse iris stromal disruption with pigment dispersion, and focal lens opacities consistent with presumed thermal lens injury. After corneal edema improved, focal, tapered corneal opacities became visible, especially in the right eye. The cosmetic clinic reported use of a 1.5-mm focal-depth probe at 7.0 MHz with an energy setting of approximately 1 J/cm2; however, further procedural details were not available. The patient received topical and systemic anti-inflammatory treatments, intraocular pressure-lowering medications, hypertonic sodium chloride ointment, and supportive care. During follow-up, inflammation subsided and intraocular pressure stabilized without medication. At about 2 months, visual acuity was stable at 20/30 in the right eye and 20/25 in the left eye, although corneal, iris, and lens abnormalities remained. This case broadens the known range of cosmetic periocular HIFU-related ocular injuries by documenting a severe bilateral, multistructural anterior segment injury with acute ocular hypertension, diffuse iris stromal disruption, focal corneal opacities, and persistent focal lens opacities. It emphasizes the importance of conservative energy use during periocular procedures, ocular protection, trained operators, and prompt eye examinations if symptoms occur after the procedure.

etudes.titre: Comparing performance on a continuous visual stimulus tracking task between real and simulated visual field defects: Evidence for long-term adaptation.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « visual field »
etudes.resume: Individuals with visual field defects (VFDs) can adapt to their VFDs by making compensatory eye movements. Establishing whether such adaptation improves functional vision could enhance rehabilitation programs. Here, we used continuous visual stimulus tracking (CVST) and compared tracking performance (agreement between the gaze and stimulus positions) in participants with a glaucomatous VFD (VFD participants) with that of controls that experienced a similar but simulated VFD. Our VFD simulation used the deviations in contrast sensitivities from standard automated perimetry to create a gaze-contingent transparency mask. We collected eye movement data from 20 controls and 20 VFD participants while they monocularly tracked a moving stimulus (Goldmann III, 0.43° diameter) at three contrast levels (40%, 160%, and 640%). Each control performed the task with the VFD of a matched VFD participant in simulation. For early-stage VFDs, tracking performance was not significantly different between VFD participants and controls with the simulated VFD. However, for more severe VFDs, the difference increased in favor of the VFD participant. Additionally, predicting VFD severity from tracking performance was more accurate for controls than for VFD participants. We concluded that CVST performance can reveal the presence of adaptation to actual VFDs. Our findings suggest that tracking with a simulated VFD primarily reflects visual sensitivity loss, and tracking with an actual VFD also reflects adaptation. Moreover, our findings suggest that long-term adaptation to actual VFDs manifests as (implicit) knowledge about the location of the defect, guiding compensatory viewing behavior and improving functional vision. CVST may aid in quantifying this improvement.

etudes.titre: The impact of nutrition on glaucoma progression: evidence from systematic literature review and meta-analysis.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
TOPIC: This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to determine if nutritional interventions have an impact on glaucoma progression. The clinical question being answered is whether nutritional supplementation compared to baseline values has an impact on measures of glaucoma progression, i.e., intraocular pressure (IOP), visual field mean deviation (MD), pattern standard deviation (PSD), and retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Glaucoma is a chronic neurodegenerative optic neuropathy and is a major cause of irreversible blindness worldwide. The conventional treatment for glaucoma is to reduce IOP to slow the progression of glaucoma. However, progression of glaucoma is seen in patients with well-controlled IOP levels, suggesting that there is a need to look for additional therapeutic options, including nutritional factors, antioxidants, omega-3 fatty acids, vitamins, and nutraceuticals.
METHODS: A comprehensive search of the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), PubMed, PubMed Central (PMC), and Google Scholar was undertaken from date of inception to 6 March, 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies evaluating the diet, nutritional status, or nutritional supplementation in adults with glaucoma and reporting outcomes on the progression of the disease were considered for inclusion. Risk of bias in the included studies was assessed with the revised Cochrane Risk of Bias tool (RoB 2) for RCTs and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale for cohort studies.
RESULTS: Qualitative synthesis included 21 studies with 1,209 participants, and 11 studies were available for meta-analysis. Antioxidants, omega-3 fatty acids, vitamins, and neuroprotective agents such as coenzyme Q10, ginkgo biloba extract, citicoline, and palmitoylethanolamide were included. Meta-analysis found no statistically significant change at six months in IOP (mean difference - 2.42 mmHg, 95% CI - 7.53 to 2.70), MD (2.23 dB, 95% CI - 1.04 to 5.50), or RNFL thickness (- 16.00 µm, 95% CI - 70.77 to 38.76), although there was a significant decrease in PSD (- 0.33 dB, 95% CI - 0.47 to - 0.19).
CONCLUSION: The current evidence suggests that nutritional interventions do not significantly affect major indicators of glaucoma progression in the short term; the small PSD reduction, based on three cohort studies, should not be interpreted as a clinically meaningful neuroprotective effect. Given the low-to-moderate certainty of the underlying evidence, nutritional supplements may be considered as a potential adjunct to conventional treatment, though evidence supporting their routine clinical use remains insufficient; the long-term effects of nutritional supplements on glaucoma need to be determined through large, long-term RCTs.

etudes.titre: Four-year corneal hysteresis and intraocular pressure outcomes after ab-interno canaloplasty with phacoemulsification in glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « canaloplasty »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To evaluate longitudinal changes in intraocular pressure (IOP), medication burden, and corneal biomechanical parameters over 4 years following phacoemulsification combined with ab-interno canaloplasty (AbiC) in patients with primary open-angle glaucoma.
METHODS: This retrospective, longitudinal, non-comparative cohort study included 40 eyes from 28 patients. Clinical data were collected preoperatively and up to 4 years postoperatively. Continuous outcomes, including absolute and relative IOP reduction, were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Secondary analyses included Kaplan-Meier estimates based on predefined IOP thresholds (≤ 18 mmHg), evaluated both with and without medications. Sensitivity analyses were performed using alternative thresholds (≤ 15 and ≤ 21 mmHg).
RESULTS: Mean IOP decreased significantly over time (global p = 0.009), with the greatest reduction at one year (- 1.71 mmHg; 95% CI - 2.94 to - 0.47; p = 0.003). Although attenuation was observed at later time points, IOP remained numerically below baseline through year four. Medication burden decreased significantly at one year (- 1.48 medications; 95% CI - 1.85 to - 1.10; p < 0.001), followed by gradual reintroduction. Corneal hysteresis increased after surgery and remained significantly higher than baseline during follow-up (p < 0.001). The cumulative probability of maintaining IOP ≤ 18 mmHg was 85.0% at four years, whereas medication-free control was 10.0%. No sight-threatening complications occurred.
CONCLUSIONS: Phacocanaloplasty was associated with an early significant reduction in IOP with partial attenuation over time, while remaining numerically below baseline during long-term follow-up. The increase in corneal hysteresis is consistent with a favorable postoperative biomechanical profile.

etudes.titre: Baseline Macular OCT Thickness of Ocular Hypertensive Patients Improves Prediction of Glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « OCT »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To determine whether baseline macular ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GCIPL) and circumpapillary retinal nerve fiber layer (cpRNFL) thickness add prognostic value for glaucomatous visual field (VF) damage in patients with ocular hypertension.
DESIGN: Retrospective clinical cohort study.
PARTICIPANTS: 330 eyes of 235 patients with ocular hypertension, defined by intraocular pressure of 22 mmHg or higher or an International Classification of Diseases coded diagnosis, without repeatable glaucomatous VF damage at baseline. Eyes came from both the African Descent and Glaucoma Evaluation Study and a clinical cohort at the Shiley Eye Institute.
METHODS: Baseline GCIPL and cpRNFL thickness were measured from the first good-quality Cirrus optical coherence tomography (OCT) macular and optic-disc cubes. Clinical predictors were assessed with the Ocular Hypertension Treatment Study (OHTS)-European Glaucoma Prevention Study (EGPS) Risk Calculator. Repeatable glaucomatous VF damage required a Glaucoma Hemifield Test outside normal limits or a pattern standard deviation at the 5% level or worse on three consecutive reliable Humphrey 24-2 examinations.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Hazard ratios per 1 standard deviation (SD) of thinner global and sectoral GCIPL or cpRNFL, and the change in the Harrell concordance (C) index (ΔC) after adding each measure to the Risk Calculator.
RESULTS: Glaucomatous VF damage developed in 47 of 330 eyes (14%) over a median 4.4 years. Adjusted for the Risk Calculator, thinner macular GCIPL was associated with conversion (hazard ratio [HR] 1.89 per 1-SD thinner; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.50 to 2.37; P < .001), and every macular sector was significant (HR 1.71 to 2.02). The Risk Calculator alone showed modest discrimination (Harrell C-index, 0.57). Adding macular GCIPL improved discrimination (ΔC +0.101; 95% CI, +0.022 to +0.220). Global cpRNFL thickness did not improve discrimination (ΔC +0.004; 95% CI, -0.021 to +0.133); among cpRNFL quadrants, only the inferior quadrant was associated with conversion (HR 1.50; 95% CI, 1.02 to 2.22).
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with ocular hypertension, thinner baseline macular GCIPL was associated with glaucomatous VF damage and improved the discrimination of the OHTS-EGPS Risk Calculator, whereas global cpRNFL thickness did not.

etudes.titre: Three-Year Outcomes of Trabeculotomy vs Combined Trabeculotomy-Trabeculectomy for Primary Congenital Glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Trabeculectomy »; mot du titre : « Trabeculotomy »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To determine whether trabeculotomy is noninferior to combined trabeculotomy-trabeculectomy (CTT) for primary congenital glaucoma (PCG) with a horizontal corneal diameter (HCD) of 12-14 mm.
DESIGN: Prospective, randomized, controlled noninferiority trial.
PARTICIPANTS: Children from birth through 3 years of age with PCG, a HCD of 12 to 14 mm, and no previous intraocular or laser surgery were eligible. Two hundred and forty-eight children were enrolled from January 2015 through April 2021, and the final follow-up was completed in April 2024.
METHODS: One eligible eye per child was randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to trabeculotomy or CTT.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was qualified surgical success at 36 months, defined as an intraocular pressure (IOP) of 5 to 21 mmHg with or without glaucoma medications, without vision-threatening complications or additional glaucoma surgery. The noninferiority margin was -15 percentage points. Exploratory secondary outcomes included changes in IOP, ocular morphometric and functional outcomes, and adverse events.
RESULTS: Overall, 124 children were assigned to trabeculotomy (mean age, 9.8 months; 76.6% male) and 124 to CTT (mean age, 9.9 months; 68.5% male). In the intention-to-treat population, qualified success at 36 months was achieved in 102 of 124 eyes (82.3%) in the trabeculotomy group and 105 of 124 eyes (84.7%) in the CTT group (risk difference: -2.4%; 95%CI, -11.7 to 6.9; Pnoninferiority= 0.004). Corresponding rates in the per-protocol population were 90.3% and 92.9%, respectively (risk difference -2.6%; 95%CI -10.3 to 4.9; Pnoninferiority< 0.001). Mean IOP reduction was -12.1 mm Hg (95%CI, -12.9 to -11.4) and -13.2 mm Hg (95%CI, -14.0 to -12.4) in the trabeculotomy and CTT groups, respectively (P=0.067). No statistically significant between-group differences were observed in other secondary outcomes. Adverse events occurred in 56 children (45.2%) in the trabeculotomy group and 67 (54.0%) in the CTT group (P = 0.162). Hyphema was the most common adverse event in both groups, and most cases resolved spontaneously.
CONCLUSIONS: Trabeculotomy was noninferior to CTT for qualified surgical success at 36 months in PCG patients with a HCD of 12-14 mm. These findings suggest that trabeculotomy may be an alternative to CTT in this population.

etudes.titre: Incidence and Predictors of IOP-Lowering Treatment Following Detection of Referable Glaucoma in a Teleretinal Screening Program.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Screening »; mot du titre : « Detection »

labos.nom: Southern California Clinical and Translational Science Institute
National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences

etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the incidence and baseline predictors of intraocular pressure (IOP)-lowering treatment following detection of referable glaucoma by teleretinal screening.
DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.
PARTICIPANTS: Participants were derived from a safety-net teleretinal diabetic retinopathy screening program (2013-2024) and included individuals who screened positive for referable glaucoma (cup-to-disc ratio [CDR] ≥0.6 or CDR asymmetry ≥0.2) and completed in-office diagnostic evaluation.
METHODS: Cumulative incidence functions were estimated for the initiation of IOP-lowering treatment, with loss to follow-up handled as a competing event. Fine-Gray models were used to identify baseline screening predictors of treatment and surgery, and to perform cross-validated risk stratification. Glaucoma diagnosis was approximated using diagnostic codes and chart review.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was initiation of IOP-lowering treatment (medication, laser, or surgery). The secondary outcome was glaucoma surgery.
RESULTS: 2,367 participants were included. The cumulative incidence of treatment was 19.6% (95% CI: 18.0-21.2) at Year 1 and 39.1% (36.7-41.6) at Year 5. Early treatment occurred primarily in glaucoma cases, whereas treatment accumulated longitudinally in glaucoma suspects, reaching 29.3% (25.8-32.7) by Year 5. Surgery was less common (2.2% [1.3-3.1] at Year 5). Risk stratification with baseline screening data produced meaningful separation at Year 5 (treatment: 51.2% [46.9-55.5] vs. 26.7% [22.8-30.7]; surgery: 3.8% [2.1-5.5] vs. 0.7% [0.1-1.3]). Older age (sub-distribution hazard ratio [SHR] 1.03 [1.02-1.04] per year, p<0.001), Black race (SHR 1.50 [1.21-1.87], p<0.001), and personal history of glaucoma (SHR 1.90 [1.34-2.70], p<0.001) were associated with treatment; Asian race was protective (SHR 0.71 [0.52-0.97], p=0.03). Older age (SHR 1.06 [1.03-1.09], p<0.001), worse visual acuity (SHR 5.11 [2.15-12.12] per logMAR unit, p<0.001), and screening at a hospital-based site (SHR 2.46 [1.35-4.49], p=0.003) were associated with surgery.
CONCLUSION: Among safety-net diabetic patients who screened positive for referable glaucoma and were untreated at screening, nearly 40% initiated IOP-lowering treatment within 5 years, while few received surgery. Baseline screening characteristics enabled risk stratification of treatment and surgery. These findings address an evidence gap about longitudinal consequences of screening and suggest that its impact extends beyond detection of prevalent glaucoma to include identification of high-risk glaucoma suspects who warrant surveillance.

etudes.titre: Differential Survival of Retinal Ganglion Cell Types Following Branch Retinal Vein Occlusion.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Retinal Ganglion Cell »

labos.nom: Richard and Isabel Goldstein Family Foundation

etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: Branch retinal vein occlusion (BRVO) is a common cause of retinal ischemia, rapidly inducing neuronal death and often producing irreversible vison loss. Interventions such as thrombolysis restore perfusion but cannot recover neurons already lost, and most patients retain permanent visual deficits. Identifying which neuronal populations die, and how rapidly, may therefore reveal timing windows and targets for neuroprotective treatment. To determine the timing of pathology, we evaluated vascular changes and neuronal degeneration in a photocoagulation-induced mouse model of BRVO. To determine differences in retinal ganglion cells (RGC) type susceptibility, we tracked the survival of RGC subpopulations using immunofluorescence markers.
METHODS: BRVO was induced by Rose Bengal injection followed by targeted photocoagulation of a branch vein. Obstruction was confirmed by fluorescein angiography and vascular damage assessed by optical coherence tomography angiography. Cell survival was quantified by immunostaining at 3, 7, and 14 days using RNA-Binding Protein with Multiple Splicing (RBPMS, pan-RGC). RGC subtype markers for intrinsically photosensitive RGCs (TBR2), α-RGCs (SPP1), ON-OFF direction-selective RGCs (CART), and F-RGCs (FOXP2) were used to compare subtype survival.
RESULTS: Occlusion selectively disrupted the superficial and intermediate capillary plexus, sparing the deep plexuses. All examined neuronal populations were significantly depleted, but with markedly different magnitude and timing. α-RGCs and F-RGCs were the most vulnerable subtypes, both approaching complete loss by one week, whereas intrinsically photosensitive RGCs were the most resistant.
CONCLUSIONS: α-RGCs, typically resilient in glaucoma, trauma, and excitotoxicity, were markedly vulnerable in BRVO, indicating that RGC subtype susceptibility is insult-specific.

etudes.titre: IOP-independent treatment for neurodegeneration in glaucoma using optimized ROS-scavenging microparticles for sustained release of erythropoietin.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « neurodegeneration »

labos.nom: Vanderbilt Institute of Nanoscale Science and Engineering
National Institute of Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering

etudes.resume: Glaucoma is a slow-progressing neurodegenerative disease of the optic projection to the brain and a leading cause of blindness worldwide. Current treatments are targeted towards lowering intraocular pressure (IOP), the only known, modifiable risk factor; however, this strategy is ineffective in many patients. An early hallmark of glaucomatous neurodegeneration is increased reactive oxygen species (ROS), representing an alternative opportunity for intervention to halt or slow disease progression. In this work, we optimize a ROS-scavenging copolymer, poly(propylene sulfide-co-ethylene sulfide) (PPSES), for formulation of size-controlled, stabilized, antioxidant microparticles (MPs) for sustained release of the protein erythropoietin (EPO). EPO promotes biological antioxidant defense via activation of NRF2-mediated transcription of antioxidant genes. This MP system overcomes the short half-life of EPO and leverages the combined benefits of bioactive EPO with long-lasting, inherently antioxidant PPSES MPs. The lead EPO-MP formulation preserves neurons in both mouse and non-human primate models of glaucoma through suppression of oxidative stress and optic nerve degeneration. EPO-loaded PPSES MPs represent a translationally relevant therapy for long-term management of glaucoma independent of IOP.

etudes.titre: Beyond Billing Codes: An Agentic Large Language Model Pipeline for Extracting Glaucoma Procedural Data from Free-Text Clinical Notes.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the accuracy of a large language model (LLM)-based agentic workflow to extract procedural data from free-text glaucoma clinical notes in the electronic health record (EHR).
DESIGN: Cross-sectional.
SUBJECTS: 1,250 subjects in the Bascom Palmer Ophthalmic Repository.
METHODS: Randomly sampled clinical notes from glaucoma encounters dated 2014 to 2024 were labeled by two glaucoma specialists (with an adjudicator as needed) for prior glaucoma-related procedures (name, date, details) and recommended future procedures (name, details). Notes were split into development (10%), validation (10%), and test (80%) sets. Five LLMs (Claude Opus 4.6, DeepSeek-V4 Pro, GPT-5.5, Grok 4.1, and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B) were accessed in Microsoft Foundry through HIPAA-compliant containers. The extraction pipeline comprised a three-step agentic workflow (extraction, validation, and conditional revision) followed by text standardization. Detection of procedure data was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1-score. Among positive cases, performance was evaluated using exact-match accuracy and Jaccard Index (JI). Prior procedure labels were also compared with EHR glaucoma-related Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codes.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Accuracy, exact-match accuracy, JI.
RESULTS: A total of 1,984 (992 notes × 2 eyes) labels were evaluated for each task in the test set. Prior and future procedures were identified in 1,057 (53.3%) and 152 (7.7%) eyes, respectively. Accuracy ranged from 0.965 (Grok) to 0.996 (Claude) for prior procedures and 0.969 (DeepSeek, Qwen)-0.978 (Claude) for future procedures. Among positive cases, exact-match accuracy ranged from 0.681 (Grok) to 0.890 (Claude) for prior procedures and 0.704 (Grok)-0.849 (Claude) for future procedures; JI ranged from 0.827 (Grok) to 0.956 (Claude) and 0.734 (Grok) to 0.883 (Claude), respectively. Among all 1,760 prior procedures present in adjudicated labels, only 441 (25.1%) were captured by CPT-coded EHR data.
CONCLUSIONS: A secure agentic LLM pipeline accurately extracted glaucoma procedural data from clinical notes, recovering data largely absent from structured EHR fields. Claude performed best across both tasks. Limited agreement between labels and CPT codes likely reflects procedures performed at outside institutions and the limited granularity of CPT coding. This approach may support a scalable, comprehensive characterization of procedure burden among glaucoma patients for research and clinical applications.

etudes.titre: Palladium-103 brachytherapy with continuous periodic intravitreal Anti-VEGF bevacizumab for ciliary body medulloepithelioma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To report a case of medulloepithelioma treated with palladium-103 (103Pd) plaque brachytherapy, followed by adjunctive continuous periodic intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy, highlighting a novel combined strategy for tumor control and management of its neovascular complications.
OBSERVATIONS: A 9-year-old male presented with a ciliary body mass causing anterior displacement of the iris and iris neovascularization in the right eye. Initial tumor dimensions were 8 × 8 mm in basal diameters and 3.9 mm in thickness. Aspiration cutter-assisted biopsy was used to confirm the diagnosis of medulloepithelioma. Treatment involved temporary placement of a 14-mm 103Pd plaque, which irradiated the tumor's apex to 101.4 Gy (Gy) over 7 days. Despite tumor control, progressive iris neovascularization with secondary angle-closure glaucoma was managed by continuous periodic intravitreal anti-VEGF pharmacotherapy and two peripheral iridotomies. At 18 months post-plaque brachytherapy, a posterior subcapsular cataract developed that required extraction with intraocular lens placement. At 5 years post-plaque brachytherapy, a macular epiretinal membrane developed that was pealed during pars plana vitrectomy surgery. At 6 years 2 months follow-up post-plaque brachytherapy the tumor's thickness had decreased from 3.9 to 2.1 mm (46.2%) and the visual acuity had declined from 20/20 to 20/63. No metastases were detected.
CONCLUSIONS AND IMPORTANCE: 103Pd plaque brachytherapy was used to control a ciliary body medulloepithelioma. However, iridotomies and continuous periodic anti-VEGF therapy were needed to suppress tumor-related secondary neovascular glaucoma. This approach achieved durable local tumor control while preserving the globe and functional vision. Targeted radiation and pharmacologic neovascular suppression offered a novel globe and vision-sparing treatment for medulloepithelioma.

etudes.titre: Delayed blood reflux-related secondary open-angle glaucoma with ghost cells more than 3 years after ab-interno goniotomy.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « goniotomy »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To report delayed blood reflux-related secondary open-angle glaucoma with a pathology-supported ghost-cell component more than 3 years after ab-interno goniotomy.
OBSERVATIONS: A 73-year-old man with primary open-angle glaucoma underwent left ab-interno goniotomy using a Tanito microhook (TMH) over 120° about 45 months before presentation; a 1-mm hyphema was documented on postoperative day 1. IOP was 17.0 mmHg at 3 months, 14.0 mmHg at 1 year, 18.0 mmHg at postoperative month 36, and 15.3 mmHg at postoperative month 44, but increased to 45.3 mmHg approximately 2 weeks before admission and 45.1 mmHg at admission despite topical therapy. Gonioscopy showed an open angle with a small inferior hyphema, and B-scan showed no clinically evident vitreous hemorrhage. During early anterior chamber paracentesis/decompression, 0.1 mL of aqueous humor was aspirated for direct-smear examination with routine hematoxylin-eosin staining; during decompression/washout, blood-tinged reflux was observed from the nasal angle corresponding to the prior goniotomy site. Pathology showed degenerated erythrocytes and ghost cells. Because washout did not provide sustained IOP control, trabeculectomy with mitomycin C and two adjustable scleral-flap sutures was performed. At postoperative month 11 after trabeculectomy, IOP was 10.0 mmHg with a clear anterior chamber.
CONCLUSIONS AND IMPORTANCE: Delayed blood-reflux-related secondary open-angle glaucoma may occur years after ab-interno goniotomy. These findings indicate that the surgically opened trabecular pathway remains a potential route for retrograde bleeding whenever episcleral venous pressure exceeds intraocular pressure. Clinicians should be mindful of this late phenomenon, which warrants further clinical observation and mechanistic research.

etudes.titre: Bilateral interstitial keratitis following intracameral Durysta® (bimatoprost).
etudes.raison_rubrique: étiquette : produit suivi étudié (rôle suggéré, à vérifier)
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To report a case of bilateral interstitial keratitis following repeat intracameral bimatoprost injections.
OBSERVATIONS: A 92-year-old female with advanced primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) and poor adherence to topical glaucoma medications received bilateral intracameral Durysta® (bimatoprost) implants twelve months apart. Four months following the second intracameral injections, she developed bilateral interstitial keratitis (IK) as evidenced by keratitic precipitates and deep corneal stromal vascularization on slit lamp examination. There was no history of prior herpetic keratitis or blepharoconjunctivitis, and syphilis testing was negative. The patient was treated with valacyclovir and prednisolone acetate, with subsequent slow improvement in her corneal findings.
CONCLUSIONS AND IMPORTANCE: This case highlights a rare adverse event following repeated intracameral bimatoprost implants. We speculate that the IK was triggered by herpes simplex virus (HSV) reactivation from the repeated bimatoprost injections although other etiologies including a delayed hypersensitivity reaction to the implant cannot be ruled out. Physicians should weigh the benefits of improved intraocular pressure control against the potential infectious or non-infectious inflammatory risks this agent possesses for individual patients.

etudes.titre: Timing of Structural Foveal Maturation on Serial OCT in Preterm Infants: Association With Retinopathy of Prematurity Severity.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « OCT »
etudes.resume:
INTRODUCTION: Retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) is a major cause of visual impairment in childhood and a recognised cause of lifelong ocular morbidity, since the structural changes established in infancy predispose to retinal detachment, glaucoma, cataract and vitreous haemorrhage in later life and mandate lifelong surveillance. Objective biomarkers of disease severity are therefore needed. Handheld spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) enables high-resolution, non-invasive assessment of retinal microstructure in non-sedated infants, but the relationship between the timing of structural foveal maturation and ROP severity remains poorly understood.
PURPOSE: To evaluate whether the timing of structural foveal maturation, defined as the first appearance of the outer retinal bands at the foveal centre, is associated with ROP severity, anti-VEGF treatment requirement and the degree of prematurity.
METHODS: In this prospective observational study, 36 preterm infants (72 eyes) underwent serial handheld SD-OCT imaging (Envisu C2300) during routine ROP screening, with a mean of 8.6 examinations per infant. The primary outcome was postmenstrual age (PMA) and chronological age (CA) at the first appearance of the outer retinal bands at the foveal centre, a milestone hereafter referred to as ellipsoid zone (EZ) emergence. Statistical analyses included Mann-Whitney U tests, Pearson and Spearman correlations, and linear regression.
RESULTS: Structural foveal maturation was significantly delayed in severe ROP. Infants with aggressive posterior ROP (AP-ROP) reached EZ emergence later than those without AP-ROP (median PMA 36.79 vs 34.07 weeks, p=0.041; median CA 10.07 vs 5.21 weeks, p=0.024; n=18). A comparable delay was observed in infants with plus disease (median PMA 36.79 vs 34.07 weeks, p=0.041; median CA 10.07 vs 5.21 weeks, p=0.024; n=18). Infants requiring anti-VEGF therapy also demonstrated delayed EZ emergence (median PMA 36.86 vs 34.43 weeks, p=0.035; n=18), and the age at first anti-VEGF injection correlated positively with the age at EZ emergence (r=0.69, p=0.019, n=11). Gestational age was negatively correlated with CA at EZ emergence (r=-0.65, p=0.003), whereas birth weight was not associated with the timing of this particular milestone (p=0.878). Although maximum central retinal thickness increased with age (32 µm per week, 95% CI 17-46, p<0.001), it did not differ across ROP stages (p=0.162).
CONCLUSIONS: Delayed EZ emergence at the foveal centre is associated with severe ROP and with the need for anti-VEGF treatment, suggesting that the timing of structural retinal maturation may serve as an objective biomarker of disease severity. These findings, derived from a single-centre cohort of 36 infants, warrant validation in larger prospective multicentre studies.

etudes.titre: A Teleglaucoma Screening System for Individuals at Risk of Open-Angle Glaucoma: Long-Term Clinical Outcomes and Comparative Cost Analysis.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Screening »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the clinical effectiveness and economic impact of a teleglaucoma screening program for individuals at increased risk of developing open-angle glaucoma (OAG).
DESIGN: Prospective cohort study with retrospective evaluation of long-term clinical outcomes and comparative cost analysis.
PARTICIPANTS: Consecutive individuals with risk factors for OAG enrolled in a teleglaucoma screening program between 2020 and 2022.
METHODS: A targeted teleglaucoma screening program was implemented within the Donostialdea Integrated Healthcare Organization (Gipuzkoa, Spain). Consecutive individuals with risk factors for OAG were included. The teleglaucoma assessment included best-corrected visual acuity, non-contact tonometry, pachymetry, and peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer optical coherence tomography (pRNFL-OCT), performed by an optometrist and reviewed asynchronously by glaucoma specialists. Findings consistent with glaucoma or suspicious for glaucoma were considered positive screening results, whereas ocular hypertension (OHT) or the absence of abnormalities were considered negative screening results. Clinical effectiveness was evaluated through analysis of glaucoma-related diagnoses recorded using ICD-10 codes during a five-year follow-up period. A comparative cost analysis was conducted from a societal perspective. Patient satisfaction was assessed using the Client Satisfaction Questionnaire (CSQ-8).
MAIN OUTCOMES MEASURES: Agreement between teleglaucoma classifications and glaucoma-related ICD-10 diagnoses recorded during follow-up, diagnostic performance indicators, patient satisfaction, and costs.
RESULTS: A total of 1,112 patients were included (mean age 60.2 years), of whom 63.1% were women. Positive screening results were identified in 8.2% of participants. Overall agreement between the teleglaucoma assessment and follow-up ICD-10 diagnoses was 92.6%, with a mean follow-up of 3.7 ± 0.8 years. Sensitivity was 64.5%, specificity 93.4%, and negative predictive value 98.9%. Patient satisfaction was high, with a mean score of 8.5/10. The economic analysis demonstrated a 50% reduction in total costs compared with conventional care, with a cost per patient of €40.7 versus €81.2.
CONCLUSIONS: The teleglaucoma system demonstrated a high ability to rule out disease among individuals at risk of glaucoma, reduced costs and achieved high patient satisfaction. However, moderate sensitivity and the use of coded clinical records as the reference standard should be considered.

etudes.titre: Engineered hyalurosomal gel co-delivering citicoline sodium and nifedipine for potential glaucoma management: formulation and pharmacodynamic evaluation.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
INTRODUCTION: Glaucoma is a neurodegenerative ocular disorder that requires multi-targeted therapeutic strategies to counteract intraocular pressure (IOP) elevation and oxidative stress-mediated retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) loss. This study developed an innovative hyalurosomal hydrogel platform co-delivering Nifedipine (NFD, a calcium channel blocker that promotes ocular vasodilation and IOP reduction) and Citicoline sodium (CTC, a potent neuroprotective and antioxidant agent) as a potential topical therapeutic approach for glaucoma.
METHODS: NFD-loaded hyalurosomes (NFD-HAs) were prepared using thin-film hydration and statistically optimized via a D-Optimal design. The optimized formulation (NFD-OF) was probe-sonicated, combined with CTC, and incorporated into an HPMC hydrogel.
RESULTS AND DISCUSSION: Sonicated NFD-OF displayed nanosized spherical vesicles (198.6 ± 23.1 nm), high entrapment efficiency (70.7 ± 1.8%), and stable zeta potential (-39.1 ± 1.3 mV). Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) analysis confirmed the distinct spherical morphology, non-aggregated state, and structural integrity of NFD-OF. The final CTC/NFD-OF gel exhibited pseudoplastic shear-thinning flow, an optimal ocular pH (6.9 ± 0.02), and sustained release over 24 h (65.5% for NFD and 99.5% for CTC). The dual gel demonstrated superior free radical scavenging capability (IC50 = 16.44±0.7 μg/mL) compared to free NFD (219.43 μg/mL) and CTC (234.62 μg/mL). Confocal microscopy confirmed a 2.2-fold enhancement in transcorneal penetration depth (110 μm) compared with the control solution (50 μm). In vivo pharmacodynamic evaluation revealed a significantly higher maximum IOP decrease (51.85 ± 8.2%), extended mean residence time (8.9 ± 2.7 h), and increased relative exposure (AUC0-∞ = 494.1 ± 191.9) compared to commercial Xola™ eye drops (36.4 ± 5.9% max IOP decrease, AUC0-∞ = 182.8 ± 33.7). Terminal gamma sterilization preserved physicochemical characteristics and release profiles. Draize and histopathological assays confirmed excellent ocular tolerability. Overall, the CTC/NFD-OF gel demonstrated promising ocular hypotensive activity and safety, supporting its potential as a multifunctional topical therapeutic approach for glaucoma.

etudes.titre: Predicting Future Visual Field Status from Baseline OCT Scan in Early to Moderate Glaucoma Using Deep Learning.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Deep Learning »; mot du titre : « OCT »

labos.nom: National Health and Medical Research Council

etudes.resume:
OBJECTIVE: The visual field (VF) test results of many eyes with glaucoma progress despite treatment. This suggests that some eyes are either untreated or that the management of intraocular pressure does not influence the outcome. In this work, we explore whether future VF parameters can be predicted from a baseline OCT-retinal nerve fiber layer (OCT-RNFL) scan using a deep learning model.
DESIGN: Retrospective multicenter cohort study with external validation.
PARTICIPANTS: A total of 1792 eyes from 1610 patients were used for model development. External validation was performed on 150 eyes from a second center (Zeiss Cirrus OCT) and 280 eyes from a third center (Heidelberg Spectralis OCT).
METHODS: A Vision Transformer (ViT)-based regression model was trained on baseline OCT-RNFL scans to predict 3 key VF indices (follow-up interval: 4.74 ± 2.59 years). Model performance was evaluated using regression metrics with 95% confidence intervals. Saliency maps were generated to identify OCT-RNFL regions for making decisions in predicting functional visual status.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Future VF indices, including mean deviation (MD), pattern standard deviation (PSD), and Visual Field Index (VFI), were predicted and evaluated using mean absolute error (MAE) and root mean squared error (RMSE).
RESULTS: The model achieved MAE of 3.23 (2.91-3.56), 1.76 (1.61-1.93), and 1.14 (1.03-1.27) for future VFI, MD, and PSD in internal validation, with comparable performance in external data sets (Zeiss OCT: 3.19 [2.73-3.66], 1.92 [1.69-2.16], and 1.11 [0.95-1.29]; Heidelberg OCT: 4.14 [3.82-4.46], 2.71 [2.51-2.91], and 1.37 [1.21-1.55]). The corresponding RMSE values reflect similar trends across the internal and external data sets. Saliency maps revealed that the inner and outer RNFL layers were key structures in driving the model's predictions.
CONCLUSIONS: Our ViT-based regression model effectively predicts key future VF indices objectively from a single OCT-RNFL scan, with strong performance across 2 OCT devices, offering a novel tool for predicting functional visual status.
FINANCIAL DISCLOSURES: Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found in the Footnotes and Disclosures at the end of this article.

etudes.titre: Burden, spectrum and associated factors of ocular disease among incarcerated populations in sub-Saharan Africa: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique

labos.nom: Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology

etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: Ocular morbidity remains poorly characterized among prisoners; this systematic review and meta-analysis quantified its prevalence, spectrum and associated factors across sub-Saharan Africa (SSA).
METHODS: This review followed a published Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA) Protocols (PRISMA-P) and searched eight databases using prespecified terms, with study selection guided by PRISMA. Data were standardized and synthesized using random-effects meta-analysis to estimate pooled prevalence with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with heterogeneity assessed using I 2 and sensitivity and condition-specific analyses used to assess variation.
RESULTS: Six studies comprising 3,361 participants from four SSA countries, Nigeria, Uganda, Tanzania and Kenya, met the inclusion criteria. The pooled prevalence of ocular morbidity was 43.1% (95% CI: 12.4-77.1%; I 2 = 99.2%). Conjunctivitis was the most prevalent condition (23.9%; 95% CI, 10.7-40.1%), followed by refractive error (19.5%; 95% CI, 12.5-27.5%) and presbyopia (18.6%; 95% CI, 5.2-37.7%). Cataract (7.4%), glaucoma (5.6%) and corneal scar or opacity (3.0%) were less prevalent. Age >50 years (OR = 11.96; 95% CI, 5.31-26.94) and a history of ocular trauma (OR = 5.21; 95% CI, 1.52-17.87) were associated with higher odds of ocular morbidity. Longer imprisonment was associated with xerophthalmia (OR = 20.1; 95% CI, 8.3-48.8%), whereas access to food from outside prison was associated with lower odds of ocular morbidity (OR = 0.45; 95% CI, 0.26-0.79).
CONCLUSION: Ocular morbidity affects approximately four in ten prison inmates in SSA, with much of this burden preventable or treatable, despite considerable between-study heterogeneity and limited geographical evidence. Collectively, these findings support integrated prison eye care and standardized research to advance equitable interventions across SSA.

etudes.titre: Temporal trends in radiation-induced optic neuropathy: a meta-analysis.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: Radiation-induced optic neuropathy (RION) is a rare but disabling toxicity. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate temporal trends in the incidence of RION according to advances in radiotherapy techniques and fractionation schemes over time.
METHODS: A systematic search identified 1994-2025 studies reporting optic neuropathy in patients after radiotherapy (hereby defined as RION). Data on RION incidence, diagnostic criteria, ocular or extraocular tumor, radiotherapy modality, conventional fractionation or hypofractionation, and modeling strategies were extracted. Random effects meta-analysis was performed to estimate pooled incidence rates and assess heterogeneity.
FINDINGS: The pooled RION incidence for ocular tumors was 17.0% (95%CI:12.1-23.5%; range 0.0-81.7%; 1.3-11.0-year follow-up) (brachytherapy studies = 33, proton therapy = 3). Risk factors included tumor proximity to the optic nerves, dose exceeding 50Gy in 2Gy-equivalent dose (EQ.D2), tumor size, and patient comorbidities. The pooled RION incidence for extraocular tumors was 4.7% for conventionally fractionated (39 studies, 5.1-year follow-up) and 2.1% for hypofractionated radiotherapy (28 studies, 3.4-year follow-up). Head-and-neck tumors were significantly associated with a greater incidence of RION (estimate = 0.7185, p = 0.0076). Among extraocular tumors, only central nervous system (CNS) tumors underwent hypofractionated radiotherapy. Using meta-regression, fractionation, fraction size, and EQ.D2 did not significantly influence RION incidence in CNS tumors. Median follow-up time varied widely between studies. Meta-regression using recruitment period as a covariate did not identify a statistically significant temporal trend in RION incidence (p = 0.183). Dedicated meta-regressions on publication year, with and without outlying studies, likewise showed no significant temporal trend in intraocular (odds ratio [OR] per decade 0.87, p = 0.51), conventionally fractionated extraocular (OR 0.94, p = 0.74) or CNS tumors (OR 0.90, p = 0.46).
INTERPRETATION: RION incidence varies with tumor location, radiotherapy modality, and fractionation. Although strongly dose-dependent, RION is also influenced by pre-existing optic pathway damage, ocular comorbidities (e.g., glaucoma, diabetes), and multimodal treatments. These findings highlight the limits of dosimetric optimization alone and support a shift toward biologically driven strategies. Therapeutic development or repurposing requires a deeper mechanistic understanding of RION, for which high-resolution ophthalmological imaging offers a unique in vivo approach to identify actionable targets.

etudes.titre: Delayed recognition and therapeutic misdirection in cytomegalovirus corneal endotheliitis: A case series from Vietnam.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « recognition »
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: In immunocompetent adults, cytomegalovirus (CMV) corneal endotheliitis shares clinical features with herpesvirus-associated endotheliitis, anterior uveitis, and Posner-Schlossman syndrome, so the diagnosis is easily misdirected in our patients for periods ranging from one month to two years. Aqueous humor polymerase chain reaction (PCR), the test that establishes the etiology, is invasive and carries a non-trivial cost, so clinicians often hesitate to request it, further prolonging the time to a correct diagnosis.
CASE SERIES: We report six immunocompetent adults who experienced delayed diagnosis and deferred targeted therapy for CMV corneal endotheliitis at Ho Chi Minh City Eye Hospital. The primary objective of this report is to delineate the distinct clinical trajectories culminating in misdiagnosis. Across these diagnostic pathways, patients sustained dual ocular harm: unabated progression of CMV endotheliitis alongside treatment-related ocular toxicity from prolonged, non-targeted empirical regimens. Aqueous humor PCR confirmed CMV infection in all patients, with one case demonstrating concomitant methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus positivity. Due to substantial financial constraints, access to oral valganciclovir was markedly restricted, whereas topical 0.15% ganciclovir proved insufficient for advanced disease. These cases highlight critical economic dilemmas governing both etiologic investigation-specifically the selective use of qualitative versus quantitative PCR assays-and therapeutic accessibility in resource-limited settings.
CONCLUSION: CMV should be regarded as a mandatory differential diagnosis in the relevant clinical presentations, whether as the primary cause or as a secondary reactivation during topical corticosteroid or glaucoma therapy. Aqueous humor PCR should be viewed as a cost-saving investigation obtained early, rather than a test reserved for after empirical treatment has failed.

etudes.titre: Iris melanoma with seeding along a glaucoma drainage device: A case report.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « drainage device »
etudes.resume:
INTRODUCTION: Iris melanoma represents approximately 4% of uveal melanomas, and extraocular seeding is rare. Tumor spread along a glaucoma drainage device is exceptionally uncommon and may mimic inflammatory or vascular processes, leading to delayed diagnosis.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 78-year-old male with advanced glaucoma and prior glaucoma drainage devices developed a progressively enlarging, vascular, initially amelanotic iris lesion with rising intraocular pressure. Over several months, the lesion became increasingly pigmented with new subconjunctival changes. Early fine-needle aspiration was limited by low cellularity and lack of ocular pathology review, yielding a small nonspecific lymphoid population insufficient for diagnosis. As clinical progression continued, conjunctival biopsies performed using a no-touch technique confirmed malignant melanoma. Intraoperative findings demonstrated tumor extension from the iris into the subconjunctival space along a prior glaucoma drainage tract, prompting orbital exenteration. The patient was advised to complete adjuvant radiation therapy, but was subsequently lost to follow-up. He later re-established care with outside oncology providers, where he was diagnosed with metastatic parotid involvement and began systemic immunotherapy.
CONCLUSION: This case illustrates a rare presentation of iris melanoma with extraocular seeding through a glaucoma drainage device. Recognition of vascular or amelanotic iris lesions, attention to rising intraocular pressure, and timely no-touch biopsy are critical. Long-term multidisciplinary surveillance remains essential due to metastatic potential.

etudes.titre: Angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) drives human Tenon's capsule fibroblast activation and myofibroblast transformation via the RhoA/ROCK signaling pathway.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « pathway »
etudes.resume: Although the angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) participates in systemic tissue remodeling, its exact contribution to human subconjunctival fibrosis remains poorly understood. This study investigated the expression of AT1R in human clinical scar specimens, the downstream involvement of the RhoA/ROCK pathway, and the independent anti-fibrotic effects of receptor blockade. Primary human Tenon's capsule fibroblasts (HTCFs) were isolated from patient tissue biopsies and verified as a pure mesenchymal lineage using immunofluorescence and quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR). To model the scar microenvironment, primary cells were stimulated with transforming growth factor-beta 1 (TGF-β1), either alone or in combination with Angiotensin II, the AT1R antagonist Olmesartan (OMS), or the selective ROCK inhibitor Y-27,632. Profibrotic and structural markers, including AT1R, alpha-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA), RhoA, ROCK1, fibronectin, and collagen I alpha (COL1A1), were quantified via Western blotting, qRT-PCR and immunofluorescence. Cellular proliferation and migration were evaluated using CCK-8 and Transwell migration assays. Our ex vivo tissue analyses revealed that AT1R expression was upregulated at gene and protein levels in human Tenon's capsule scars compared to normal controls. In vitro, stimulation with TGF-β1 induced a dose-dependent upregulation of AT1R alongside core profibrotic biomarkers, while accelerating HTCF proliferation and migration rates. Conversely, treatment with OMS or Y-27,632 counteracted this TGF-β1-induced activation, reversing cellular proliferation, cell motility, and the expression of extracellular matrix components. Together, these findings indicate that subconjunctival fibrosis is driven by AT1R-RhoA/ROCK1 axis which might provide a promising mechanistic pipeline to modulate tissue scarring and optimize outcomes in glaucoma management.

etudes.titre: Investigating the impact of delisting routine eye examinations on common chronic ocular conditions in Ontario, Canada, between 1997 and 2021:a retrospective, population-based analysis.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
OBJECTIVE: Routine eye examinations under the Ontario Health Insurance Plan (OHIP) were delisted in November 2004 for individuals with no pre-existing eye conditions. We aimed to investigate the impact of delisting on the prevalence and incidence rates of common ocular conditions in adults ≥40 years.
METHODS: Using OHIP claims submitted in 1997-2021 of adults ≥40 years, common chronic ocular conditions, namely glaucoma, corneal disease, and retinopathies, were identified. A 5-year lookback period was used. Segmented linear regressions were used to determine the significance of change in incidence rates before and after delisting.
RESULTS: In adults 40-64 years, the annual prevalence of having ≥1 chronic ocular condition increased from 4.3% (2002) to 6.7% (2021). The annual incidence rate was 1.0% in 2003, decreased in 2005 (0.9%), and was followed by a period of increase to 2019 (1.5%), with fluctuations to 2021 (1.2%). Individuals in this age group not captured because of the delisting of eye examinations were estimated to be 260 273 between 2005 and 2021. For adults ≥65 years, the prevalence of having ≥1 chronic ocular condition increased from 15.4% (2002) to 24.7% (2021). Annual incidence rates in this age group remained stable during the time of delisting.
CONCLUSIONS: The annual prevalence of chronic ocular conditions increased over time. However, the increase in having ≥1 condition appeared to have slowed in adults 40-64 years since 2005, with >260 000 Ontarians likely undetected with an ocular condition. This illustrates the impact that delisting eye examinations may have on the accessibility of early diagnosis and management of chronic ocular conditions.
etudes.revue: Canadian journal of ophthalmology. Journal canadien d'ophtalmologie

etudes.titre: Role of smartphone-based digital adherence support for glaucoma medication therapy.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « medication »
etudes.resume: Sustained adherence to intraocular pressure-lowering medications is essential for preventing progressive visual loss in patients with glaucoma on pharmacotherapy. However, adherence remains suboptimal across patient populations as the result of cognitive, behavioural, physical, and socioeconomic barriers. Recent advances in digital health have introduced smartphone-based adherence supports intended to reinforce glaucoma medication routines, improve treatment organization, and support self-management. This narrative review synthesises evidence examining smartphone-based reminder applications and related digital adherence supports in glaucoma care, with attention to usability, patient experience, behavioural determinants, and clinical feasibility. Preliminary studies have reported improvements in short-term self-reported adherence and glaucoma-specific quality of life, particularly among patients with low baseline adherence. However, reminder-based interventions may provide only temporary benefit if they do not address broader structural, behavioural, and situational barriers to adherence. Current evidence remains limited by short follow-up durations, reliance on self-reported adherence measures, and limited evaluation of long-term clinical outcomes such as intraocular pressure stability and visual field preservation. Digital adherence tools may therefore be most effective when integrated alongside broader behavioural and relationship-based support strategies, including patient education, clinician communication, and caregiver involvement. Emerging technologies such as automated messaging systems and artificial intelligence-assisted tools may represent future directions for adherence support, although evidence in glaucoma remains limited. Further research is required to establish personalised, durable, and equitable adherence support frameworks in glaucoma care.
