etudes.titre: TBX3 is required for the differentiation of a subset of retinal ganglion and cone photoreceptor cells.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
UNLABELLED: Retinogenesis is a key step driving the formation of the neurons that later coordinate angiogenesis in the retina. Understanding these complex interactions requires dissecting apart its cellular and molecular drivers. To tease apart the molecular links coupling retinogenesis to vascular development, we utilized conditional knockout mouse models to selectively delete the transcription factor T-box 3 ( Tbx3 ) in 1) astrocytes, 2) postnatal retinal ganglion cells (RGCs), or 3) retinal progenitors. We demonstrate that the hypovascular retina phenotype observed upon Tbx3 loss most likely stems from a disruption of early retinogenesis. Embryonic analyses revealed that TBX3 is required during a critical retinogenic window coinciding with ATOH7 activity. While ATOH7 + progenitors are more abundant in Tbx3 mutants, the expression of key RGC and cone precursor factors (including TBX5, RXRγ, ISL1/2, POU4F2, SHH, LHX4 and OTX2) is severely diminished, halting proper RGC and cone differentiation. Utilizing birthdating experiments and developmental immunostaining, we establish TBX3 as a novel upstream regulator of RGC and cone photoreceptor specification. Because the degeneration of RGCs is the definitive hallmark of diseases like glaucoma, identifying TBX3 as a driver of early RGC formation positions it as a promising new candidate biomarker for early-stage glaucoma diagnosis and potentially therapeutic targeting.
SUMMARY STATEMENT: This study demonstrates for the first time that TBX3 plays a role in mammalian retinogenesis and in the establishment of retinal ganglion cell and cone photoreceptor subtypes.
etudes.revue: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

etudes.titre: Global, regional, and national trends in glaucoma burden among adults aged 45 years and older, 1990-2021.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide. This study aimed to assess global, regional, and national trends in glaucoma burden among adults aged ≥45 years from 1990 to 2021.
METHODS: Data were obtained from the Global Burden of Disease 2021 study. Prevalence and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) for glaucoma were analyzed by age, sex, region, and Sociodemographic Index (SDI). Joinpoint regression identified trend changes, and frontier analysis benchmarked country-level performance.
RESULTS: Globally, age-standardized prevalence declined from 116.29 to 90.12 per 100 000 (average annual percentage change, AAPC = -0.82), and DALYs from 13.37 to 9.05 (AAPC = -1.24), while absolute cases increased by 86.33% due to population aging. Five significant trend changes were identified (1994, 2001, 2006, 2010, 2019). The largest prevalence reduction was in adults aged 90-94 years. East Asia experienced the most substantial declines. SDI showed a strong negative correlation with glaucoma burden. Sub-Saharan Africa had the highest burden, while high-SDI regions had the lowest.
CONCLUSIONS: Global age-standardized prevalence and DALYs for glaucoma declined between 1990 and 2021, with accelerated declines temporally coinciding with key therapeutic advances. The absolute number of affected individuals increased due to population aging, underscoring the need for targeted screening programs and public awareness campaigns emphasizing regular eye examinations for early detection.
etudes.revue: Advances in ophthalmology practice and research

etudes.titre: A Longitudinal Comparison of Baseline Predictors of Five-Year OAG Development.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To compare sensitivities for prediction of development of open angle glaucoma (OAG) in 5 years in eyes initially assessed as clinically suspect open angle glaucoma in a prospective longitudinal study.
METHODS: Data were collected prospectively every fourth month for five years from both eyes of 88 subjects with at least one clinically glaucoma suspect eye. Presently, observations at occasions 1, 2, 15 and 16 were analyzed. An eye was considered clinically glaucoma suspect eye if it met at least one of the criteria: suspicious ophthalmoscopic optic nerve head appearance, ocular hypertension, pigment dispersion syndrome, exfoliation syndrome, or visual field asymmetry. Measurements of mean deviation (MD) with standardized automatic perimetry (SAP) were used for classification of OAG at 5 years follow-up. The OAG conversion criterion was defined as a mean SAP MD below the critical limit for normality (-3.7 dB) across occasions 15 and 16. At specificity of 95% for measurement at baseline, 95% confidence intervals for sensitivity were estimated for intraocular pressure (IOP), cup-to-disc ratio (C/D-vertical) and neuro-retinal rim area (NRA), both measured with confocal scanning laser ophthalmoscopy (CSLO) and nerve fiber layer thickness measured with laser scanning polarimetry (GDx TSNIT-global) and optical coherence tomography (OCT cpRNFLT-global), respectively. Confidence intervals were estimated using Hilgers, Delta-Wald with logit transformation, and Bootstrap strategies.
RESULTS: During the 5-year follow-up, 20 clinically suspect eyes met the OAG conversion criterion. The different strategies resulted in confidence intervals of the same order. The 95% confidence intervals estimated with Bootstrap strategy were 0.57 [0.30;0.84] for OCT cpRNFLT, 0.32 [0.08;0.61] for GDx TSNIT, 0.30 [0.08;0.59] for HRT NRA, 0.26 [0.05;0.58] for HRT vertical C/D, and 0.11 [0.02;0.27] for IOP.
CONCLUSIONS: For the currently used MD-based OAG conversion definition, OCT-cpRNFLT has the highest sensitivity for prediction of OAG development at the initial visit among the morphometric variables. The low sensitivity for IOP questions the value of IOP slightly above 21 mmHg for prediction of OAG at baseline.

etudes.titre: Artificial intelligence in glaucoma diagnosis and management: a systematic review of the past decade (2015-2026).
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Artificial intelligence »; mot du titre : « diagnosis »
etudes.resume:
INTRODUCTION: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being used to support glaucoma detection and monitoring, with rapid advances in deep learning, multimodal imaging, and longitudinal prediction. This review evaluates the evidence supporting these developments and identifies barriers to clinical translation.
AREAS COVERED: A systematic search of PubMed, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, and SpringerLink was conducted following PRISMA guidelines, with the protocol registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261450819). Of 3,758 records identified, 63 eligible peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2026 were included. The review examined AI techniques, imaging modalities, datasets, diagnostic and predictive performance, validation strategies, and reported limitations in Glaucoma care. Most studies used deep learning applied to fundus photography, optical coherence tomography (OCT), OCT angiography, visual fields, or multimodal data. Many models achieved an area under the ROC curve of approximately 0.95.
EXPERT OPINION: AI has substantial potential to improve glaucoma detection and monitoring, but high reported accuracy alone does not establish clinical readiness. Prospective multicenter validation using diverse populations, explainable and reproducible models, standardized evaluation, and integration into clinical workflows are essential before widespread implementation.

etudes.titre: Ab-interno Ripcord Reinsertion for Overfiltration-related Hypotony After A-stream Glaucoma Shunt Surgery.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Shunt »; mot du titre : « Surgery »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To describe a novel ab-interno ripcord reinsertion technique for the management of persistent overfiltration-related hypotony following ripcord removal or loss after A-stream glaucoma shunt implantation, and to report its clinical outcomes. Patients and.
METHODS: This retrospective consecutive case series included three eyes of three young women with juvenile or open-angle glaucoma who underwent ab-interno ripcord reinsertion at a single tertiary center. The primary outcome was successful resolution of hypotony, defined as restoration of IOP to 6 mmHg or higher with resolution or improvement of hypotony-related structural changes on optical coherence tomography and no further deterioration of best-corrected visual acuity attributable to hypotony. One additional eye treated with an ab-externo approach was included as a paired-eye observation for surgical comparison.
RESULTS: Ab-interno reinsertion restored IOP and resolved or improved hypotony-related structural changes in all three eyes. One week postoperatively, IOP increased from 2-6 mmHg preoperatively to 8-15 mmHg. Two eyes maintained clinically acceptable IOP without recurrent hypotony maculopathy. In one eye, hypotony resolved, but progressive IOP elevation occurred despite the ripcord remaining in situ and maximum tolerated medical therapy, requiring subsequent ripcord removal. The ab-interno approach avoided conjunctival reopening in all cases, with outcomes comparable to the paired-eye ab-externo observation.
CONCLUSION: Ab-interno ripcord reinsertion is a feasible and conjunctiva-sparing technique for resolving persistent overfiltration-related hypotony following ripcord removal or loss after A-stream glaucoma shunt implantation. Close postoperative IOP monitoring is warranted, as restoration of intraluminal resistance may result in IOP elevation requiring additional intervention in some patients.

etudes.titre: Anxiety and Depression in Glaucoma: A Narrative Review of Bidirectional Associations, Causal Evidence, and Clinical Implications.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: Anxiety and depressive symptoms are common neuropsychiatric comorbidities in glaucoma, but the direction and causal meaning of these associations remain uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate evidence in both directions by assessing whether glaucoma contributes to anxiety and depression and whether anxiety or depression influences glaucoma-related outcomes or progression.
METHODS: We conducted a structured narrative review of PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, CNKI, Wanfang Data, and VIP Database, supplemented by Google Scholar, reference screening, and citation tracking through 31 July 2026. We critically synthesized prevalence, longitudinal observational, acute-stress, intervention, and genetically informed causal evidence.
RESULTS: Evidence that glaucoma-related visual impairment and long-term management contribute to anxiety and depressive symptoms is relatively consistent. Reverse-direction evidence is weaker and heterogeneous. Acute stress may transiently raise intraocular pressure or affect visual field testing, while observational studies link psychological factors with retinal nerve fiber layer thinning, glaucoma conversion, or incident glaucoma. These associations do not establish accelerated glaucomatous neurodegeneration. Mendelian randomization and related genetic analyses do not show robust direct causal effects. Psychological interventions may improve symptoms and short-term physiological measures, but no identified trial has shown sustained slowing of visual field or retinal nerve fiber layer progression.
CONCLUSION: Current evidence supports an asymmetric relationship. Anxiety and depression are clinically important comorbidities that warrant assessment and treatment, but they are not established modifiers of glaucoma progression.

etudes.titre: Construction of Highly Viable, Excitable, Aligned Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cell-Derived Retinal Ganglion Cell Sheets on Poly-ε-caprolactone Nanofibers by Targeting Integrin β1-Mediated Adhesion Pathways.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Pathways »; mot du titre : « Retinal Ganglion Cell »

labos.nom: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science

etudes.resume: Transplantation of induced pluripotent stem cell-derived retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) is a promising strategy for optic nerve regeneration and vision restoration in glaucoma. However, injections of conventional single-cell suspensions have low engraftment rates, hindering the formation of the complex neural circuits essential for functional recovery. This study addresses this challenge by investigating an in vitro biomimetic tissue engineering approach designed for future translational objectives, such as RGC transplantation therapy. We systematically evaluated coating materials and culture supplements critical for the survival and morphological development of RGCs on biocompatible, aligned poly-ε-caprolactone (PCL) nanofiber membranes. Notably, we identified the xeno-free extracellular matrix (ECM) conditions that promote RGC neurite extension at levels comparable to animal-derived ECM, thereby overcoming a major barrier to clinical translation of this technique. Furthermore, while RGCs typically have compromised viability and limited outgrowth on nanofibers, enhancing cell-scaffold adhesion signaling via the integrin β1/focal adhesion kinase pathway significantly improved both survival and neurite development. Crucially, RGCs on aligned PCL nanofibers extended neurites along the longitudinal axes of the nanofibers, with both somata and neurites exhibiting functional calcium responses to depolarization. These findings represent a significant advancement in biomimetic in vitro tissue engineering aimed at recapitulating retinal neurite orientation, providing a scalable platform for future nanofiber-based neural regeneration therapies, with the ultimate goal of clinical applicability.

etudes.titre: A Novel Intronic OCRL1 Variant Causing Lowe Syndrome with an Atypical Phenotype Mimicking Mucopolysaccharidosis.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Lowe syndrome is a rare X-linked recessive multisystem disorder caused by pathogenic OCRL1 variants. We describe a 19-month-old child with global developmental delay, bilateral congenital cataracts, glaucoma, and hypotonia but without clinically apparent renal involvement at last follow-up. Brain and spine magnetic resonance imaging revealed scaphocephaly, a J-shaped sella, peritrigonal white-matter abnormalities, and a soft-tissue lesion causing compression at the craniovertebral junction, suggestive of mucopolysaccharidosis. Whole-exome sequencing (WES) identified a novel pathogenic hemizygous splice-site variant, c. 1880-2A > G, in OCRL1 . This case highlights the atypical phenotype of Lowe syndrome, which mimics mucopolysaccharidosis, and the diagnostic utility of WES in such presentations.
etudes.revue: Annals of Indian Academy of Neurology

etudes.titre: Doyne honeycomb retinal dystrophy with primary angle closure: a case report.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique

labos.nom: National Natural Science Foundation of China

etudes.resume:
OBJECTIVE: To report a clinical case of Doyne honeycomb retinal dystrophy (DHRD) caused by an EFEMP1 gene mutation complicated by primary angle closure, and to discuss its clinical characteristics, reasons for misdiagnosis, and therapeutic challenges.
METHODS: The clinical data of a 53-year-old male patient were retrospectively analyzed. The patient presented with binocular metamorphopsia and decreased visual acuity persisting for over 9 years. He had been previously misdiagnosed with "macular degeneration" and "macular edema" and received corresponding treatments for a prolonged period. During the current consultation, multimodal fundus imaging (FFA/ICGA/OCT), ultrasound biomicroscopy (UBM), and ophthalmic genetic testing were performed.
RESULTS: Fundus examination and imaging revealed characteristic radial drusen in the posterior pole and nasal to the optic disc, retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) atrophy, and secondary choroidal neovascularization (CNV) in the macular region. Genetic testing identified a heterozygous c.1033C>T (p.Arg345Trp) variant in the EFEMP1 gene, confirming the diagnosis of DHRD. The patient was also diagnosed with primary angle closure due to bilateral angle closure/narrowing and initially underwent bilateral laser peripheral iridotomy (LPI). Subsequently, intravitreal injections of faricimab were administered for the secondary CNV. However, due to the advanced stage of the disease, severe disruption of retinal structures, and fibrosis, no significant improvement was observed in visual acuity or anatomical structure.
CONCLUSION: The clinical manifestations of DHRD significantly overlap with age-related macular degeneration (AMD), leading to a high risk of misdiagnosis. For patients with early onset (< 50 years) and typical drusen nasal to the optic disc, genetic testing is crucial for confirmation. This case presents a rare concurrence of primary angle closure, differing from the previously reported association with open-angle glaucoma, which adds to the therapeutic complexity. Furthermore, the limited response observed in this patient may be attributed to the advanced atrophic and cicatricial macular changes, rather than indicating generalized resistance to anti-VEGF therapy in late-stage DHRD, highlighting the importance of early precise diagnosis and comprehensive management.

etudes.titre: Outcome of gonioscopy-assisted transluminal trabeculotomy in glaucoma: 5-year results.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « trabeculotomy »
etudes.resume:
OBJECTIVE: Gonioscopy-assisted transluminal trabeculotomy (GATT) has gained popularity as a microinvasive glaucoma surgery procedure, yet long-term outcomes remain understudied. Our study evaluated the 5-year efficacy and safety of GATT.
DESIGN: Multicentre retrospective cohort study.
PATIENTS: Adult patients with open-angle glaucoma who underwent GATT with or without phacoemulsification between 2016 and 2019 were included. We excluded eyes with previous glaucoma surgery, angle-closure, or traumatic glaucoma.
METHODS: The primary outcome was surgical success, defined as the absence of a need for reoperation or a laser procedure for uncontrolled intraocular pressure (IOP) or disease progression. Secondary outcomes additionally required IOP thresholds of ≤21, ≤18 and ≤15 mm Hg without an increase in anti-glaucoma medication (AGM) use. Five-year changes in IOP, AGM use, best-corrected visual acuity, OCT parameters, and adverse events also were assessed.
RESULTS: In total, 74 eyes from 62 patients (mean age 59.1 ± 13.9 years; 54% male) were analysed, including 56 standalone GATT and 18 Phaco-GATT cases. Mean baseline IOP was 23.1 ± 8.0 mm Hg on 3.2 ± 1.3 AGMs. At 5 years, mean IOP decreased by 9.6 mm Hg (41.6% reduction), and AGM use decreased by 1.1 (34.4% reduction), both P < 0.001. Success rates varied from 28% to 51% on the basis of different criteria. Cox proportional hazards analysis identified greater success in the Phaco-GATT group (hazard ratio 0.23; P = 0.015) and lower success in eyes with previous selective laser trabeculoplasty (hazard ratio 2.5; P = 0.017).
CONCLUSIONS: GATT provides sustained 5-year IOP and medication reductions with a favourable safety profile, supporting its use as an effective long-term option.
etudes.revue: Canadian journal of ophthalmology. Journal canadien d'ophtalmologie

etudes.titre: Late-onset filtering bleb complications: A review.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Late-onset filtering bleb dysfunction remains an important determinant of long-term outcomes following glaucoma filtration surgery. Although trabeculectomy provides sustained intraocular pressure (IOP) reduction, progressive changes in bleb architecture and wound healing can result in filtration failure, hypotony, leakage, ocular discomfort, and sight-threatening infection. This review examines the clinical characteristics, underlying mechanisms, assessment, prevention, and management of late-onset bleb complications, with emphasis on individualized, mechanism-directed care. Standardized bleb grading systems facilitate documentation of morphology and longitudinal assessment. Anterior segment optical coherence tomography and ultrasound biomicroscopy complement clinical examination by delineating bleb architecture and identifying potential sites of outflow obstruction, while optical coherence tomography angiography offers an evolving approach to evaluating bleb vascularity. Elevated IOP may arise from internal ostial obstruction, scleral flap adhesion, subconjunctival fibrosis, or encapsulation. Management depends on the site and extent of dysfunction and includes medical therapy, laser intervention, antifibrotic-augmented needling, and surgical revision. Conversely, excessive filtration and compromised conjunctival integrity may cause persistent hypotony, bleb leakage, and hypotony-related structural changes. Treatment ranges from selected conservative measures to compression sutures, conjunctival advancement, and tissue grafting, according to the underlying defect and associated complications. Bleb-related infection requires urgent recognition and treatment, with management determined by the extent of intraocular involvement. Related complications following glaucoma drainage device implantation, nonpenetrating surgery, and subconjunctival microstent procedures are also considered. Successful long-term care requires balancing adequate aqueous drainage against the risks of overfiltration, tissue fragility, and infection. Lifelong surveillance, patient education, and timely intervention remain central to preserving visual function. Future advances in quantitative imaging, targeted wound modulation, and safer filtration strategies may improve the durability and safety of bleb-dependent glaucoma surgery.

etudes.titre: Determining the Quality of Functional Evidence for Coding Variants in CYP1B1 for Use in Variant Classification.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique

labos.nom: National Health and Medical Research Council

etudes.resume: Biallelic variants in the CYP1B1 gene are associated with primary congenital glaucoma and some instances of anterior segment dysgenesis and juvenile open-angle glaucoma. Genetic testing is increasingly used in the diagnosis of these conditions and to inform future family planning decisions. Variant-specific functional data play a critical role in variant classification during the interpretation of genetic test results. In this study, the ClinGen Glaucoma Variant Curation Expert Panel (VCEP) evaluated published functional assays assessing CYP1B1 protein stability and enzymatic activity to determine which assays meet the recommended standards for use in variant classification, specifically when applying the PS3 or BS3 criteria from the ACMG/AMP variant interpretation guidelines. Following a comprehensive literature review, the panel identified assays that examined protein abundance and stability, as well as enzymatic activity across a range of substrates. The VCEP determined that BS3 (benign functional evidence) should not be applied to CYP1B1 as variants exhibit substrate-specific effects. After detailed review, the panel determined that two assays had an adequate number of validation controls and could distinguish between pathogenic and benign variants. The first measured 17β-estradiol activity using a commercially available luminescence kit in yeast microsomes. The second assessed benzo[a]pyrene activity via HPLC detection, also in yeast microsomes. A consensus review of additional assays recommends the inclusion of more clinical controls to either establish a significant OddsPath or to better define thresholds for applying pathogenic evidence. Incorporating validated functional data into the curation of CYP1B1 variants will enhance the accuracy of variant classification.

etudes.titre: Cross-organ translation of antifibrotic strategies from skin and lung fibrosis to glaucoma filtration surgery.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « surgery »
etudes.resume: Filtering bleb scarring after glaucoma filtration surgery (GFS) remains the leading cause of surgical failure, and current antimetabolites are limited by non-selective cytotoxicity that restricts their long-term use. Research on skin and lung fibrosis has accumulated extensive experience in antifibrotic mechanisms and therapeutic approaches. These tissues share a common transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β)-driven program of fibroblast activation and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling with Tenon capsule fibroblasts, providing a theoretical basis for translating antifibrotic strategies across organs. From a cross-organ translational medicine perspective, this review systematically summarizes progress in translating antifibrotic research from skin and lung fibrosis to antiscarring therapy for GFS, focusing on four aspects: shared fibrotic mechanisms; repurposed approved drugs and emerging molecular targets; local drug delivery systems (DDS); and ophthalmology-specific translational challenges. It also highlights mechanotransduction via Yes-associated protein (YAP)/transcriptional co-activator with PDZ-binding motif (TAZ), lysyl oxidase (LOX)-mediated ECM crosslinking, and the translational potential of local sustained-release delivery in filtering blebs. Building on this foundation, we propose that multi-target combination therapy, precision local delivery, and individualized antiscarring strategies based on biomarkers such as aqueous humor TGF-β2 may represent important future directions for improving the long-term success rate of GFS.

etudes.titre: Translational lipidomics in glaucoma: mechanisms, biomarkers, and therapeutic horizons.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « biomarkers »
etudes.resume: Glaucoma is a multifactorial optic neuropathy. Intraocular pressure (IOP), aging, vascular dysregulation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial failure, and chronic neuroinflammation converge on retinal ganglion cell (RGC) degeneration and optic nerve damage. Lipid mediators are central to this biology, linking membrane remodeling to aqueous humor (AH) dynamics, glial activation, vascular tone, extracellular matrix turnover, and neuronal survival. Lipidomics has widened the field beyond prostaglandin pharmacology to include oxylipins, lysophospholipids, sphingolipids, endocannabinoids, and specialized pro-resolving mediators (SPMs). Human studies in AH, tears, and plasma report reproducible perturbations in arachidonic acid (AA) metabolism, oxidized linoleate products, phosphatidylcholines, lysophosphatidylcholines, sphingomyelins, and ceramides; experimental models further implicate ceramide accumulation, phospholipase A2 activation, cyclooxygenase signaling, endocannabinoid tone, and failed inflammation resolution in retinal injury. Recent work also shows that latanoprost itself induces an aqueous-humor AA/LXA4 circuit in glaucoma patients, indicating that established prostaglandin therapy may engage endogenous resolution pathways and complicate the interpretation of treated-cohort lipidomic studies. This review covers the mechanistic roles of lipid mediators in IOP regulation, TM dysfunction, neuroinflammation, and neurodegeneration; the emerging biomarker literature in AH, tears, and plasma; and potential therapeutic directions, including soluble epoxide hydrolase (sEH) inhibition, sphingolipid modulation, endocannabinoid augmentation, and SPM-based neuroprotection. We conclude with the main barriers to translation: small ocular sample volumes, treatment confounding, limited longitudinal data, and the need for disease-subtype stratification.

etudes.titre: A Response to "Evaluation of the Perimouse Online Suprathreshold Visual Field Test for Glaucoma Screening in a Chinese Population: A Comparison with the Humphrey Field Analyzer" [Letter].
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Screening »; mot du titre : « Visual Field »

etudes.titre: Discharge Readiness After Ophthalmic Day Surgery: A Patient-Centered Perspective on Nursing Assessment, Self-Management, and Adherence.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Surgery »
etudes.resume: Medical eligibility for discharge after ophthalmic day surgery does not establish whether patients can manage recovery at home. This conceptual Perspective uses Transition Theory to examine how nursing assessment can connect discharge preparation with practical self-management tasks. The pathway adapts established discharge-preparation and transitional-care principles by specifying ophthalmic tasks to verify, incorporating patient preferences into feasible support arrangements, and linking unresolved deficits to reassessment and follow-up. Relevant tasks include eye-drop administration, understanding changes to treatment, recognising warning symptoms, and carrying out prescribed positioning or restrictions. Direct readiness evidence remains predominantly cataract-based, with additional observational evidence from vitreoretinal day surgery; glaucoma and corneal studies provide adjacent evidence on postoperative care and adherence. Patient-reported readiness, observed skill, medication use, positioning adherence, follow-up attendance, and patient experience should be assessed as distinct outcomes. The framework specifies how these established principles can inform procedure-specific nursing assessment and transition support.

etudes.titre: Polypseudophakia with the J&J synergy lens in high myopia: case report.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
INTRODUCTION AND IMPORTANCE: As clinicians strive to provide personalized recommendations for patients, polypseudophakia may be an option for those outside the range of traditional extended depth-of-focus lenses. We describe a case with initial refractive success but the development of a potentially vision-threatening complication.
PRESENTATION OF CASE: A 40-year-old Asian man with high myopia presented for a refractive surgery consultation with a goal of total spectacle independence and underwent bilateral refractive lens exchange with the J&J Synergy lens in the capsular bag, and a minus-power Alcon MA60MA lens in the sulcus. Initially, there was refractive success with post-operative uncorrected distance vision of 20/20 in the right eye and 20/25 in the left eye at 6 months. However, both eyes developed transillumination defects with pigment in the anterior chamber, consistent with Uveitis-Glaucoma-Hyphema (UGH) syndrome. The patient ultimately elected bilateral explantation of the sulcus intraocular lenses (IOLs) due to this complication.
CLINICAL DISCUSSION: To our knowledge, this is the first case using the J&J Synergy lens in polypseudophakia and the second to correct for high myopia. Surgical techniques for those with high myopia and thin corneas are rare, and this technique initially provided a hopeful refractive outlook. However, loss of the refractive target and the development of UGH syndrome challenged the safety of this technique.
CONCLUSION: Further studies are needed to determine which patients can tolerate this procedure. Providers should proceed cautiously and anticipate complications such as UGH syndrome following secondary sulcus IOL placement.
etudes.revue: International journal of surgery case reports

etudes.titre: Difficult strabismus surgery following subconjunctival silicone oil migration: a case report.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « surgery »
etudes.resume:
INTRODUCTION AND IMPORTANCE: Subconjunctival migration of silicone oil is a rare but clinically significant complication following vitreoretinal surgery. The resulting inflammation and fibrosis can increase the difficulty of subsequent ocular operations, such as strabismus surgery. Understanding this phenomenon is crucial for preventing intraoperative complications and ensuring better surgical outcomes.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 26-year-old female presented with sensory exotropia in the right eye following multiple vitreoretinal surgeries involving silicone oil tamponade. During strabismus surgery, multiple subconjunctival cysts filled with silicone oil and extensive fibrosis were encountered, particularly around the rectus muscle insertions. The procedure required extensive dissection and hemostasis, prolonging operative time. Despite intraoperative challenges, the postoperative ocular alignment achieved orthotropia in the primary position, with satisfactory cosmetic results.
CLINICAL DISCUSSION: Silicone oil is widely used as an internal tamponade in complex retinal detachment surgeries. Migration of silicone oil to extraocular tissues can occur through unsutured sclerotomies, wound dehiscence, or glaucoma drainage devices. Such migration may cause localized granulomatous inflammation, fibrosis, and adhesions of extraocular structures, complicating future surgeries. In this case, repeated vitreoretinal interventions and postoperative ocular hypertension were likely predisposing factors. Awareness of this potential complication is essential to minimize operative risk and optimize outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Patients with a history of silicone oil tamponade and multiple vitreoretinal procedures are at higher risk of surgical complications during routine strabismus surgery. Surgeons should anticipate difficult tissue handling, prolonged operative time, and potential bleeding. Preventive measures, such as proper sclerotomy closure and management of postoperative hypertonia, are crucial for preventing silicone oil migration.
etudes.revue: International journal of surgery case reports

etudes.titre: Axial Length-Dependent Macular Choroidal Topography in POAG: A Wide-Field Swept-Source Optical Coherence Tomography Study.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Optical Coherence Tomography »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To characterize the topography of the macular choroidal thickness (mCT) in POAG across axial lengths (AXLs), and to determine the clinical factors associated with the mCT.
METHODS: Wide-field swept-source optical coherence tomography with a 30 × 30 macular grid (6 mm × 6 mm) was used to generate spatial maps of the mCT and macular ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer thickness (mGCIPLT). The mCT was compared pointwise between POAG and control eyes, and cluster-based permutation testing was used to assess topographic significance in the entire cohort and in three subgroups stratified by AXL (<24.5 mm, 24.5-26.0 mm, and ≥26.0 mm). Clinical factors associated with the mCT were evaluated using regression analyses.
RESULTS: This study included 117 POAG eyes and 157 control eyes. While the mCT was only marginally thinner in POAG eyes than in controls, topographic analyses of the mCT revealed areas of localized thinning in the papillomacular and inferotemporal peripapillary areas in POAG, which did not overlap with the pattern of mGCIPLT reduction. These topographic changes were observed only in eyes with an AXL of <26.0 mm, with no regional differences in eyes with an AXL of ≥26.0 mm.
CONCLUSIONS: In POAG eyes, the mCT reduction was localized to the papillomacular and inferotemporal peripapillary regions, which are critical areas for central visual function and topographically distinct from structural retinal ganglion cell loss. This pattern was not observed in eyes with long AXLs, presumably because significant axial-elongation-induced thinning restricts further discernible changes. Future studies are needed to determine the clinical significance of mCT alterations in POAG.

etudes.titre: Electrical stimulation targeting optic nerve regeneration following acute and chronic neuropathies.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique

labos.nom: National Health and Medical Research Council

etudes.resume: Optic neuropathies such as glaucoma or optic neuritis are conditions whereby the optic nerve is damaged by mechanisms including ischemia, compression, inflammation or immune-mediated processes, leading to progressive degeneration of retinal ganglion cells and subsequent loss of vision. Strategies including medication and surgery help to slow down these diseases but fail to repair the neurons of the optic nerve themselves. In this review, we first detail the range of optic nerve neuropathies and their current front line treatment options, briefly outline various experimental treatment strategies and their limitations, before focusing on electrical stimulation as a treatment strategy, covering the current state of the art and potential routes for further development.

etudes.titre: Assessment setting affects the evaluation of functional mobility in older adults with glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: Older adults with glaucoma are at a greater risk of falls than those without, and visual field loss is associated with mobility limitations and fall risk. In-clinic gait assessments can identify those with mobility limitations, but these tools are underused in routine glaucoma care. Further, it remains unknown if gait measured in clinic is associated with gait in everyday environments for older adults with glaucoma.
METHODS: In this pilot study, older adults with glaucoma (n = 36, 77 ± 5 years) completed a 2-minute walk test in the clinic and then in their home. Participants wore three inertial measurement units, and spatiotemporal gait metrics were computed from this data. In-clinic and at-home gait metrics were compared to test the effect of setting and whether at-home gait metrics were associated with in-clinic metrics.
RESULTS: Nearly all gait metrics differed by setting. On average, participants walked slower, less symmetrically, and more variably at home than in the clinic. Despite these differences, most at-home gait metrics were linearly associated with those measured in-clinic. Glaucoma severity did not moderate the setting-related effects.
CONCLUSIONS: Gait assessed in clinic was different, but associated with, at-home gait. These preliminary findings suggest that relying solely on clinic-based gait assessments may underestimate mobility limitations. Instead, combining brief in-clinic assessments with wearable sensor-based real-world monitoring may better identify older adults with glaucoma who are at an elevated risk for falls and functional decline. Further study is needed to test these hypotheses and determine if additional patient, disease, or at-home gait features could contribute to a more sensitive composite risk assessment.

etudes.titre: Risk of angle-closure glaucoma after lens extraction versus laser peripheral iridotomy in primary angle-closure suspects.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « laser »
etudes.resume:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between lens extraction versus laser peripheral iridotomy (LPI) and progression from primary angle-closure suspect (PACS) to coded angle-closure glaucoma (ACG).
DESIGN: Retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study.
PARTICIPANTS: Patients with PACS undergoing lens extraction or LPI (January 2014 to February 2026) in the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network and matched 1:1 on demographics, systemic and ocular comorbidities, medications, and body mass index, yielding 6059 patients per group (mean age, 68 years; 69% female; 59% White).
METHODS: The primary outcome was a new coded ACG diagnosis assessed using Cox regression. Prespecified subgroup analyses by age (<60, 60-70, >70 years) and sex used separately matched cohorts, with optic neuritis as a negative control outcome.
RESULTS: Coded ACG occurred in 3.5% of the lens-extraction group versus 5.4% of the LPI group (hazard ratio [HR] 0.66, 95% CI 0.56-0.79, P < 0.001). A significant benefit was observed in patients >70 years (HR 0.62, P < 0.001), but not in patients <60 years (HR 0.85, P = 0.63) nor 60-70 years (HR 0.78, P = 0.16). Among patients with LPI, 45% subsequently underwent lens extraction, with lower risk than LPI alone (HR 0.60, P = 0.001). Corneal edema, retinal detachment, and macular hole occurred more frequently after lens extraction than after LPI.
CONCLUSIONS: Lens extraction was associated with lower risk of coded ACG than LPI in patients with PACS, most consistently in those >70 years, but was also associated with more frequent complications. Given the observational design, prospective studies are needed to confirm these findings and identify which patients are most likely to benefit from early lens extraction.
etudes.revue: Canadian journal of ophthalmology. Journal canadien d'ophtalmologie

etudes.titre: Chronic Topical Water-Soluble Cannabidiol Formulation Reduces Intraocular Pressure and Corneal Mechanical Sensitivity in DBA/2J Mice.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Mice »
etudes.resume: Glaucoma is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disease and a leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide. Although elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) is the main modifiable risk factor, current therapies often fail to fully prevent disease progression and may cause ocular discomfort. Cannabidiol (CBD) has attracted increasing interest due to its anti-inflammatory, analgesic and vasoregulatory properties, yet its ocular effects remain controversial, partly due to formulation-dependent limitations and short-term administration paradigms. We evaluated a novel water-soluble topical CBD formulation in a spontaneous murine model of glaucoma (DBA/2J mice), using CD-1 mice as a non-glaucomatous comparator strain. IOP, tear production, corneal mechanical sensitivity and body weight were assessed longitudinally in conscious animals following acute and chronic CBD administration (once or twice daily). Contralateral untreated eyes were analyzed to investigate potential systemic or bilateral effects. Following an initial transient IOP increase, topical CBD progressively induced a significant and sustained reduction of IOP in the treated eyes of DBA/2J mice, particularly during chronic twice-daily administration. IOP changes in contralateral eyes were smaller and inconsistent, supporting a predominantly local ocular effect. CBD also increased corneal touch threshold in DBA/2J mice, indicating reduced corneal mechanical sensitivity, with effects persisting after treatment withdrawal. Tear production and body weight were not significantly affected in either strain, suggesting good ocular and systemic tolerability. Overall, chronic topical administration of a water-soluble CBD formulation lowered IOP and modulated corneal sensitivity in a strain-dependent manner. These findings support CBD as a potential adjunctive therapeutic strategy targeting both ocular hypertension and sensory dysfunction.

etudes.titre: [Multiple mechanisms and intervention strategies of monocytes/macrophages in ocular diseases].
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « mechanisms »

labos.nom: National Natural Science Foundation of China

etudes.resume: Monocytes/macrophages possess prominent heterogeneity and functional plasticity, and their functional imbalance participates in the initiation and progression of multiple ocular diseases. This review summarizes the roles of monocytes/macrophages in age-related macular degeneration, diabetic retinopathy, high myopia, uveitis and glaucoma. It particularly elaborates their pathogenic mechanisms involving oxidative stress, inflammatory amplification, blood-retinal barrier disruption and pathological neovascularization, alongside their immunomodulatory and tissue-repairing functions. We also outline intervention strategies targeting monocytes/macrophages, including blocking pro-inflammatory recruitment and signaling pathways, inducing anti-inflammatory polarization, and immune reprogramming, which may offer novel ideas for precision therapy of chronic inflammatory ocular diseases.
etudes.revue: [Zhonghua yan ke za zhi] Chinese journal of ophthalmology

etudes.titre: Piezo1 mechanobiology in high myopia and glaucoma: compartment-specific evidence, gaps, and a hypothesis-generating susceptibility framework.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: High myopia and glaucoma are clinically distinct but mechanobiologically connected conditions. High myopia is commonly associated with marked axial elongation, posterior-segment stretch, scleral remodeling, and altered posterior-pole and peripapillary biomechanics, whereas glaucoma involves intraocular pressure (IOP)-related outflow stress, optic nerve head (ONH) strain, and retinal ganglion cell (RGC) vulnerability. Both disorders therefore converge on chronic mechanical stress and compartment-specific susceptibility. Piezo1, a mechanically activated cation channel, is well positioned to connect membrane tension, extracellular matrix (ECM) state, Ca2+ signaling, reactive oxygen species (ROS)-associated stress responses, and cellular remodeling. This review develops a hypothesis-driven but evidence-bound framework centered on a possible Piezo1-linked mechanobiological susceptibility axis between high myopia and glaucoma. The strongest ocular evidence remains in the trabecular meshwork and conventional outflow pathway, where activation, perturbation, Ca2+ signaling, matrix and prostaglandin readouts, and outflow-related assays converge. Evidence in optic nerve head astrocytes is moderate, retinal ganglion cell evidence is emerging, and myopia-related evidence currently supports retinal or posterior-segment stress signaling more strongly than scleral fibroblast-specific ECM causality. Myopia-specific scleral fibroblast evidence and peripapillary-scleral evidence remain exploratory. Critically, current evidence does not demonstrate a continuous Piezo1-dependent causal chain linking scleral remodeling or peripapillary load redistribution to optic nerve head deformation and glaucomatous RGC degeneration. Accordingly, the proposed high-myopia-glaucoma susceptibility axis should be regarded as a hypothesis-generating framework rather than an established causal pathway. This evidence-graded approach distinguishes directly supported tissue-level mechanisms from cross-compartment relationships that require targeted experimental validation.

etudes.titre: Glaucoma in Somalia: From Late Presentation to Prevention, Building a National Pathway for Glaucoma Care.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Pathway »
etudes.resume: Glaucoma is a major cause of irreversible vision loss for which timely detection and sustained treatment can reduce disease progression. In Somalia, a tertiary eye-clinic study reported primary open-angle glaucoma in 7% of 1550 attendees older than 40 years, while a community outreach report classified 9% of 628 screened participants as having glaucoma risk; 28 people were referred for glaucoma evaluation. These estimates arise from different selected populations, use different case definitions, and are not comparable estimates of national prevalence. A recent tertiary-center study also identified glaucoma among causes of adult blindness. This commentary proposes a six-stage, integrated glaucoma care pathway for Somalia: awareness and risk recognition, primary-level detection, referral and referral refinement, specialist confirmation, individualized treatment, and continued follow-up. Its specific proposed adaptations are closed-loop referral tracking, competency-based triage, an essential-care package, and a minimal clinical registry. Published Somali observations are distinguished from regional evidence and untested implementation proposals. Suggested referral triggers and pilot performance measures are provided, but their local feasibility, effectiveness, and cost-effectiveness require prospective evaluation. The pathway is a framework for phased service development, not a validated national protocol.

etudes.titre: Effect of Eye Movement and Body Position on Optic Nerve Sheath Width.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: Orbital cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) dynamics are poorly understood but are postulated to play a role in several optic nerve pathologies. This study aims to evaluate the effects of eye movement and body position on perioptic CSF clearance by optic nerve sheath width (ONSW) measurement.
METHODS: Healthy adult patients were recruited prospectively from an outpatient ophthalmology clinic at an academic center. B-mode ultrasound was used to measure optic nerve sheath width (ONSW) 3 mm posterior to the optic disc after 5 minutes of no eye movement (-EM) and 1 minute of eye movement (+EM) in three body positions: upright, supine, and prone. CSF clearance is the difference between ONSW +EM and -EM in each body position.
RESULTS: Thirty-eight adults with healthy optic nerves were recruited. ONSW -EM were significantly wider than +EM in all three positions (P = 0.002, 0.024, 0.002). Body positioning only significantly affected ONSW -EM (P = 0.030), while +EM ONSW was not significantly different in any body position, indicating a baseline effect.
CONCLUSION: Eye movement and body position significantly impact orbital CSF dynamics and ONSW. Prone positioning increased ONSW, highlighting the role of gravity dependence in perioptic CSF clearance. Identifying factors that impact CSF dynamics is imperative to understanding its part in optic nerve disease.

etudes.titre: Unilateral Angle Closure as the Initial Presentation of Multiple Myeloma Metastasis.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: Ocular manifestations of multiple myeloma (MM) are rare but may affect all tissues of the eye. This report describes a patient with recurrent MM initially presenting with ocular hypertension due to angle closure, revealing extensive ocular, orbital, and systemic metastatic disease.
CASE REPORT: A 54-year-old female patient with previously treated MM presented with left eye pain, blurred vision, and an intraocular pressure of 38 mmHg. Examination revealed proptosis, restricted upward gaze, conjunctival injection with two salmon-patch lesions, and complete angle closure. Further findings included multiple ciliary body cysts, a massive choroidal mass, and retinal/choroidal detachments. She had pancytopenia. Magnetic resonance imaging confirmed recurrent MM with superior rectus muscle and spine infiltrations, and a large prevertebral lymph node mass. The patient responded well to antiglaucoma medications and was referred to her oncologist.
CONCLUSION: MM can involve various ophthalmic structures. Patients with MM require regular examinations for early detection of ocular metastasis.

etudes.titre: Gut-hormone receptor systems in the eye: Pharmacological, local and putative endocrine signalling.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Pharmacological »
etudes.resume: The neural retina has traditionally been viewed as a downstream target of systemic metabolic disease, yet experimental and clinical evidence suggests that ocular tissues may also respond directly to peptide-hormone signalling. This review critically examines gut-hormone-related receptor systems in the eye across three biologically distinct evidence streams: endogenous circulating gut peptides, pharmacological receptor agonism, and locally synthesised ocular peptides. Physiological retinal access of native gut peptides remains poorly characterised, while receptor localisation is highly dependent on species and detection methodology. Mechanistic evidence is strongest for pharmacological GLP-1 receptor activation and local NPY and ghrelin systems, particularly in relation to neuroprotection, immunomodulation, metabolic and oxidative homeostasis, and neurovascular regulation. Human evidence remains disease-specific: diabetic retinopathy findings vary with glycaemic trajectory and endpoint definition; age-related macular degeneration associations are heterogeneous; glaucoma studies suggest a possible reduction in incidence without establishing protection against progression; and dry-eye evidence remains preliminary. Semaglutide also carries a regulatory safety signal for non-arteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy. Future research should establish physiological ligand access and receptor engagement, validate ocular receptor localisation, characterise retinal and optic-nerve-head microvascular responses, and incorporate prospective ophthalmic phenotyping into metabolic-drug trials. Overall, current evidence supports pharmacological and local ocular peptide-receptor signalling, whereas direct physiological endocrine communication between the gut and eye remains unproven.

etudes.titre: Incidence and Management of Ocular Hypertension Following the 0.19 mg Fluocinolone Acetonide Implant for Diabetic Macular Edema.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To investigate the real-world incidence and management of ocular hypertension (OHT) following the intravitreal 0.19 mg fluocinolone acetonide implant (FAi, Iluvien) for diabetic macular edema (DME).
METHODS: Retrospective review of eyes treated with FAi (2015-2025) with ≥1 month follow-up. Primary outcome was OHT (IOP >25 mmHg). Secondary outcomes included IOP >30 mmHg, IOP rise ≥10 mmHg from baseline, and OHT management.
RESULTS: A total of 118 eyes (90 patients) were included with mean follow-up of 33.1 ± 1.3 months. Mean baseline IOP was 14.0 ± 3.0 mmHg. Pre-existing glaucoma or OHT was present in 32.2% of eyes, and 78.8% had a prior periocular or intravitreal corticosteroid injection. Overall, 11 eyes (9.3%) developed OHT (IOP >25mmHg) following FAi. Peak IOP >30 mmHg occurred in 6 eyes (5.1%), and 12 eyes (10.2%) had an IOP rise ≥10 mmHg above baseline. OHT developed at variable time points, with 36.4% of cases occurring between 6-12 months and 27.3% after 24 months; mean time to OHT development was 15.6 ± 13.1 months. Higher baseline IOP was associated with increased odds of developing OHT (OR per 1mmHg increase 1.32, p=0.02). Of the 11 eyes with OHT, most were managed medically (63.6%) or with observation (36.4%) alone, with only 1 eye (9.1%, 0.8% of entire cohort) requiring incisional glaucoma surgery.
CONCLUSION: FAi was associated with low rates of OHT, with most cases managed with observation or topical therapy, with surgery rarely required. This supports the safety of FAi and highlight the importance of extended IOP monitoring.

etudes.titre: Staged surgical management of an acute angle-closure crisis with medically refractory intraocular pressure elevation: A case report and literature review.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « surgical »
etudes.resume:
RATIONALE: Acute angle closure with markedly elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) is an ocular emergency. Initial management aims to lower IOP, reduce corneal edema and inflammation, and permit definitive relief of pupillary block, usually by laser peripheral iridotomy (LPI). When IOP remains uncontrolled and corneal edema or an extremely shallow anterior chamber precludes safe LPI, urgent surgical intervention may be required.
PATIENT CONCERNS: A 61-year-old woman presented with a 7-hour history of pain, redness, and blurred vision in the right eye (RE), accompanied by headache.
DIAGNOSES: Acute primary angle closure in the RE and primary angle-closure suspect status in the left eye (LE).
INTERVENTIONS: During initial treatment with topical pilocarpine, carteolol, and brinzolamide, IOP in the RE increased from 32 to 58 mm Hg. It remained markedly elevated despite 2 intravenous infusions of 20% mannitol (50 grams each), and emergency surgical peripheral iridectomy was performed. After the acute episode stabilized, the RE underwent phacoemulsification with intraocular lens implantation; the fellow eye subsequently underwent lens extraction with intraocular lens implantation.
OUTCOMES: After peripheral iridectomy, IOP in the RE decreased from 58 to 11 mm Hg without additional IOP-lowering medication, and central anterior chamber depth increased from 1.24 to 1.60 mm. At 6 months after subsequent bilateral lens extraction, IOP was 14 mm Hg in the RE and 15 mm Hg in the LE without IOP-lowering medication. Central anterior chamber depth increased from 1.24 to 4.36 mm in the RE and from 2.27 to 4.35 mm in the LE. Uncorrected visual acuity was 20/20 in the RE and 20/33 in the LE, and best-corrected visual acuity was 20/20 in both eyes.
LESSONS: Emergency surgical peripheral iridectomy may serve as a rescue procedure in selected patients with medically uncontrolled acute angle closure when LPI is not feasible. Subsequent lens extraction may relieve residual lens-related anterior-segment crowding. However, this single case cannot establish the comparative effectiveness of the staged approach or whether peripheral iridectomy followed by lens extraction is the optimal treatment sequence.

etudes.titre: Do Adjunctive Anti-scarring Agents Including Mitomycin-C Improve Glaucoma Tube Shunt Surgery: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Shunt »; mot du titre : « Tube »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: Adjunctive anti-scarring agents (ASAs), including mitomycin C (MMC), 5-Fluorouracil (5FU), corticosteroids and vascular endothelial growth factor antagonists (anti-VEGF), aim to improve glaucoma tube shunt (GTS) surgery by attenuating peri-endplate fibrosis. While used in trabeculectomy, ASAs are less established in GTS surgery, leading to varied practices. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated their efficacy and safety.
METHODS: Prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD 4,202,236,526), MEDLINE, EMBASE, and CENTRAL were searched for randomised controlled trials (RCTs) and comparative cohort studies (CCSs) comparing ASA and non-ASA use in GTS surgery. Outcomes included changes in intra-ocular pressure (IOP), anti-glaucoma medications, re-operation, and complication rates between baseline and post-operative months 3, 6, and 12.
RESULTS: 28 studies (n = 1621 eyes) were included: 12 RCTs (n = 624 eyes) and 16 CCSs (n = 997 eyes). ASAs included MMC (n = 11/28), corticosteroids (n = 7/28), Anti-VEGF (n = 6/28), and 5FU (n = 2/28). Two studies used dual agents. ASA did not affect post-operative IOP [pooled difference (PD) 1.99 mmHg, 1.06 mmHg, 1.15 mmHg at month 3 (p = 0.059), 6 (p = 0.30), and 12 (p = 0.23), respectively]. ASA and MMC use resulted in fewer anti-glaucoma eyedrops required at month 3, 6, and 12 (PD = 0.56, 0.42, 0.49; p < 0.001, = 0.031, 0.013); (PD = 0.76, 0.73, 0.73; p < 0.001, = 0.001, < 0.013), respectively. Both increased hypotony development risk (OR = 2.06, p = 0.001; OR = 2.27, p = 0.001). All other complication rates were similar (all p > 0.05). The re‑operative rate was lower with MMC (OR = 0.42, p = 0.007).
CONCLUSION: ASAs, particularly MMC, reduced glaucoma medication burden at 12 months, but increased the risk of post-operative hypotony.

etudes.titre: A diagnostic challenge: syphilitic optic neuropathy.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « diagnostic »
etudes.resume: Syphilitic optic neuropathy is an uncommon but treatable cause of visual loss and may occur as an isolated manifestation of neurosyphilis. We report a 72-year-old man who presented with progressive painless unilateral visual loss. He was initially diagnosed as non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy but later developed progressive worsening, optic nerve MRI abnormalities and delayed visual evoked potentials. Other causes of optic neuropathies, such as demyelination were considered. Despite immunotherapy, vision continued to deteriorate. Subsequent investigations demonstrated positive serum VDRL and TPPA. With the exclusion of other causes of chronic optic neuropathy, syphilitic optic neuropathy was diagnosed. Treatment with intravenous benzylpenicillin stabilized vision, although established optic atrophy prevented visual recovery. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges and emphasizes the importance of routine syphilis serology in atypical, progressive, or treatment-refractory optic neuropathies.

etudes.titre: Chromatin dynamics secondary to dexamethasone exposure identifies 67 genes linked to elevated IOP and primary open-angle glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « genes »
etudes.resume: Primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) is a chronic neurodegenerative disorder, and elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) represents its only modifiable risk factor. We modeled increased IOP by treating three primary human trabecular meshwork cell strains with dexamethasone and generated a high-resolution map of promoter-centered chromatin contacts and regulatory modules. We identify dynamic changes in chromatin compartments and looping, cis-regulatory elements, and transcription factor hubs corresponding to altered expression profile. By integrating Genomewide association studies associated variants with dexamethasone induced chromatin landscape, we ascertain 29 target genes linked to 23 lead IOP variants and 57 genes for 46 POAG variants, with 19 shared between the two. Pathway analysis of 67 IOP- and POAG-associated genes reveals enrichment in vesicle transport, TLR, MAPK, and hippo-YAP signaling pathways. We also uncover transcriptional regulatory role of 103 noncoding lead variants. Our studies provide a mechanistic framework of genetic complexity accompanying steroid-induced IOP and related POAG pathology.
etudes.revue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

etudes.titre: Isolation and characterization of primary canine peripapillary scleral fibroblasts, optic nerve head astrocytes, and lamina cribrosa cells from glaucomatous and non-glaucomatous eyes.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Glaucoma involves cell-specific remodeling within the optic nerve head (ONH) and peripapillary sclera, yet disease-relevant primary cell culture systems in large-animal species remain limited. The objective of this study was to establish reproducible methods for the isolation, culture and characterization of primary canine scleral fibroblasts, ONH astrocytes, and lamina cribrosa (LC) cells from glaucomatous and non-glaucomatous eyes based on their morphological features and immunocytochemical marker expression. ONH and peripapillary scleral tissues were collected from glaucomatous and non-glaucomatous dog eyes. Scleral fibroblasts were isolated from peripapillary scleral tissue, while ONH astrocytes and LC cells were derived from LC explants using cell-type-specific culture conditions. Cell identity was assessed by morphological assessment and immunocytochemical staining using established cell-specific markers. Primary scleral fibroblasts were successfully cultured from both glaucomatous and control eyes. LC explants initially yielded mixed populations of ONH astrocytes and LC cells, which were subsequently separated using differential culture protocols. Immunocytochemical characterization demonstrated scleral fibroblasts (vimentin+, laminin+, cytokeratin-, CD45-), ONH astrocytes (GFAP+, α-SMA-), and LC cells (GFAP-, α-SMA+). This study provides the first report of primary cultures of scleral fibroblasts, ONH astrocytes, and LC cells in the canine species. The morphological and immunocytochemical characteristics of the cultured cells are consistent with those reported in humans and other species. These culture systems establish a novel platform for investigating cell-specific biomechanical and molecular mechanisms relevant to glaucoma pathophysiology using a clinically relevant large-animal model.

etudes.titre: Step change in glaucoma polygenic risk score performance enables clinical utility.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « polygenic »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: Open-angle glaucoma (OAG) is the leading cause of irreversible blindness and is highly heritable. Despite effective treatments, approximately 50% of cases remain undiagnosed. We aimed to develop and validate a clinically applicable, genetics-based risk prediction tool for OAG across diverse ancestries.
DESIGN: Genetic association study and risk prediction analysis.
PARTICIPANTS: More than 6 million individuals contributing genome-wide association study data from multiple ancestry groups.
METHODS: We constructed a comprehensive polygenic risk score (PRS) for OAG using a multitrait modeling framework that integrated glaucoma-related traits, including intraocular pressure, optic disc parameters, and ocular hypertension. PRS performance was evaluated for OAG risk across major ancestry groups and assessed for associations with age at diagnosis, treatment escalation, surgical outcomes, and familial risk.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Odds ratios (ORs) for OAG by PRS percentile, age at disease onset, absolute risk estimates, treatment escalation, glaucoma surgery, and OAG risk in first-degree relatives.
RESULTS: In Australian individuals of European ancestry, those in the top 10% of the PRS distribution had a 10-fold increased risk of OAG compared with the remainder (OR 10.04, 95% CI 7.43-13.59), substantially outperforming our previously published PRS (OR 4.2). Similar performance was observed in U.S. European ancestry data (OR 9.09, 95% CI 5.09-16.26). In UK Biobank Europeans the OR for the top 10% versus the remainder was 4.91 (95% CI 4.25-5.69). Although performance was attenuated in other ancestry groups (OR top 10% vs. remainder: 4.01 in South Asian, 3.39 in East Asian, and ranging from 2.26 to 3.81 in African ancestry populations depending on cohort), high PRS percentiles corresponded to elevated absolute risk across all groups. On average, individuals in the highest-risk decile developed glaucoma approximately 25 years earlier than those in the lowest decile and had ∼100-fold (OR 96.83, 95% CI 52.61-178.21) higher risk. The PRS also predicted treatment escalation in early disease, prevalent and incident glaucoma surgery, and OAG risk among first-degree relatives.
CONCLUSIONS: This enhanced PRS, available for clinical use through an accredited genotyping workflow, enables effective risk stratification for OAG across diverse ancestries, facilitating earlier identification and treatment of high-risk individuals while supporting resource rationalisation for those at low risk. Performance is strongest in European ancestry populations, and further work is needed to improve equity of performance across ancestries.

etudes.titre: Implications of Image-Level Duplication in Public Glaucoma Datasets.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
IMPORTANCE: Medical artificial intelligence (AI) can be trusted only if validated in patients not used for development. In glaucoma AI, a few public datasets from 1 laboratory serve as those independent cohorts.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether 3 public glaucoma datasets used for external validation and fairness evaluation are independent patient cohorts.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cross-sectional dataset audit and record-linkage analysis was conducted in July 2026 using the publicly distributed files of Harvard-GDP (1000 eyes), Harvard-GF (3300 eyes), and Harvard-FairVision (10 000 eyes), all from a single laboratory. Records were linked by exact visual field and demographic fingerprints, with chance modeled from the within-dataset collision rate and permutation. All 1302 candidate pairs underwent direct image comparison.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Number of shared eyes and image-level identity of optical coherence tomography (OCT) scans distributed under different identifiers.
RESULTS: Harvard-GF and Harvard-FairVision matched on 1302 eyes against 1.9 expected by chance. Direct comparison confirmed 1031 (79.2%; 95% CI, 76.9%-81.4%) as the same 3-dimensional OCT volume (cosine similarity ≥0.9999; 88% of voxels exactly equal), at least 31% of the 3300 Harvard-GF eyes, a lower bound. Duplication was similar across the 3 Harvard-FairVision splits (78.5%-80.8%). Harvard-GDP and Harvard-GF shared 22 eyes matching exactly on all 52 total-deviation points and mean deviation, all in the Harvard-GF validation split; Harvard-GDP distributes no OCT volume, so its overlap rests on weaker evidence. No file carried a patient identifier, and no release disclosed the overlap; among the 64 of 105 citing studies whose full text we obtained, none reported it. Across 5 training runs, a classifier trained on 1 dataset and evaluated on the other gave an area under the curve of 0.90 (95% CI, 0.83-0.94) where 78.5% (95% CI, 74.0%-82.5%) of test eyes were training data, against 0.78 (95% CI, 0.72-0.83) out of sample (inflation, 0.12; 95% CI, 0.06-0.18). Inflation occurred in every racial subgroup and was larger where out-of-sample performance was lower (Spearman ρ = -0.57; permutation P = .02).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: These findings suggest that the examined datasets were not independent cohorts. Treating them as independent benchmarks inflates reported performance and might mask fairness gaps through data leakage and nonindependent validation.

etudes.titre: Oculoplastic and ocular surface morbidity after medication-first therapy versus selective laser trabeculoplasty: A 6-year analysis of the LiGHT trial.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « medication »
etudes.resume: PurposeLong-term topical glaucoma medication may contribute to ocular surface and oculoplastic morbidity. This study compared ocular morbidity after medication-first versus selective laser trabeculoplasty (SLT)-first therapy over six years in the LiGHT Trial.MethodsThis post hoc secondary analysis used adverse-event and quality-of-life data from the 6-year LiGHT Trial extension cohort. Patients were grouped by randomised strategy (SLT-first or medication-first); the SLT-first arm was subdivided into those who later received medication and those who remained medication-free. Adverse events were categorised as ocular surface disease, oculoplastic changes, or surgical intervention, compared by logistic regression adjusted for age and sex. Quality-of-life change was assessed with mixed-effects models.ResultsA total of 633 patients were included: 313 SLT-first and 320 medication-first. Ocular surface disease was more frequent in the medication-first arm than in the SLT-first arm (65.3% vs 51.8%; OR 1.75, 95% CI 1.27-2.41; p = 0.001), as were oculoplastic changes (33.4% vs 17.9%; OR 2.30, 95% CI 1.59-3.35; p < 0.001). Surgical intervention rates were similar. Within the SLT-first arm, patients who later required medication had higher morbidity than those who remained medication-free.ConclusionsMedication-first therapy was associated with greater ocular surface and oculoplastic morbidity than SLT-first therapy. Findings should be interpreted as treatment-strategy effects rather than isolated prostaglandin-specific effects.

etudes.titre: Keratoconus - Common, yet uncommon.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique

labos.nom: Stiftelsen Kronprinsessan Margaretas Arbetsnämnd för Synskadade

etudes.resume: In this Acta Ophthalmologica Award and Gold Medal Honorary Lecture (the Lundsgaard Gold Medal Honorary Lecture) I will summarize and review the work on the elusive corneal disease keratoconus (KC) I have carried out together with collaborators and research students over more than 30 years. It has been a long journey, from basic biochemical work to clinical studies comparing and evaluating different regimens for corneal crosslinking. KC is a bilateral, albeit usually asymmetric, progressive ectatic corneal disorder, in which the cornea becomes thinner and regionally biomechanically weaker. Due to the intraocular pressure the weakest part of the cornea is extruded, forming a central or paracentral cone, which in turn generates irregular optical aberrations and deterioration of the quality of vision. KC has traditionally been considered a noninflammatory, rather rare corneal degeneration, but over the past decades such a description has become increasingly difficult to defend. KC shares many biochemical features with inflammatory diseases for example in the pattern of cytokine expression and is-at least according to some studies-associated with atopic dermatitis and eye rubbing. Furthermore, with the emerge of modern corneal imaging techniques, an increasing number of KC cases is discovered today, and today's consensus is that KC should be considered as a relatively common eye disease with a prevalence "approaching" 1:300. It typically begins during adolescence or early adulthood and progresses until the age of 30-35. Thus-in contrast to many of the major causes of visual impairment such as cataract, glaucoma and age-related macular degeneration-KC is uncommon, almost unique, in being predominantly a disease of young people. I have spent the past 30 odd years trying to understand this intriguing corneal degeneration and will try to explain why and how in this article.
