etudes.titre: Association of Ambient Air Pollution Exposure With Early Failure After Incisional Glaucoma Surgery.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Surgery »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the associations between exposure to 6 ambient air pollutants and the risk of early failure after incisional glaucoma surgery.
DESIGN: Multicenter retrospective cohort study.
PARTICIPANTS: Patients who underwent incisional glaucoma surgery at 3 tertiary centers in China from 2015 to 2025.
METHODS: Individual-level exposure to 6 ambient air pollutants, including particulate matter with aerodynamic diameter less than 2.5 μm (PM2.5), particulate matter with aerodynamic diameter less than 10 μm (PM10), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), sulfur dioxide (SO2), ozone (O3), and carbon monoxide (CO), was estimated using residential geocoding-linked spatiotemporal data. Associations between pollutant exposure and surgical failure within 30, 60, and 90 days after surgery were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models with progressive adjustment for demographic, clinical, surgical, and environmental covariates. Restricted cubic spline analyses and center-level meta-analyses were also performed to assess exposure-response relationships and between-center heterogeneity.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Surgical failure within 30, 60, and 90 days after incisional glaucoma surgery.
RESULTS: A total of 7,820 eyes were included, with 466 failures by 30 days, 711 by 60 days, and 1,083 by 90 days. PM2.5 was consistently associated with an increased risk of surgical failure across the 30-, 60-, and 90-day analyses, with adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) of 1.090 (95% CI, 1.001-1.187), 1.141 (95% CI, 1.064-1.224), and 1.240 (95% CI, 1.162-1.324), respectively. O3 and CO were associated with failure during the early postoperative period, whereas PM10 and NO2 showed stronger associations at later postoperative intervals. PM2.5 demonstrated an approximately linear exposure-response pattern, whereas SO2 was not significantly associated with surgical failure. No substantial between-center heterogeneity was observed. In subgroup analyses, the associations of O3 and CO with surgical failure were stronger in older and female patients, and the association between PM10 and 90-day failure differed by intraoperative 5-fluorouracil use (P for interaction = 0.016).
CONCLUSIONS: Exposure to several ambient air pollutants was associated with increased risk of early failure after incisional glaucoma surgery. These findings suggest that perioperative ambient air quality may be relevant to early postoperative prognosis after glaucoma surgery.

etudes.titre: FOXC1-related Axenfeld-Rieger spectrum secondary to 6p25 deletion with concomitant distal 13q duplication arising from a maternal balanced t(6;13) translocation.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: Anterior segment dysgenesis (ASD) encompasses a heterogeneous group of developmental disorders arising predominantly from disrupted neural crest cell migration and differentiation. We report an extremely rare case of FOXC1-related Axenfeld-Rieger spectrum associated with a dual chromosomal imbalance inherited through a maternal balanced translocation.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 4-month-old female presented with bilateral corneal opacity, posterior embryotoxon, iridocorneal adhesions, early-onset glaucoma, and an atrial septal defect. By 18 months, additional features included dysmorphic facies, severe hypotonia, profound global developmental delay, failure to thrive, short stature, and sensorineural hearing impairment.
GENETIC FINDINGS: Clinical exome sequencing identified no clinically relevant single-nucleotide variants. Copy number variation (CNV) analysis revealed a heterozygous 6p25 deletion (~2.8 Mb) encompassing FOXC1 and a concomitant distal 13q duplication (~14.15 Mb). Parental karyotyping confirmed a maternal balanced translocation, 46,XX,t(6;13)(p25;q22). The proband inherited a derivative unbalanced chromosome through adjacent segregation. FOXC1 haploinsufficiency explains the anterior segment phenotype, while the distal 13q duplication likely contributes to the severe systemic manifestations through a multigenic dosage effect.
CONCLUSION: This case expands the phenotypic and genetic spectrum of FOXC1-related ASD beyond classical monogenic presentations and highlights the importance of CNV analysis and parental cytogenetic evaluation in syndromic anterior segment dysgenesis when sequencing-based variant analysis is non-diagnostic.

etudes.titre: Feasibility and appropriateness of integrating quality-of-life computerised adaptive tests into routine ophthalmic care: a pre-implementation study at a tertiary eye centre in Singapore.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the feasibility and appropriateness of integrating computerised adaptive testing (CAT) enabled patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) into routine ophthalmic care; assess organisational readiness and clinician perspectives across subspecialty clinics; and determine the impact of an educational strategy on clinician confidence in addressing related patients’ questions.
DESIGN: Preimplementation study.
SETTING: Singapore National Eye Centre, Singapore.
PARTICIPANTS: Preoperative cataract patients completing CATs in clinic and ophthalmology clinicians from cataract, retina and glaucoma services.
INTERVENTIONS: Tablet-based administration of the Impact of Vision Impairment CAT (IVI-CAT) assessing visual functioning and emotional well-being, with results integrated into electronic medical record (EMR) in real-time.
PRIMARY AND SECONDARY OUTCOME MEASURES: Primary outcomes were feasibility (participation, CAT completion rate, time and SEM) and appropriateness (unaided completion rate). Secondary outcomes included organisational readiness (Readiness Thinking Tool), clinician perspectives and change in clinician confidence following education. Barriers and facilitators were identified and mapped to implementation strategies.
RESULTS: Among 467 eligible patients, 399 (85.4%; 95% CI 81.9% to 88.5%) participated, yielding 826 IVI-CAT administrations with 97% completion (95% CI 95.1% to 97.7%), median duration 3:13 min, 7–8 items per domain and high measurement precision (SEM ≤0.358; reliability ≥0.85). Nearly half of the participants (n=187, 46.9%; 95% CI 41.9% to 51.9%) completed the assessment unaided; 41.9% required full assistance. Key barriers included low digital literacy and clinic workflow constraints, which were mitigated through staff support, patient education, workflow redesign and technical improvements. Clinicians were often unaware of CAT results in the EMR due to the lack of automated alerts. Organisational readiness was strong and supported by leadership. Clinician’s self-reported confidence in addressing related patient questions on how CAT scores will be used improved 1 week posteducation in exploratory analyses (n=19; exact p=0.031, unadjusted for multiple comparisons).
CONCLUSIONS: Administering CAT-based PROMs in cataract clinics was feasible in a high-volume well-resourced tertiary eye care setting with dedicated staff support. More than half of the patients required assistance to complete the test. Sustained implementation may require ongoing clinician education, in-clinic support, workflow optimisation and technical refinements such as EMR alerts. Staffing requirements also need to be quantified. These preliminary, context-specific findings provide a foundation for subsequent implementation efforts, but their transferability to other ophthalmic settings will require further evaluation.

etudes.titre: Micro-flow LC- drift tube IMS-MS with high-resolution demultiplexing for enhanced lipidome coverage of volume-limited biological samples.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « tube »
etudes.resume: The analysis of volume-limited biological specimens remains a major challenge in lipidomics, requiring analytical platforms with improved sensitivity and structural characterization capabilities. Here, a microflow liquid chromatography ion mobility mass spectrometry (microLC-IMS-MS) platform incorporating high-resolution demultiplexing (HRdm) was developed and benchmarked against conventional ultraperformance liquid chromatography (UPLC) for untargeted lipidomics. Following optimization of the LC hardware and ion source conditions, microLC provided median 2- to 14-fold increases in peak area, up to 10-fold increases in peak height, and approximately 3-fold higher signal-to-noise ratios relative to UPLC. Calibration with 34 isotopically labeled standards spanning eight lipid classes gave detection limits of 0.22-14.3 μg/L (median 1.6 μg/L; 0.80 pg on column) and quantitative ranges covering a median of 2.2 orders of magnitude. Analysis of NIST SRM 1950 plasma enabled the annotation of 130 lipid species compared with 74 by UPLC-MS, representing a 76% increase in lipid coverage. When combined with HRdm, the platform resolved five lipid isomer pairs that remained unresolved under conventional UPLC conditions. The method was further applied to volume-limited biological specimens, enabling the identification of 62 lipids from as few as 1x103 human Müller glia cells and lipid profiling of human vitreous humor samples from a pilot cohort of glaucoma patients and matched controls. Variations in lipid features were observed in an exploratory pilot clinical study, supporting the applicability of the platform to clinically relevant ocular biofluids; given the small cohort, these observations should be regarded as hypothesis-generating. These results establish microLC-HRdm-MS as a sensitive and reproducible platform for lipidomics of volume-limited and structurally complex specimens.

etudes.titre: Neovascular glaucoma: from ischemic pathophysiology to drainage tubes and modern pharmacotherapy.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « pharmacotherapy »
etudes.resume: This narrative review summarizes the pathophysiology, diagnosis, and management of neovascular glaucoma and provides a comprehensive guide for clinical ophthalmologists. An iterative snowballing approach, together with targeted searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library, identified 81 studies addressing key aspects of neovascular glaucoma, including molecular mechanisms, advanced diagnostic modalities, and surgical strategies. Neovascular glaucoma is an aggressive form of secondary glaucoma driven by ischemia-induced upregulation of vascular endothelial growth factor and angiopoietin-2 through the hypoxia-inducible factor-1α pathway. Diagnosis is primarily based on clinical findings and is increasingly supported by advanced imaging techniques. Management requires a multimodal approach combining panretinal photocoagulation and anti-vascular endothelial growth factor therapy with intraocular pressure-lowering interventions, including glaucoma drainage devices, micropulse transscleral cyclophotocoagulation, and slow-coagulation transscleral cyclophotocoagulation. Glaucoma drainage devices achieve the greatest intraocular pressure reduction, whereas micropulse transscleral cyclophotocoagulation offers the most favorable safety profile. Slow-coagulation transscleral cyclophotocoagulation represents an intermediate option, with a reported success rate of 71.7% and favorable safety outcomes. Emerging therapies aim to provide sustained angiogenic control while targeting fibrosis and neuroprotection.

etudes.titre: Conjunctiva-scleral thickness over the Ahmed glaucoma valve tube in eyes at clinically suspected risk of tube exposure: Anterior segment optical coherence tomography findings.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « valve »; mot du titre : « tube »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To characterize conjunctiva-scleral thickness over the Ahmed glaucoma valve tube in eyes clinically considered to be at increased risk of tube exposure based on a superficially positioned tube on anterior segment optical coherence tomography, and to explore the association between post-operative follow-up duration and conjunctiva-scleral thickness.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 22 eyes of 21 patients with 23 Ahmed glaucoma valve tubes. One patient contributed both eyes, and another had two Ahmed glaucoma valve tubes in one eye. All eyes had a minimum post-operative follow-up of 6 months and a clinically apparent superficial tube trace on slit-lamp examination. Over-the-tube conjunctiva-scleral thickness and total conjunctiva-scleral thickness were measured at corresponding locations using anterior segment optical coherence tomography. Associations between conjunctiva-scleral thickness measurements and post-operative follow-up duration were evaluated using correlation analysis and generalized estimating equation models to account for clustering.
RESULTS: The mean age was 56 ± 12 years (range, 38-80 years). Best-corrected visual acuity was 1.00 (range, 0.10-3.00) LogMAR, and intraocular pressure was 16 (range, 7-27)mmHg. The median post-operative follow-up duration was 40 months (range, 6-135 months), and the median CST overlying the tube at its most superficial location was 190 μm (range, 54-552 μm). A modest inverse correlation was observed between post-operative follow-up duration and conjunctiva-scleral thickness overlying the tube (ρ=-0.44, p=0.034). generalized estimating equation analysis showed a similar association (p=0.019). However, when eyes were categorized according to post-operative follow-up duration (≤1 year, 1-5 years, and ≥5 years), no statistically significant differences in conjunctiva-scleral thickness measurements were detected were observed among the groups: 273 (79-552), 190 (54-402), and 119 (64-227) μm, respectively (p=0.087).
CONCLUSION: In this preselected high-risk cohort, a modest inverse correlation was observed between post-operative follow-up duration and conjunctiva-scleral thickness overlying the tube; however, this association was not consistently demonstrated across analytical approaches and should therefore be considered exploratory. Anterior segment optical coherence tomography allows objective characterization of tissue coverage over the Ahmed glaucoma valve tube. Further prospective studies with larger cohorts and appropriate control groups are warranted to determine the clinical significance of these findings.

etudes.titre: Patient-Reported Outcomes After Glaucoma Surgery: A Narrative Review for Clinical Decision-Making.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Surgery »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To synthesize evidence on patient-reported outcomes (PROs), including vision-related quality of life, after glaucoma surgery and to organize this evidence into a clinically oriented framework for selecting, interpreting, and applying these outcomes across procedures, with particular attention to evidence gaps in angle-closure glaucoma, Asian populations, and combined cataract-angle surgery.
METHODS: This narrative review considered studies involving adults undergoing trabeculectomy, glaucoma drainage device implantation, minimally invasive glaucoma surgery, lens-based surgery, or combined cataract-angle procedures, together with studies evaluating PRO instruments used in glaucoma. We searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library for English-language studies published from January 2000 through July 7, 2026, while retaining seminal earlier articles. We prioritized randomized controlled trials, prospective cohorts, registries, and studies of instrument development and measurement properties. Studies were selected for clinical relevance and synthesized qualitatively without a formal risk-of-bias assessment.
RESULTS: We identified three main instrument families: disease-specific questionnaires, generic and preference-based utility measures, and adaptive item banks. Across procedures, patient-reported benefits appeared to be more consistently associated with reduced medication and symptom burden and avoidance of surgical morbidity than with the magnitude of intraocular pressure reduction. Comparative evidence suggested broadly similar vision-related quality of life after trabeculectomy and glaucoma drainage device implantation. Benefits reported after minimally invasive procedures were often accompanied by reductions in medication burden, whereas direct PRO evidence for combined cataract-angle procedures remained very limited. Evidence was particularly sparse for angle-closure glaucoma and Asian populations, as well as for PRO responsiveness in surgical settings and thresholds for meaningful change.
CONCLUSION: PROs provide clinically relevant information beyond intraocular pressure and medication counts, but their interpretation is limited by instrument heterogeneity, uncertain responsiveness, and limited evidence on minimal important differences. A standardized, surgery-relevant core set of PRO measures, validated across glaucoma subtypes and populations, could improve cross-procedure comparison, preoperative counseling, and shared decision-making.

etudes.titre: Ocular Magnification Correction Influences Glaucoma-Related Microvascular Measurements in OCT Angiography.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « OCT »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the impact of axial length (AL) handling strategies on optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA)-derived vessel density and its interpretation in glaucoma.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 1091 participants (1823 eyes). Vessel density was quantified using fixed region of interest (ROI) and AL-rescaled ROI approaches. Comparisons of glaucoma versus normal eyes were evaluated using generalized estimating equation (GEE) models adjusted for age, sex, systemic hypertension, OCTA signal strength index, and AL. Associations between vessel density and visual field mean deviation (VF MD) were evaluated using multivariable GEE models.
RESULTS: Glaucoma eyes had longer AL than normal eyes (P < 0.001). Under the fixed-ROI approach, deep vessel density was positively associated with AL, whereas superficial vessel density showed no significant association. After rescaling, both were inversely associated with AL (P < 0.001). Although rescaling increased apparent glaucoma-normal differences, estimates were similar after AL adjustment (superficial: β = -0.35 vs. -0.36 mm⁻1; deep: β = -1.03 vs. -1.09 mm⁻1). In the age- and sex-matched cohort (544 participants; 890 eyes), differences remained similar between approaches (superficial: β = -0.293 vs. -0.310 mm⁻1; deep: β = -0.963 vs. -0.992 mm⁻1). Both vessel density measures were associated with VF MD after AL adjustment. AL rescaling improved deep vessel density model fit and yielded slightly higher discrimination in sensitivity analyses allowing nonlinear AL effects (superficial: area under the curve [AUC] = 0.884 vs. 0.868; deep: AUC = 0.895 vs. 0.869).
CONCLUSIONS: Ocular magnification correction influenced OCTA measurements, but its incremental impact on glaucoma-related associations after AL adjustment was small. The clinical relevance remains uncertain.

etudes.titre: Tetrahydrobiopterin Supplementation Protects Retinal Ganglion Cells Against NMDA-Induced Excitotoxicity Through nNOS-Coupled Nitric Oxide Signaling.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Retinal Ganglion Cells »; étiquette : stade préclinique (indexation PubMed)
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: Excitotoxic injury triggered by excessive N-methyl-d-aspartate (NMDA) receptor activation represents an important mechanism underlying retinal neurodegeneration in glaucoma. Tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4), an essential cofactor for nitric oxide synthase (NOS), exhibits neuroprotective potential in multiple neurodegenerative diseases, but its role in retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) under excitotoxic injury remains unclear. This study assessed the neuroprotective effects of BH4 against excitotoxic retinal injury and explored its underlying mechanisms.
METHODS: Glutamate-treated R28 cells and intravitreal NMDA-injected rat retinas were used as in vitro and in vivo excitotoxic injury models, respectively. BH4 levels were measured after injury. Cell viability, oxidative stress, apoptosis, RGC survival, retinal morphology, visual function, and NOS activity were assessed following BH4 supplementation.
RESULTS: BH4 levels were significantly reduced in glutamate-injured R28 cells and NMDA-damaged retinas. BH4 supplementation improved cell survival, reduced oxidative stress, and attenuated apoptosis in injured R28 cells. In vivo, BH4 preserved RGC survival, alleviated retinal damage, and improved visual function after NMDA injury. Mechanistically, BH4 restored neuronal nitric oxide synthase (nNOS) coupling and activity, increased nitric oxide levels, re-established nitroso-redox homeostasis, and suppressed apoptotic signaling.
CONCLUSIONS: BH4 deficiency contributes to glutamate-induced retinal neurodegeneration by promoting nNOS uncoupling and nitroso-redox imbalance. Restoring BH4 levels protects against excitotoxic RGC damage, suggesting the BH4-nNOS axis as a potential therapeutic target for retinal neurodegeneration.

etudes.titre: Geographic concordance of cataract and glaucoma burden and associated country-level exposures across 204 countries and territories.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: Cataract and glaucoma are major causes of vision loss, but their shared geographic burden and potentially modifiable population-level exposures remain incompletely characterized.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included adults aged 55 years and older across 204 countries and territories, using data from the Global Burden of Disease Study (GBD). For both outcomes, national prevalence was age-standardized using the 2021 global population aged 55 years and older as the reference. Based on quartiles of national age-standardized prevalence for both outcomes, we classified the 204 countries and territories into three geographic concordance categories: Concordant, Cataract-dominant, and Glaucoma-dominant. For 2021, we modeled each of 26 literature-informed candidate summary exposure values (SEVs) separately against log age-standardized prevalence, adjusting for the Socio-demographic Index (SDI) with a three-degree-of-freedom natural spline. Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) correction was applied within each outcome, with additional regional and spatial models used to assess sensitivity.
RESULTS: In 2021, 89 countries (43.6%) were Concordant, 52 (25.5%) were Cataract-dominant, and 63 (30.9%) were Glaucoma-dominant. Fifteen countries were in the highest quartile for both outcomes, mainly in North Africa, the Middle East, and parts of sub-Saharan Africa. Five exposures-ambient particulate matter pollution, ambient ozone pollution, high body-mass index, low bone mineral density, and high temperature-had positive coefficients with outcome-specific BH q < 0.05 for both outcomes in the primary SDI-adjusted models. After adjustment for GBD super-region, only high temperature remained positive for both outcomes with BH q < 0.05. In both spatial-error models, only ambient particulate matter pollution met this standard.
CONCLUSION: National cataract- and glaucoma-related vision-loss burdens showed geographic concordance. The exposure findings were country-level associations, and their statistical support varied across regional and spatial models. These geographic patterns may help inform planning for cataract and glaucoma services in settings where both contribute substantially to vision-loss burden. Further individual-level research is needed to clarify the relationships suggested by these country-level findings.

etudes.titre: Selective Laser Trabeculoplasty in Advanced-to-Severe Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma: Six-Month Clinical Outcomes.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Trabeculoplasty »; mot du titre : « Laser »
etudes.resume:
INTRODUCTION: Selective laser trabeculoplasty (SLT) is an established treatment for reducing intraocular pressure (IOP) in patients with primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG). However, evidence on the use of VISULAS green SLT in advanced-to-severe POAG remains limited, particularly in real-world clinical settings. This study aimed to evaluate the six-month outcomes of VISULAS green SLT in patients with advanced-to-severe POAG.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included seven patients (10 treated eyes) with advanced-to-severe POAG who underwent SLT at a tertiary ophthalmology center in Malaysia between January and December 2025. IOP and topical IOP-lowering medication burden were assessed at baseline and at one week, one month, three months, and six months after SLT. Changes over time were analyzed using the Friedman test, followed by exploratory Wilcoxon signed-rank tests for paired comparisons. Subsequent glaucoma interventions were also recorded.
RESULTS: Of the 10 treated eyes, seven (70%) had advanced POAG and three (30%) had severe POAG. The mean patient age was 65.29 ± 8.88 years, and five patients (71.4%) were female. Overall, mean IOP decreased from 22.40 ± 7.21 mmHg at baseline to 19.29 ± 2.81 mmHg at six months, although the number of eyes with available measurements decreased from 10 to 7. Among the seven eyes with complete six-month data, mean IOP increased from 18.86 mmHg at baseline to 19.29 mmHg at six months, representing a paired mean increase of 0.43 mmHg. No statistically significant overall change in IOP was observed (Friedman test, p = 0.511). The median topical medication burden remained at two medications throughout the follow-up (p = 0.092). None of the seven evaluable eyes (0%) achieved the predefined target IOP at six months. Subsequent glaucoma surgery was documented in three eyes (30%), comprising two trabeculectomies and one iStent implantation.
CONCLUSIONS: In this small real-world cohort, no statistically significant changes in IOP or topical medication burden were demonstrated over six months following VISULAS green SLT. These findings should be interpreted cautiously given the very small sample size and incomplete follow-up and should be considered exploratory rather than evidence of an absence of treatment effect. SLT may serve as an adjunctive or interim treatment in selected patients who decline or temporarily defer surgery; however, close monitoring and timely escalation of treatment remain essential.

etudes.titre: NORMATIVE OCULAR METRICS IN HEALTHY INFANTS ATTENDING IMMUNIZATION CLINIC IN ILORIN, NIGERIA.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: The management of different childhood ocular conditions requires measurement of ocular metrics, which changes continuously as the child grows and approaches adulthood. In childhood glaucoma, intraocular pressure, corneal diameter, and cup-to-disc ratio are measured and monitored. This study aimed to establish a normative value for intraocular pressure readings, corneal diameter, and cup-to-disc ratio among healthy infants.
METHODS: This was a one-year descriptive cross-sectional study involving 1,198 eyes from 599 children, sampled from an age-stratified population attending the routine child immunization clinic of the tertiary hospital. All children had measurement of corneal diameter and intraocular pressure as well as the cup-to-disc ratio assessment. Frequency tables were generated for the demographic variables while comparisons of ocular metrics across the age groups were performed using the Kruskal-Wallis H test and post-hoc Dunn's test.
RESULTS: The median intraocular pressure (IOP) increased slightly with age, from 9.0 mmHg in the 6-12 weeks group to 10.0 mmHg in the other age groups. Median corneal diameter rose progressively from 9.5 mm in the 6-12 weeks group to 10.0 mm in the 13-24 weeks group and 10.5 mm in both the 24-36 weeks and >36 weeks groups. The median cup-to-disc ratio (CDR) showed minimal variation, with values ranging between 0.30 and 0.35 in the age groups.
CONCLUSION: The study established normative values for intraocular pressure, corneal diameter, and cup-to-disc ratio among healthy infants providing a valuable reference for pediatric ocular assessments.

etudes.titre: Systemic influences of dietary NAD+ supplementation relevant to the search for ocular hypertensive therapies for glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: étiquette : stade préclinique (indexation PubMed)
etudes.resume:
UNLABELLED: Dietary nicotinamide (NAM) is neuroprotective in rodent models of glaucoma. With dietary delivery, additional systemic influences of NAM are possible, prompting us to test for influences on non-neuronal phenotypes relevant to glaucoma. Test cohorts of mice on high-fat diets differed by NAM content (control, "CON-diet"; 2,000 mg/kg/day supplementation, "NAM-diet") and by ocular treatments inducing various levels of ocular hypertension (Naïve; Ad5-Empty; Ad5-ATF4). Masked observers assessed intraocular pressure (IOP), body weight, and slit-lamp appearance. Naïve and Ad5-Empty cohorts were analyzed for gut microbiome composition. Regardless of diet, Naïve cohorts maintained consistent IOP. On CON-diet, the Ad5-ATF4 and Ad5-Empty cohorts developed IOP elevation. Based on results from a linear mixed-effects model evaluating the effects of diet and ocular treatment on IOP, NAM-diet lowered IOP in only the Ad5-Empty cohort. NAM-diet also prevented weight gain associated with a high-fat diet. NAM-diet was linked to altered alpha and beta diversity of the gut microbiome, including changes to a butyrate-producing genus, Faecalibaculum. Among the systemic influences resulting from dietary NAM consumption, NAM's ability to affect both neuroprotection and IOP would be favorable for glaucoma therapy. The possibility of dietary NAM influencing body weight and microbiome composition in humans warrants additional investigation.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-58123-8.

etudes.titre: Correlation between anterior segment optical coherence tomography parameters and visual field results after a single episode of acute angle closure glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « optical coherence tomography »; mot du titre : « visual field »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To study the correlation between baseline anterior segment parameters and visual field results over one year in subjects who had undergone a single episode of acute primary angle closure followed by phacoemulsification with posterior chamber intraocular lens implantation.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed data from the Hebei Eye Hospital from December 2021 to November 2022. Baseline anterior segment optical coherence tomography parameters, including central corneal thickness (CCT), axial length (AL), pupil diameter (PD), anterior chamber depth (ACD), anterior chamber volume (ACV), anterior chamber width (ACW), lens vault (LV), iris curvature (IC), trabecular-iris angle at 500 and 750μm from the scleral spur (TIA500 and TIA750), iris thickness at 750μm from the scleral spur (IT750), angle opening distance at 500 and 750μm from the scleral spur (AOD500 and AOD750), trabecular-iris space area at 500 and 750μm from the scleral spur (TISA500 and TISA750), were documented, and correlations between these and visual field results were examined.
RESULTS: The combined model for the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve for five significant factors (time between acute attack and normalization of IOP (duration), peak IOP at the moment of the acute angle-closure attack (IOP), central corneal thickness (CCT), lens vault (LV), trabecular-iris angle at 500μm (TIA500) suggested better predictive sensitivity (84%) and specificity (98%) with a greater AUC, 0.945 (0.894-0.996, P=0.004), than any single parameter, and the Youden's J statistic was 0.817.
CONCLUSION: Patients with a longer delay between the acute attack and normalization of the IOP, a higher IOP at the time of the attack, a thicker cornea, a higher lens vault, and a narrower trabecular-iris angle at 500μm from the scleral spur at baseline appear to be more vulnerable to a manifest visual field defect after a single episode of acute primary angle closure followed by phacoemulsification with posterior chamber intraocular lens implantation.

etudes.titre: 12-month visual and safety outcomes of the ELIOS procedure with cataract surgery in primary open-angle glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « surgery »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To characterize early safety and visual outcomes through 12 months following combined phacoemulsification and ELIOS excimer laser trabeculostomy procedure in patients with mild-to-moderate primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG).
SETTING: Conducted at 20 US sites.
DESIGN: Prospective, multicenter, non-randomized clinical trial (NCT04899063).
METHODS: Adults aged ≥45 years with cataract and mild-to-moderate POAG underwent phacoemulsification with intraocular lens implantation followed immediately by the ELIOS procedure. Corrected distance visual acuity (CDVA), pachymetry, endothelial cell density (ECD), visual field measurements, and adverse events (AEs) were reported up to 12 months.
RESULTS: A total of 318 patients underwent the procedure; mean±SD age was 70.3±7.3 years, 172 (54.1%) were female, and 263 (82.7%) were White. Five intraoperative AEs were reported during cataract procedure and none during ELIOS procedure. Visual recovery was rapid and sustained: at month 12, all patients achieved CDVA 20/40 or better; CDVA was <1 line of baseline in 28.0% of patients and improved by ≥1 line in 214 (69.8%), and no losses ≥2 lines. Corneal edema occurred predominantly early and resolved without sequelae. ECD loss occurred early then stabilized; median change and median percent change in ECD at month 12 were -237.0 cells/mm2 and -9.10%, respectively. Through 12 months, 73 postoperative ocular AEs were reported in 17.3% of patients; the most common AEs were anterior chamber cell/flare requiring increased or reinitiated steroid therapy (5.7%), and worsening of visual field mean deviation by ≥2.5 dB from baseline (4.4%).
CONCLUSIONS: Combined phacoemulsification-ELIOS was associated with a safety profile consistent with published outcomes following phacoemulsification alone, with predominantly early, self-limited postoperative events.
etudes.revue: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

etudes.titre: Beta-Amino Alcohols as Key Frameworks in Drug Discovery: A Review of Medicinal Applications and Biological Profiles.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Drug »
etudes.resume: Beta-Amino alcohols, as pivotal frameworks in organic and medicinal chemistry, play a prominent role in drug design and development. This comprehensive review evaluates the therapeutic potential of β-amino alcohols, highlighting their significance in the management of a broad spectrum of human pathologies, including cancer, bacterial infections, malaria, and viral diseases. Furthermore, the efficacy of these molecules in cardiovascular, respiratory, and ocular disorders is assessed. Alongside their therapeutic applications, the epoxide ring-opening process, the primary and most established synthetic pathway for constructing β-amino alcohol cores, is critically discussed and integrated with structure activity relationship (SAR) insights to demonstrate how specific chemical modifications dictate pharmacological potency. The consolidated findings reveal that β-amino alcohols exert their therapeutic effects through diverse molecular mechanisms. These pathways encompass the suppression of malignant cell proliferation, potent bactericidal activity against resistant Staphylococcus aureus strains, inhibition of Plasmodium species in malaria, targeting the main protease (Mpro) of SARS-CoV-2 for COVID-19 therapeutics, and functioning as dual-binding cholinesterase inhibitors for Alzheimer's disease management. Additionally, these derivatives have been reported to modulate adrenergic receptors, highlighting their potential relevance to cardiovascular, respiratory, and ocular therapeutic research, including conditions such as hypertension, asthma, and glaucoma. Overall, this review provides an up-to-date analysis of β-amino alcohol-based therapeutic applications and offers a new perspective on the potential role of these compounds in modern medicinal chemistry, which may contribute to the rational design of novel drug candidates.

etudes.titre: Cataract surgery in pseudoexfoliation syndrome: perioperative considerations and glaucoma-related outcomes.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « surgery »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Pseudoexfoliation syndrome (PXS) confers well-recognized intraoperative risk during cataract surgery. Recent evidence, however, has provided greater insight into predictors of complications, surgical strategies to mitigate risk, and the effects of lens extraction, alone or combined with minimally invasive glaucoma surgery (MIGS), on glaucoma-related outcomes. This review synthesizes recent data on perioperative management and outcomes to inform surgical decision-making in eyes with PXS and pseudoexfoliation glaucoma (PXG).
RECENT FINDINGS: Preoperative imaging and risk-prediction models increasingly identify shallow anterior chamber depth, poor mydriasis, and lens decentration as predictors of zonular complications. Intraoperative adaptations, including modified chop techniques and selective use of capsular tension ring, may reduce zonular stress and improve refractive predictability, while evidence supporting femtosecond laser assistance remains inconclusive. Postoperatively, eyes with PXS appear more susceptible to early intraocular pressure (IOP) spikes and, in some series, to a greater inflammatory response and endothelial cell loss, although evidence for the latter two remains mixed. Visual outcomes are driven primarily by coexisting ocular comorbidities rather than PXS itself. Cataract surgery alone lowers IOP in PXG through anterior segment remodeling, while combined phacoemulsification and MIGS, particularly excisional angle procedures, provide additional reductions in IOP and medication burden.
SUMMARY: Careful preoperative risk stratification, surgical technique modification, and judicious use of combined glaucoma surgery allow well-tolerated and effective cataract surgery in PXS, with the added potential to meaningfully improve long-term IOP control in PXG.

etudes.titre: Multiplex Analysis of Cytokine Profiles in the Aqueous Humor of Glaucoma Filtration Surgery Models and Its Effect on Scarring.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Surgery »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To characterize the dynamic evolution of aqueous humor cytokine profiles after glaucoma filtration surgery (GFS) and to identify molecular signatures associated with bleb survival outcomes.
METHODS: GFS was performed on 26 rabbits' right eyes. Intraocular pressure (IOP), bleb morphology, and aqueous humor samples were collected before and after surgery. Thirty cytokines were quantified using RayBio Rabbit Cytokine Array Q30. Statistical analyses included Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, repeated-measures analysis of variance, independent samples t-tests or nonparametric tests, and Spearman correlation.
RESULTS: IOP decreased significantly in the early postoperative period and then gradually increased and stabilized. The mean bleb survival time was 15.19 ± 2.47 days. Among the 30 cytokines, 25 showed significant time-dependent changes, with peak times ranging from postoperative day 1 to day 21. After surgery, 12 cytokines were significantly higher in the early bleb failure group compared to the late failure group, with the greatest number and strongest negative correlations with bleb survival time observed on postoperative day 7, among which Contactin-1 (r = -0.6018), follistatin-related gene (FLRG; r = -0.5906), and thrombospondin-2 (TSP-2; r = -0.5847) exhibited the strongest correlations.
CONCLUSIONS: GFS can induce time-dependent elevations in multiple cytokines in the aqueous humor, with high expression of factors (such as Contactin-1, FLRG, and TSP-2) on postoperative day 7 closely associated with earlier bleb failure.
TRANSLATIONAL RELEVANCE: This study profiles post-GFS cytokine dynamics in rabbit aqueous humor, suggesting day 7 as a potential key window where Contactin-1, FLRG, and TSP-2 may act as scarring contributors, providing potential molecular targets and timing for future targeted interventions to improve the long-term success of filtration surgery.

etudes.titre: From homeostasis to neurodegeneration: Müller glia in retinal disease.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « neurodegeneration »
etudes.resume: Müller glia are the principal macroglia cells of the retina and are essential for maintaining structural, metabolic, synaptic, and vascular homeostasis. They regulate neurotransmitter recycling, ion and water balance, antioxidant defense, and neurovascular coupling, positioning them as central coordinators of retinal function in health and disease. In response to injury or stress, Müller glia transition from homeostatic support to reactive states that may initially preserve tissue integrity but, when sustained, contribute to chronic neuroinflammation, barrier dysfunction, and neuronal degeneration. In this review, we examine the core physiological functions of Müller glia and highlight emerging evidence that their responses are heterogeneous, reflecting spatial, molecular, and disease-specific differences across retinal layers and pathological contexts. We discuss major drivers of Müller glia activation, including mechanical stress, metabolic and oxidative imbalance, and inflammatory signaling, with emphasis on convergent pathways such as gp130-JAK-STAT3, NFκB, and mechanosensitive calcium signaling. We then consider how disruption of Müller glia homeostatic functions contributes to retinal disease, focusing on glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy, and age-related macular degeneration. Across these disorders, Müller glia emerge not as passive support cells, but as active regulators of neuronal and vascular microenvironments whose state of transition may shape disease progression. Finally, we discuss therapeutic strategies aimed at modulating Müller glia states, including lipid metabolism and signaling, restoration of ion and metabolic homeostasis, gene-based targeting, and regenerative reprogramming, and consider how single-cell, spatial, and multi-omic approaches define distinct layers of Müller glia state. Defining when and how Müller glia shift from adaptive to maladaptive states will be critical for developing therapies that restore retinal homeostasis and limit neurodegeneration.
etudes.revue: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

etudes.titre: Retinal neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration in a mouse model of glaucoma: cilastatin as a protective agent in male and female mice.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « mice »; mot du titre : « mouse »
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: Glaucoma is a leading cause of irreversible blindness characterized by retinal ganglion cell degeneration and neuroinflammation. Although sex-related differences have been reported in glaucoma, most experimental studies have predominantly used male animals. This study evaluated retinal responses to experimental glaucoma and the neuroprotective effects of cilastatin in male and female pigmented C57BL/6J mice.
METHODS: Ocular hypertension (OHT) was induced by unilateral laser photocoagulation of the left eye in male and female C57BL/6J mice. Animals received daily cilastatin (300 mg/kg, i.p.) or vehicle from 2 days before surgery until sacrifice at 28 days. Intraocular pressure was monitored throughout the study. Brn3a+ retinal ganglion cells, GFAP+ macroglial cells, and Iba-1+ microglial cells were assessed by immunohistochemistry and quantitative image analysis. OHT, normotensive contralateral (CONTRA) and NAÏVE eyes were compared in both sexes and treatment groups.
RESULTS: OHT increased intraocular pressure in both sexes and was associated with a reduction in Brn3a+ RGCs, in both male and female mice. In sex-stratified analyses, regional and layer-specific assessments revealed distinct descriptive spatial patterns of retinal inflammation, with differing microglial and macroglial reactivity profiles observed in the male and female cohorts. Cilastatin did not produce a sustained IOP-lowering effect but significantly attenuated the OHT-associated reduction in Brn3a+ RGCs and reduced glial activation in both sexes.
CONCLUSION: Experimental glaucoma induces neurodegenerative and neuroinflammatory retinal responses in pigmented C57BL/6J mice, with distinct descriptive spatial patterns observed between sexes. Cilastatin attenuated the OHT-associated reduction in Brn3a+ RGC counts and glial activation without producing a sustained IOP-lowering effect, supporting further investigation of its potential relevance in glaucoma.

etudes.titre: Primary Congenital Glaucoma in Kano, Northern Nigeria
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Background: Primary congenital glaucoma is one of the causes of childhood blindness and it appears to be common in our environment. This study evaluated the pattern of presentation and management of primary congenital glaucoma in children. Patients and Methods: This was a prospective questionnaire-based study of primary congenital glaucoma over a three year period. The information analyzed included patients' bio-data, vision, laterality of disease, presenting symptoms, family history, and history of traditional medicine application to the eye. Others included horizontal corneal diameter, intra ocular pressure and outcome of management. Results: There were 26 patients, 20 were males and 6 were females (M:F=3.3:1). Their ages ranged between 3 months and 5 years. Over a half of the patients presented during the first year of life. Primary congenital glaucoma was bilateral in 19 patients (73%). The commonest presenting symptoms were large eyes (85%), cloudy eyes (77%), photophobia (46%) and lacrimation (31%). In 44 eyes (98%) the intra ocular pressure was 20-49 mmHg before surgery and below 20 mmHg after surgery. Ttrabeculectomy resolved almost all the presenting symptoms, reduced intra-ocular pressure (IOP) and improved vision in all the patients. No sight threatening complications were recorded. Conclusion: Primary congenital glaucoma is common in our environment. Trabeculectomy remains a valuable treatment modality because it abolished most of the symptoms and IOP.

etudes.titre: Differences in corneal biomechanical parameters in normal tension glaucoma versus normotensive glaucoma suspect eyes
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « biomechanical »
etudes.resume: Abstract Multicenter retrospective study to evaluate differences in corneal biomechanical parameters provided by Corvis ST to segregate those with normal tension glaucoma (NTG) from glaucoma suspects. We included only newly diagnosed and treatment naïve glaucoma patients. Several corneal biomechanical parameters provided by Corvis ST were investigated. The discrimination ability of BGF was investigated through the area under the receiver operating characteristics curve (AUC). We included a total of 200 eyes from 100 patients with NTG and 200 eyes from 100 controls. We found statistical difference in Corneal velocity at second applanation (A2) with − 0.264 ± 0.061 m/s (OD) and − 0.270 ± 0.067 m/s (OS) in the control group, versus − 0.226 ± 0.084 m/s (OD, p = 0.0004) and − 0.223 ± 0.079 m/s (OS, p = 0.0001) in the NTG group. In addition, we found statistical difference in biomechanical glaucoma factor (BGF) between groups, with 0.568 ± 0.239 (OD) and 0.560 ± 0.229 (OS) in the control group, versus 0.674 ± 0.212 (OD, p = 0.001) and 0.659 ± 0.231 (OS, p = 0.056) in the NTG group. The AUC value was 0.63 BGF for discriminating NTG eyes from normal eyes. Both BGF and corneal velocity at second applanation were statistically different between groups. Using BGF parameter from Corvis ST can improve diagnostic accuracy when dealing with NTG.

etudes.titre: GlaucoFormer: A transformer-based model for glaucoma detection and segmentation
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « transformer »; mot du titre : « detection »

labos.nom: Institute for Information and Communications Technology Promotion
Korea Technology and Information Promotion Agency for SMEs

etudes.resume: Glaucoma is a major cause of irreversible blindness worldwide, primarily due to optic nerve damage caused by elevated intraocular pressure. Early detection is vital to prevent vision loss, emphasizing the need for accurate and efficient diagnostic methods. The proposed model enhances optic disc (OD) and optic cup (OC) segmentation, as well as glaucoma classification, by integrating transformer-based attention and the convolutional block attention module (CBAM) into a UNet architecture. To improve segmentation precision, we employ multiscale losses at different decoding stages, allowing the network to progressively refine predictions across multiple resolution levels. By accurately segmenting OD and OC, we extract critical features for glaucoma risk assessment, combining these metrics with encoder features to enhance classification performance. The experimental results show that our approach significantly surpasses the existing methods in terms of both segmentation accuracy and glaucoma prediction, offering a reliable tool for early glaucoma diagnosis. For glaucoma classification, our method outperformed traditional approaches on the RIM-ONE, REFUGE, and DRISHTI-GS1 datasets, with accuracies of 95.8%, 96%, and 92%, respectively, and was comparable to that of the CUHKMED team, the leading team in the REFUGE challenge, achieving an accuracy of 95.59% on the REFUGE dataset. This advancement in automated glaucoma detection through deep learning can enable timely intervention, ultimately helping preserve the vision of patients.

etudes.titre: Explainable AI for glaucoma detection and classification: a comprehensive review
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « AI »; mot du titre : « detection »
etudes.resume: Glaucoma is a leading cause of irreversible blindness and often advances without symptoms. This PRISMA/PICOS–guided systematic review synthesizes 100 studies (to January 2025) on artificial intelligence (AI) for glaucoma detection, staging, and monitoring using color fundus photography (CFP), optical coherence tomography (OCT), and OCT angiography (OCTA). Roughly 45% of studies use CFP, 55–60% use OCT, and 10–15% use OCTA; about one quarter fuse multiple imaging types with clinical data. Across methods—convolutional neural networks, Transformers, and hybrid fusion—internal test results are strong, with several systems reporting specialist-level sensitivity and specificity. Translation to practice remains limited by small, single-center cohorts, device/domain shifts that reduce generalization, a lack of prospective trials, and explainability approaches that are misaligned with clinical reasoning. We recommend multi-center, multi-ethnic, multi-vendor benchmarks, rigorous external and prospective validation, clinically meaningful and standardized explainability, and cost- and workflow-aware deployment. Addressing these gaps could enable earlier detection, more personalized monitoring, and real-world impact in reducing preventable blindness. Within this review, we investigate key challenges revolving around the use of AI models for glaucoma imaging across different learning paradigms, improving model efficiency, and coupling them with complementary techniques and multimodal data (CFP, OCT, and OCTA). We hope this review can give a comprehensive picture of AI-based methods for glaucoma to readers in the field of medical image analysis.

etudes.titre: Pitx2-associated early-onset glaucoma alters corneal innervation and sensory function in a sex-specific manner
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Abstract Purpose Pitx2-associated developmental glaucoma is characterized by anterior segment dysgenesis, ocular hypertension, and optic neuropathy. Its consequences for corneal sensory innervation remain poorly understood. We investigated whether this disease alters corneal nerve structure and sensory function in a sex-dependent manner. Methods Male and female Pitx2 egl1/egl1 and Pitx2 +/+ mice were examined at 1 and 3 months. Ocular phenotyping included intraocular pressure, fundus imaging, visual evoked potentials, and optic nerve ultrastructure. RNA sequencing of corneas and trigeminal ganglia was performed at 3 months. Corneal innervation was assessed by βIII-tubulin immunofluorescence and volumetric quantification of nerve fibers. Corneal sensitivity was measured using Von Frey filaments. Results Pitx2 egl1/egl1 mice developed progressive ocular hypertension, fundus abnormalities, reduced visual evoked potential amplitudes, and optic nerve degeneration, supporting the model as early-onset glaucoma. Baseline sex-related transcriptional differences were limited in both cornea and trigeminal ganglia. In contrast, Pitx2 mutation induced sex-dependent molecular responses. Female corneas showed broader transcriptional changes enriched in inflammatory, stress-response, and tissue-remodeling pathways, whereas male corneas showed a more restricted response involving metabolic and homeostatic processes. Similar sex divergence was observed in trigeminal ganglia. Corneal nerve fiber volume was reduced in both sexes at 3 months but not at 1 month, whereas reduced sensitivity was detected only in mutant males. Conclusions This study identifies sexual dimorphism as a component of Pitx2-associated developmental glaucoma. Furthermore, our findings suggest that glaucoma affects the corneal sensory system beyond optic nerve pathology, highlighting a potentially overlooked dimension of disease relevant to ocular surface monitoring and patient management. Highlights Disruption of the cornea–trigeminal ganglion axis with coordinated molecular and functional alterations in Pitx2-associated early-onset glaucoma Sex-dependent modifications in both cornea and trigeminal ganglion responses to early-onset glaucoma Progressive corneal neurodegeneration in early-onset glaucoma

etudes.titre: Mechanisms of Neurodegeneration and Retinal Imaging Biomarkers in Glaucoma
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Imaging »; mot du titre : « Biomarkers »
etudes.resume: Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide and is characterized by progressive retinal ganglion cell (RGC) neurodegeneration with optic nerve head (ONH) damage and visual field loss. Although intraocular pressure (IOP) is the main modifiable risk factor, disease onset and progression reflect a multifactorial cascade involving mechanical strain at the lamina cribrosa, impaired axonal transport, neurovascular dysregulation with early neurovascular unit dysfunction, oxidative stress, mitochondrial failure, and chronic glial-driven neuroinflammation. Alongside IOP lowering, neuroprotective strategies have gained increasing attention; among the most studied, citicoline, nicotinamide, and coenzyme Q10 are supported by a strong biological rationale and encouraging early clinical signals, although robust evidence for long-term clinical efficacy remains limited. Because functional defects typically emerge only after substantial RGC loss, structural biomarkers are pivotal for early detection and monitoring. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) provides high-resolution, quantitative assessment of circumpapillary RNFL thickness, macular ganglion cell-related metrics, and ONH rim measures such as Bruch’s membrane opening-minimum rim width. OCT angiography (OCTA) complements OCT by quantifying retinal and peripapillary microvascular abnormalities, although its temporal and clinical relationship with neural loss remains incompletely defined. Longitudinal OCT follow-up can be supported by event-based and trend-based analyses to distinguish true change from test-retest variability and estimate rates of structural loss. Detection of Apoptosing Retinal Cells (DARC) represents an emerging investigational approach for in vivo visualization of retinal cell apoptosis. Overall, these advances support a multimodal structure-function-biomarker framework for glaucoma assessment while highlighting important clinical gaps that remain to be addressed.

etudes.titre: Essential Vascular Supply of the Eye in Glaucoma
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: This project is a comprehensive review of the vascular supply of the eye, tracing a continuous pathway from the heart and aortic arch through the great vessels, carotid system, circle of Willis, and ophthalmic artery to the intraocular microvasculature, including its venous and lymphatic drainage. Each vascular segment is examined for its normal anatomy and clinically relevant variation, its pathophysiology, and the congenital, acute, and chronic diseases specific to it, read throughout through the lens of ocular perfusion and its relationship to glaucoma. Elevated intraocular pressure remains the only proven modifiable risk factor for glaucoma, yet many patients progress despite adequate pressure control, and a vascular contribution to glaucomatous optic neuropathy has long been proposed. This review addresses the absence of a single work that treats the ocular vascular supply as one continuous system tied to that contribution. The review draws on a PRISMA-guided literature search across PubMed, Cochrane Library, ScienceDirect, Scopus, Google Scholar, and ProQuest. It builds directly on existing anatomical reviews of ocular vasculature and the established literature on ocular perfusion pressure in glaucoma. Its contribution is the integration of a continuous systemic-to-ocular pathway with a consistent disease framework applied to every segment. Expected outcomes are a peer-reviewed manuscript targeted for submission, multiple figures detailing blood perfusion, and a table mapping each vascular segment to its variation, associated disease, and ocular or glaucoma-related consequence.

etudes.titre: The expression level of PGAM5 regulates acute ocular hypertension-induced retinal ganglion cell injury
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « retinal ganglion cell »

labos.nom: National Natural Science Foundation of China
Natural Science Foundation of Zhejiang Province
Key Research and Development Program of Zhejiang Province

etudes.resume: Phosphoglycerate mutase 5 (PGAM5) is a critical regulator of mitochondrial quality control. This study aims to investigate the role of PGAM5 in retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) following acute ocular hypertension (AOH)-induced retinal ischemia-reperfusion (RIR) injury. A mouse RIR model in vivo and an oxygen-glucose deprivation and reoxygenation (OGDR) model in R28 retinal progenitor cells in vitro were established to mimic AOH injury. Endogenous PGAM5 expression was manipulated in R28 cells via siRNA-mediated knockdown and lentivirus-mediated overexpression, while RGC-specific PGAM5 modification was achieved by intravitreal injection of adeno-associated virus (AAV). Cell apoptosis and mitochondrial function were evaluated by LDH release assay, Western blotting (WB), immunofluorescence (IF), mitochondrial calcium detection, ATP measurement, and flow cytometry analyses of apoptosis, mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS), and mitochondrial membrane potential (ΔΨm). Retinal morphological damage, RGC survival, neuroinflammation, and retinal function were assessed using H&E staining, retinal flat-mount immunostaining, WB, IF labeling, and electroretinography (ERG). PGAM5 expression was significantly downregulated in both the in vivo RIR mouse retinas and in vitro OGDR R28 cell models. Under OGDR stress, PGAM5 deficiency aggravated LDH release, apoptosis, and mitochondrial dysfunction, including elevated mitochondrial ROS accumulation, mitochondrial depolarization, mitochondrial calcium overload, and impaired ATP synthesis. In the RIR model, RGC-specific PGAM5 knockdown exacerbated ganglion cell complex thinning, loss of RGC somata and axons, retinal function impairment, and retinal neuroinflammation. In contrast, PGAM5 overexpression effectively alleviated OGDR-induced cell apoptosis and mitochondrial dysfunction in R28 cells, and ameliorated RIR-induced retinal degeneration and neuroinflammation. The core protective effects were further validated in primary RGCs. Mechanistically, PGAM5 facilitated mitophagic flux to maintain mitochondrial homeostasis. Adequate PGAM5 protects RGCs against AOH-induced ischemic injury by suppressing apoptosis and improving mitochondrial homeostasis via enhancing mitophagy, highlighting PGAM5 as a promising therapeutic target for neuroprotection in acute glaucoma.

etudes.titre: CHIASM: A Self-Supervised Visual Field Encoder for Neuro-Ophthalmology
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Visual Field »
etudes.resume: Abstract Importance Artificial intelligence (AI) is under active development to support diagnosis and prognostication of glaucoma from visual fields (VF). These systems do not audit for vertical- meridian-respecting field loss patterns—known sequelae of stroke, hemorrhage, and neoplasm. Objective To develop a self-supervised encoder of automated perimetry that learns anatomically interpretable visual field structure without labels and to evaluate its capacity to identify suspected neurologic VF patterns in an independent public glaucoma dataset. Design, Setting, and Participants Diagnostic study (TRIPOD+AI). Pretraining: 23,223 unlabeled Humphrey VFs (patient-grouped training split of 28,943 fields from 3,871 University of Washington patients; UWHVF, all-comers perimetry). External evaluation: Harvard-Glaucoma Fairness dataset (Harvard-GF; 3,300 patients with paired VF and OCT from a single academic center). The encoder was never exposed to Harvard-GF during training. Exposures A 128-dimensional masked autoencoder of monocular Humphrey VF pattern- deviation data, with a supervised linear classifier on vertical-midline latent dimensions trained on per-eye expert neurological/nonneurological labels. Main Outcomes and Measures Primary: classifier accuracy under hard-negative evaluation (cross-validated balanced accuracy and AUC). Secondary: held-out specificity on structurally separated UWHVF controls; expert confirmation and OCT structural correlates of classifier- identified Harvard-GF suspects. Results Masked reconstruction recovered structure concordant with retinal neuroanatomy; 50 of 128 latent dimensions emerged spatially specialized (vs 23 for the TD encoder). Under hard- negative evaluation the classifier achieved cross-validated balanced accuracy 0.78 (95% CI, 0.75-0.82) and AUC 0.85 (95% CI, 0.82-0.89), with no false positives among 100 held-out controls. Applied to Harvard-GF without fine-tuning, it identified a top-20 of 1,748 glaucoma- labeled patients (1.1%) with morphology inconsistent with glaucoma; all 20 were NHT-positive (mean 62.4), and OCT showed preserved superior (Cohen d = +0.68; P < .001) and inferior (d = +0.63; P = .003) RNFL versus severity-matched controls. Conclusions and Relevance A self-supervised VF encoder learned anatomically interpretable visual field structure from unlabeled data and identified suspected neurological cases in a curated glaucoma dataset, with expert, rule-based, and OCT corroboration. Visual field datasets used to train glaucoma AI may benefit from neurological screening; the encoder reported here supports such audits and provides a foundation for neuro-ophthalmic AI beyond fundus photography and OCT. Key Points Question Can self-supervised learning learn anatomically interpretable visual field structure from unlabeled visual fields and identify neurological field loss? Findings Trained on 28,943 unlabeled visual fields, the encoder learned anatomically interpretable visual field structure and revealed ≥20 of 1,748 patients (≥1.1%) in an external glaucoma dataset with vertical-midline loss and retinal nerve fiber layer preservation. Meaning A self-supervised encoder learned anatomically interpretable visual field structure, and can audit glaucoma datasets for neurological field loss, reducing the risk that future AI misclassifies intracranial disease.

etudes.titre: A Gamified Virtual Reality Perimeter for Rapid Glaucoma Pre-Screening in Community Settings: Pilot Evaluation of "Meteor Blaster VR" (Preprint)
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Screening »
etudes.resume: BACKGROUND Undiagnosed glaucoma remains highly prevalent, and raising awareness of subtle visual impairments in daily life is essential for early detection. Although virtual reality (VR)–based perimetry has previously been investigated, little is known about whether a gamified VR system can accurately detect glaucomatous visual field loss while maintaining user engagement, which could enable opportunistic pre-screening for glaucoma. Therefore, we developed an immersive VR shooting game, Meteor Blaster VR. OBJECTIVE The study included 23 eyes of 23 patients with glaucoma and 28 eyes of 28 patients without glaucoma. To avoid the correlation between paired eyes, only right eyes were included in the analysis. Associations between game score and HFA indices were evaluated, and the diagnostic performance for glaucoma was assessed using receiver operating characteristics curves. METHODS The study included 23 eyes of 23 patients with glaucoma and 28 eyes of 28 patients without glaucoma. To avoid the correlation between paired eyes, only right eyes were included in the analysis. Associations between game score and HFA indices were evaluated, and the diagnostic performance for glaucoma was assessed using receiver operating characteristics curves. RESULTS There was no significant difference in age between the glaucoma group and the non-glaucoma group (54.7 ± 7.2 years vs. 58.0 ± 11.2 years, respectively; P = 0.234). On the other hand, there was a significant difference in game score (glaucoma 24.2 ± 5.3 vs. non-glaucoma 29.1 ± 2.4; P = 0.005). There was a significant correlation between game score and mean deviation (MD): for the entire visual field, the Pearson correlation coefficient was r = 0.85 (P < 0.001); for the upper half, r = 0.88 (P < 0.001); and for the lower half, r = 0.73 (P < 0.001). MD was the only independent predictor of game score (β = 0.90, adjusted R² = 0.72). Logistic regression analysis for game score showed relatively good glaucoma diagnostic performance (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.81, P < 0.001), and combining age with game score improved glaucoma discrimination ability (AUC = 0.83, P < 0.001). In contrast, age alone did not provide sufficient discriminatory ability for glaucoma (AUC = 0.65, P = 0.222). CONCLUSIONS The gamified VR platform demonstrated strong agreement with conventional visual field indices and may serve as an accessible, low-barrier pre-screening tool to prompt players to be aware of their visual status, thereby facilitating early glaucoma detection in an everyday community setting.

The system employs four dedicated specialist models, surpassing the ODIR benchmark baseline. AEGIS ORAS is part of the AEGIS Human-AI Augmenting System suite. Full interactive application and all AEGIS projects are available at https://aegishumanai.com

etudes.titre: Effect of iStent inject on unmedicated intraocular pressure in glaucoma: exploratory analysis of clinical trial data
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « iStent »
etudes.resume: Abstract Purpose The direct effect of iStent inject on intraocular pressure (IOP) in patients with glaucoma is difficult to quantify in pragmatic trials where rates of post-surgical IOP-lowering therapy differ between intervention groups. We aimed to quantify the causal effect of iStent inject on unmedicated IOP at 12- and 24-months post-surgery. Methods Adults with mild-to-moderate glaucoma were 1:1 randomised to receive cataract surgery with iStent inject or cataract surgery alone at an Australian hospital (2017-2020, NCT03106181 ). IOP-lowering medications were prescribed as per clinician discretion. An exploratory analysis was used to estimate the controlled direct effect of iStent inject on IOP, analogous to the effect expected if all participants had undergone medication washout prior to assessment. Results Ninety-five eyes from 80 people were included (67.4% male, mean age 73.0 years, mean baseline IOP 17.1 mmHg). IOP-lowering medication was required for 53% of eyes in each group at 12 months (n=76); at 24 months (n=86) it was required for 43% and 64% in the active and control groups, respectively. Mean IOP was similar between intervention groups at each outcome visit. The controlled direct effect favoured the iStent inject group at 12 months (-2.1-mmHg difference, 95% CI -4.0,-0.3) but was attenuated at 24 months (-0.5 mmHg-difference, 95% CI -2.6,1.6). Conclusion Although the iStent inject was estimated to have an effect on lowering unmedicated IOP at 12 months, this effect had largely disappeared by 24 months. Medication washout is recommended when safe and practical in future trials to estimate these direct effects with more certainty.

etudes.titre: Enantiomorphic Glaucoma Displayed in Monozygotic Twins
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Background: Numerous theories exist about the etiology of glaucoma and various forms of research, including twin studies, are conducted to provide answers. Twin studies are an exceptional method of examining the genetic and environmental influences on primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) since comparison of monozygotic and dizygotic twins can infer a genetic causative factor. Case Report: A pair of monozygotic twins revealed strikingly similar examination results with the eventual diagnosis of POAG. Visual fields and fundus photography revealed enantiomorphic, or mirror image, likeness. The right eye of twin one (T1) and the left eye of twin two (T2) displayed a repeatable inferior arcuate defect and retinal nerve fiber layer defects (RNFL). Conclusion: An obvious genetic link within POAG is demonstrated by these twins. A dual case presentation will be described and a conclusion of the genetic backbone of glaucoma will be presented with supporting research. These studies provide information on genes responsible for POAG, environmental factors inducing POAG, and more insight for clinicians and patients so that better treatments may evolve in the future.
etudes.revue: Canadian journal of optometry/CJO. Canadian journal of optometry

etudes.titre: Abridged Retinal Fluorescence Lifetimes in Glaucoma
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Fluorescence »
etudes.resume: This study investigates the relationship between glaucoma and retinal fluorescence lifetimes using FLIO. The results show that participants with glaucoma have shorter mean lifetimes compared to those without glaucoma, even after adjusting for age and diabetes status. The study suggests that glaucoma may be associated with altered metabolic activity in the retina.
