etudes.titre: Primary intraocular lens implantation is associated with lower observed odds of secondary glaucoma than aphakia after congenital cataract surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « surgery »
etudes.resume: This registration documents a systematic review and meta-analysis that synthesizes the comparative evidence on the risk of secondary glaucoma after primary intraocular lens (IOL) implantation versus aphakia in children undergoing surgery for congenital or infantile cataract. Purpose. Secondary glaucoma is a major sight-threatening complication of congenital/infantile cataract extraction, and the choice of optical rehabilitation—primary IOL implantation or correction of aphakia—may influence long-term glaucoma risk. Existing evidence is conflicting and the evidence base has expanded substantially since earlier comparative syntheses, motivating an updated comparison restricted to studies that contain both lens-status groups and report glaucoma outcomes separately. The primary aim is to compare the within-study odds of secondary glaucoma after primary IOL implantation relative to aphakia; secondary aims are to examine whether any association varies by study design (retrospective versus prospective/randomized), age at surgery, geographic region, and mean follow-up duration, and to estimate single-arm pooled incidence of secondary glaucoma in each group. Methods. The review was conducted and reported in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 statement. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Google Scholar, the Cochrane Library, and CNKI were searched from January 1999 through August 8, 2026, using search strings that combined concepts for cataract surgery/lensectomy, congenital/infantile/pediatric cataract, glaucoma, intraocular lens/pseudophakia, and aphakia; reference lists of included studies and prior reviews were also screened. Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials and prospective or retrospective comparative cohorts of children undergoing cataract extraction for congenital or infantile cataract, with primary IOL implantation as the intervention and aphakia as the comparator, and with glaucoma outcomes reported separately for both groups. Studies of traumatic, drug-induced, metabolic, or secondary cataract, pre-existing congenital glaucoma, non-separable severe ocular anomalies, and follow-up shorter than one year were excluded. Records were screened independently in two stages (title/abstract and full text) by two investigators, and disagreements were resolved by discussion and consensus; data were extracted independently in duplicate using a standardized form. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool for randomized trials and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale for observational studies. Study-specific odds ratios were pooled with random-effects inverse-variance meta-analysis using restricted maximum likelihood estimation and the Hartung-Knapp adjustment; heterogeneity was quantified, and prespecified subgroup, sensitivity, influence, and small-study-effect analyses were planned, with certainty of evidence assessed using the GRADE approach. Expected outcomes. The review was designed to deliver (1) a pooled within-study odds ratio with 95% confidence and prediction intervals for secondary glaucoma in the primary IOL group versus the aphakia group, (2) subgroup estimates by study design, age at surgery, geographic region, and follow-up duration, (3) single-arm pooled incidence of secondary glaucoma in each group, (4) measures of between-study heterogeneity together with an assessment of small-study effects and robustness, and (5) a GRADE-based rating of the certainty of evidence, with implications for surgical decision-making and recommendations for future research. As a retrospective registration, this record documents the methods of the completed review.

etudes.titre: Accessibility of Open-Angle Glaucoma Patient Education Materials Written and Simplified by AI Chatbots (Preprint)
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « AI »
etudes.resume: BACKGROUND Through handouts, physicians can offer patient information that lasts outside of appointments. However, patient education materials (PEMs) must be accessible to a patient audience, including being written at a suitable reading grade level. Organizations like the American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO) have improved accessibility of high-quality online resources, particularly within the field of glaucoma. However, topics are limited and readability of PEMs varies depending on disease process. OBJECTIVE Readability of glaucoma patient education materials (PEMs) generated by ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and OpenEvidence was compared to American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO) and UpToDate resources to determine whether these large language models (LLMs) adjust reading levels to a fifth-grade standard. METHODS Three freely available LLMs—ChatGPT (GPT-5.1), Google Gemini (Flash 2.5), and OpenEvidence (2.0)—were used to generate glaucoma PEMs. Readability was scored before and after a standardized language simplification prompt using Flesch Reading Ease (FRE) and Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL). Readability was compared across LLMs and against AAO and UpToDate patient materials using paired t-tests and ANOVA with Bonferroni correction. RESULTS LLM-generated PEMs exceeded a fifth-grade level as measured by FKGL (all p ≤ 0.03). Following prompting for language simplification, the LLMs significantly reduced reading grade level (all p < 0.05) and achieved FKGL near the fifth-grade (all p < 0.05), with Google Gemini producing the highest FRE and lowest FKGL. Simplified LLM-generated PEMs were significantly more readable than AAO materials (all p ≤ 0.02) and comparable to UpToDate patient education articles, which were already written around a sixth-grade reading level. CONCLUSIONS LLM-based AI tools can be prompted to generate glaucoma PEMs with readability approaching recommended fifth-grade levels. While unprompted outputs remain too complex, targeted language simplification substantially improves accessibility.

etudes.titre: Efeitos Vasculares no Glaucoma de Pressão Normal
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: O glaucoma de pressão normal representa uma variante clínica complexa do glaucoma primário de ângulo aberto, caracterizada pelo desenvolvimento de neuropatia óptica típica e perda progressiva de campo visual, mesmo com a pressão intraocular mantendo-se constantemente em níveis estatisticamente normais, ou seja, menores ou iguais a vinte e um milímetros de mercúrio. Tradicionalmente, o manejo do glaucoma concentrava-se de forma quase exclusiva nos fatores mecânicos pressóricos, porém a persistência da progressão do dano axonal em uma parcela significativa de pacientes com pressão controlada direcionou a atenção da comunidade científica para mecanismos alternativos de lesão celular. Diante desse cenário patogênico multifatorial, o presente estudo tem como objetivo realizar uma revisão sistemática da literatura para analisar os efeitos vasculares no glaucoma de pressão normal, discutindo as principais alterações na perfusão ocular, a regulação do fluxo sanguíneo e suas implicações clínicas na população brasileira. Para tanto, foi conduzido um levantamento bibliográfico nas bases de dados SciELO e LILACS utilizando descritores de saúde específicos para selecionar artigos de alta relevância científica no país. Os resultados evidenciam que a desregulação vascular primária, episódios frequentes de hipotensão arterial noturna e o fenômeno de vasoespasmo exercem um papel preponderante na indução de crises de isquemia e reperfusão na cabeça do nervo óptico. Conclui-se que o glaucoma de pressão normal deve ser compreendido como uma manifestação ocular de um distúrbio circulatório sistêmico, tornando indispensável a avaliação do perfil hemodinâmico global do paciente para instituir terapias neuroprotetoras e vasculares complementares eficazes.

etudes.titre: Mecanismos de Depósito Proteico no Glaucoma Pseudoesfoliativo
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: O glaucoma pseudoexfoliativo representa uma forma agressiva e complexa de glaucoma secundário de ângulo aberto, decorrente da síndrome de pseudoexfoliação, uma desordem generalizada da matriz extracelular relacionada ao envelhecimento. Esta condição clínica é caracterizada pela produção excessiva e pelo acúmulo progressivo de um material fibrilar esbranquiçado e amorfo em diversas estruturas do segmento anterior do olho, com especial tropismo pela cápsula anterior do cristalino, pela margem pupilar e pela malha trabecular. Diante do impacto severo que essa deposição exerce na dinâmica do humor aquoso e na integridade das estruturas oculares, o presente estudo tem como objetivo realizar uma revisão sistemática da literatura para analisar os mecanismos moleculares e bioquímicos envolvidos no depósito proteico do glaucoma pseudoexfoliativo, discutindo suas implicações na elevação da pressão intraocular e no manejo clínico dentro da realidade médica brasileira. Para isso, foi conduzida uma busca detalhada nas bases de dados SciELO e LILACS utilizando descritores em saúde controlados para selecionar artigos científicos de alta relevância nacional. Os resultados revelam que o estresse oxidativo crônico e a regulação positiva do fator de crescimento transformador beta um funcionam como os principais gatilhos para a síntese celular aberrante de glicoproteínas e proteoglicanos, cujo acúmulo na via de escoamento gera obstrução mecânica e disfunção endotelial trabecular. Conclui-se que o entendimento aprofundado desses caminhos bioquímicos é fundamental para otimizar as abordagens preventivas, antecipar complicações cirúrgicas decorrentes de fragilidade zonular e guiar terapias hipotensoras mais eficazes para conter o dano axonal crônico.

etudes.titre: Glaucoma: The Silent Thief of Sight as the End-Stage of the Brain's Ocular Decree
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Background: Glaucoma is currently defined as a progressive optic neuropathy characterised by retinal ganglion cell death and visual field loss, with elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) as the primary modifiable risk factor. Yet many patients continue to lose vision despite well-controlled IOP, and some develop glaucoma without ever having elevated pressure. This manuscript proposes that glaucoma is not primarily a pressure disease but the end-stage of the brain's ocular vasoconstrictive decree, executed over decades through chronic retinal and optic nerve head hypoxia. Framework: The brain's primary function is the maintenance of temperature and blood pH through the control of blood flow. Under chronic, unresolvable threat, the brain becomes a miser for blood. It constricts the choroid, retinal arterioles, and posterior ciliary arteries, producing the Stasis-Acidosis-Proteinopathy (SAP) cascade in the inner retina and optic nerve head. Retinal ganglion cells—among the most metabolically demanding neurons in the body—are starved. The amacrine network, especially the AII bridge, fails first functionally. Then the retinal ganglion cells die structurally. Intraocular pressure is an aggravating factor, not the root cause. Why Pressure-Lowering Alone Fails: Pressure-lowering drops suppress one mechanical blade. They do not restore choroidal or optic nerve perfusion. They do not resolve the brain's threat state. The Law of Pressure Reflection predicts that the hypoxic cascade continues despite normal IOP. This explains the clinical observation of progressive glaucoma in eyes with "controlled" pressure. Clinical Integration: The Ocular UBTI provides a non-invasive readout of the brain's ocular decree: choroidal thickness, retinal vessel calibre, OCTA perfusion density, RNFL thickness, and pupillary dynamics. The environmental path—quieting the knock, restoring sleep, reducing social threat—is primary. The starter motor (low-dose PDE5 inhibitor ± GLP-1 receptor agonist) is proposed as a time-limited vascular thaw for the starving optic nerve before irreversible cell death. Conclusion: Glaucoma is the silent thief because the brain steals blood from the optic nerve long before pressure rises. The eye appears normal until the retinal ganglion cells are already dying. The current model treats the thief's accomplice—pressure—while the real thief remains untouched. The framework redirects attention upstream, to the brain's decree and the hypoxic retina. Keywords: Glaucoma; retinal ganglion cells; optic nerve; hypoxia; choroid; vasoconstriction; SAP cascade; Ocular UBTI; intraocular pressure; Law of Pressure Reflection; environmental path; starter motor; PDE5 inhibitor; GLP-1

etudes.titre: Glaucoma and Diabetes Mellitus: A Comparative Evaluation of Comorbid Effect on Tear Quantity among Patients in Owerri, Imo State, Nigeria.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Abstract Objective: Glaucoma is a chronic disorder that impairs ocular health and may exacerbate ocular surface disease leading to tear film instability, dry eye symptoms and decreased quality of life. This study compared changes in tear quantity among glaucoma subjects living with and without diabetes mellitus, attending an eye clinic in Nigeria. Methods: A comparative cross sectional research design was used. 157 subjects which comprised 74 glaucoma subjects living with diabetes mellitus and 83 glaucoma subjects living without diabetes mellitus participated in the study. Tear quantity assessment included the Schirmer I test and tear meniscus height (TMH) measurement. Descriptive statistics, independent samples t-test and Chi-square test were used to examine the data at 0.05 level of significance. Results: Glaucoma subjects living with diabetes mellitus showed substantially decreased tear production (11.4 +/- 6.8 mm) compared with glaucoma subjects living without diabetes mellitus (19.6 +/- 9.6 mm; p < 0.001). Tear meniscus height in glaucoma subjects living with diabetes mellitus (0.8 +/- 0.3 mm) was significantly greater than in subjects living without diabetes mellitus (0.7 +/- 0.3 mm; p = 0.034). Conclusion: Diabetes mellitus dramatically deteriorates the ocular surface function in glaucoma subjects by decreasing tear production, altering the tear meniscus height and increasing the severity of ocular surface symptoms. Routine glaucoma care, especially in patients with diabetes mellitus, should include a full ocular surface evaluation including Schirmer I test, TBUT, TMH, and OSDI assessment to allow early detection and management of ocular surface disease, better treatment adherence, and improved visual outcomes. Keywords: Glaucoma, Diabetes Mellitus, Tear production, Tear Meniscus Height, Ocular Surface Disease.

etudes.titre: Assessment of Tear film Stability and Ocular Surface Disease Index among Glaucoma Subjects living with and without Diabetes Mellitus in Owerri, Imo State, Nigeria
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Abstract Objective The ocular surface is an integral unit of the visual system. Its smooth and wet surface which is maintained by the tear film, is the most important refractive interface of the visual system. This study compared ocular surface alterations among glaucoma subjects living with and without diabetes mellitus in a Owerri, Imo State, Nigeria Methods Subjects diagnosed of glaucoma living with and without diabetes mellitus were included in the study. Ocular surface assessment included the Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI) questionnaire, and tear break-up time (TBUT). Descriptive statistics, independent samples t-test and Chi-square test were used to examine the data at 0.05 level of significance. Results Considerable shorter tear break-up time (11.3 ± 9.0s) was seen among glaucoma subjects living with diabetes mellitus than those living without diabetes mellitus (16.0 ± 10.6s; p = 0.003), demonstrating the higher tear film instability. This was similarly reflected by the mean OSDI score, which was considerably higher in glaucoma patients living with diabetes mellitus (40.0 ± 23.4) compared with those without diabetes mellitus (28.1 ± 21.8; p = 0.001) showing a larger ocular surface symptom load. However, although the frequency of severe OSDI symptoms was greater in glaucoma subjects living with diabetes mellitus, the relationship between diabetes status and OSDI severity categories was not statistically significant (χ 2 = 7.584, p = 0.055). Conclusion Diabetes mellitus significantly impacts the health of the ocular surface in glaucoma subjects. The combination of glaucoma and diabetes may result in more rapid tear film instability, increased ocular pain, and decreased quality of life and adherence to long-term glaucoma medication.

etudes.titre: The potential of antioxidants as glaucoma therapy
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « antioxidants »
etudes.resume: BACKGROUND: Glaucoma is a form of progressively worsening optic neuropathy evidenced by the loss of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs), with consequent visual impairment. While an elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) and oxidative stress are cornerstones in the pathological study of glaucoma, there is growing evidence that antioxidant supplementation may enhance ocular blood flow, reduce IOP, protect mitochondrial function, and decrease neuroinflammation, thus serving as a possible adjunctive treatment for glaucoma.METHODS: A systematic search of the literature was performed with the databases PubMed, ScienceDirect, and Springer Link using the keywords “antioxidant,” “glaucoma,” and “ocular hypertension” for studies published from the years 2020 to 2024. There were 4797 articles in the beginning, so all but the most relevant 13 were selected based on criteria such as randomized control trials, original research design, and systematic reviews predominantly focused on the proposed topic.RESULTS: The selected studies showed that oxidative stress is a significant contributing factor in the reduced blood flow to eyes, and that certain antioxidants, for example, vitamins C and E, Coenzyme Q10, hesperidin, as well as some natural extracts significantly improved the perfusion as well as lowers the IOP whilst protecting the RGCs from oxidized and apoptotic damage. A number of trials reported marked improvements.CONCLUSIONS: The information analyzed proves that antioxidants may be helpful as part of caring for persons with glaucoma. Antioxidant supplementation could lead to improved ocular blood circulation and reduced IOP because of enhanced mitochondral activity, and less oxidative stress to RGCs and trabecular meshwork (TM). These findings, however, need to be substantiated by better clinical trials capable of determining their ideal values in regard to dosage and long-term benefits. Studies, however, suggest that incorporating antioxidants into glaucoma management strategies is likely to ameliorate progressive glaucomatous damage and enhance the patient’s quality of life.
etudes.revue: Gazzetta Medica Italiana Archivio per le Scienze Mediche

etudes.titre: Sequential Inflammatory and Pupillary-Block Ocular Hypertension in Streptococcus suis Endogenous Endophthalmitis: An Observational Analytic Case Study
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Background: Streptococcus suis, a zoonosis acquired from pigs and raw pork, is a rare cause of endogenous endophthalmitis, and no quantitative account of the pressure complications of such an eye has been published. Objective: To characterize, in a single culture-proven case of Streptococcus suis endogenous endophthalmitis, the two mechanisms and the course of the raised intraocular pressure, and to derive the clinical implications for management. Methods: a structured analysis of one culture-proven case managed at a tertiary hospital in Bali, Indonesia, over 48 days. Acuity was converted to logMAR on four published scales, all 19 pressure readings were analysed with a repeatability model, and corticosteroid causation was scored with the Naranjo instrument. Results: a 46-year-old man who had eaten raw pork a week earlier presented with meningitis, reduced hearing and a left eye with light perception, hypopyon and vitritis. Cerebrospinal fluid and vitreous both grew S. suis. Pressure rose in two distinct episodes: an inflammatory one peaking at 29.0 mmHg on day 7, and a pupillary block from posterior synechiae with iris bombé peaking at 30.0 mmHg on day 16, which fell 11.0 mmHg after iridotomy with simultaneous reintroduction of timolol. Corticosteroid causation scored 3, a value largely fixed by the temporal sequence alone. Acuity improved by 0.70 logMAR overall, but the division of that gain across the vitrectomy reversed with the conversion scale: 0.40 before and 0.30 after by clinical convention against 0.10 and 0.60 with measured hand-movement values. The eye remained blind. Conclusion: raised pressure in such eyes is not one entity, the pupil must be examined before pressure-lowering therapy is escalated, and a logMAR change at this level of vision is uninterpretable unless its scale is stated.
etudes.revue: Bioscientia Medicina Journal of Biomedicine and Translational Research

etudes.titre: Shrinkage invalidates the Hosmer-Lemeshow test: goodness of fit for penalized logistic regression, with an application to glaucoma diagnosis
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « diagnosis »
etudes.resume: Clinical prediction models are increasingly fitted by penalized logistic regression, because collinearity or many candidate predictors makes maximum likelihood unstable or impossible. Calibration is then almost always assessed by a grouped goodness-of-fit test such as the Hosmer-Lemeshow test. We show that this combination is invalid. Under ridge regression the grouped standardized residuals acquire a non-centrality induced by shrinkage, so the reference distribution used in practice is wrong, and at the penalty that most improves the fitted probabilities the test rejects correctly specified models between 92 and 100 per cent of the time. We derive the corrected law and define the shrinkage-corrected Hosmer-Lemeshow test, which subtracts an estimate of that non-centrality, restoring the maximum likelihood reference exactly to first order, and is made valid by prepivoting at a power cost we measure. We also give the attenuation law governing what any such test can detect once the linear predictor must be estimated. In glaucoma diagnosis by confocal laser tomography, where the maximum likelihood estimate does not exist, the corrected test finds the evidence for misfit weaker by more than three orders of magnitude: the fitted risks are too flat rather than mis-ordered, so the model needs recalibration rather than rebuilding.

etudes.titre: Mitochondrial DNA Copy Number Is Associated With Visual Field Progression in Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Visual Field »
etudes.resume: A bstract Purpose To investigate the association between mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) copy number (CN) and the rate of visual field progression in patients with primary open-angle glaucoma. Design Retrospective cohort study Participants 200 patients with primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) with a mean of 11 years of longitudinal clinical data and DNA extracted from peripheral blood. Methods DNA extraction was performed on peripheral blood leukocytes collected from 200 POAG patients who had an average follow-up of 11 years. Mitochondrial CN was quantified by multiplex quantitative TaqMan PCR using custom primers and probes against cytochrome b and ß-2 microglobulin as measures of mitochondrial and nuclear genes, respectively. Univariable and multivariable linear regression models were used to evaluate the association between mtDNA CN and rates of visual field progression, quantified by the slope of standard automated perimetry (SAP) mean deviation (MD) over time. Main Outcome Measures Association of mtDNA CN with MD slope. Results Mean mtDNA CN was 107.6 copies per cell (interquartile range, 70.5–126.7). Higher ln(mtDNA CN) was associated with slower rates of MD loss in both univariable ( β = 0.29, p < 0.001) and multivariable analyses ( β = 0.25, p = 0.003). Higher peak IOP was independently associated with faster visual field progression in both analyses. A significant interaction was observed between mtDNA CN and peak IOP ( β = −0.054, p < 0.001), with the association between lower mtDNA CN and faster SAP progression being more pronounced at lower levels of peak IOP. Conclusion Lower mtDNA CN was associated with faster SAP progression, with the association being most pronounced at lower levels of peak IOP. These findings support mtDNA CN as a potential systemic biomarker of mitochondrial genomic reserve and susceptibility to visual field loss.

etudes.titre: Attention-Enhanced Deep Features with Heterogeneous Ensemble Learning for Glaucoma Detection
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Detection »
etudes.resume: Glaucoma is a progressive optic neuropathy characterized by irreversible damage to the optic nerve, making timely diagnosis critical to prevent permanent vision loss. Although deep learning has demonstrated promising performance in automated glaucoma detection, existing approaches often overlook feature refinement, suffer from class imbalance, and rely on individual classifiers that limit prediction robustness. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a hybrid glaucoma detection framework that integrates attention-enhanced deep feature extraction with heterogeneous ensemble learning. Specifically, deep representations are extracted using InceptionV3 and subsequently refined by incorporating the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) to enhance discriminative retinal features. To improve classification robustness, the extracted features are classified using multiple machine learning models together with Single-Level Ensemble (SLE) and Double-Level Ensemble (DLE) strategies, while SMOTE combined with Tomek Links (SMOTE+TL) is employed to alleviate class imbalance. Furthermore, a systematic comparison of handcrafted, deep, and attention-enhanced deep feature representations is conducted. Experimental evaluation on two public retinal fundus datasets demonstrates that deep feature-based methods consistently outperform handcrafted feature-based methods, while the proposed attention-enhanced framework achieves the best overall performance. Furthermore, Grad-CAM visualizations confirm that the proposed model focuses on clinically relevant retinal regions, providing interpretable evidence on the model's prediction process.

etudes.titre: Corneal Biomechanics in Glaucoma: Current Evidence for Diagnosis, Risk Stratification, and Prognosis
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Diagnosis »; mot du titre : « Biomechanics »
etudes.resume: Xian Wu,1,2 Hongbo Luo,1 Huanping Chen,1,3 Rui Luo1,31Center for Rehabilitation Medicine, Department of Ophthalmology, Zhejiang Provincial People’s Hospital (Affiliated People’s Hospital, Hangzhou Medical College), Hangzhou, Zhejiang, People’s Republic of China; 2The Second Clinical Medical College, Zhejiang Chinese Medical University, Hangzhou, Zhejiang, People’s Republic of China; 3Postgraduate Training Base Alliance of Wenzhou Medical University (Zhejiang Provincial People’s Hospital), Wenzhou Medical University, Wenzhou, Zhejiang, People’s Republic of ChinaCorrespondence: Hongbo Luo, Center for Rehabilitation Medicine, Department of Ophthalmology, Zhejiang Provincial People’s Hospital (Affiliated People’s Hospital, Hangzhou Medical College), Hangzhou, Zhejiang, People’s Republic of China, Email luohongbo1213@163.comBackground: Corneal biomechanical measurements influence the interpretation of intraocular pressure and may also capture aspects of ocular-wall susceptibility that are not represented by central corneal thickness alone. Their diagnostic and prognostic relevance in glaucoma has therefore attracted increasing attention.Methods: A structured narrative search of PubMed/MEDLINE was performed from database inception through July 25, 2026, using combinations of terms related to glaucoma, ocular hypertension, corneal biomechanics, corneal hysteresis, the Ocular Response Analyzer, Corvis ST, dynamic Scheimpflug imaging, and emerging elastographic techniques. Reference lists of eligible publications and key reviews were also screened. Peer-reviewed clinical studies, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, authoritative reports, and selected foundational experimental studies were considered.Review Findings: The Ocular Response Analyzer and Corvis ST provide device-specific measurements that are not directly interchangeable. Lower corneal hysteresis is consistently associated with glaucoma and with faster structural or functional progression, whereas the diagnostic performance of Corvis ST-derived parameters is more heterogeneous and varies by glaucoma subtype, intraocular pressure, central corneal thickness, axial length, and treatment exposure. Unlike previous broad overviews, this review explicitly separates diagnostic from prognostic evidence, contrasts findings across glaucoma phenotypes and devices, and examines the effect of major confounders. Brillouin microscopy and optical coherence elastography may eventually provide spatially resolved tissue measurements, but neither has been validated for routine glaucoma management.Conclusion: Corneal biomechanical measurements should currently be regarded as complementary biomarkers rather than stand-alone diagnostic endpoints in glaucoma. Future progress will depend on standardized acquisition and reporting, subtype-specific prospective validation, and multimodal integration with structural and functional glaucoma assessments.Keywords: Corneal biomechanics, corneal hysteresis, ocular response analyzer, Corvis ST, glaucoma progression, ocular hypertension, risk stratification
etudes.revue: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)

etudes.titre: Hydrus® Microstent Combined with Cataract Surgery in Pseudoexfoliation Glaucoma Versus Primary Open Angle Glaucoma
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Microstent »; mot du titre : « Surgery »
etudes.resume: Background/Objectives: Our objective was to compare clinical outcomes of the Hydrus® Microstent implantation combined with cataract surgery in eyes with pseudoexfoliation glaucoma (PXG) and primary open angle glaucoma (POAG). Methods: This retrospective, single-center comparative cohort study included eyes with POAG or PXG undergoing combined cataract surgery and Hydrus® Microstent implantation between June 2021 and December 2025 at the University Eye Hospital of the Ludwig Maximilian University in Munich, Germany. Clinical outcomes were evaluated until 8–14 months after surgery. Results: A total of 74 eyes were included, comprising 49 POAG eyes and 25 PXG eyes. After cataract surgery plus Hydrus® Microstent, IOP decreased significantly in both groups from baseline to the final 8–14-month follow-up (POAG: 17.6 ± 3.9 to 13.8 ± 2.3 mmHg, p < 0.0001; PXG: 19.2 ± 4.3 to 14.6 ± 2.7 mmHg, p < 0.0001). The magnitude of IOP reduction did not differ between groups (p = 0.410). Meanwhile, the number of IOP-lowering medications decreased significantly in both groups with no between-group difference (POAG: −1.20 medications; PXG group −1.09 medications, p = 0.724). Surgical success rates were comparable. Conclusions: Hydrus® Microstent implantation combined with cataract surgery showed comparable surgical outcomes in POAG and PXG eyes. Regardless of the more aggressive disease characteristics of PXG, no significant differences were observed between PXG and POAG eyes regarding IOP reduction, medication burden, BCVA, surgical success, complications or safety outcomes. These findings suggest that combined cataract surgery and Hydrus® Microstent implantation may be a useful treatment option in selected patients with PXG.

etudes.titre: Genetic discovery using deep learning-derived optic nerve integrity phenotypes
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « deep learning »
etudes.resume: Abstract The peripapillary retinal nerve fibre layer (pRNFL) thickness and Bruch’s membrane opening-minimum rim width (BMO-MRW) are three-dimensional retinal biomarkers for glaucoma. We aimed to demonstrate that AI-derived thickness from two-dimensional fundus images can act as proxies, enabling the discovery of novel neurodegenerative loci. AI-derived pRNFL and BMO-MRW strongly correlated with OCT-derived thickness (r: 0.69 and 0.79, respectively). After validation, these phenotypes were predicted in two cohorts lacking disc-centred OCT: the UK Biobank and the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging. The predicted phenotypes showed strong genetic correlations with directly measured phenotypes from a previous study for both phenotypes (0.70 and 0.96, respectively). This data increased statistical power, identifying 29 loci for pRNFL thickness and 122 loci for BMO-MRW, including 14 loci that were independent of VCDR. We observed shared and sector-specific thickness loci overlapping glaucoma loci and revealed loci independent of known risk factors. Together, these results emphasise that multidimensional inferences can be drawn from 2D imaging, enabling downstream genetic analyses.

etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: El glaucoma va dañando de forma lenta y progresiva el nervio óptico. Quienes tienen glaucoma pierden visión antes de notar que tienen problemas con sus ojos. La forma más común es el Glaucoma Primario de Ángulo Abierto, seguido del Glaucoma por Cierre Angular Primario, se acompaña de múltiples factores de riesgo, donde el principal es el aumento de la presiónintraocular. La visión periférica es la que se daña inicialmente, no obstante con el tiempo se pierde la visión central y las dificultades visuales se incrementan y empeora la calidad de vida.La visión que se pierde por glaucoma, no es recuperable; sin embargo, hay formas de evitar pérdidas graves de visión y ceguera por esta enfermedad.

etudes.titre: Ocular Surface Symptoms, Objective Redness, and Intraocular Pressure After a Switch from Fixed Dorzolamide/Timolol to Netarsudil in Latanoprost-Treated Glaucoma and Ocular Hypertension: A Prospective Real-World Cohort Study
etudes.raison_rubrique: étiquette : produit suivi étudié (rôle suggéré, à vérifier)
etudes.resume: Background and Objectives: Conjunctival hyperemia is common with netarsudil, but redness may not reflect the overall patient experience when treatment burden is reduced. We evaluated ocular surface symptoms, objective redness, tear-film parameters, intraocular pressure (IOP), and treatment preference after a routine-care switch from twice-daily fixed dorzolamide/timolol to once-daily netarsudil 0.02%, while continuing latanoprost. Materials and Methods: This prospective, single-center observational cohort included 30 consecutive adults with primary open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension and controlled IOP. Outcomes were assessed at baseline and months 1 and 2. The primary outcome was the Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI). Continuous eye-level outcomes were analyzed using mixed-effects models accounting for fellow-eye and repeated-measures correlation; grade ≥ 2 hyperemia was analyzed using participant-clustered logistic regression. Results: Twenty-seven participants (54 eyes) completed evaluable 2-month follow-up. Median OSDI decreased from 7.50 at baseline to 6.25 at month 1 and 5.00 at month 2 (Friedman p = 0.0015). The mean baseline-to-month 2 change was −2.95 points (95% CI, −4.80 to −1.10), and 6/27 participants (22.2%) improved by at least 7 points. Serle grade ≥ 2 hyperemia increased from 7.4% of eyes at baseline to 51.9% at month 1 and 44.4% at month 2. Estimated mean bulbar redness index increased from 1.57 to 2.14 (p < 0.0001), tear meniscus height increased modestly, and non-invasive keratograph break-up time showed no significant longitudinal change. Estimated mean IOP changed from 14.50 to 13.65 mmHg (p = 0.0083), with no eye showing an increase of at least 4 mmHg. Burning improved after multiplicity adjustment, and 17/27 participants with available month-2 preference data (63.0%) preferred netarsudil. Conclusions: The switch was associated with modest OSDI improvement and maintained short-term IOP control despite increased objective redness. Patient preference appeared to reflect factors beyond redness alone.

etudes.titre: Clinical and Patient-Reported Outcomes of Premium Intraocular Lenses in Glaucoma Patients Undergoing Combined Cataract and Minimally Invasive Glaucoma Surgery
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Minimally Invasive Glaucoma Surgery »; mot du titre : « Surgery »
etudes.resume: Jack Wolsky,1 Christianah Jemiyo,1 Michael Greenwood21School of Medicine and Health Sciences, University of North Dakota, Grand Forks, ND, USA; 2Vance Thompson Vision, West Fargo, ND, USACorrespondence: Jack Wolsky, School of Medicine and Health Sciences, University of North Dakota, 1301 N Columbia Rd Stop 9037, Grand Forks, ND, 58202-9037, USA, Tel +1 701 509-9883, Email jack.wolsky@und.eduBackground: Premium intraocular lenses (IOLs), including multifocal, extended depth-of-focus (EDOF), and light adjustable lenses (LALs) are used to reduce spectacle dependence after cataract surgery. However, their use in glaucoma patients remains controversial due to concerns that reduced contrast sensitivity and pre-existing visual field loss limits functional benefits from these optics. Increasing use of minimally invasive glaucoma surgery (MIGS) at the time of cataract surgery has made combined refractive and glaucoma management more common, but data on real world outcomes remains limited.Methods: This single-center, IRB-approved retrospective observational study with cross-sectional survey analysis included glaucoma patients who underwent bilateral cataract surgery with implantation of multifocal, EDOF, or LAL IOLs with concurrent MIGS from 2020 to 2025. Postoperative visual outcomes, intraocular pressure (IOP), glaucoma medication burden, spectacle dependence, dysphotopsias, and patient satisfaction were assessed. Longitudinal outcomes were analyzed using mixed-effects models adjusted for baseline glaucoma severity (mean deviation). Satisfaction was evaluated using proportional odds logistic regression adjusting for age and baseline disease severity.Results: Seventy-nine patients (Multifocal n=43, EDOF n=24, LAL n=12) were included. All groups demonstrated significant postoperative improvement in distance visual acuity and reduction in IOP and glaucoma medication burden. Adjusted IOP trajectories and most recent IOP were similar between groups. Distance visual acuity outcomes were similar between groups after adjustment for baseline glaucoma severity. Near visual acuity favored multifocal IOLs, while LAL demonstrated the highest spectacle dependence. Dysphotopsias were more frequent with multifocal lenses and lowest in LAL. Satisfaction was high across all groups, with predicted probabilities of being "very” or "somewhat satisfied” of 94% (multifocal), 88% (EDOF), and 87% (LAL).Conclusions: In appropriately selected glaucoma patients undergoing cataract surgery with MIGS, multifocal, EDOF, and LAL IOLs provide comparable visual outcomes, excellent IOP control, and high satisfaction. Differences in spectacle dependence and dysphotopsia support individualized IOL selection.Keywords: glaucoma, intraocular lens, patient-reported outcomes, spectacle independence, visual acuity

etudes.titre: Rapid, Non-Contact, Objective Multifocal Assessment of Visual Function in Glaucoma
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: We compared a rapid fifth-generation (5G) objectiveFIELD Analyser® (OFA®) test with two fourth-generation (4G) 8-minute tests in the assessment of glaucoma. We assessed the relative diagnostic power of these three OFA tests, namely two high-resolution 4G tests (wide-field OFA30 and macular OFA15), and a new 5G 90-second test (wide-field OFA30-20). Glaucomatous eyes were classified into mild, moderate and severe based upon Matrix 24-2 perimetry Mean Defect (MD). Diagnostic power was estimated by Area Under Curve of Receiver Operating Characteristic plots (AUROC) and Standardised Effect-Sizes (Hedge’s g) for each category of glaucoma severity. We tested 35 glaucoma patients (11 females), aged 72 ± 6.88 years. Their average Matrix MD was -7.71 ± 6.35 dB. Age-matched normal controls were acquired for the 4G and 5G tests. For the rapid 90-second test combined sensitivity and delay reports typically provided the best diagnostic power. For severe eyes, the OFA30-20 produced an AUROC of 90.4 ± 2.98, which was not significantly different to the OFA30 and OFA15. Hedge’s g was ≥ 2.68 for all those comparisons. AUROCs based upon sensitivity alone were not significantly different. We examined the agreement of the MD and Pattern Standard Deviations (PSD) of the two wide-field (OFA30 and OFA30-20) tests. The significant correlations for the sensitivity and delay MDs were > 0.85, and for PSDs 0.53 and 0.69. The rapid 5G OFA30-20 test was comparable to the 8-minute tests. It may be highly useful in young adults with short attention span and infirm persons who cannot tolerate longer tests.

etudes.titre: Diagnostic challenges of glaucoma in patients with diabetes mellitus
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Diagnostic »
etudes.resume: Glaucoma in patients with diabetes mellitus (DM) is a clinically and diagnostically challenging condition whose formation and detection are complicated by the combined influence of metabolic, vascular and neurodegenerative factors. This review summarizes current data on glaucoma as a comorbid condition in diabetes mellitus, as well as on secondary neovascular glaucoma developing in the setting of diabetic retinopathy. The article discusses mechanisms of increased intraocular pressure in chronic hyperglycemia, including impaired aqueous humor secretion and outflow, trabecular meshwork remodeling, and endothelial dysfunction. This study places particular emphasis on the diagnostic limitations of standard examination methods and analyzes in detail how changes in corneal biomechanical properties affect the reliability of transcorneal tonometry. It also discusses the difficulties of interpreting optical coherence tomography and standard automated perimetry findings in patients with DM, which are caused by diabetesassociated morphofunctional changes in the retina and optic nerve and by the consequences of laser treatment for diabetic retinopathy. These changes may mask or mimic signs of glaucomatous optic neuropathy, creating a risk of diagnostic errors and incorrect assessment of disease progression. The article emphasizes the need for a comprehensive approach to glaucoma diagnosis in patients with DM that takes metabolic status into account, as well as the need to develop diagnostic criteria with better specificity.

etudes.titre: Correlation of Mitochondrial Flavoprotein Fluorescence and Sectoral OCT in Patients with Glaucoma, Suspects, and Ocular Hypertension
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « OCT »; mot du titre : « Fluorescence »
etudes.resume: Tiffany Heaster-Ford,1,* Rafaella Nascimento e Silva,2,* Justin Elstrott,1 Dolly S Chang,1,3 Julia A Kim,2 Joyce Kang,4 Yan Zhao,3 Yihao Li,5 Chen Chen,5 Sofia De Arrigunaga,4 Sandra E Freeman,4 Kanza Aziz,4 Collin A Rich,6 Michael M Lin,4 David S Friedman41Department of Translational Imaging, Genentech Inc, South San Francisco, CA, USA; 2Department of Early Clinical Development, Genentech Inc, South San Francisco, CA, USA; 3Byers Eye Institute, Stanford University School of Medicine, Palo Alto, CA, USA; 4Department of Ophthalmology, Massachusetts Eye and Ear, Boston, MA, USA; 5Department of Product Development Data Sciences, Genentech Inc, South San Francisco, CA, USA; 6OcuSciences Inc, Ann Arbor, MI, USA*These authors contributed equally to this workCorrespondence: David S Friedman, Department of Ophthalmology, Massachusetts Eye and Ear, 243 Charles Street, Boston, 02114, USA, Email David_friedman@meei.harvard.eduPurpose: Flavoprotein fluorescence (FPF) can be measured using a noninvasive investigational device, the OcuMet Beacon (OcuSciences). The Beacon uses blue light to stimulate oxidized mitochondrial flavoproteins, which subsequently emit green autofluorescence. As mitochondrial metabolic stress may reflect axonal damage in glaucomatous eyes, this cross-sectional, exploratory study investigated relationships between optical coherence tomography (OCT) structural parameters and FPF values in patients with glaucoma, ocular hypertension, and glaucoma suspects.Patients and Methods: Individuals with mild/moderate glaucoma, suspected glaucoma, or ocular hypertension receiving treatment. FPF images were obtained at the optic nerve head (ONH), peripapillary, and macula regions. FPF intensities in the peripapillary and macula regions were divided into 4 and 6 sectors, respectively, corresponding to Cirrus OCT retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) and ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer thickness (mGCIPL). FPF values adjusted for lens autofluorescence and signal attenuation were averaged within each sector and applied for regression modeling with OCT measures.Results: A small cohort of 73 eyes from 54 patients was assessed from the initial study population (141 eyes, 83 early/mild/moderate glaucoma patients undergoing treatment) following image quality exclusion. Older age, thinner RNFL, and phakic status were significantly associated with higher FPF intensity at the ONH (age, P=0.009; RNFL, P< 0.001; lens status, P=0.04) and peripapillary region (age, P< 0.001; RNFL, P=0.01). Inferior peripapillary correlation between RNFL thickness and FPF was significant (P=0.003), while nasal peripapillary correlation was significant only after adjusting for age and lens status (adjusted P=0.04; unadjusted P=0.08). Global macular FPF intensity was not associated with age (P=0.25), lens status (P=0.14) or mGCIPL thickness (P=0.79), nor were there any sectoral mGCIPL–FPF associations potentially given limited disease severity.Conclusion: Age, lens status and RNFL thinning were the main correlates of ONH and peripapillary FPF values. After accounting for age and lens status covariates, higher FPF intensity values mainly correlated with inferior peripapillary RNFL thinning.Keywords: glaucoma, mitochondrial imaging, optical coherence tomography, flavoprotein fluorescence

etudes.titre: Multimodal Deep Learning for Humphrey 24-2 Visual Field Prediction: Evaluating the Contribution of Fellow-Eye Information in Glaucoma and Ocular Hypertension
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Deep Learning »; mot du titre : « Visual Field »
etudes.resume: Background/Objectives: To develop a multimodal deep learning framework for Humphrey 24-2 visual field prediction using multimodal OCT-derived structural information and to investigate whether incorporating fellow-eye information improves pointwise threshold sensitivity estimation in glaucoma and ocular hypertension. Methods: This retrospective study included 591 patients, 892 eyes, and 1099 eye-visit samples. Four OCT-derived image modalities were combined with demographic, optic disc, RNFL, and image-quality variables. Three architectures were evaluated using a patient-level 60/20/20 split: A0, a single-eye baseline; A1, bilateral Siamese feature fusion; and A2, fellow-eye-guided α-gated residual refinement applied exclusively to the 52-point threshold sensitivity output (TS52). Results: The baseline A0 model achieved MAEs of 2.97 dB (MD), 1.62 dB (PSD), and 3.26 dB (mean TS), with corresponding RMSEs of 4.40, 2.30, and 4.74 dB, respectively. Overall predictive performance remained comparable across architectures. Among the bilateral models, A1 achieved the lowest RMSE for mean threshold sensitivity (4.66 dB), whereas A2 achieved the lowest MAE (3.13 dB). In the paired-eye test subset (102 eyes from 51 patients), enabling fellow-eye input did not significantly improve TS52 prediction in A1 but significantly reduced TS52 RMSE (Δ = 0.08 dB, p = 0.0004) and MAE (Δ = 0.07 dB, p < 0.0001) in A2. Spatial analyses further demonstrated that A1 mainly induced a global calibration-like shift, whereas A2 selectively refined central and paracentral threshold sensitivity predictions. Conclusions: Fellow-eye information contributed to pointwise visual field prediction in a model-dependent manner. Within the paired-eye test subset, A2 achieved modest but statistically significant reductions in prediction error, supporting controlled residual refinement as a promising approach to incorporating fellow-eye information.

etudes.titre: Retinal organoid-derived exosomes enhance retinal ganglion cell survival in chronic ocular hypertension
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « retinal ganglion cell »
etudes.resume: Abstract Background To date, the therapeutic potential of retinal organoid–derived exosomes (Exo-ROs) for retinal ganglion cell (RGC) preservation in chronic ocular hypertension (COH) has not been explored. We aimed to evaluate the neuroprotective effects and underlying molecular mechanisms of Exo-ROs in a rat COH model. Methods Human induced pluripotent stem cell–derived retinal organoids (ROs) were differentiated, and exosomes were isolated from conditioned medium at day 60. COH was induced by circumlimbal suture in Sprague–Dawley rats, followed by intravitreal delivery of Exo-ROs. RGC survival and function were assessed by Brn3a immunostaining and photopic negative response (PhNR). To elucidate the mechanisms, MAPK pathway activation was analyzed at day 3, and total RNA sequencing was performed at 1 month post-treatment. Results Exo-ROs significantly improved RGC survival and preserved PhNR amplitudes in COH eyes ( p < 0.001). At day 3 post-treatment, Exo-ROs markedly suppressed the COH-induced phosphorylation of ERK, JNK, and p38, indicating an early inhibition of stress-induced MAPK signaling. Exosomal microRNA profiling further supported these findings, showing an enrichment of miRNAs targeting the MAPK pathway. Furthermore, total RNA sequencing performed 1 month after treatment revealed that Exo-ROs partially restored the transcriptomic profile of the COH retina, specifically modulating biological processes associated with fatty acid beta-oxidation and immune response regulation. Conclusions Exo-ROs confer robust neuroprotection in experimental COH, a process associated with early suppression of stress-induced MAPK signaling and long-term modulation of the retinal transcriptome and metabolism. Exo-ROs represent a promising cell-free therapeutic strategy for glaucoma management.

etudes.titre: Interpretable AI plus Handheld, Portable Retinal Photographs: A Low-Cost Glaucoma Screening Solution for West Africa
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « AI »; mot du titre : « Screening »
etudes.resume: Purpose: To develop and evaluate an interpretable artificial intelligence (AI) framework for glaucoma screening from low-cost portable, handheld retinal fundus photographs in a West African population and to compare its performance with clinical tabletop fundus imaging. Methods: We used data from a community-based study of 681 participants (1,362 eyes) in Nigeria, comprising 414 glaucoma, 478 glaucoma suspect, and 470 non-glaucoma eyes. Fundus photographs were acquired using the low-cost handheld, portable Volk Viva retinal camera and the Canon CR-2-AF tabletop camera. We fine-tuned component models separately to each device to perform vessel segmentation, cup and disc boundary segmentation, and feature extraction to detect optic nerve head features. A final classification model combined these components to classify scans as glaucoma, glaucoma suspect or non-glaucoma. Feature-weight analysis and Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping were used for interpretation. Results: The models performed well on both Volk Viva and Canon CR-2-AF images: Vessel segmentation: 0.98 Dice Coefficient (DC) (Volk) and 0.94 DC (Canon); Cup and disc segmentation: 0.95 DC (Volk) and 0.96 DC (Canon); Optic nerve head feature detection: area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.83$\pm$0.03 (Volk) and 0.87$\pm$0.04 (Canon); Classification model: AUCs of 0.85$\pm$0.01 (Volk) and 0.93$\pm$0.01 (Canon). Reports for each image, present model decision confidence scores and decision-rationale visualizations to support clinical interpretation. Conclusions: Volk Viva results were reasonably comparable to Canon CR-2-AF in the component models and not far behind in classification. This shows that interpretable AI combined with low-cost, portable imaging may enhance community-level glaucoma screening, especially in settings with limited specialist access and resources.

etudes.resume: Juvenile glaucoma is a rare but clinically important condition that may cause progressive optic nerve damage during childhood and adolescence. In addition to intraocular pressure (IOP), genetic predisposition and structural changes of the optic nerve, systemic physiological dysregulation may influence disease development and progression. Allostatic load (AL) reflects the cumulative physiological cost of repeated or chronic stress and integrates cardiovascular, metabolic, inflammatory and neuroendocrine components [1–3].

etudes.titre: Five-Year Real-World Outcomes of iStent inject W® Combined with Phacoemulsification in Ocular Hypertension and Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « iStent »
etudes.resume: Abstract Purpose: To evaluate the long-term real-world efficacy, safety, and functional and structural outcomes in patients with ocular hypertension (OHT) or primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) undergoing trabecular micro-bypass surgery with the iStent inject W®. Methods: This retrospective longitudinal study included 149 eyes of 149 patients with OHT or POAG who underwent implantation of the iStent inject W®, combined with phacoemulsification, and were followed for up to five years. Outcomes included intraocular pressure (IOP), number of hypotensive medications, best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), optical coherence tomography (OCT) structural parameters, and visual field indices. Follow-up data were available at 1 year (n = 123), 2 years (n = 94), 3 years (n = 61), 4 years (n = 35), and 5 years (n = 15). Results: BCVA improved significantly after surgery (p < 0.01). A mild but statistically significant decline in visual field index (VFI) was observed over time (p = 0.03), consistent with expected long-term glaucoma progression. OCT structural parameters remained stable throughout follow-up. IOP was significantly reduced at all postoperative visits except at years 3 and 5, where reductions did not reach statistical significance despite a sustained downward trend. Medication burden was significantly reduced at all time points (p < 0.01). Men exhibited lower postoperative IOP than women (p = 0.02), and OHT patients had higher IOP levels than those with POAG (p < 0.01). Conclusions: In a real-world clinical setting, the iStent inject W® provided sustained IOP reduction, durable medication burden reduction and long-term structural stability over five years. These findings support its long-term clinical effectiveness in the management of OHT and POAG.

etudes.titre: Association of Adduction-Induced Optic Nerve Head Strain with Visual Field Loss Progression in Myopic Normal-Tension Glaucoma The Wenzhou Glaucoma Progression Study
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Visual Field »

labos.nom: National Natural Science Foundation of China

etudes.resume: ABSTRACT Purpose To characterize the biomechanical response of the optic nerve head (ONH) in myopic versus non-myopic individuals with normal-tension glaucoma (NTG), and to evaluate the association between ONH strains and the rate of visual field (VF) progression. Design Retrospective clinical cohort study. Participants A total of 118 NTG eyes from 77 patients with ≥ 2 years of follow-up and 5 VF tests were enrolled, including 66 eyes with myopia and 52 eyes without. Methods Each participant underwent three-dimensional (3D) optical coherence tomography (OCT) imaging of the ONH under three mechanical loading conditions: 20° adduction, 30° abduction and acute intraocular pressure (IOP) elevation by applying a 0.80 N force to the lower eyelid. Effective strains across the global ONH complex and within specific segmented tissues (pre-lamina, lamina cribrosa, choroid, and sclera) were quantified using a validated 3D strain-mapping algorithm. Results Myopic NTG eyes exhibited significantly higher ONH strains compared to non-myopic eyes under acute IOP elevation (10.1±2.7% vs. 9.3±1.8%, P = 0.044) and abduction (9.2±2.3% vs. 8.4±2.1%, P = 0.048). In the non-myopic group, ONH strains varied significantly across conditions (P < 0.001), with adduction (9.9± 2.0%) and acute IOP elevation (9.3±1.8%) eliciting greater strains than abduction (8.4±2.1%). These condition-dependent variations were less pronounced in the myopic group (10.1±2.7% vs. 9.8±2.7% vs. 9.2±2.3%, P = 0.07). Multivariable linear mixed-effects analysis revealed that in myopic NTG, higher ONH strains induced by adduction were significantly associated with faster MD decline (estimate: -0.139 dB/year per 1% increase, P = 0.03, adjusted for age, spherical equivalent and baseline perimetric mean defect). Conversely, larger strains during acute IOP elevation were associated with slower progression (estimate: 0.184 dB/year per 1% increase, P = 0.004). Tissue-specific analysis confirmed that adduction-induced strains in the choroid and pre-lamina tissue as well as IOP-induced strains across all ONH tissues were significantly correlated with the rate of perimetric progression in myopic eyes (all P < 0.05). Conclusions In this cohort, greater adduction-induced ONH strain was associated with faster perimetric deterioration in myopic NTG. These findings support further investigation of gaze-related optic nerve traction as a potential non-IOP-related biomechanical factor in myopic NTG.

etudes.titre: Retinal Nerve Fibre Layer Thickness Analysis using Spectral-domain Optical Coherence Tomography in Normal Eyes, Ocular Hypertension, Glaucoma Suspects, and Early Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma: A Cross-sectional Comparative Study
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Optical Coherence Tomography »
etudes.resume: Introduction: Structural alterations of the Retinal Nerve Fibre Layer (RNFL) are among the earliest detectable manifestations of glaucomatous optic neuropathy and may precede measurable visual field defects. Spectral Domain Optical Coherence Tomography (SD-OCT) enables objective quantification of these changes and facilitates early detection of glaucoma. This study compared RNFL thickness among normal eyes, ocular hypertensives, glaucoma suspects, and eyes with early Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma (POAG). Aim: To compare retinal nerve fibre layer thickness using spectral-domain optical coherence tomography among normal eyes, ocular hypertensive eyes, glaucoma suspects, and early primary open-angle glaucoma eyes, and to evaluate its association with intraocular pressure. Materials and Methods: This hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted at the Outpatient Department (OPD) Ophthalmology of a Tertiary Care Hospital in Tamil Nadu, India, from August 2024 to October 2025. This study included 120 consecutively recruited participants categorised into normal eyes (n=30), ocular hypertension (n=30), glaucoma suspects (n=30), and early POAG eyes (n=30). All participants underwent a comprehensive ophthalmic evaluation, including intraocular pressure measurement by Goldmann applanation tonometry, gonioscopy, Humphrey visual field analysis, optic nerve head assessment, and spectral-domain optical coherence tomography-based RNFL analysis. Average and quadrant-wise RNFL thicknesses were compared among the groups using One-way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA). Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) analysis was used to evaluate the diagnostic performance of OCT-derived RNFL parameters. Results: Average RNFL thickness showed a significant progressive decline from normal eyes (102.9±5.6 µm) to ocular hypertensives (95.8±5.9 µm), glaucoma suspects (82.0±6.2 µm), and early POAG eyes (72.1±6.1 µm) (p<0.01). Quadrantwise analysis showed more pronounced RNFL reduction in the inferior and superior regions than in the nasal and temporal quadrants. OCT demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy, with area under the curve values of 0.96 for average RNFL thickness and 0.97 for inferior quadrant RNFL thickness. Conclusion: Spectral-domain OCT-derived RNFL thickness may serve as a useful structural biomarker for early glaucomatous damage and may aid in risk stratification and early glaucoma detection.

etudes.titre: Augmentation Strategy for DINO in Glaucoma Classification
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Self-supervised learning (SSL) offers a promising approach to medical image representation learning, yet augmentation strategies of SSL frameworks validated on natural images do not reliably transfer to specialized medical imaging domains. We analyze DINO, a knowledge-distillation based SSL framework, and empirically demonstrate that its default augmentation strategy produces unreliable representations for retinal fundus images, degrading downstream glaucoma classification performance. Guided by the principle that effective cropped views should share minimal redundant information while retaining clinically relevant signal, we redesign DINO's augmentation strategy. Our approach biases the learned representations toward diagnostically critical features rather than low-level image statistics. We evaluate our method for glaucoma classification by training a linear classifier on the frozen representations, achieving strong generalization across seven benchmark datasets. URL for code and weights: https://github.com/ashish-256/task_dino

etudes.titre: Evaluation of Postoperative Steroid-induced Ocular Hypertension after Phacoemulsification: An Observational Study
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Introduction: Topical corticosteroids are routinely prescribed after cataract surgery to control postoperative inflammation. However, these agents may induce ocular hypertension, with a subset of individuals exhibiting significant Intraocular Pressure (IOP) elevation. Understanding the magnitude and timing of steroid-induced IOP rise is essential for early detection and prevention of glaucomatous damage. Aim: To evaluate changes in IOP and determine the prevalence of steroid-induced ocular hypertension in patients receiving topical prednisolone acetate 1% following uncomplicated phacoemulsification. Materials and Methods: This hospital-based prospective observational study was conducted in the Department of Ophthalmology at Jagjivan Ram Hospital (JRH), Mumbai Central, Maharashtra, India, from October 2022 to October 2023. It included 53 patients undergoing uncomplicated cataract surgery at a tertiary eye care hospital. Eligible participants had normal preoperative IOP and received topical prednisolone acetate 1% in tapering doses for four weeks. Patients with glaucoma, ocular hypertension, complicated cataract, intraoperative complications, or prior steroid use were excluded. IOP was measured using Goldmann applanation tonometry preoperatively and at 1, 4, and 6 weeks postoperatively. Steroid responsiveness was classified as low (<5 mmHg rise), intermediate (6–15 mmHg), or high (>16 mmHg). The Statistical Package for Social Sciences (SPSS) version 25.0 was used for statistical analysis. The p-value<0.05 considered significant. Results: The mean baseline IOP was 17.02±2.85 mmHg, which increased significantly to 19.23±2.10 mmHg at the first week IOP remained elevated at week 4 (18.80±2.26 mmHg) and week 6 (18.92±2.59 mmHg), without returning to baseline levels (p<0.001). Most patients were low responders (73.4%), followed by intermediate responders (22.6%). High steroid responsiveness was observed in 4% of subjects. Conclusion: Topical prednisolone acetate 1% following cataract surgery leads to a significant early rise in IOP, with persistent elevation up to six weeks. Although the majority exhibit a mild response, a small but important proportion demonstrate marked IOP elevation. Routine postoperative IOP monitoringparticularly within the first week- is recommended to promptly identify high steroid responders.

etudes.titre: Uveitis-associated glaucoma and treatment-requiring ocular hypertension in a tertiary referral center
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Background: Elevated uveitis-associated intraocular pressure (IOP) may result from inflammatory, structural, and corticosteroid-related mechanisms and lead to secondary glaucoma. This study aimed to describe patients with uveitis who subsequently developed glaucoma or treatment-requiring ocular hypertension (OHT) in a tertiary referral clinic. Methods: This retrospective study was conducted at the Uveitis Clinic of Nikookari Eye Hospital, Tabriz University of Medical Sciences. Records of patients with uveitis diagnosed or managed during the preceding 10 years were reviewed. Patients were eligible if, after uveitis onset, they had IOP > 21 mmHg documented on at least two occasions separated by at least one week and requiring intervention, or documented glaucomatous findings based on available clinical assessment. Patients with IOP elevation or glaucomatous findings predating uveitis or insufficient documentation to establish the temporal relationship were excluded. Demographic, clinical, and treatment variables were extracted. Results: Among 441 patients with uveitis, 93 (21.1%) subsequently developed glaucoma or treatment-requiring OHT. Mean (standard deviation [SD]; range) age was 42.5 (17.4; 5–80) years, and 58 patients (62.4%) were female. Mean (SD) uveitis duration was 5.2 (4.3) years, and mean (SD) interval from uveitis diagnosis to glaucoma/OHT diagnosis was 2.1 (2.6) years. Panuveitis was the most frequent anatomical category (33.3%), followed by anterior (31.2%), intermediate (29.0%), and posterior uveitis (6.5%). Chronic uveitis was present in 76.3%, infectious uveitis in 39.8%. Herpes-family infection accounted for 14.0% of the cohort, Fuchs heterochromic iridocyclitis for 16.1%. Topical and systemic corticosteroid exposure was documented in 94.6% and 50.5%, respectively. The anterior chamber angle was open in 82.8% and closed in 17.2%. Medical, laser, and surgical treatment were documented in 95.7%, 15.1%, and 10.8%, respectively. Conclusions: In this tertiary referral cohort, approximately one in five patients with uveitis subsequently developed glaucoma or treatment-requiring OHT. The affected population was clinically heterogeneous, with chronic and panuveitic disease, infectious etiologies, Fuchs heterochromic iridocyclitis, corticosteroid exposure, and predominantly open-angle findings. These findings support continued IOP surveillance throughout uveitis, with attention to inflammatory activity, corticosteroid exposure, angle status, and glaucomatous changes. Given the retrospective design and lack of a comparator group, these characteristics cannot be considered independent risk factors. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to clarify risk factors, clinical course, and treatment outcomes.

etudes.titre: Auto-GlaKG: Automated Biomarker Reasoning for Explainable Glaucoma Detection
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Detection »; mot du titre : « Biomarker »
etudes.resume: Interpretable glaucoma detection requires a transparent connection between fundus images, clinically meaningful biomarkers, and diagnostic predictions. Knowledge graph (KG) reasoning provides this structure, but performance measured using annotated biomarkers does not establish performance when only images are available. We present Auto-GlaKG, an automated framework that combines image-based biomarker prediction with fixed clinical-prior rules. A ResNet50 network predicts the cup-to-disc ratio (CDR) and six morphological signs using biomarker supervision, and a KG reasoner aggregates their signed rule contributions into a glaucoma score. On 689 fundus images evaluated using stratified, group-aware five-fold cross-validation, Auto-GlaKG achieves a pooled area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.951 (95\% confidence interval: 0.931--0.969), with sensitivity of 0.970 and specificity of 0.779. The matched image classifier also achieves an AUC of 0.951, while the rule stage adds 0.2~ms per image. Replacing predicted CDR with its annotation increases fold-mean AUC from 0.953 to 0.995. The framework provides an explicit rule-level account of image-based predictions and identifies CDR estimation as a priority for validation using independently measured biomarkers.

etudes.titre: Glaucoma: Classification and Methods of Treatment, with Special Reference to Congenital and Secondary Glaucoma
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Glaucoma is a group of progressive optic neuropathies characterized by retinal ganglion-cell loss, structural damage to the optic nerve head and corresponding visual-field defects. Raised intraocular pressure (IOP) is the most important modifiable risk factor, but glaucoma may occur even when measured IOP is within the statistically normal range. Because established glaucomatous damage is generally irreversible, early diagnosis and sustained treatment are essential.This review describes the basic anatomy and physiology of aqueous humour, mechanisms and classification of glaucoma, clinical presentation, diagnostic evaluation and current treatment approaches. Particular attention is given to primary congenital glaucoma and secondary glaucoma. Congenital glaucoma is usually caused by developmental abnormalities of the anterior chamber angle and may lead to corneal enlargement, buphthalmos and optic-nerve damage. Secondary glaucoma results from an identifiable ocular or systemic condition, medication exposure, trauma or previous surgery.Management is individualized and may include topical or systemic medication, laser procedures and incisional surgery. In childhood glaucoma, surgery is often the main treatment, while medication is used as an adjunct or temporary measure. In secondary glaucoma, treatment must address both IOP and the underlying cause.The central message is that glaucoma is not a single disease and cannot be managed by pressure measurement alone. Accurate classification, optic-nerve and visual-field assessment, appropriate pressure targets and lifelong follow-up are fundamental to preserving vision.Keywords: glaucoma; intraocular pressure; optic neuropathy; open-angle glaucoma; angle-closure glaucoma; congenital glaucoma; buphthalmos; secondary glaucoma; trabeculotomy; trabeculectomy.

etudes.titre: Evaluating global glaucoma awareness efforts: A study of World Glaucoma Week activities and influencing factors
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Purpose To assess the global distribution of awareness and screening activities conducted during World Glaucoma Week (WGW) and to identify national-level factors associated with activity frequency. Design Cross-sectional observational study. Subjects Countries and cities reporting WGW activities (2015–2024) on the official WGW website. Methods Activity rates were standardized per 10,000 individuals with glaucoma-related blindness in each country. Pearson’s and Spearman’s correlation analysis was used to examine associations between WGW activity levels and national indicators, including the presence of a glaucoma society, the number of ophthalmologists, Gross Domestic Product (GDP), and Inequality-adjusted Human Development Index (IHDI) Results An average of 548.1 WGW activities were reported annually. Public education (30.9%) and awareness campaigns (30.2%) were the most frequently conducted activities. Manila, Philippines, reported the highest average number of activities per year (35.3), followed by Quito, Ecuador, and Bogotá, Colombia. When adjusted for glaucoma-related blindness, Antigua and Barbuda had the most frequent activities, followed by Barbados and Croatia. Countries with a national glaucoma society reported significantly more activities (median 19.50 [IQR 4.00–54.75] vs. 0.00 [IQR 0.00–2.50]; p < 0.001). Significant correlations were observed between WGW activity levels and population size, IHDI, number of ophthalmologists, and glaucoma blindness prevalence as estimated by the Global Burden of Disease Study. Conclusions Marked global disparities exist in glaucoma awareness efforts. The presence of a national glaucoma society is strongly associated with increased WGW activity levels, underscoring the critical role of organized professional support as a major driver of glaucoma awareness worldwide.
