etudes.titre: Effects of Visual Function Impairment on Depression in Patients With Glaucoma
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Background: This study aimed to investigate the relationship between the degree of visual impairment and depressive symptoms in patients with glaucoma, and examine whether disease duration moderates this relationship. Methods: We enrolled 208 patients with glaucoma who received standardised treatment at The Affiliated Huaian No.1 People’s Hospital of Nanjing Medical University from February 2022 to February 2025. Clinical data and visual function indicators were collected. Patient-reported visual function was assessed using the 25-item National Eye Institute Visual Function Questionnaire (NEI-VFQ-25), and depressive symptoms were assessed using the SelfRating Depression Scale (SDS). Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) and central macular thickness (CMT) served as indicators of visual impairment. Statistical analyses, including descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, linear regression analysis and subgroup analysis with Fisher’s r-to-z transformation, were performed using SPSS 26.0 software. Results: The mean BCVA was 0.31 ± 0.12, and the mean CMT was 263.22 ± 29.01 µm. Depressive symptoms (SDS score ≥ 53) were present in 45.67% of patients. BCVA was negatively correlated with the SDS total score (r = −0.23, p < 0.001), whereas CMT was positively correlated with the SDS total score (r = 0.27, p < 0.001). The NEI-VFQ-25 total score was also negatively correlated with SDS scores (r = −0.22, p = 0.002). Linear regression showed that for every 0.1 increase in BCVA, SDS scores decreased by 1.53 points (p < 0.001); for every 10 µm increase in CMT, SDS scores increased by 0.74 points (p < 0.001). Subgroup analysis and formal interaction testing revealed that disease duration significantly moderated the associations of visual function with depression: the correlations between BCVA (r = −0.44 vs. −0.07, p < 0.010) and NEI-VFQ-25 (r = −0.49 vs. −0.03, p < 0.001) with SDS scores were significantly stronger in patients with longer disease duration (≥5 years), with significant interaction terms (both p < 0.010). Conclusions: The degree of visual impairment in patients with glaucoma was significantly associated with depressive symptoms. Objective measures (BCVA and CMT) and NEI-VFQ-25 were independently related to depression risk, and these relationships were more pronounced in patients with longer disease duration. Clinical practice should emphasize visual function protection and psychological treatments to improve patients’ mental health.

etudes.titre: Automated Perimetry in Children with Suspected and Known Glaucoma: Virtual Reality Versus Tabletop
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Perimetry »
etudes.resume: Abstract Humphrey visual field (HVF)-equivalent virtual reality fields (VRFs) have shown promise in adult glaucoma. Research comparing HVF-equivalent VRF to standard automated perimetry (SAP) in pediatric glaucoma is limited. We aimed to evaluate agreement and concordance between HVF-equivalent VRF and SAP for children with glaucoma. This prospective study enrolled children with known or suspected glaucoma. Participants completed HVF then VisuALL HVF-equivalent VRF at one visit. A masked ophthalmologist graded visual fields for defects and location. Global parameters were compared between devices. A point-by-point deviation plot analysis was performed. A total of 60 patients (116 eyes) were included, mean age 13.1 ± 2.93 years. Mean retinal nerve fiber layer thickness was 86.1 ± 21.20 µm. Average mean deviation (MD), pattern standard deviation (PSD), and foveal sensitivity significantly differed for HVF versus VRF. There was moderate association between HVF and VRF for MD (P < 0.001) and PSD (P < 0.001). Concordance by region for any defect was 76.2%; point-by-point match rate for total deviation plots was 75.8%. Test duration was longer for HVF versus VRF (4.17 ± 1.19 vs. 2.10 ± 0.18 minutes, respectively, P < 0.001). Most children (98%) preferred VRF over HVF. HVF and HVF-equivalent VRF testing modalities yielded moderate association. HVF-equivalent VRF offers a shorter test that children preferred and may supplement SAP.

etudes.titre: Lamina Cribrosa Strain as a Glaucoma Prognostic Factor: The STRAIN Study Methodology and Initial Outcomes
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Objective: To estimate the lamina cribrosa (LC) strain response to intraocular pressure (IOP) change in open angle glaucoma (OAG) patients and examine associations between LC strain and demographic and clinical characteristics relevant to OAG in an ongoing longitudinal study. Design: Cohort study Participants: Adult patients with OAG (205 eyes of 119 patients) Methods: The STRAIN study is an ongoing longitudinal study designed to determine whether LC biomechanical strain is associated with present, prior, and future OAG damage. In this initial analysis, patients either temporarily stopped ≥ 1 eye drop, initiated an eye drop, or underwent selective laser trabeculoplasty to produce IOP change. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) scans of the optic nerve head (ONH) acquired before and up to several weeks after IOP change were analyzed using digital volume correlation (DVC) to estimate LC strain. Strain measurements were compared with age, race, sex, axial length, central corneal thickness (CCT), corneal hysteresis, optic disc area, years of known OAG, retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness, and visual field mean deviation (MD). Main Outcome Measures: LC strain estimated by DVC from OCT scans acquired before and after IOP alteration. Results: Axial LC strain ( E zz ) was tensile with IOP decrease and compressive with IOP increase. Maximum principal strain was tensile (mean E max = 1.09%), and maximum shear strain was positive (mean Γ max = 1.16%) in the radial-axial plane. Both increased quadratically with the IOP change. Older age was significantly related to greater tensile circumferential strain ( p = 0.02) and lower Γ max ( p = 0.01). Sex, CCT, corneal hysteresis, and optic disc area were not significantly associated with LC strain. In combined multivariable models adjusting for IOP change, demographics, and accounting for correlations between eyes from the same patient, eyes with thinner inferior-quadrant RNFL had smaller Γ max for a given IOP change ( p = 0.02). Conclusions: LC strain in patients with OAG is associated with the degree of neuronal loss, age, and axial length, supporting a relationship between the LC biomechanical response and factors relevant to glaucomatous damage.

etudes.titre: TRACE: a framework for traceable biomedical resource construction demonstrated through single-cell glaucoma data
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique

labos.nom: National Health and Medical Research Council

etudes.resume: The growing availability of public omics datasets presents opportunities for biomedical research, yet constructing research question-driven resources from distributed studies remains challenging due to heterogeneous data, incomplete metadata and limited documentation of curation decisions. Here, we present TRACE (Traceable Resource Assembly and Curation Ecosystem), a general framework that links systematic knowledge discovery, data curation and resource delivery while preserving provenance throughout resource construction. We demonstrate TRACE through TRACE-scGlaucoma, a curated single-cell transcriptomics resource for glaucoma and optic nerve biology. Systematic screening identified 57 eligible studies, of which 42 provided accessible datasets comprising approximately 3.3 million cells. The resource provides harmonised metadata, standardised cell-type annotations and reusable expression objects while retaining original study information and curation provenance. We demonstrate its analytical utility through cellular enrichment of glaucoma GWAS-associated genes, comparing candidate drug-repurposing signals across distinct biological contexts and assessment of cell-type annotation reliability. TRACE provides a systematic and traceable approach to transforming fragmented public datasets into reusable biomedical resources, supporting reproducible analyses and future extensions across disease areas and data modalities.

etudes.titre: Plasma Proteogenomics Identifies RGMB as a Candidate for Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma Detected Only in East Asians
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Abstract Purpose In East Asians most primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) occurs at statistically normal intraocular pressure (IOP). We sought plasma proteins linked to POAG through genetic signal not shared with IOP. Methods We integrated the BioBank Japan POAG GWAS with a Japanese plasma pQTL resource (Nagahama; SomaScan v4) using SMR/HEIDI and colocalization against POAG and IOP datasets, including a Genomic-SEM–derived non-IOP POAG component, adding a symmetric proteome-wide cross-ancestry colocalization, fine-mapping and multi-signal colocalization of the RGMB region, a formal heterogeneity test, and expression mapping in retina and trabecular meshwork. Results Of 679 plasma proteins, four colocalized with POAG in East Asians only, five in Europeans only, none in both. SMR nominated RGMB as a suggestive risk factor (b_SMR = +0.277; HEIDI P > 0.05; PP4 = 0.684; rs1037599); none survived Bonferroni correction. RGMB did not colocalize with European IOP, a European non-IOP POAG component, or European POAG on the same platform, despite a common, directionally consistent pQTL instrument. Multi-signal colocalization reproduced both the East Asian signal and the European null. The per-allele POAG effect differed between ancestries (Cochran’s Q P = 0.0036; I² = 88%), the better-powered European data excluding an effect of East Asian magnitude. RGMB and its receptors were expressed in trabecular meshwork cells and unchanged by TGF-β2. Conclusions This triangulation nominates the RGMB–neogenin–BMP axis as a POAG candidate detected in East Asians but not Europeans, which does not colocalize with IOP-related traits. The findings are exploratory; ancestry-matched replication and functional validation are required.

etudes.titre: FEATURES OF ULTRASOUND BIOMICROSCOPIC FINDINGS IN DIFFERENT FORMS OF GLAUCOMA
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Glaucoma is a heterogeneous group of disorders that differ in the mechanisms of intraocular pressure ele­vation, anatomical characteristics of the anterior segment of the eye, and the nature of disturbances in aqueous humor outflow. Conventional diagnostic methods, such as slit-lamp biomicroscopy and gonioscopy, allow assessment of the anterior chamber and its angle, but often do not provide adequate visualization of the ciliary body, posterior chamber, zonular fibers, and retroiridal structures. Ultrasound biomicroscopy (UBM) enables detailed evaluation of the spatial relationships between the iris, ciliary body, crystalline lens, zonular fibers, and structures of the anterior chamber angle. UBM findings differ signifi­cantly in primary open-angle and angle-closure glaucoma, plateau iris syndrome, pigmentary and pseudoexfoliative glaucoma, as well as in lens-induced and ciliary block mechanisms. Identification of the predominant anatomical mechanism of intraocular pressure elevation is of considerable importance for selecting a pathogenetically justified treatment strategy. UBM is also used to evaluate the outcomes of laser and surgical treatment of glaucoma. The aim of the present study was to investigate the characteristic ultrasound biomicroscopic findings in different forms of glaucoma and to determine the diagnostic value of UBM in differentiating the major mechanisms responsible for increased intraocular pressure.

etudes.titre: Evidential Deep Learning with conditional entropy for glaucoma detection
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Deep Learning »; mot du titre : « detection »
etudes.resume: We propose a novel conditional entropy function as a basis for quantifying predictive uncertainty in Evidential Deep Learning (EDL) for glaucoma detection from retinal fundus images. Using the EyePACS-AIROGS-light-V2 and RIM-ONE-DL datasets for validation, we found that our proposed EDL model regularized by conditional entropy function produced uncertainty estimates with substantially lower calibration errors than Deep Ensembles, MC Dropout, post-hoc calibration and the conventional EDL framework based on Dempster uncertainty. To further probe our models' interpretability, we analyzed Grad-CAM heatmaps using a focus index representing spatial concentration. Compared with the other uncertainty quantification methods, EDL models exhibited greater separation between the index distributions of correctly and incorrectly classified fundus images. In particular, false negatives were associated with localized Grad-CAM activations that were displaced from the optic disc, consistent with its established clinical importance in glaucoma assessment. Overall, our findings suggest that our proposed EDL framework for glaucoma detection provides not only enhanced uncertainty calibration but also admits a more physiologically consistent interpretability.

etudes.titre: Baseline neuroticism and subsequent reporting of doctor- treated glaucoma in the Health and Retirement Study
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Abstract Background Personality has usually been measured after glaucoma diagnosis, limiting temporal interpretation. We examined whether baseline neuroticism was associated with subsequent survey reporting of doctor-treated glaucoma among older participants in the Health and Retirement Study (HRS). Methods This exploratory longitudinal analysis included HRS participants aged 65 years or older whose first psychosocial leave-behind assessment was in 2006 or 2008, who had no positive glaucoma report at or before baseline, and who had at least one later glaucoma assessment through 2020. Neuroticism was the standardized mean of four Midlife Development Inventory items, requiring at least three observed items in the primary analysis. The endpoint was the first subsequent respondent- or proxy-reported positive response to “Has a doctor ever treated you for glaucoma?” Observation intervals were split at fixed 2-year elapsed-time boundaries. Complementary log-log models included log segment duration as an offset, a fixed elapsed-time baseline hazard, age, sex, race/ethnicity, and education, with participant-clustered standard errors. Results The analysis included 7,217 participants, 1,067 first positive reports, and 61,833 person-years (median follow-up, 8.5 years). Of the events, 954 occurred at respondent interviews and 113 at proxy interviews. Each 1-SD higher neuroticism score was associated with a hazard ratio (HR) of 1.091 (95% CI, 1.025–1.161; P = .006). Reconstructing follow-up from respondent interviews only yielded HR 1.082 (95% CI, 1.013–1.156). Results were similar in the inverse-probability-of-censoring weighted attrition sensitivity (HR, 1.086; 95% CI, 1.018–1.159) and with the HRS guide-based two-of-four-item scoring rule (HR, 1.090; 95% CI, 1.024–1.160). In the healthcare-use complete-case sample, the HR was 1.076 before and 1.041 after adjustment for all measured general healthcare-use variables. Four- and 6-year landmark estimates were 1.072 (95% CI, 0.995–1.154) and 1.064 (95% CI, 0.972–1.166). Accounting for competing death, standardized 10-year probabilities at the 25th and 75th percentiles of neuroticism were 11.40% and 12.60%, a difference of 1.20 percentage points (95% CI, 0.25–2.13). Conclusions Higher baseline neuroticism was associated with a modestly higher rate of subsequent reporting of doctor-treated glaucoma in this selected HRS cohort. Attenuation after adjustment for general healthcare use, depressive symptoms, and baseline eye-health measures leaves disease occurrence, detection, and reporting as unresolved explanations.

etudes.titre: Beyond the Index: Association of AI-CO Central Image Area with Central Visual Field Damage in Glaucoma
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « AI »; mot du titre : « Visual Field »
etudes.resume: Abstract Purpose To evaluate the associations of the numerical AI-CO center index and visually classified central dark-area extent with Humphrey 10-2 mean deviation (MD). Methods This single-center retrospective study included 320 eyes of 169 patients with AI-CO imaging, broad-field 24-2F or 30-2 testing, and 10-2 testing. Both visual field examinations were performed within 365 days before or after AI-CO imaging. Two ophthalmologists independently classified central dark-area extent into five Levels (0–4). Analyses assessed Spearman correlations, areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs), distributions across final central dark-area Levels, and interrater reliability. Patient-cluster bootstrap confidence intervals and a one-eye-per-patient sensitivity analysis addressed inclusion of both eyes. Results AI-CO center correlated with 10-2 MD (ρ=0.829; 95% CI, 0.773–0.873). AUCs for 10-2 MD below −2, −6, and −12 dB were 0.902, 0.939, and 0.961, respectively. The numbers of eyes in Levels 0–4 were 66, 57, 94, 53, and 50; median 10-2 MD values were −0.59, −1.48, −3.54, −6.24, and −18.15 dB, respectively. Quadratic-weighted kappa was 0.970 (95% CI, 0.958–0.981). Sensitivity analyses yielded broadly similar findings. Conclusions The numerical AI-CO center index and visually classified central dark-area extent were associated with central visual field damage. Assessing the extent of dark regions in the central image alongside the numerical index may provide useful information for interpreting central visual field status from the AI-CO display.

france.nom: CATIOLANZE 50 microgrammes/mL, collyre en émulsion

presentations.libelle: 30 récipients unidoses de 0,3 mL polyéthylène basse densité (PEBD) en sachets de (6 x 5 récipients unidoses) aluminium polyéthylène

smr.libelle: Le service médical rendu par CATIOLANZE 50 µg/mL (latanoprost), collyre en émulsion, est important dans les indications de l’AMM.

asmr.libelle: Compte-tenu : • d’une démonstration de la non-infériorité de CATIOLANZE (latanoprost sans conservateur) par rapport à XALATAN (latanoprost avec conservateur) sur la réduction de la pression intraoculaire (PIO) matin et soir, après 12 semaines de traitement, • d’une démonstration de la supériorité de CATIOLANZE par rapport à XALATAN sur la réduction du score de coloration cornéenne à la fluorescéine (CFS) chez les patients ayant un score CFS >= 1 à l’inclusion, après 12 semaines de traitement, mais : • de l’absence d’une démonstration de la supériorité de CATIOLANZE par rapport à XALATAN à 12 semaines sur : • la réduction de la PIO matin et soir, compte-tenu de la différence non significative entre les deux groupes sur la mesure du soir, • la variation du score des symptômes de maladies de la surface oculaire (MSO), chez les patients avec un score moyen > 0 à l’inclusion, • du profil de tolérance à court terme (12 semaines) de CATIOLANZE similaire à celui de XALATAN et marqué notamment par des événements indésirables oculaires tels qu’une hyperhémie oculaire et conjonctivale, une irritation oculaire, une kératite ponctuée, une douleur oculaire, une photophobie ou une conjonctivite, et des effets indésirables liés à la classe des analogues de prostaglandines (hyperpigmentation de l’iris, croissance des cils), • de l’absence de données de tolérance comparatives à long terme versus XALATAN permettant de démontrer un avantage de la formulation sans conservateur, la Commission considère que CATIOLANZE 50 µg/mL (latanoprost), collyre en émulsion, n’apporte pas d’amélioration du service médical rendu (ASMR V) par rapport à XALATAN (latanoprost), collyre en solution.

non_couverts.raison: Le registre ARTG de la TGA n'a pas d'API publique et son site n'a pas répondu aux requêtes automatiques. Le remboursement australien (PBS), lui, est couvert dès que la clé publique PBS est dans .env.

L'API de NICE est réservée aux organisations (pas aux particuliers ni aux étudiants), avec certification de cybersécurité (Cyber Essentials Plus ou ISO 27001), licence et redevance hors Royaume-Uni ; l'usage d'IA sur ses contenus exige cette licence. La MHRA ne publie ses autorisations que sous forme de pages web et de documents, sans API ni fichier ouvert.
Les évaluations du bénéfice sont publiées en pages web et PDF, sans API ni fichier de données ; les extraire demanderait un scraping fragile.
